text:
You can tell they are not as high quality as some of the other magnetic lashes. I have used LashLiner for a while and these feel way cheaper, but they are also a third of the price. I also only use the anchors to hold them on, so that caused some issues (below).

A few things -

Some of the anchors the magnet was backwards. Why I put 3 star because I only use the anchors and couldn’t use some of them.

There are only 5 magnets, so when I have to cut them down, there are only 4. LashLiner does 6, 5 when cut down and I can tell a big difference.

The anchors and magnets aren’t near as strong as other brands, so they are a little harder to put on, but once on they do seem to stay in place.

They did seem to irritate my eyes compared to other brands, so maybe it’s the glue they used to put on the magnets? I don’t know. Time will tell to see if it gets worse with wear.

title: WHY did they change the formula?It's an oily mess.
text: Why? Why? Why? I've been using this gentle cleanser for years - so many that I can't remember when I first used it. I've loyally used it through 3 name changes, packaging changes, and now new branding and packaging (why the same blue that that everyone else uses and a teeny-tiny logo that you can't read? Does not stand out on the shelf.) and a new formulation. But, with this new formulation, it is the end of the line for me. They made sunflower seed oil the most prominent ingredient besides water. It makes the cleanser oily - my face, hands, and washcloth are coated in sticky, oily residue mess that I can't get off. Gross. If I want oil on my skin, I will decide to put it there - and it would NEVER be sunflower seed oil. I don't add sunflower seed oil to my food - why would I want it all over my skin, my largest organ? It's just awful. I use several Earth Science products - I really like the brand. But this is not going to be one of them moving forward. So sad, it's like a bad break-up that I didn't see coming....

text:
This is an extremely moisturizing cream that my 4a/4b hair absolutely drinks up!! My hair is extremely dry after washing and letting it air dry (even though I always add a leave-in and oil). So, I decided to use this to help moisturize and twist my hair. I could just feel my hair going from super dry to extremely soft and moisturized from just one application of each section! I also applied this over castor oil, which I applied to my hair beforehand. (I use the L.O.C. moisturization method).

I then twisted my hair and applied this generously (my twist outs always come out better when I'm more generous with my product of choice). After 10 hours or so, I took out my twists and had a very well-defined twist out! There was absolutely no frizz - even after separating each twist (I undo the twist and the split each section in half). I'm really happy with the results.

The pics I'm included are of a two-day-old twist out (I forgot to take a pic on the first day) and my hair still looks great - a little frizzy from sleeping on it, but nothing horrible. I just spritzed on a little leave-in conditioner to refresh my hair and it looked just as good as the first day. This cream is wonderful and allows me to easily go 4-5 days on one twist out - something that many other products just don't do for my hair.

This has a really sweet, pleasant smell to it. It's a white cream that's on the thick side, but very easy to work with and absorbs nicely into the hair - doesn't just sit on top. I also love that it doesn't make my hair feel all crunchy or crispy. My twist out was really soft and my curls were bouncy. Thanks to providing great hold, amazing definition, and complete hydration for dry, frizzy hair, you can't get wrong using this product!

I received this product complimentary in exchange for my honest review. All opinions are 100% mine.

title: Doesn't work for me :(
text:
I saw the reviews for this toothpaste and decided I would give it a try instead of paying my dentist for expensive teeth whitening. I also opted for this one over all the other brands because for years, the only brand I use Colgate Total.

I grabbed 2 tubes, because they were on sale, and have already used 1 whole tube and have started on the second one. I can not detect ONE ounce of difference, neither can my dentist's assistant. My teeth are the same color as when I started. I'd understand it not working if my teeth were extremely discolored but they are only slightly discolored but still very noticeable to me (curse my childhood of drinking teas & cola!!! lol). I even bought the special 360 Optic White toothbrush (which I absolutely LOVE btw) because it was supposed to help with the whitening but still a no go. :(

It's a good toothpaste, as a toothpaste, but as for whitening, it doesn't work. I'm glad that it's working for other people but it has not worked a lick for me which is a bummer I really had high hopes. I guess I will finish this current tube and go back straight back to my Total. If your looking to buy it, I would give it a try because even though it didn't work for me, it might work for you.

title: Just my honesty
text:
Honest review:
Okay so I have worn this wig since Saturday and today is Tuesday. My take on the wig since its been washed, knots bleached and flat ironed.

Pros:
Wig didnt smell
Is very full and has body
Knots bleached easier than expected
Lace blends well against skin..may want to use glue rather than hair spray bc it don't hold well.
Wig looks good and dried well after washing.

Cons:
Alot of fly aways, thinner ends in frontal
Construction isnt the best. The wig has a track seperating the frontal from the sewn bundles which is irritating because the part isnt that long which leaves me with the only option; remove it or monitor whether its showing or not which is uncomfortable bc a wig shouldnt expose you. This irritates me BIG !!!!
The frontal of the wig is whispy and not as full as the back. Im not sure if its the humidity outside or not but I flatironed it this morning and it looks more of a body wave in the front and straight in the back. Most bobs dont look like that, so this was is a must for me.
Wig cap is HUGE. If tou have an average sized small head you will have to customize this unit. I do understand that they make them to where they can be adjusted to the customers liking abd or big head friendly bc everyones head comes in different sizes but I struggled today lol. I reconstructed the whole wig in the back. I took four tracks out the back and cut the comb out and replaced it to help on the track line and sewed it through the cap for the much needed support. I had to cut the sides down as well bc it was really bulky. I sewed the band that came with the wig into the wig as well to hold the bulkeness down more. When I say I was tired I was but all in all I like it better now, my head is just small. Hopefully I can figure this seperatung track out. I may just use this wig when I want to pull the hair up or something bc I cant be worried about this. 😬 Im not sure of anyone else experienced this with their purchase, but it may have been just mine. I will update once it get colder as far as the hair spray sticking good and the the whispyness of the sides that cant seem to stay straigh all day.

title: For Oily Problem Skin Yes, For Drier Skin, Feels Dried Out And Tight
text:
HOW THIS COMES
This bar of soap comes wrapped in plastic with a label on each side.

TEXTURE
This bar of soap is very crumbly before unwrapped. The soap feels like it will crumble but when you put water on it, it turns into a very muddy bar of soap. You can feel the mud in it.

CLEANING
This does clean the skin well, but if you have normal to dry skin, it really does make it feel stripped and tight when done using it.

INGREDIENTS
There is nothing in this bar of soap to indicate its ingredients other than Dead Sea Mud.

COUNTRY OF ORIGIN
Israel

WHO MIGHT LIKE THIS
Anyone with very dirty greasy skin or who has problems with oil and blemishes might be able to use this.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This bar of soap does not list ingredients but you can definitely feel there is a lot of mud in it. It cleans well but strips the skin.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. No ingredient list took a star off for me. The performance is good for some skin, but mine is more on the normal to dry side so I don't use it as much as the guys do.

title: Good, but could be a lot better
text:
I bought 2 of these. One for myself and one for my Mom. My Mom liked it but I did not. I have always used wooden back brushes with natural bristles but decided to try a plastic one to see if it would last longer. I have never liked nylon bristles and sometimes they irritate my skin. The description said that the bristles on this brush were boar bristles.

First problem I noticed was the handle was shorter than I was used to. I am a short average build guy and I have some difficulty reaching my entire back easily with it. Second issue, the bristles are some sort of soft plastic not boar as advertised. The bristles are tightly packed which is nice but very soft. They didn't irritate my skin like some but the softness left me questioning how clean my back was getting. The tightly packed bristles seem like a great feature but after you use it a couple of times you realize that it makes air tough to get through the bristles so the brush takes longer to dry than most. If you don't really sling the remaining water out of them and/or pat down with a cloth the brush may still be damp the next time you go to use it which doesn't seem hygienic. The last issue I have with this back brush is there are no grips or non-slip material where you hold it. It can become kind of slippery and cumbersome when the handle gets wet.

This does seem to be a well made brush that should last a long time, it just wasn't for me. It is definitely better than the the plastic back brushes you find in most retail stores. My Mom loves it. She kept hers and I was easily able to get return authorization through Amazon with no issues for mine. Going back to a wooden natural bristle brush. Sometimes it's better to stick with what you know.

It's a lightweight and effective serum that leaves my skin feeling pampered and very soft. It works very well during the dry cold months of autumn and winter.

The cleanser is gentle but effective. The moisturizing cream has a lovely scent and the antioxidants that have made the brand famous. It is particularly welcome during the cold, dry months. I love that Caudalie's products work so well. I have sensitive skin but these products have not caused me sensitivity or irritation or redness.

The set is beautifully packaged and would be a lovely gift.

title: Love the colors in this sponge set; sponge texture is dense; metal holder is great
text:
This is a lovely set of three sponges in Easter colors of green, pink, and lilac. It also comes with a great metal sponge holder. The sponges are dense unlike most sponges like this on the market. As a result, make-up does not soak in as easily.

The one lilac sponge with a flat side is great for smooth applications. The typical egg-shaped (pink) and the hour-glass (green) sponges are good for blending or any large make-up application. The hour-glass one is easy to hold in the center.

These feel good in the hands, blend reasonably well, and feel soft against my skin. These blenders make a great gift for the make-up obsessed. I love that the sponges do not smell. I tried other colored sponges and they smell like pencil shavings or other chemicals and these do not.

The sponges themselves are similar in style to all of the others that I tried before this with the exception that the sponges are on the dense side instead of airy. To me what set of sponges to buy all comes down to the price and the angles one wants on the sponges as well as whether it is for gifting or not. The colors are important too - at least to me. These colors also make it perfect for the Easter Basket.

At the current price of $6.99 it is a reasonable $1.75 per piece if I count the holder.

title: I like it a lot, with a couple of caveats
text:
I really enjoy using this oil on my skin. It smells fantastic and seems to absorb quickly, so it doesn’t feel greasy. I can put it on a few minutes before bed, and not worry about getting oil or lotion all over the sheets. I’ve been using it mostly on my legs and arms, but also made a point to use it on my hands and cuticles, and my hands felt great. I think it will be really good this winter as the air gets drier.

I did not, however, like this in my hair. Oils usually work really well in my hair, but I felt like the scent changed almost immediately after putting it on. I smelled a rancid smell, which it does not have in the bottle, and my hair and scalp were clean. Perhaps it’s just my body chemistry, but I was not a fan of this use.

A couple of other things that I wanted to mention that I think are important to know before you buy this:

1. Peppermint and Eucalyptus Essential oils are not recommended on children under the age of six and 10 respectively, so I would not use this on babies or toddlers despite the recommendation on the insert. Children under the age of two should generally avoid topical use of any essential oil. Yes, the oils in this product appear to be highly diluted, but I wouldn’t chance it. They are still smelling it even if you’re not putting it on them.

2. I’m hesitant to use anything with essential oils as an “intimate” lubricant as recommended. Too much potential (in my mind) for mucosal membrane damage, and no, I’m not talking about your nose. Also, oil-based lubricants will break down latex, so be aware of this.

Other than the above concerns I mentioned (which are not concerns if you are using it correctly) I really like using this moisturizer. I will definitely continue to enjoy it.

title: Now I'm too sexy
text:
Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest.

Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job.

And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many.

Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design.

The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach.

Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer.

The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy...

The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice.

The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it.

As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

They do the job but I never got a really close shave after the first one with the same razor. I also got at least one nick or cut every 3 or 4 shaves. I bought a Mach 3 Turbo, March 9, and have been pleasantly surprised at the ease of use, the lack of nicks and cuts, and the very close shave I get.

title: LumaRx facial cleaning brush is like a Sonicare ElectricToothbrush for the face
text:
After moistening my face and the brush heads with water, I tested the sensitive and normal heads with both soap and [[ASIN:B01648QDS4 L'Oreal Paris Age Perfect Facial Cream Cleanser, 5 Fluid Ounce]] and the massaging head with water alone. After a one-minute "application" with any one of the brushes, I love how smooth and clean this makes my face feel.

The packages includes:

- three brush heads (sensitive, normal, and massage) and their covers which have air vents to hasten drying
- one charging base with power cord
- one brush wand that operates at 3 speed levels
- one white plastic zippered travel case
- one instruction pamphlet

PROS:

- The wand contains a rechargeable battery that last for 30 uses. The first charge takes up to six hours. It also has a 30 minute fast-charge feature that will provide 4-5 uses. By the way, I love the charging light on the base; it has a "cool" factor to it.

- There's a one minute timer that has what I call a "tripacer" (like Sonicare's quadpacer) timer built in for each of the three zones of the face. These zones are the T zone, left side, and right side. What this means is that the unit pauses ever so slightly ever twenty seconds to let the user know when it's time to move on to the next zone so that the cleaning time can be distributed evenly among zones.

- None of the three brushes were rough or extremely abrasive. The rotating and vibrating brush heads were as gentle as could be and I have sensitive skin.

- The wand with brush can be used in the shower as long as it's not fully submerged in water.

- This can be used to remove cosmetics.

- The unit comes with a 2-year limited warranty.

CONS:

- Although these brushes remove make-up effectively, I personally only like to use this on the days I do not wear makeup. The reason is that the eye area has to be avoided. I use eye makeup so I wind up washing my entire face with my hands instead as it does not make sense to me to use a brush on only part of my face.

- There are a lot of don'ts in the manual like don't submerge in water, don't use around the eyes, don't use if you are taking steroid-based medication, don't operate outdoors or where there are aerosol products or oxygen being administered, etc.

- If used daily at no more than the maximum two times per day, the brush heads need to be replaced every three months. The Massaging head (since it doesn't not have bristles) can be replaced every six months. This can get expensive. I contacted the company for the replacement price and they said they would let me know when it's orderable on Amazon. I will update the comments section of this review with that information when I receive it.

- The battery on this unit is NOT replaceable as per the email from them which I posted in the comments section of this review.

At first I questioned why would I need such a facial cleansing tool. After using this, however, I realized that I love how it makes my face feel so clean and smooth. This is not a tool I would use more than twice per week since I really hate using this to remove makeup, however, it's so gentle on my skin that I look forward to the cleansing action, mildly exfoliating properties, and the light massage it provides me all without the use of a chemical masque.

text:
These are the flexible, plastic, 3" roller picks. Not the ones Diane makes with a stiffer, metal shaft inside the plastic.
They fit into and secure the magnetic rollers Diane makes, as well as Velcro/brush rollers.

They are not white, despite the item description stating they are and despite the packaging marking them such. They are creamy yellow, very beige, off white, whatever. I'm not sure it matters very much, but if you have a white color scheme going on in the bathroom or on your bedroom vanity table, be aware these picks won't match with that.

Minus one star, because some (about 10%) of the picks are not polished, smooth or well-finished. Some have leftover, ragged plastic from the molding or manufacturing process still attached at the points/ends and along their length. This can make them a bit difficult to quickly insert into the rounded holes of some plastic rollers, and they may also snag your hair when removing them.

These were just not comfortable for my face due to 2 major design decisions. First, the "front" blade is about 6mm behind the front of the razor, so there's a quarter of an inch worth of facial hair under my nose that this cannot reach. Second, the blades are too close together, which causes pull if you have anything longer than a 5 o'clock shadow.

These would be a lot better for a man's face if the head was smaller with just 2-3 blades spaced out more.

title: So much better than 5 magnet eyelashes
text:
After trying several of the 5 magnet type, I found these and I'm so glad I did! The 5 magnet type never worked after I tried to cut them to the right size because there was never a magnet on the end, which made it impossible to get them to stay on without using glue. I found these with 10 smaller magnets and thought I would give them a try! I was able to cut them to the right size and still have magnets on both ends, so they would stay on. I am not very good at applying liquid liner, but I was able to get this liner to work just fine. I used these for my wedding and they stayed on all day/evening and weren't too heavy feeling like some lashes. They really made my eyes pop and stand out beautifully in pictures! In the photos, the close ups were before the wedding to try them out, and although the one end wouldn't stay on that time, I was able to get it to stay on the wedding day.

The only thing I didn't like (which is the same with all of these magnetic liners) is that the liner is difficult to remove. The lashes themselves came off fine, but the liner was not easy to remove (from my skin or the lashes). I don't like to use makeup removers, so I used coconut oil. It took some time to get it off. But I don't think that's anything specific to this liner, it's the magnetic liners in general.

I recommend these lashes over all of those 5 magnet ones!

title: Stayed sticky for 15 minutes
text:
The Multivitamin Sleeping Mask by Vitamasques is made in Korea. The tube has a foil safety seal under the cap.

I liked the concept of a face mask I could wear to bed. I’m not as good as I should be at keeping to a proper skincare routine. So I thought this sleeping mask would be great. Put it on before bed and wake up with a hydrated, healthier face.

The directions say “Apply a generous layer before you sleep or whenever your skin needs a nourishing boost.” I started with a small pea-sized drop, which was enough for my whole face.

The mask has a gel consistency and goes on clear. But it did not absorb into my skin. After fifteen minutes, my face was still sticky and tacky. No way would I go to sleep like that, my face would stick to the pillow.

So I washed the mask off, which was a disappointment since it’s supposed to be a “non-wash off mask.” My skin was a little softer, but having to wash my face because it was still sticky defeats the purpose of a mask that I’m supposed to be able to wear to sleep.

title: another solid epilator from Braun (plus no more underarm bumps!)
text:
Some quick thoughts on this model specifically:
* Removes smaller hairs (0.5mm) than older models, so you can be more aggressive as stray hairs start to grow back
* The "massagers" on the epilation head really do help
* You can use it dry or completely-wet, but not damp (e.g., right after the shower won't work)... and I must say that using it under running water dramatically reduces any discomfort, although it's a bit harder to notice stray hairs
* You can't use it while plugged in (that would be a serious safety hazard in the shower!) but it means that whenever the battery eventually stops holding a charge, you'll have to toss the unit)
* I wish this included a trimming head like other models, for the cases when you have longer hairs you want to attack (they have to be 7 mm or shorter before this will really pull them out)
* This doesn't include an attachment for facial hair like some do (which is OK)... just make sure that your epilator is clean if you're going to use it on your face, because otherwise it will make you break out
* The small spotlight on the unit makes it much easier to see hairs you may have missed
* The exfoliating brush is a nice touch, because epilating frequently leads to ingrown hairs. It says to use it a day or two before epilating, and it's super-gentle... almost feels like it's not doing anything, but I found it's more effective and more comfortable (if more slow) than just using a loofah. The "wait 2 days" advice is good because otherwise your skin gets sensitive

And some thoughts on epilation in general:
* This seems obvious, but I have to say it: it only hurts when a hair is being removed. This means that the first time you epilate, it's very uncomfortable. But since only a small percentage of the hair grows back before you epilate again (assuming you do it at least once every 3 months!), the subsequent touch-ups really aren't bad at all, especially on your legs. (Underarms are less comfortable, and bikini area even less so. Face is also quite sensitive, though that probably varies by person, depending on how much tweezing you normally do.)
* The first time you epilate, your legs will be unbelievably smooth. But hair grows back at different rates, so after a month or so of epilating (maybe one time each week), you'll have tiny hairs here and there, that are starting to grow back but are still too small to get. It's less of an issue with this epilator than others, and the hairs aren't really visible. So if you think someone's going to be touching your legs, then shave :-D but otherwise life is much easier if you just epilate once a week or so. Then if you don't bother doing anything for a month or so, you'll have a few stray hairs here and there, but nothing like someone who shaves regularly and then skips a month (or even a week... or even 3 days). Visible stubble is entirely a thing of the past.
* Remember that the exfoliation is important to prevent ingrown hairs (just little bumps on your legs--mine don't turn red). But if you wax, or if you age ;) you'll have to do that anyway. And this unit's exfoliator is more gentle than a loofah
* And how could I forget the #1 reason to epilate: no more underarm bumps. You know, the ones that you ALWAYS have, despite a million products on the market that say they'll banish them but don't? Sometimes when you epilate, your skin will be red for 30-90 seconds afterward, but then it fades. So NO MORE BUMPS. That alone is reason enough to own an epilator, IMO :) This also helps with bikini-area bumps, but I find in those cases that the redness can take several hours to fade, so it's fantastic to use the day before swimming but would not be a good choice immediately before pool time

title: Fragrance is really strong
text:
This was my first time trying shampoo or conditioner in bar form, and I had the opportunity to try both from this company's line of products. My first impressions were very positive - the ingredients looked clean and natural, as well as being cruelty-free and vegan, I love that it’s plastic free (both the lack of bottle and the packaging), and that the scent options were relatively gender neutral. The bars were a little smaller than I expected, but ergonomically they fit comfortably in the palm of my hand and don't seem to be shrinking too fast after a week or so of use. I'm glad that they have different colors, so that I can differentiate between my bar soap, shampoo, and conditioner!

My experience using them was pretty good. It felt odd at first as I've only ever used bottled shampoo and conditioner, but quickly got used to it and could definitely see myself using more bars in the future. The shampoo bar lathered up easily and left my hair feeling clean and nourished.

I only have two concerns - the first is that I'm struggling to find a place to put them in my shower where they won't get misted by water and disintegrate more quickly that way. The second is the smell. Although it's not unpleasant, it reminded me a little of a scented candle, and was very strong. Three different people commented on the smell of my hair that week, which is not something that usually happens to me. My husband thought that I smelled like cologne! I could see this being a pro or a con depending on how you feel about fragrances. Personally, I found it overwhelming as I'm more on the sensitive side to smells.

Overall, I would consider trying this or a similar product again in the future, but only with a different/less intense scent.

title: Quality Reusable Glass Pump Container, Soap Lathers Well & Feels Good, Has Light Natural Scent
text:
This Cleancult liquid hand soap comes in a high quality, glass container that’s thick and strong with a plastic pump that works well. I’ve been using this coconut based hand soap daily and find it pleasant. It glides and lathers well when I rub my hands together and stays on my hands long enough to be thorough washing. This soap isn’t overly drying, though I almost always need lotion after hand washing. The lavender scent from essential oils is light, which is a plus as I’m not a fan of heavy scent. The container holds 12 oz. and the company sells 16 oz. refills (currently $6.95) in a paper based container styled like a milk carton to reduce plastic waste.

The glass container has a modern design that looks nice countertop. It has a beige or taupe color silicone (or similar) material on the bottom and lower sides that prevents slipping and adds breakage protection. The plastic pump is also beige and good quality but may not last as long as the glass container. Beige isn’t my favorite color but it’s neutral and the company offers a blue shade that looks pretty in the photo. This soap has coconut oil, olive oil, potassium soap, aloe juice, vitamin E, citrus acid, sodium chloride and a natural essential oil blend (not in that order). I assume “potassium soap” is potassium hydroxide (caustic lye), but believe it’s found in all liquid soap under various names. Overall, I like the hand soap and container. 4 stars.

text: This sleep cap was better than I expected in terms of comfort and functionality, although it left a bit to be desired in the style category. text:
I was highly skeptical about this gadget, but when I ruptured a disk in my back, I decided to take a chance. I should have listened to my instincts.

But even if you can get it to stay still enough to rub your foot on the brush, the bristles are weak and cheap. They flattened out with the third attempted use. This is the perfect example of a sucker product! Wouldn't it be great if this worked? But it doesn't. SAVE YOUR MONEY!

A long handled bath brush/pumice stone combo actually does work. If you use it while seated, there is very little bending involved, saving your back.

title: Almost perfect
text:
I purchased an sleep mask just like this in a store and, when it went missing, searched for it high and low until I found it here on Amazon. The mask blocks light well with little or no light leaking in around your nose and none around the eyes. The contoured eye coverings place no pressure on your eyelids. I never felt comfortable sleeping in a traditional sleep mask until I used this style. I can even open my eyes in my mask and my lashes don't even brush it.

The comfort in wearing meant I quickly adjusted to its use and now can't hardly sleep without it. As someone who has had trouble sleeping and finds napping almost impossible, having the routine of perfect dark when I sleep at night has allowed me to build a trigger. Now, when I need to sleep early, want to catch a nap, find myself in a plane, or other times I might ordinarily find it hard to sleep, I can place my mask on and it signals sleep perfectly. It's improved my sleep length and frequency, as well as reduced the time it takes me to fall asleep, which I think anyone could appreciate.

My only gripe is that, while I thought this one was exactly like my previous mask, there's a little difference. There's a little plastic piece on the side of the elastic that joins loops for the adjustment system and they sit very near my ears. I can sometimes feel it digging in and I never remember feeling that on my previous mask. For occasional use, you may not notice it, but using them nightly, the little part can bother me sometimes. My solution plan involves breaking the part and replacing it with something soft or hand-sewing that connection point. Customization is a very small price to pay for the amazingly comfortable contoured foam that makes up the main body of the mask.

[[VIDEOID:bb5d02bd6cdc2aacb49b1a0f62af91fb]] My husband is a professional tattoo artist and he is always looking for the newest and best equipment.

Tattoo machines are an important part of the tattoo process so having a machine that preforms well is a must have.

The description says this machine is a 3.5 stroke but after using this my husband would have to say he believes it to be a 2.8 stroke in his professional opinion.

When doing the tattoo he had to make several passes to get the line bold enough in the skin versus his other machines. He said this would be fine for doing black and grey tattoos but it is not a good machine to pack color.

The machine is bulky and fits in the hand nice. There is no added weight and it doesn't feel uncomfortable in the hand.

This is a rotary machine so traditional clip cords are not compatible with this.

Overall this is a decent machine. Perfect for an apprentice.

title: Great results from this wax!
text: I had a leg and bikini wax with this product and liked it a great deal.  In the past, I've used soy wax (Nufree) in salons and this is also a great product because it doesn't bond to the skin making it much less painful and more to the point doesn't cause near the amount of skin irritation.  The Plum Smooth wax does the same thing but with the added bonus of having a more pleasant smell.  I also found that I had even less post-wax irritation with this than with any other wax I've used.  For my at-home waxing I've used consumer available wax strips like Veet, etc.  but these universally are low quality and, in addition to being more painful (even to an experienced waxer like me), cause irritation and sometimes even bruising/broken skin in the more sensitive areas where the skin it thinner.  This product is better than anything else I've tried and here's hoping that the results continue to be as good as the first couple times of use.  As a side note - the other reviewer had negative results and correctly stated that what works for some people may not work with others - in my experience people that have not had good results with soy wax or the Plum Smooth due to irritation it has been because of allergies or incorrect use of the product, but these are generally considered to be much gentler on the skin than any sugar waxes or products you can purchase as a consumer.

title: Too heavy for use
text:
Out of the box, I loved this. It's soft and smooth and looks like decent quality.

Unfortunately, usability is another thing. The pony tail is HEAVY. And while it didn't seem to matter that my own ponytail was small, the weight of the extension was uncomfortable and it felt like it would slip off at any minute, even when I added an extra scrunched and some clips to hold it down.

The other question I have is regarding the hair itself. Mine was just a little too shiny and perfect to be real human hair. And while I don't have a scientific test at home, anyone can burn a few strands of hair and see how they smell. I did this and then burned a bit of my own and they do NOT burn or smell the same at all. If I had to bet money, I would bet that this is just really good synthetic hair.

But the hair quality is good regardless of what it actually is. It's the fact that it's not usable as a ponytail that makes it less desirable. I may try to use this to sew into a hat for winter because I love the "hair," but really wonder how the other reviewers got this to stay on their head without feeling like they have a heavy weight pulling out their hair.

title: A fair diffuser
text:
I've been diffusing essential oils for almost 30 years, ever since I purchased my first diffuser from Whole Foods back in the 1980s. This diffuser is not representative of the latest generation of diffusers, but it fits nicely within the last generation. The latest generation of diffusers are not waterless, cordless (rechargeable) and portable. I have both types of diffusers in my home and much prefer the latest gen.

This is a nice diffuser but is slightly more expensive than it should be, even with the ceramic appointments. Like all water diffusers you put water in the chamber with a few drops of oil and let it go. The light is nice but doesn't serve much purpose other than to remind you that the unit is on when you cannot see the cold steam. I'm not a fan of the whole thing being lit because it does cause me to take a second look if my eyes slightly open while I'm sleeping. I prefer a thin band of light. Of course on this unit you can turn the light off.

It doesn't come with any oil which is actually good. I find that when an oil is included in with a diffuser it's often the cheapest brand around and smells awful. It might be enough to turn a newbie off of diffusing if they don't know that high quality oils exist. I recommend Plant Therapy.

I don't buy into the claim that this can be used as a humidifier because the output is just not strong enough. After shut-off there is always water still left in the chamber. This is not a good thing because if you want to change oils, you have to diffuse water with vinegar for a couple of run-throughs and then wipe down the inside. Of course there is nothing wrong with left over oil if you don't mind a blend, but sometimes I want one pure smell for a specific purpose.

title: Floral Oil
text:
Ever taken a bath in warm liquefied velvet? If you answered yes to that, look at you livin’ on the wild side! If you answered no, that’s perfectly understandable because I haven’t either and I suppose liquefied velvet wouldn’t get me very clean!

I have however gotten pretty close to what I imagine bathing in liquefied velvet would feel like. Let me take you back in time little ways before we fully dive into my velvet bath experience. You see it all started a month ago when my intriguement (yes, I’m aware that it’s not a real word) with essential oils began. At first, there was nothing in particular that I wanted to know about essential oils, I was just trying to soak everything up I could about them. After figuring out which oils pair well together and the benefits they provide, awesomely enough I was sent a complimentary of New York Biology Lavender Essential Oil. I gotta admit I’m not the biggest fan of the smell of lavender, but I figured I’d give it a whirl! I did some research and I discovered that lavender oil relieves pain, disinfects the scalp, and improves blood circulation. Obviously, that’s just a few tidbits of the awesomeness of lavender; you can dig deeper if you wish!

While researching all things lavender, I read somewhere (I don’t recall the publication) that cats enjoy the smell of lavender. So, I mixed a few drops of lavender essential oil with some water in a spray bottle, gave the spray bottle a few shakes to make sure it was mixed a little bit, and then sprayed the fragrant mixture into the air! Nothing happened. My cats were unphased!

Next, I tried dabbing a bit on myself, you know like one would when they are applying perfume, a few dabs on the wrist, neck, and chest area. I figured out that for the purpose of first smell impressions it was best if I applied the essential oil within five minutes of leaving to go hang out with whoever I was going to hang out with. Applying the essential oil too soon before departure meant that the smell just didn’t last or linger. However, those who did notice my lavender scented awesomeness said I smelled like “raw flower.”

Finally, we (or you) have arrived at my liquefied velvet bath story! Kudos for reading this long, I know I had a few different things going on in this post! One evening, my skin was feelin’ extra dry (thanks to the dry Colorado climate) and my bones were just a smidge achy. I filled up my tub with water, added a spoonful of coconut oil (because coconut oil is like the Beyonce of oils), and added a few drops of #NewYorkBiology essential oil. Bath time wasn’t the same that evening, I felt so cozy and the dryness of my skin was ever so slowing fading away. Not to mention my bedroom smelled of lavender so, with the warmth and coziness of the bath coupled with the calming scent of lavender, I knew I drift off to dreamland with no worries.

title: Decent Shaver with a few Quirks
text:
I've been using Norelco shavers since I began shaving. I briefly tried both another brand and bladed shaving, and didn't like either. I tried this out as a replacement to my 8140XL.

As with most electric shavers on the market, you get convenience, simple charging, savings on consumable blades and cream, and a nice little gadget for your bathroom with this shaver. A blade always wins on optimum closeness, but takes longer and is more "dangerous" to those of us with a not so fine touch. Those aside, there were a few things that I liked, and a few things that bugged me about this specific shaver.

Pros:

-Lightweight
Wow, this shaver is really light and easy to handle when shaving, especially tougher areas that require holding the shaver upright at times.

-Waterproof
The fact that you couldn't get in contact with water or even in a shower used to be a huge disadvantage to electric razors. This unit is fully waterproof, which also makes it easier to clean.

-Uses Li-ion batteries instead of NiCad
One of the things that irked me about the last razor I bought was that it still contained a ridiculously obsolete NiCad battery. NiCad cells suffer from the "memory effect", which means they can hold a smaller and smaller amount of charge over time. This shaver has Li-Ion, the best kind of battery available, with no memory effect. This means it will continue to hold the same charge for years to come.

-Cool Charger base
This is a lot cooler looking, and takes up less space on the countertop than just plugging into the wall and laying the shaver sideways to charge. It also keeps track of the cord.

-Flex Tracker System
The head conforms to whatever surface I'm shaving pretty well, and just looks cool.

Cons: (these won't apply to everyone, and are my opinion only)

-Built in lotion dispenser
I've never wanted this feature. It's simply another way for them to continue to charge for refills of the product, when part of the reason for having an electric razor is so you don't have to keep paying for blades! I also have extremely sensitive skin that doesn't enjoy contact with any kind of chemical, especial alcohol. The stuff doesn't smell too great either. You don't need this goop to use the shaver, so I would skip it.

-Not as speedy as older models
This is something I also noticed with my past model, but it seems like Norelco shavers have for whatever reason gotten *less* effective and take longer to shave. It's not a huge issue for me because I have a light beard, but I thought these things were supposed to get faster with time, not slower.

-40 minutes of charge time
This is not amazing compared to other models, I wish they had skipped the lotion chamber and put three times as many batteries inside instead.

Overall I'd recommend this shaver, it has some great features you'll probably enjoy. You might want to be aware of the cons I've noted, and keep in mind you can follow up on Norelco's guarantee if you're not happy with your individual shave.

title: A great way to trim your beard!
text:
This is a great way to trim your beard. A definite step up from traditional trimmers. The magic in it is the vacuum that captures and stores trimmed beard and mustache hair instead of letting it fall into your sink to make a mess. You don't make your lady mad, and everyone is happy.

The trimmer itself fits comfortably in your hand. It has an detachable cord that allows the unit to be charged. It can operate on the cord or off it's batteries for cordless use. The trimmer is NOT submersible.

The attached guard can be adjusted to 9 length settings with a rotating selector. It can also be taken off for trimming necklines or other areas. There is also a separate smaller attachment that can be used for precision cuts.

The vacuum is power and made more powerful over earlier models through the use of the "Turbo" button that amps up the cutting power and vacuum power substantially. When you are done cutting your hairs are captured in a removable tray for disposal. There are still a few hairs that don't get sucked up but it a huge improvement over using trimmers without suction.

The only negatives are that the hair capture cup is a tad small. There is also a plastic piece that guides hair into the cup that makes neck and cheek-line trimming a little tricky until you get the hang of it.

Overall a great trimmer for those of us real men with beards. A must have!!

title: Good power, would recommend but a few small changes would make the Micro-Pedi even better
text: So far, I'm pretty pleased with this buffer, but there are a few small things that I think Emjoi could improve on. I was able to use this buffer for both feet after only charging for 30 minutes, then plugged it in for the recommended time. It would be nice if the red light ever went off to let you know when it was charged, but this hasn't been an issue since it's always charged when I need it. I don't know exactly how long a full charge lasts, because I've never run it all the way down buffing both feet (about 15 min). The power is good, although I could see that a man with really thick calluses might need more power. It does slow down a little if you press down really hard, but at least on my feet, pressing that hard hurts. So for my purposes, the power is just perfect. The blue buffer has lasted 4 uses so far and seems to still work fine, which is pretty good considering how much has buffed off my feet during these first uses. The primary reason why I'm giving 4 instead of 5 stars is because of two things: 1) the rotating head isn't viewable 360 degrees  (i.e. covered on one side), so it really limits the ability to see what you're buffing. It's particularly hard to use with your non-dominant hand on your opposite foot, because you can't see what's being buffed unless you're looking at the skin from the side. I have friends who have the Amope, which allows you to see your foot better, but has insufficient power and isn't rechargeable. 2) the buffer/roller on this Micro-Pedi is inset pretty deeply between the side pieces meaning that you can't really buff anything that's not convex  (i.e. can't really buff flat or concave surfaces on your feet, only things that stick up/out like heels and toes). This means that I can't adequately buff the callus just below my 2nd toe on the ball of my foot, which is a slightly concave area. As this is my worst callus, that was very disappointing. Press as hard as I might at different angles, I just can't get that spot with this buffer. But for my heels, toes, and the rest of my foot, it's great. So overall, I would recommend this product based on the batteries saved by recharging, the power, the comfort in your hand, and it's effectiveness on most parts of my feet. But I wish the side pieces didn't stick so far out beyond the roller limiting usefulness on concave parts of the foot, and I wish the roller wasn't covered on the back limiting visibility.

title: GREAT FOR DRY HANDS, KNEES & ELBOWS.. But..
text: Vaseline has been around forever; and for good reason!  With all the extra hand washing and constant sanitizer applications, this is an amazing occlusive to seal in moisture back into your hands after you've moisturized.  Personally, I enjoy the Original formula more.  Even though you cannot smell anything, this Vitamin E formula is loaded with added fragrance (CITRONELLOL, COUMARIN, GERANIOL, LIMONENE & LINALOOL) in the ingredients list for no apparent reason.  Fragrance can cause skin sensitivity; i.e. contact dermatitis which completely defeats the purpose of a 'healing jelly'.  Short-term use is fine, but you don't really want to use fragranced products directly on the skin over the long-term.  Stick to the Original Blue Seal 100% Petroleum Jelly.

The deodorant is comfortable, non itchy, and doesn't leave a lot of residue. Spreads easily along skin. And the natural lavender scent is very pleasant.

title: Good slip, highly recommended
text:
I was given the opportunity to review Keeva's tee tree oil shampoo and fell in love with it right after first use. I wasn't around to when they were selecting reviewers for their conditioner but now that it's available for purchase I'm glade to say I've bought it for full sale price being 20 USD. Like it's shampoo counterpart the bottle is 28oz total.

Texture: White and creamy
Scent: Pleasant and definitely not reeking of tea tree oil like it's shampoo sister
Slip: Slip is a product's ability to allow one to detangle hair effectively and not need to use too much product to do so. For the amount I used which is pretty standard across the board with all conditioners I've tried, this conditioner is rated at 5/5 for slip
Moisture: Next to none but that isn't a real issue due to most of the oils being found in Keeva's tea tree oil shampoo
Standout Ingredients: hydrolyzed keratin ( protein ), argania spinose ( Moroccan argon oil ), cetearyl alchol ( fatty alcohol )

Cons:
Cocos nucifera ( Coconut Oil ) isn't listed as an ingredient, however it is featured as an ingredient on the front of the bottle.
Melaleuca alternifolia ( Tea Tree Oil ) isn't listed as an ingredient either.
Both of these oils is on the front of the bottle being featured however, the product doesn't list the oils as ingredients.

Overall, I believe this to be a quality conditioner even better than some brands found in salons. Price of the bottle is reasonable for the quantity received. This conditioner does provide one with good slip and it doesn't leave hair feeling heavy or weighted down after rinsing. I feel that when used with it's sister shampoo, you'll benefit from this conditioner most .

title: Much better then the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer
text:
Until a year ago, I never liked the idea of owning an electric toothbrush: I'd owned several cheap ones and never liked any of them. Then I figured that I'd try one again about a year ago and so I chose the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer. I chose the Spinbrush because it had a large brush, which I thought meant less time/effort brushing my teeth.

The Spinbrush worked pretty well, but the large brush head gagged me horribly. Because of this, I decided to give the Oral-B Vitality a try and I like it much better. The first reason I prefer the Vitality is because it has a much smaller brush head (you don't need a large brush with an electric toothbrush, since the toothbrush is doing all the work.) The smaller brush head also allows me to reach places the larger Spinbrush cannot reach, because it's too big. The Vitality is easier to maneuver in your hand as well, thanks to the smaller handle base.

Another thing I didn't like about the Spinbrush is how it would click off automatically after 2 minutes (I don't think all models of the Spinbrush do this, though.) The Vitality purposely sputters after 2 minutes for it's timing function, but then continues it's normal operation after a second or two. I still find this annoying, but at least I don't have to remove it from my mouth, dripping with toothpaste, just to turn it back on. And if I finish early, the Spinbrush required me to punch the button twice to stop it (again, something not easy to do with a vibrating toothbrush in your mouth), whereas the Vitality only requires a single button push. These two things alone make the Vitality much more convenient.

I also think the Vitality is more powerful then the Spinbrush. The reason you had to push the button on the Spinbrush twice was so you could use it at a lower speed if necessary, but I never found that necessary at all. I prefer the more powerful Vitality, because it feels like it's cleaning better by not slowing down if I push too hard.

About the only thing I liked better about the Spinbrush was that it had an indicator light on the base to tell you it was receiving power (I think it gauged the charge, too, but that was never a problem for me.) I'm not sure if that's even important, but it is something I tend to prefer with rechargeable items. Other than that, I love the Vitality and I much prefer it over the Spinbrush. Now I can brush my teeth without gagging and I am thankful for that.

title: enjoying this - great in tandem with a thick skin cream
text:
My mother asked me to find her a moisturizer with matrixxyl and peptides. Very specific and she didn’t want anything that did not have at least those two ingredients.

The reason is a conversation with her dermatologist. Matrixxyl is made of 2 peptides, palmitoyl-tripeptide and palmitoyl-oligopeptide, which stimulate collagen and elastin production in the skin. And peptides form a long chain of amino acids to become proteins, penetrating the top layer of skin cells and signaling the cells including collagen.

The Cazbe serum works really nicely in tandem with my mom’s Ponds cream (she has used Ponds as long as I remember). The serum absorbs pretty rapidly and unlike other serums, doesn’t seem to leave her skin feeling sort of ‘tight’ or dry. After a few minutes (she will put the serum on before brushing her teeth, and then follow with moisturizer after teeth), she will apply the Ponds cream to completely moisturize her face. I’ve tried this a few times and find I can only really use it around my eyes – it dries out my cheeks and chin. If used just around my eyes, it feels a lot better.

Her skin is looking beautiful. I think in combination with a really solid cream to sort of ‘seal in’ the benefits, after washing your face, and just before bed, it’s a great part of your beauty routine.

title: Disappointing.
text:
This product is very disappointing. Initially I was excited to find a non-peel nail polish that was water based - I'm allergic to harsh chemicals, so traditional nail polish isn't an option. I've used Suncoat peelable nail polish before and liked it a lot because it was completely odor free and did not cause any allergic reaction. It did not last long on my nails, but I figured it was essentially meant for kids, so it's OK it if only lasts for a few hours. I was only wearing it out for dinner, etc. Then I've found out that Suncoat also makes water based polish that is non-peel. I figured I would give it a try. I've read multiple reviews stating that with proper application the product would last a few days on the nails. 2 or 3 days of wear are more than enough for me as I like to change my colors often. Also, I understand that water based polish would never be as durable as the traditional polish, so I was perfectly OK to change it out every couple of days. As soon as the product arrived I applied it as instructed. I did it shortly before bed time so that I wouldn't get my nails wet and allow the polish to cure. By the time I woke up it had already chipped! So, I reapplied and went to work. By the time I got to work it was chipped again! This was embarrassing; I spent good 20 minutes trying to scrap the polish off my nails. Luckily, it came off easily.

What's even more disappointing is that Suncoat customer service does not seem to care about customers. I've contacted them asking if they had any helpful advice and so far received no response.

title: Mine had defects
text:
First, the good: hair is soft, silky and only a tiny bit too shiny. It has good style and only shed a small amount on removing from package and brushing. Not too much hair, but not thin or flimsy. Has two combs at the top in front to secure wig, and the adjustable latches at the neck. I was prepared to love it forever and buy ten more. However:
The not so good and the bad: the color is flat black, there is no natural color variation and looks like a poor dye job, the ear tabs did not align with my actual ears, and so poked out to the sides a bit. The hair line would not lay flat to my head, and when I tried to pull some of the front strands to the side to keep them out of my eyes, I saw that the seams are thick and obvious. Since it has a bit of lace at the top I figured to reset the part, but there is a seam in the middle of the lace, so parting it
in any other location within the lace area literally shows a fat black seam.

Now, I am not a wig expert. I don't know how to make a mediocre wig great, and to this wig's credit, it is better than mediocre. So if you happen to be one of those people with such knowledge, this is a fabulous wig to mess with and work your magic on. And perhaps my particular wig is a defect that slipped through, but regardless, it is a disappointment to me. I would return it, but I made the mistake of cutting the lace right away (like I said, I was excited about how great the wig looked lol). Perhaps down the road I will find a magic maker who can make my wig work for me, so it's not a total loss. Just disappointing.

title: Basic design, but effective; great for house guests
text:
This is a pretty basic toothbrush. It lacks the features found on more expensive toothbrushes, such as sculpted bristle patterns, but it performs just fine. The bristles are a medium/soft density which works well for me -- firm enough for good cleaning but soft enough that it doesn't cause any gum irritation. The handles are also pretty basic but the bamboo makes them more grippy than the basic plastic brushes.

The bristles are all firmly attached. None have come loose after a good amount of use. I can't say the charcoal infused bristles do anything beyond what a regular bristle does, but they look nice.

Each comes individually packed and includes a tiny tube of toothpaste. It's a great item to have on hand for situations such as house guests who forget to bring a brush, for traveling, to stow in your desk at work, etc.

No complaints. They work well, and I'm glad that it's a way to use/discard less plastic waste.

title: Believe The Waring Reviews and Not The Description
text:
Having mixed feelings, I fought with writing this review being that I'm a beauty industry pro and I usually purchase wholesale from an overseas vendor. Just for clarification there is a Loose Wave and a Deep Loose Wave. I have woren borh.
So after unpacking , the loose wave bundles were beautiful until I took it out of the net.... the curl dropped.. What was even more disappointing was the tangling/manageability and how dead/dry the ends were. Testing, by lightly -medium spraying with water and letting dry,I was able to see how much wave /curl was left.... No curl and was puffy/bushy very little to no wave . Usually with loose wave you can wash and go. Not the case here. I also noticed that some bundles lighten faster than the others. During the lightening process there was a toxic chemical smell, yellow residue and I noticed the hair was REALLY hot to the touch and there was a sizzling sound that made me extremely alarmed .. I immediately rinsed in luke warm water. Was afraid to process again so that I could get the potential color want not knowing if the hair was going burn due to how hot the hair was during the first process. Good thing it's for myself and not a paying client so Im fine with the color that I have. There isn't any unusual shedding even after the lightening process BUT it's still early!
To sum things up... I do not recommend using this company. Trust and integrity means a great deal in the business word. As a consumer on Amazon did read the vendors return policy before placing my order AND ALL of the hair vendors have the same policy BUT what I can't understand is how was I supposed to know the hair wasn't as the vendors description and have the problems that occurred without disturbing the bundles? I would have to give a refund if this was for paying client!! The vendor return policy implies they hold no responsibility for misrepresentation in the description so if once you've disturbed the hair... that's it! Classic case of "Take your money and run OR "Next". SMH!!!

title: Pretty amazing...
text:
I've been using this razor since it arrived, approximately 2 weeks ago, and thinking long and hard about the score I'd give it. I actually intended to give it 4/5, the reason being that, while it's an excellent razor, the price point is rather high. In the end, though, I'm so impressed that I really need to give it a full five stars in spite of the price, with the caveat that you may want to take a look at one of the less expensive, stripped-down models; this one is the flagship, but all the models should be similarly excellent (please bear in mind this is the only one I've used).

And excellent it is. While my feelings have already been summed up in the opening paragraph, read on for similarly styled (but moderate) hyperbole.

I've never gotten such a good shave with an electric razor. Norelco does recommend that you give the razor a full 21 days of your time exclusively (i.e. not shaving with anything else) before making a judgment. I haven't had the luxury of giving it a full 21 days, as I need to get my review in; however, I've already adjusted to it so well that I can't imagine going back to my old razors. It will only get better as I get more used to it, although I'm perfectly satisfied at this point and unsure if it could get any better.

Not only do I use it to shave my face (which is obviously what it was designed for, and it does a great job), I use it to shave my head. It's not going to give you as close a shave as a traditional razor, but it's also not going to scrape against your skin like a traditional razor. You'll also save money on shaving cream (the only extra expense is buying a new razor "head" for it yearly, the price of which I am uninformed of). It works "dry". This is nice for me, as it takes a lot of cream to shave both my face and my scalp, and it does, in fact, do a decent job on my head. It's a little stubbly, even right after shaving, but honestly the only thing that would do a better job would be a blade, and that's a difficult way to shave (I was previously using a Headblade). If it can shave a head, where my hair was very thick, I imagine it would be adequate for even the bushiest of beards, and, again, it's designed for faces, not heads.

If you look at the features list, you'll see that this model is full of bells and whistles. Truthfully, they are mostly extras you could live without; the lower-end models would likely be just fine, so I strongly suggest examining them as a money-saving alternative. The meter that shows you how many minutes of the charge are remaining is sort of handy, the icon that lights to remind you to clean it is somewhat useful, but to say they're necessary would be a grave overstatement. In fact, the "wash me" icon lights up after basically every use, so its necessity is particularly dubious. (As a side note, it's marvelously easy to clean.)

In the end, the product does receive my highest recommendation. I think if you tried it out, you'd be pleased, and even if you had to send it back and didn't like it after three weeks via their guarantee (it does take time for your skin to adjust), there would be little time/money wasted. I would, however, encourage you to check out the lower-end models. Ultimately, even the high price point wasn't enough for me to downgrade to four stars. I'm normally quite critical.

title: Smooth application
text:
I like this Makeup Sponge Beauty Makeup Sponge Blender Professional Foundation Sponge. It says "Snowflakes" on the plastic box but I don't know if that is the actual brand name. Given the teardrop design, it probably can be used with a powder based item like eye shadow, but I prefer to use it for foundation blending/application. I like how sponges can use a bit of water with the foundation to help with spreading the foundation on the skin and this sponge does a nice job of this. The foundation goes onto the skin so it looks sheer, fresh and polished. It also does a good job of blending so concealer conceals but doesn't appear obvious. I like that is easy to clean and doesn't have the "make up sponge" smell. If anything makes me stop using a make up sponge, it is the rubber-y used smell that it can get, but this sponge doesn't have that smell so I'm glad of that.

Overall, it is a nice makeup tool to have in the make up box. I like it.

title: Undecided still.
text:
This is perhaps one of the most difficult reviews that I have written in a while. Usually I know immediately if the product is a hit or miss, but Vitabrid C12 is different. I can’t decide. I’m torn. After using VC12 for about 3 weeks, I am still unsure of the results.

The concept: Vitamin C is slow released thru the skin by mixing a small amount of VC12, with water or a moisturizer, onto the face and neck. The results, brighter, smoother and firmer skin. The powder comes in a convenient small bottle (about the length of your thumb) with a small spoon (used for measuring). Simply mix the appropriate amount - I use about 2 spoonfuls since I put it on my face and neck- with a lightweight moisturizer. I didn’t notice any tightness, irritation or itching after I applied this to my skin (i.e., face and neck). I simply apply my makeup as usual. With that being said, I haven’t noticed anything bad either -no additional breakouts and no nasty white film (left on my face from bad blending). But I also haven’t looked in the mirror and said “wow” or “gosh, this is like a facelift in a bottle moment”. Not to mention that this product takes a little more effort than my usual skincare regime. I am not use to mixing products before I use them. **Therefore, I am going to give this product 3 stars BUT continue to use it for a little longer to see if I am wowed. After all each container is believed to last about 3 months. If I notice something earth shattering in the next month or so, I will amend my review. Otherwise, this review will stand.

text:
Had a few pieces of glitter that wouldn't come off from my last manicure, figured I'd try to just go over them. 6+ THICK coats later and I could still see the dots through the polish. It was so bulky on my nails! Looked like I had on super chunky acrylics, and it wasn't even opaque at that point. It was so thick I ended up taking it off after 2 days (which was a nightmare even using 100% acetone...).

As for the colors:
-The two middle greens look exactly the same. I had to redo one of my nails and I couldn't figure out which one that I had first used, they look exactly the same on your fingers.
-I like the yellow! It isn't green at all, it is safety yellow. I wish it was actually opaque.
-The dark green is not as dark as you'd think. As with the yellow I do really like the color, but I'm not going to put 7+ coats on just so it'll look decent.

I missed the return period, otherwise I'd probably return this item. Since I really like the colors and I'm stuck with them I'll probably try putting them on my toes since the bad polish will be less noticeable.

title: Nice Masks, but Watch Pricing!
text:
I purchased a multi-pack (direct from South Korea) that contains all of the types. They are different in that the essence is not at all watery, but rather a very thick gel. The masks can easily been worn for close to an hour before all the jelly is absorbed out of it. The overall fit is good, and there are enough cuts to fit a variety of face shapes.

The results are nice, and each mask does deliver what it sets out to do. The reason for four stars instead of five is because the remaining gel stayed very tacky (at least on me), even a few hours after removing it. So much so that I wound up wiping the remainder off with a damp cloth before finishing up with my other products. Products do tend to hover over my skin, rather than completely absorbing. So this observation may not apply if you are lucky enough to have the type of skin that absorbs products easily.

Are they worth trying? Yes, absolutely. Are they worth $10 each (the price on the page I'm reviewing is 10 for $99.99)? NO WAY. You can find a 10 pc pack for under $20 (including shipping), and I got a 5 pc pack for $12 and change.

I’m really hesitant writing a not so good review for this product given all the 5 star reviews, but what I received definitely has a different look and feel than what others are talking about.
First the texture. The fibers are really dry and definitively do not feel like real hair. When you squeeze it, especially at the top, it reminds me a lot of when you squeeze polyester fiber pillow stuffing.
Then the color. The wig I received has a pink hue that makes the wig look so unnatural when worn. Also the hair color is less textured and much more uniform except for the darker roots.
Last. The hair density. The cap can be seen through the hair at the smallest hair movement.

I would consider this wig more suited for cos-play use (I keep telling my husband he would make a perfect Elton John) than for day to day use. Disappointed.

title: The BEST for preventive maintenance &repair of your skin
text:
Quickly approaching (a still, sadly, rather vain) age 40, I have personally spent a small fortune over the years trying to slow the aging process and reverse the effects of too many days spent gardening without sunscreen. I cannot even begin to list all the products I've somewhat foolishly gambled on to get my skin looking better. This product--and several other products offered through the company NEOTERIC (all under the Alpha Hydrox brand)--are exactly the answer I've been looking for. I've used them both alone and in conjunction with a more expensive brand of anti-aging products (for which I've also left good reviews on this site), and I can see great improvements both ways.

I decided to try this brand of alpha hydroxy cream after reading in Dr. Oz's (and Dr. Roizen's) book [[ASIN:0743292561 You: Staying Young: The Owner's Manual for Extending Your Warranty (You)]]. I'd tried several other alpha hydroxy products before this one (i.e. ROC, etc.) and must say this particular line (ALPHA HYDROX) is far superior to any other I've used. That it is also apparently considerably less expensive than most is icing on the cake, in my book.

Regarding this product, I find the key is to use it AT LEAST once a day, and always after using a mild cleanser. At my age I still get acne and, despite my sometimes manic picking, I notice it (and any residual puffiness or redness, and resulting scarring) clears up much, much more quickly than it used to. Also, my skin breaks out much less than before I used this. The tone and color of my skin are far improved when compared to prior to using this product. I've run out of it before and tried to use something else until I was able to locate more locally, and to my dismay the condition of my skin began to deteriorate.

I won't try to insult anyone by saying the Alpha Hydrox line will remove every wrinkle or fix all your skincare woes. If there is a product out there that does this, I want to know! But for now, this is by far the best line of products I've used. I use this item, particularly, with the line of skincare I reviewed previously, as that seems to address reversing the signs of aging better (where this one, for me, just improves the overall condition and appearance of my skin).

title: Clunky Curler
text:
Unless you have very long eyelashes to begin with, this curler is a throwaway for me.
Sure it has a solid build/weight and looks nice, but the design in no way allows you to grip the actual lashes fully. The curler sits bulky on your face and pinches when you are using it. Plus, if you have shorter lashes, you barely can get the tips to grip (unlike, for example, Shu Uemura curler, which has a finer/thinner frame to work with that better fits to the curve and sits closer to your face).
So for those not gifted with mile-long lashes, you may want to go with another choice.
The mascara is a bit better.
But, then again, I mainly was looking for the eye curler. Too bad the smooth/delicate functionality of design is lacking in this one.

title: Falls Out
text:
I was overly excited for these nose bones.
When I received the product I removed my old nose ring and put a baby blue stud from the box in.
It was immediately too loose in my nose, but was the same gauge.
I decided it might be just because I wasn't use to it yet and returned to my normal routine.
I woke up the next morning with the stud out of my nose.
I put another stud in but felt the same way.
The second stud from this lot was slipping out of my piercing all day, and I was worried it would fall out again.
Thus, I returned to my original nose bone I had before I received these and have no problems.
I gave 3 stars instead of 1 because I cannot say it was the product's fault or mine the studs did not work out for me.
I would not be able to say I recommend this product based on my experience.

title: Hair is OK, tape is iffy. Possible return.
text:
I just installed these last night. I wanted to cover up some intense layering that I think makes my hair look frizzy when straight. Was initially pleased with the color and quality but the tape is not very strong. Now I'm realizing after styling that not only is the tape bad, but the hair is sketchy. Some of the sandwiches are already pulling apart and do not feel sticky. The hair itself smelled slightly synthetic while I styled it, and I noticed the ends bubbled up with heat application like synthetic would. I also noticed several strands of super thick, plastic-feeling pieces. I pulled one off the weft and it snapped apart like it was plastic. Tried to take a picture of the bubbled ends as well as one of the thick pieces.

I've used other inexpensive brands that have had better tape, and don't mind synthetic when you know it's what you'll get. I will probably take these out and return them as-is or have to buy better tape to fix them.

title: Definetly Works
text:
This system definitely works to whiten teeth. Everyone's teeth are different and I imagine everyone gets very different results but it isn't snake oil - it does do something! I have very sensitive teeth and have steered clear of whitening for years. During the pandemic I've found myself drinking a lot more tea and that has really discolored my teeth and was starting to get embarrassed about them. I bought this device since so many people say it's good for people with sensitivity.
I used the device as instructed. It never bothered my teeth at all. It did start to irritate my gums a little, but nothing too bad and only while I was actually doing the whitening. What I did find, is that I was incapable of keeping my tongue completely away from the whitening product (especially because there's a lot of saliva build up and spitting involved). It really hurt the tip and side of my tongue on the days I was using it. I had to stay away from certain foods which was a bummer. After the recommended 5 days of use, my teeth were absolutely whiter. I didn't have Hollywood level whiteness, but they were a lot better than they had been and I was no longer embarrassed. I could have gone on and done more whitening, but my tongue couldn't take it anymore. I will probably go back in a couple of months and do the process again.

I feel like I can definitely recommend this to people with sensitive teeth. I think everyone's whitening level will be different (some might be more or less than me) but it does work and depending on your level of tolerance for the whitening product, you can likely get to your desired level.

title: Literal Nightmare
text:
To preface my review this is my first attempt with at-home waxing & I'm Trans MTF. I've waxed plenty in my lifetime, but always at a salon by a professional. Now I'm sitting here typing this review with an incredibly thin layer of wax all way down my still very hairy left leg.

I purchased the wax roughly 3 months ago, so I don't think the wax is expired, and it was stored in the original packaging in the meantime. I think the main issue is with the roller unit in general. I was literally pulling more hairs out just rolling the wax onto my leg than I was will the couple of strips I did manage to try. I don't have an issue with pulling hairs or anything. Tweezing nose hairs, or threading is WAY more painful and I don't have an issue with either of those.

It took the unit forever to just warm up enough, instructions are laughable at best (broken unclear English), the included wax cleanup wipes are useless & dry (I'm about to google how to remove all this excess wax off my leg in a moment here). I feel if I could break open the unit and heat the wax over the stove it would work 100% better, but I don't want to risk my cookware.

Update: #1: I was able to successfully microwave the cartridge for 3 mins in a bowl of water. 5 minutes would likely work better for you as my cartridge was still warm when I started. The wax rolled much nicer this time around, but still required some pulling, however it started to pool on one side of the roller resulting in the whole roller stopping again and even got a spot onto my bathroom rug that I had been carefully avoiding... The irritation from the wax is worse than using a depilatory cream (such as Nair)

Update #2: After oven an hour of attempting to remove the wax with various products. (baby oil, oil-free makeup remover, acetone, rubbing alcohol, body wash, and finally olive oil in that order). The olive oil and now trashed white washcloth finally did the trick. I really can't recommend avoiding this product enough. I'd be willing to try hard wax, but I'm not about to attempt anything from home until I consult with my local salon at my next nail / hair apt.

title: BAD Design, Unusable Trimmer
text:
When my (non-vacuuming) Norelco trimmer would no longer take a charge, I ordered this item, not too concerned over whether the vacuum was effective or not.

What I received was a poorly designed trimmer:

1. To hold the trimmer, one must place one's hands over the vacuum air exit slots, thus throttling the vacuum.

2. The guard was so complex to attach and detach that it took 10 minutes each time to do it.

3. The closeness settings don't actually lock in, and tend to "wander" toward (1), the closest setting. And so I would find myself completing my trim with 3/4" length hair on one side of my face, graduating to stubble on the other.

I finally threw the thing in the garbage after a week and bought a leftover non-vacuum Norelco model like the one I previously had - $19.99.

So, if you see some poor soul walking down the street with long whiskers on one side of his face, and a 5 o'clock shadow on the other, be kind. He's probably not dimented - just the victim of this "new and improved" beard trimmer.
