These are made in China, and there is no clarification on the package that I can find. So I don't have a clue what these are made of.

They are not quite as soft as the ones that come with their own serum that I've tried. But they are fairly sturdy. You can rip them if you start ripping in a corner, but they don't rip as easily as I would have thought.

title: Health and product review
text:
Let me start off with saying I do not use makeup daily, more like once a week if that but I still recommend the same advice even for daily makeup wearers: change this out either once every week or every two weeks. This is not because the quality is poor, this is for health reasons. All sponges collect bacteria.

Now on to the product review, this showed up really fast with prime and comes with two cases, one to carry a single one and the second to store the rest. Having them as two different colors helps a lot and makes it fun to change. They are soft but not too porous, the makeup will sink in a bit but not too much. These are better suited for applying makeup but not blending them together. I recommend lightly (or roughly if you don’t care) patting your face rather than dragging or rubbing it on, you’ll just end up taking the makeup off your skin.

title: It' Pretty Good
text:
Saw this puppy discussed a lot on various shaving sites. They all said that you have to watch the YouTube videos to get the right technique for lathering. I watched a couple and have been trying this now for the past several weeks. I must have tried close to 40 different soaps, creams and sticks from the most expensive to the not so expensive. This one is right up there in terms of face glide and lubrication.Certainly in the top quintile. Why 4 stars? I have tried every variation to get a lather but there is no getting around that this is the most difficult soap I have ever tried. Too much water, too little water it seemed impossible to get it right the first time. No matter what I tried it seemed to either be too foamy and thin or not enough water to generate a lather. It's as if the gremlin in the soap puck was contrary enough to defeat whatever I tried until the 2nd or 3rd try.
Bottom lime- With effort and persistence it gets the job done and the fragrance is mildly pleasant but it will never be my "go-to" product. I'll stick with may favs: Kiss My Face, Cella and Proraso cream.
UPDATE:
Gave it another try with a little more patience. It seems that the end product you want is a little on the thick creamy side and not really a "lather". If you wet your brush, turn it over and let all the water drip out that you can,then you apply brush to soap and be patient and determined you will get the thick rich cream that will do the trick. One other tip I found after you apply the cream to the face let it sit for about 20-30 seconds before you apply your razor. You will then get the greatest glide you will experience. Accordingly I have moved it up the top tier and displaced the Proraso cream.I would give it 4 1/2 stars, and not 5, if I could because of the difficult lathering.
FURTHER UPDATE
After using this puppy for a little while I have come to master it and love it. Great for glide and closeness and absence of irritation. I originally rated it a 4 but now after careful consideration I must admit that it deserves a 5 star rating. Its among my top 3 favorite shaving products.

The Pros: It seems sturdy and well-made with a nice grain. It's smooth (the teeth on the plastic picks tend to splinter and peel with time). It feels comfortable to use. It probably has good stay power.

title: It isn't even close to natural bristle
text:
I wanted to try a synthetic fiber brush since it is impossible to dry your natural bristle brush sufficiently before packing it up on the day of travel. I was looking for a brush that I can use, shake out and pack within minutes. For use at home, I've had over the years a couple of natural badger brushes of varying quality, ranging from lower grade black only brushes to very fine silvertip. So, trust me, I know how they feel.
This brush is for me virtually unusable.
When i try to lather up, i spray water and soap all over the bathroom. Try as i may, i couldn't prevent the spray. When these synthetic bristles are deflected even only a little, they spring back with a snap. It appears that the spring back force increases linearly with the amount of deflection. And all the fibers move almost in unison.

This is very different in natural bristles where more force bends the hair further, but it isn't like a linear increase in force. During the lather, the bristles conform to your face and the circular action seems to gently bent the hairs in one or the other direction. The brush also spreads a bit, as fibers are pushed and bent a little. Once you lift the natural hair brush off your face, the bristles don't string back all at once. Some fibers may return to their approximate straight form, but the water and soap mixture will clump some of them together.

I want to be clear that I don’t object to a different brush feel. As long as it does the job of lathering up and isn’t so coarse to feel like sandpaper, I’m fine. This synthetic fiber, on the other hand, are best compared to very playable, soft steel springs. Even when I tried to lather up very slowly and gingerly, each fiber literally snapped back to its original position. When you lift the brush off your face, all the bristles are back in place as if you just upacked the brush.

In summary, this brush is far from coming close to the feel of badger bristles. I cant use it without spraying soap all over and I wish I could return it, but it appears I’m stuck with this thing.

title: Norelco 1050CC pros and cons
text:
I bought the Norelco 1050CC (shaver and cleaning system). Here is what I like and don't like:

Pros:
-Shaved great for an electric
-Cleaned up well in the automatic cleaner
-I know others complained but I had less razor burn than other shavers

Cons:
-Beard/Sideburn trimmer is ineffective and located in a very poor place.
-The angle of the trimmer seems awkward to use.
-MOST OF ALL the recharging system is a complete disappointment. Basically you start the cleaning cycle and have to wait around to unplug the shaver so that the battery doesn't get ruined. It even tells you in the instructions not to leave it plugged in if your battery is charged--which is 90 percent of the time. VERY VERY stupid.

I would have kept this razor otherwise if it wasn't for the illogical charging/cleaning system. You pretty much have to choose between waiting 5 minutes watching your razor clean itself every morning or be okay with ruining your battery. It is enough of an inconvenience that I am returning it and going back to my Norelco quadra trac.

title: Recommended
text: I've been very happy with this brush.  My hair has always been thin, but since it has started getting more gray, it has become more dry & coarse. I've been using a flat iron to smooth it out and get rid of the kinky nature.  This has worked great for me instead.  I wash it, dry it, and then just brush.  One word of caution, the nubs are very hot, so you can put your hand over them, also, your hair will be warm for a few seconds after you brush thru it.  I discovered I could use a dry wash cloth or heat resistant glove to assist in keeping  my hair against the warming surface.  As I place the brush under my hair & brush downward, I place my other hand (protected by cloth or glove) over the nubs, thereby holding the hair tight against the surface.  The smoothing effect is great without any burning of the hair like with a straight iron.  We also used it on my mixed race granddaughter whose hair is much thicker and kinkier.  It took a little longer than it did on me, but it did smooth her hair faster than with a hot iron.

title: Fantastic oil but just not too crazy about that strong essential oil scent
text:
I am so torn about this oil. It comes in a glass dropper bottle like most oils come, mostly to protect the oil. Make sure you mix it well since the gold settles on the bottom of it, yes it has actual gold flecks in it. Besides the actual 24k gold it has all natural ingredients making this an actual edible oil. You can use this on its own or mix it with your moisturizer or foundation if you want.

So this is a high quality product and worth every penny in my eyes. When you use it you will notice the strong essential oil scent and this is why I am torn. It is just a bi too almost medicinal to me. It is a scent that in my eyes should be in a massage parlor in the essential oil diffuser healing you of something. So for me it was just rather strong but thankfully it does not longer on your face too long.

The oil is not too thick and absorbs into your skin pretty quickly. It leaves a slight oily residue on your face and I don't fault it for that since it is an oil. However, if you give it about 10 minutes or so, that oily residue disappears and you feel just soft and smooth skin. Absolutely amazing in my eyes. I love how my face felt when I used that to be honest and was a bit shocked.

So I love how it makes my face feel and look, I just need to get over the scent but since you really don't smell it on your face for long I think I can handle it.

title: Beautiful and flawed
text: The Norelco arcitec 1050 is beautiful and flawed. The beauty lays in the eye catching design and craftsmanship found in the shaver, the flaw--unfortunately--is in it's primary purpose, which is, as a shaver. As it turns out, I've owned two other Norelcos and a mid-range Braun which have proven to be dependable, well made and produce a good, clean shave. The Norelco arcitec 1050, while doing reasonably well at the job of cleaning the scruff off one's mug, seems to require more passes to do the same thing the older models managed with one. The trimmer is also different. The idea is that you must pop off the razor head to get use of it. A novel idea I suppose, but I cannot say that it is any better or worse than the trimmer on my old Norelcos, though it is narrower. Want to buy an Norelco arcitec? Then the 1050 is absolutely the model you should get as the much pricier 1090 is identical in every respect except that the LED array includes a battery charge countdown(which ironically draws power), providing you a ballpark idea of when you'll run out of juice. This shaver is still a little expensive (mine happened to be a gift), but it is well made and should provide years of service. I've had mine for over a year and the battery still holds a good charge lasting over a week of daily use. The included travel carrier is useful, though a little tricky to figure out how to use at first.

title: Too hard to use
text:
I am surprised this product worked. It does what it claims to do. It gave me a realistic-looking tan and that tan withstood multiple showers and cleaning wipes. The tan looks like I spent the day in the sun, rather than dark brown or orange.

The problem with a product like this is the color contrast with the places you do not apply this to, or if you miss a spot, or if you have thinning hair. It can go on blotchy if it is not applied evenly. Some parts of the body might become darker or not absorb this as well. Making it appear smooth is a challenge. Also, where do you stop applying this to your body? Wherever you stop there will be a contrast with the untanned skin. One particular problem is your hairline and scalp. I have thinning hair, so the contrast between a pale scalp and a tanned face looks odd. This is a challenging product to use and I wouldn't recommend it unless you are already used to using sunless tanners.

It is not greasy, it did not stain, and it dried quickly. The ingredients seem healthy for the skin. There is no smell to the cream.

title: Great Magnetic Eyelashes/ Dries Too Quickly
text:
In the words of my Sister.
The UJM Magnetic Eyelashes comes with a nice compact case which is great to throw in your bag.
The Eyelashes themselves are bold and have great length.
The Applicator was a decent size and easy to use.
The Case fits 2 sets of Eyelashes and the kit comes with 3 sets of Eyelashes.
The Eyeliner did have a particular smell, which you do not notice after application.
The Eyeliner Brush was thicker than I am used to, which at first bothered me, but after using a couple of times. It makes sense to have a thick line for the Eyelashes to adhere to.

The only issue I had with this Eyelash kit, was the Eyeliner. It dries too quickly and the instructions say to apply the Eyelashes while it is still wet. This makes it difficult to get a good smooth line and apply quickly. It takes some getting used too.
I ended up applying my normal liquid liner, then going over it with the Magnetic Liner to get a more even look.
I do suggest giving a good amount of application to the Eyeliner to reassure they are secure.

The Removing Process definitely takes some time. You really have to soak your Eyelashes with remover to get all of the sticky pieces of Magnetic Eyeliner off.

All in all, they are good Magnetic Eyelashes. I would definitely recommend them. However, they do not get a full 5 stars, because the Eyeliner dries pretty quickly and it does take quite some time to completely clean the Eyeliner off.

title: Shifts beard length setting without warning
text:
My T980 does almost everything perfectly: it holds a charge for weeks; its vacuum reduces the number of trimmed hairs around the sink by about 70%; it feels wonderful and it works quickly.

However, my T980 does NOT stay at the level I set it at. If I don't firmly grip the length setting wheel it will jump from, say, a 5 to a 3 -- as it did this morning -- embarrassing me either by giving me a patchy trim or by forcing me to shorten my beard length.

This problem doesn't seem to be a result of the way I'm, say, holding the trimmer -- I used the [[ASIN:B0001HYL0M T765]] for four years without having this problem -- but rather a flaw in the trimmer itself. From these reviews, it seems like only a few of the T980s have this problem; still, you might want to try the [[ASIN:B000FED5D0 T780]], which doesn't seem to have this problem -- I wish I had.

Update 3/12/08: Make me look like a fool once, shame on me; make me look like a fool twice, shame on you.

I've used this trimmer about 12 times since writing this review, and by a combination of duct tape, a pinch grip, and a good deal of vigilance I had been able to avoid too many embarrassing shifts in beard length.

...until this morning, when it shifted silently from a 5 (Late Winter Academic Beard) to 3 (Peach Fuzz) in mid-shave. Two options: shave my entire beard to a 3, which is inappropriate for my face type, or look deranged because half of my face is at 5 and half is at 3.

I threw my T980 in the garbage ten minutes ago.

title: Love this wand!
text: I'm not going to lie and say using this particular wand was not time consuming...it definitely was, but the results are worth it.  I have very long hair, so wrapping was a bit of a struggle because the wand is only so long.  I was able to wrap around both the balls and the indents, giving a unique curl effect.  Works best to physically unwrap the strand of hair you're curling rather than pulling downward as with a traditional clipless wand.  Any reviews stating this wand does not give curl either has too short of hair, isn't using a high enough heat setting, or is completely doing it wrong.  You really need to use your right hand over your head to curl the left and vice versa for the right.  The black cool tip should be pointing downward as you curl.  There are some informative videos on YouTube for how to curl with this wand.  Anyhow, I'm pleased with this wand and look forward to many great looks from it.

title: Hair cutting cape or barber cape
text:
This cape for hair cutting has a generous amount of material in the front but is lacking coverage on the back.
I used this while cutting my Husband's hair and noticed this only covered his shoulders about 6 or 7 inches down the back and left a gap in the middle.
There is not a snap to secure the cape. It is 2 metal hooks that can attach to each other at the end of the elastic gathering neckline. Normally you see this type of hook with sewn in loops or slots for the hook to latch to. The hooks can dig into the neck skin.
The neck area needs to be wider and adjustable more. My husband's neck was very tight in the cape, and it was uncomfortable for him.
The material is a soft nylon with Japanese style graphics and the hair just glides off the cape and onto the floor as expected.
The item needs an updated description as it currently states velcro neck enclosure and also a snap closure with elastic neck. I would also recommend less frontal material and bring some of the material to the back to provide more coverage on the shoulders and back in the design.
I bought this item at a discounted price. My opinions are my own and I was not compensated in any way for my thoughts.

But once in awhile, you just want to blend in with the crowd, and wear a wig that simply looks like you've got great hair.
Wigs like that generally cost a heck of a lot more than this one. Was really surprised to see how natural this one looks. In a lot of situations, and by that I mean if it isn't windy or super bright sunshine, no one would think this is a wig. That makes it perfect for shopping, work, and most situations.
I find this style to be nearly universally flattering on everyone. It doesn't matter if you have a chubby face or a thin face, this style is classic because most people can wear it.
Another thing to like is that this wig doesn't get tangled as long as you keep it on a wig stand.
Very good value for a very cute wig.

title: Very nice under eye cream
text:
Fountain of Truth has some interesting products, some I have liked and others that I was just not convinced of. I am happy to say that this one is definitely worth the money. It comes in a tall small applicator with little metal ball applicators. You have to push the top down to expel the product on the top, right by the little metal eye rollers. The under eye cream smells ok, somewhat medicinal, herbal, not bad but not the best either but I can handle it.

You use those eye rollers to massage it into the skin which is neat and I personally like it since it does help firming the skin. I prefer to put it into the fridge prior to using it since the cooling helps even more, at least I found it does in my case. This cream absorbs quickly, I do use my fingers in the end to make sure everything is fully absorbed, but it does leave a slight greasy residue on the skin. This stays for some time so I would recommend using this in the evening because of that.

All in all this is a very nice product. Yes it is not cheap but this should last you a very long time to be honest since you really don’t need much at all every time you use this.

title: Slower Shaving than my old Norelco!
text:
I have been a long time Norelco shaver user. When it was time to buy a new set of Series 7 Lift-and-Cut heads for my old Norelco 6885XL razor, I decided to get the new 9170XLCC razor. Big Mistake! The new 3-ring Smart Touch heads are not as good as the old reliable Lift-and-Cut heads.

Why you say? To make the head look like it has more surface area and thus should cut faster, the Norelo engineers reduced the cutting area of the fastest, outer, ring, to squeeze in the two inner, but slower surface speed, rings. In fact the outer ring cutting blades are only 1.00 mm wide as opposted the the 1.75 mm width cutter width in the series 7 Lift-and-Cut heads. The added inner rings actually cause pulling of the beard hairs if you try to shave at the same speed you did with the older models.

By the Way, the so-called cleaning system is a big bother and not worth the extra cost. You can rinse the 9170XL under the faucet just like the older XL models. In fact, you HAVE TO rinse it because of the sticky mess the cleaning system leaves in the razor after "cleaning."

The bottom line: In a failed attempt to make a quieter, faster, shaving system, Norelco actually made it WORSE than earlier lift-and-cut models. Then to top that off, changed the drive pin design so that one can NOT use the superior heads. Do not waste your hard-earned cash on this sub-par Norelco product.

title: Took awhile but now I love it! Looking forward to trying more from the brand.
text:
I had pretty high hopes when purchasing this shampoo, especially after reading all the glowing reviews. Over the past year, I've actively been reducing the number of chemicals in our household and have saved body care for last as I struggle to find things that work as well as mainstream ones. Pretty bummed to say this but I'm adding this to the list of products I've not been a fan of.

The good - it smells fantastic and there are far less questionable ingredients in it than most. It does seem to make my hair soft, too.
The bad - While soft, it almost gives my hair too much volume or something? (I have fine hair but a lot of it.) Anytime I use it, I end up with all sorts of cowlicks and hair sticking up in odd ways no matter if it's styled or air dried. Thought it was just my hair at first but this only happens when using this shampoo. Finally, the bottle that was sent ended up having some weird manufacturing defect where the top wont stay shut. It now has to sit upside down which is kind of a pain considering the design of the shampoo bottle doesn't easily allow for that. I'm constantly scared it will tip and spill, and this stuff is far too expensive to waste!

EDITED: Wanted to return to add that I've recently been using this product consistently and my hair has never felt healthier. Maybe it just took some time for my hair to get used to? Not sure if it's due to this shampoo, the supplements I recently added, or what in particular but I am starting to really love it. Only left one star off for the minor annoyance of product defect. Fingers crossed that won't happen next time.

title: It's good
text:
This Melao lavender exfoliant foot peel works very well. The box contains one set of booties for one time use. It’s real simple to use these. You have to start off by cleaning your feet well. It doesn’t hurt to give them a bit of a soak for a time as well beforehand. Just to get them good ready. Next, you place the booties on your feet. It’s recommended that you put socks over the booties to hold them firmly in place since you have to wear them for an hour. I did just that and think that’s a mighty fine recommendation to follow. When that hour is up, you take all that off your feet and give your feet a good washing with soap and water. Now comes the waiting game. At first, I thought they did absolutely nothing.For days, I thought they did nothing. Then, around the 4th/5th day my feet just started to peel. They were shedding skin. It was so weird! They continued to do that for a few days and when it was all over my feet did look and feel really nce for quite some time. Just remember to keep moisturizing to keep them looking and feeling nice for a long time after.

The thing about this product is that you can’t expect instant results. It takes a few days and you have to still use the same moisturizers and stuff you were using on your feet, or at least I did. I have really dry feet in spots and I despise it so to have something actually work for a little while was great. You would have to use these every so often though, I think, to keep them as nice.
At this time, when I type this, there isn’t a price listed for these so I can’t tell you if it’s worth it or not but they work well and could be.

title: Pleasant scent; very gentle; not all that effective for cleaning
text:
There are a number of positive features of this face wash. I love the scent -- it's a light, "fresh" scent that is sort of floral and sort of botanical. Normally I prefer unscented (or something that just smells soapy) but this light scent is quite enjoyable. It's a thick cream that resembles a moisturizer more so than a soap.

There's virtually no lather to it. It foams up a bit, but very lightly. It's a very gentle soap but, for me, it's a bit too gentle in that I don't have a clean feeling after using it. My face feels more like I've applied a moisturizer. That's not a bad thing, especially in the dry winter months, but I want to have a clean-feeling face after using a face soap, and I don't get it from this.

Balancing the positive and negative features puts my rating at three stars (average). It smell great and it is very gentle, but it's not a face soap I'd get again. There are other gentle soaps that also offer better cleaning and a better value on a cost per ounce basis.

title: So far so good
text:
Update 20/02/10

After a year and a half of good service my HQ7140 would not start even with the cord plugged in, unless I left it connected for a couple of hours...Obviously not an option when you're trying to get to work. I was about to order another one, already cursing for having to go back to blades even if only temporarily; but before that I took it to a specialized shop; they opened it and showed me it was wet on the inside and told me the "circuit" was fried. I explained that I had followed the manual to the letter, cleaning the shaving heads and the hair chamber with hot running water. They suggested taking the shaving unit off when I rinse it, use only warm (not hot) water, and *not* cleaning the hair chamber with water... They essentially sold me a brand new Philips HQ7120 as a replacement to use with my existing shaving unit for a reasonable price; it looks exactly the same except it has a "Low" red light.

The interesting bit is that I had gone to them about a month ago to buy a new shaving unit and they told me the HQ9 heads would work fine with these models, not just the HQ8; the HQ9 feel even better, so much so that I would definitely buy the 8xxx series which use the HQ9... It was only when the 7140 failed that I realized just how much I depend on it and how well it has worked out - my technique still needs to improve and shaving still seems to take too long but no going back to blades for me!

-----------------

As a wet shaving refugee I didn't know what to expect; I was just tired of getting cuts everyday, and paying an exhuberant tax to the wet shaver companies; I didn't want to buy a top of the line model in case things didn't work out.

This has been a very pleasant surprise, as I'm getting close shaves with less fuss and no irritation; I beginning to get the hang of this and even the neck area is doing well.

The battery's first run lasted for 4 days, but I may be taking a lot longer than normal while I learn. The battery light starts blinking when it's fuly charged, by the way.

I have the Philips branded verion of this and it still says Made in Holland...

title: Surprisingly comfortable for double-layer masks
text:
Now that masks are the new fashion accessory I've discovered that not all masks fit the same. There's definitely a difference in how they fit over your nose and mouth. My favorite mask, which is stretchy, isn't always practical. I'm not fond of cloth masks because of how they sit on my face, but these brackets actually make them comfortable.

Basically, I put the bracket inside a double-layer mask. This works great to keep the bracket from pinching your face while at the same time keeping the mask a little bit further away. The difference in comfort is significant, and it's very easy to forget you're wearing a mask with one of these on.

That said, you still need to wash it,and sliding these brackets in and out of a double-layer mask isn't easy. But if you're willing to put in the effort in a mask that you'll wear all day, it's definitely more comfortable.

title: Not totally easy clean brush & tines do not pull through all the way
text:
I used this on my three long-haired cats and it picked up some hair. Since the surface area of the brush is small, there is not much hair that is picked up compared to other brushes. Also, I tried several of these types of brushes and this one is not as easy to clean as the others. The way this is supposed to work is to retract the bristles with the button and the hair that remains on top can be slid off. Since the tines do not retract fully on the top part of the brush, the hair does not slide off easily. Instead, I have to pick it off.

Note that this is for long-haired pets only; I would not use this with a pet with short hair. I have three long-haired cats and even though this works some, I am not impressed for the two reasons I mentioned above. My favorite brush like this is [[ASIN:B09RH8FMMS this one]].

The current price of $20.99 is outrageous for this as it is about $10 to $12 more than others of better or similar quality.

I use Cetaphil facial cleanser and whatever moisturizing samples I have on hand from Glossy Box.  I don't work outside the home and don't spend a lot of money on my face. The eb5 Collagen Booster Serum claims to reduce the appearance of fine lines on the skin and to "plump" up the skin with collagen.  I really haven't noticed any difference using this or using any other moisturizer or serum.  What I would warn you about is that it contains both sesame oil and sweet almond oil, so if you have nut allergies, avoid this product.  Would I spend money on this product -- at over $15 for one ounce, probably not.

title: Definitely not real tepezcohuite
text:
I've used tepezcohuite for years and purchased creams and ointments in Mexico with truly amazing medicinal properties, but I was absolutely disappointed with this product. It is clearly a petroleum base that smells and has the texture of machinery grease. It doesn't have the color of the real bark, and since there are no ingredients listed, my guess is, it's petroleum jelly with some coloring. I'm surprised Amazon sells it without any information at all.

The positive reviews are either fake or people don't realize that if you put any type of oil or grease on your skin it will keep the moisture in. But this product will never do what real tepezcohuite can. I'd never put this grease on my skin, so it was a complete waste of money.

title: Disappointing Cleanser
text:
I was really excited to try the Nano Botanix | Detoxifying Cleanser Gel; I liked the idea it could reduce redness, among other things. With all of the things it is free of (Parabens, PEG, Petrols, Mineral Oil, EDTA, Phthalates, Sulfates, SLS, Gluten, Artificial Fragrances) I felt confident it would work for my sometimes-sensitive skin.

I was wrong. This cleanser caused me to have a mild itchy reaction. It's hard for me to believe that it doesn't have any artificial fragrances, as it has a heavy scent. The cleanser is thick and almost takes a moment to go on well; you've got to make sure your hands and face are wet enough or the gel is a little too thick to spread.

A small note regarding its packaging; I would prefer some kind of top that could be opened and closed with one hand. This one has a traditional screw on-screw off top that was a bit cumbersome once I squirted cleanser into my hand. I rate this cleanser at two stars.

title: Cordless or corded snipping
text:
I was looking at this as an extension to the [[ASIN:B000EG8HLE Philips Norelco BG2020 Bodygroom Shaver]]. Not really its intended purpose but it does work pretty well in that role as long as you are careful. Emphasis on the being careful; it can, and will, grab loose skin.

Overall I'm pleased with it. It cuts through hair quickly and easily making it easy for quick touch up trims. It's also fairly quiet, much quieter than my electric shaver so it doesn't affect my hearing when trimming sideburns and hair that's grown longer than my ears. It will also operate in either corded or cordless mode, handy when the battery dies.

Only a few negatives from my view:
-The charging LED in the handle does not shut off when the unit is charged. It is lit the entire time it's plugged in. Little annoying considering almost very rechargeable device will let you know when it has completed charging.
- It does not charge at the same time you are using it while plugged in. Not really a big deal, just something to be aware of.
- Only the head portion can be rinsed; the base / battery can not get wet. Again, not really a big deal.
- Hair trimmings get stuck in the lubricant grease inside the head. Not a lot, only a few very small pieces, but if you're a perfectionist it can be a little aggravating.

I'm expecting this will also work well to trim out the tufts of overgrown toe fur that my cat gets. I can, and do, trim with scissors periodically but it takes a bit of time due to being careful. The longer it takes the more annoyed he gets. Using this I should be able to trim the fur much quicker so he gets less annoyed. Less annoyed cat == less annoyed human. We both win!

Update: Dec 1, 2010
15 months later and I'm still using this. Does a fantastic job of keeping the hair around my ears trimmed just enough so that it isn't touching or rubbing. Very quick and quiet. It still irks me a little bit that it doesn't tell you when charging is complete. The other nitpicks I've gotten over.

I can't say how well it works on trimming toe fur on a long haired cat. The shaver is in one room and when I see that he needs a trim we're in a different one. I did use it once to snip out some matted up fur and it did a decent job.

title: Spill proof lid yeah not quite
text:
Cup seems very good quality. I bought this SPECIFICALLY for the spill proof lid. The slider part leaks like a sieve. I spilled hot coffee as soon as I started moving. NOT COOL. I'm really not happy but can't justify spending almost HALF of what I paid to send it back. MAJOR disappointment.

***update*** 3/29/17

So after my initial review on this cup expressing my extreme disappointment with the so-called spill proof lid, I was contacted buy a customer representative from Gus. He expressed his apologies and they ended up refunding my total purchase price even after I told them they didn't have to and sent me a replacement lid.

Unfortunately they did not understand my complaint was not about the rubber gasket around the lid itself but the slider that covers the drinking hole. It is the slider that leaks because it does not seal. I informed them of my opinion on the design, which is I believe is a poor design for what is supposed to be a spill free top.

Having said that, the Cup itself is absolutely fantastic. It's well-made and does indeed keep my coffee hot for quite a while. I have not tested it with cold yet. The way Gus stands behind their product definitely tells me that there concern is for customer satisfaction.

They were very prompt and courteous. I really can't ask any more of them. I have put the rating up to 4. If nothing else it's because of the simple fact they reached out to me to try and make it right. That to me speaks volumes of this company's commitment to ensuring their customers are happy. That's not something you see a whole lot of these days.

If they can come up with a design that makes the lid truly spill free I would definitely buy this again.

text:
Be sure to check the size of the product in the listing. These were smaller than I expected for the price!

It’s challenging to dispense the product, especially when wet. I have to really shake and SQUEEZE again and again.

That said, the shampoo is AMAZING. I have a ton of fine hair, which I wash 3 times a week. I feel it needs sulfates to feel clean and stay feeling clean, and this shampoo keeps it feeling fresh for days. It also lathers beautifully, unlike a lot of other “free-from” shampoos!

The scent is downright nonexistent. No “no scent” scent, like soy-based products often have (this is soy free).

The dry shampoo does not have a white cast, but I need a LOT of it to get any cleaning or degreasing effect. So meh.

Some people apparently find the shampoo fairly drying, but I’m a greasy scalped gal, so it works really nicely for me.

I used this product as a tester, and wound up purchasing a full size of the shampoo.

title: Love the colors in this sponge set; sponge texture is light; metal holder is great
text:
This is a lovely set of three sponges in nice colors of  pink, burgundy, and teal. It also comes with a great metal sponge holder, a silicone brush cleaner, and some cleaning solution. The sponges are light and airy like most sponges like this on the market. 

The burgundy sponge with the flat side is great for smooth applications. The typical egg-shaped (teal) and the hour-glass (pink) sponges are good for blending or any large make-up application. The hour-glass one is easy to hold in the center.

These feel good in the hands, blend reasonably well, and feel soft against my skin. These blenders make a great gift for the make-up obsessed. I love that the sponges do not smell. I tried other colored sponges and they smell like pencil shavings or other chemicals and these do not.

I personally do not use a silicone sponge cleaner. I prefer to use my hands and soap and water but having the silicone cleaner with cleaning solution provided is a nice touch.

The sponges themselves are similar in style to all of the others that I tried before this. To me what set of sponges to buy all comes down to the price and the angles one wants on the sponges as well as whether it is for gifting or not. The colors are important too--at least to me. 

The current price of $7.99 is a great deal for this.

text: I have been using this for about 3 years now. I have lighter blond hair when it comes to my eyebrows so it looks like I only have half an eyebrow. Let me tell you chicks don't like that. I tried this product and to me nothing beats it so far. You can go as dark as you would like because it depends on how long you leave it on. For me the best method is to cover the very light part of my eyebrows and Link that on for about 30 seconds then apply to the rest of the eyebrow and leave that on for about another 30 seconds. Mine come out perfect each time. Do not full bleed wash your face right afterwards and I would not take a shower for at least 2 or 3 hours afterwards to let the colorful fully set. If you do one minute intervals you will not die the skin and you will keep yourself from going to dark and working absolutely weird. I use the extra on my beard just to give it a little more Darkness around the mustache. To me it varies on how long it lasts. title: Beautiful rainbow set of glass nail files!
text:
I've been wanting to try the glass nail files now for several years. The cost of them was always a deterrent until I found this great 5 piece value set.

I was so excited to get them and try them out. I was so tired of buying nail files over and over again only to have them break or bend in my purse or just wear out after a month or two. I wanted to invest in something that would last a little bit longer even if it was more than the usual dollar store Emery boards I've become so frustrated with. It seems the cheap files I had been buying were constantly had to replace them.

The nail files were shipped to me promptly and they are not only extremely functional, but beautiful. I ordered the rainbow set of 5 and they're soooo pretty. My favorite is the emerald green one, which is so much more vibrant than it appears in the stock photo and In my crappy phone photo. I love them. The set comes with a hard case to store them in. And the 5 files in their cases come in a larger zipped pouch! they are the perfect size to throw in a purse, keep in my desk at work, stow in the console of my car, and store in my makeup bag while still having one extra in my medicine cabinet at home. When you consider how much I spend on files for my nails and feet on a monthly basis, and I should never have to replace these --- they come with a lifetime guarantee. That is just crazy to me. I will be buying these for gifts for sure. I can’t wait to tell everyone about them.

Disclaimer: I received this product at a reduced rate in exchange for my honest opinion/review. If I had paid full price for it, I would still say the same thing. I rely heavily on reviews before I make a purchase so I realize how important they are. Hopefully, you have found this review helpful. Thanks and happy shopping!

title: Decent Straightener/No So Good Curler/Great Lock-In Temperature function

Con: Straightens fine but doesn't curl that much. Feels a little rough on my hair while using the curling feature, and I don't feel like it leaves any shine. Product it self feels cheap; there's a rattling inside the unit, and it sounds like a loose piece of plastic.

Pro: affordability & concept. Also, the feauture to lock-in the temperature is genius. Once it's turned on and on the heat setting you want, double click on the on-button and it will lock. It's really nice when you're using this tool and accidentally click on the temperature or on buttons, which will happen quite often; the buttons are on the handle, so that's understandable. Even more expensive units don't usually have the temp-lock-in feature, so I was very impressed with that.

Overall, great concept but I will be returning it.

title: Does not work for course body hair
text: Trying to save you some time reading through all the reviews.  From my own personal experience, and that of many others I have seen on this and various other sites for reviews on this product, it just does not work well at all for course body hair, so do NOT purchase it for that.  To be fair, it may work better for it's title area, but I still have to give it one star, because it makes bold claims to remove body hair for extended periods of time over your entire body (which it failed miserably on for me and many others).  In fact, even on some of the positive reviews, people indicated it was like "a close shave" and that they have to use it very frequently, which goes against the company's claims.  A lot of hair removal gels and creams remove hair to skin level, so that is not really effective (or pleasant, as it leaves you with almost immediate stubble).  It also seems to be a cheesy company run out of somebody's basement, based on the Ziploc bag packaging, photocopied instructions, and weird 1960s children's glove.  If you have course body hair, this stuff is not going to help you, unfortunately.  So, buy it for your balls, but not for your body if you have course hair.  Major failure in that respect.

title: Two strikes is enough
text:
This e-file works really well, except mine only rotates in one direction. It has a switch for changing directions but mine only spins clockwise. You might not think it's a big deal but it is actually helpful to have the option to switch back and forth. I'm exchanging it and will update this review once I get the new one, which hopefully will work as advertised.

The included bits are decent, although only the sanding bands work efficiently on UV gel overlays. I bought a separate ceramic carbide bit to use on my UV gels (2/32 is the correct bit size). The included metal bits work fine on natural nails.

EDIT: I received my replacement file a few days ago and it does rotate in both directions as it should. It is a little balky when changing directions and requires trying a few combinations of flipping switches and turning knobs before it will start up again. Really serious nail enthusiasts or professionals should probably invest in a higher quality e-file, but for hobbiests and home users, this one is pretty good.

EDIT 2: Just a day after my last update, the replacement drill died. It's only been used 3 times, and I had it for less than a week. The power light comes on but that's it. So back it goes, and off I go to find a different drill, probably for more money but hopefully with more reliability.

text:
I have been using Philips/ Norelco shavers for the past 12 years; and for the past 5 years, I have been using the 8894 model. for no good reason, I wanted a change and assumed that the new Philips Norelco 1090 would be more improved than the 8894.

1. Louder.
2. less power; 65 minutes verses 100 minutes
3. the shave is not better; practically the 8894 shaves closer.
4. Plastic casing; 8894 had a leather travel case.
5. Slightly lighter than the 8894.
6. All the 10 series, rate the same
Bottom line if you have been using the 8894 and want a change; my advice is stick to your old shaver and save the money. If you are buying a new shaver, go for the 7810 instead, as the 8894 is no longer in stock.

title: NOT spirals in any way shape or form - but did a decent job making some body in my hair
text:
First off - how these arrive in the bag - like a little roll - is the way they will end up in your hair. There is no way to make them spiral at all. More like standard old school curls.

I found them a bit hard to use as well - as I found it a big pain to get the stick through the curler. I ended up squashing like four of five on the stick at a time (since that was the truly painful part) and then using it on my hair one after the other. Plus even though I cut my hair to like shoulder length - these are actually pretty short - just for the ends of your hair really.

With that being said - I tried these one night after a shower - letting my hair dry by at least half. I put the curlers in while watching TV. Left them in for like an hour, ran my hairdryer over them until my hair felt dry and took them out. My hair definitely had some bounce and was sort of curly. So if you are looking for body - these might definitely work. If you are looking for tight curls (especially spirals) - probably look elsewhere. On the plus side - for work the next day - my hair still had some body and felt thicker when I put it up. So again - they did definitely add body to my hair.

title: Really seems to work for me!
text:
My eyelashes are thin, sparse, and short (like my hair, haha). I had a eyelash grower product that seemed to work for me before, so I thought I would give this one a try. My previous one stressed to only apply once per day, before bed; this one encourages you to apply twice per day. I started with once at bedtime but then began adding mornings too.

This definitely seems to work for me! Now, if you are expecting full, lush lashes, I think that's unlikely--at least that's not what happened for me. For me, this product added length but not really any fullness. And the length is mainly noticeable when I use mascara--my lashes actually hold the mascara and look significantly longer. Also, it only takes a week or two to see results! My only complaint is that this is a tiny tube, and after just a few weeks, there doesn't seem to be much product left. Still, overall I really like this product and would recommend it!

UPDATE 1/18/19:
I am still using this product, although I think I might be getting to the end. It is still giving me longer lashes. I attached a photo to provide an idea of how it works for me. I am wearing mascara for this photo, but even with mascara, my lashes would NOT usually come all the way close to my brows like they are in this photo! But you can also see that while my lashes are longer, they are still pretty thin/sparse. Given this, I think this product would work best for those who have thicker but short lashes.

title: One Of My Favorite Shave Soaps.
text:
Of the traditional great shaving soaps, MWF is the postshave king. Barrister & Mann, L&L, Wholly Kaw, A&E, Italian Extro, there are wonderful soaps out there. They all have great scents and most can match MWF in slickness, cushion and glide. And they’re really close on the post shave. But good old MWF still rules the post shave roost. I love Mitchell’s Wool Fat. I have a Simpson’s Emperor badger brush that was very expensive. Tried and tried to get it to work with MWF, couldn’t get a lather no matter what I tried. I liked the stuff anyway. Then I got a $20 synthetic Plisson knockoff brush. It is the missing link. Loads in 30 seconds, face lathers wonderfully.

If you are having trouble lathering MWF do what I did and get a fat synthetic brush. It transforms the Mitchell’s experience.

Combined with my favorite razor, the Rockwell 6s set to “3” with a Feather blade, a good aftershave lotion and cologne, I’ve got an awesome shave here.

Provides plenty of slickness and cushion like any traditional tallow soap. But the addition of unsaponified lanolin (which also makes it hard to lather) gives this stuff its unparalleled post-shave feel. You will love your soft face after shaving with Mitchell’s and so will your wife, girlfriend or both.

Clean off with a hot damp washcloth, then pat dry and hit with a generous amount of Speick aftershave splash. Your pores will immediately tighten up, whiskers will retract, and you will have a perfectly smooth face.

If you are going to use Feathers, the samurai sword of DE blades, you need a slick soap like Mitchell’s to keep from cutting yourself. Mitchell’s does its job well.

Get some. It might be your favorite too. I will always keep it in my rotation.

title: Eco friendly, healthier for baby, and fantastic?  Win, win, win!
text:
As the mother of two young children, I have become increasingly concern about environmental chemicals and their effects on children. I've spent hours reading about pesticides and commonly-used chemical components in cosmetics, and have ultimately decided to do whatever I can to eliminate chemicals from my home. After doing a lot of research on The Good Guide, I decided to try Method's product, as it received one of the best scores on the site.

First off, I want to say that I absolutely love the pump! I've had two babies, and wrestling with the tube of cream has always annoyed me. The pump is far neater and easier to handle. Now that I've tried it, I don't intend to ever go back to one of those nasty tubes.

The other thing I noticed is how this cream is the only one I've tried that actually stays where it is put. I've used Desitin and California Baby's cream, and this is the only one that sticks to the red areas on my son's bottom. The other two had a tendency to slide right off the really red parts and onto the skin surrounding them. Needless to say, that was very annoying, considering the point of using the cream was to try to eliminate the read sores. This cream has a nice, thick consistency and spreads far more easily than the other two brands I've mentioned.

The big advantage to buying this in bulk on Amazon is that it no costs me no more than the tubes of Desitin that I used to buy. I've already used many other Method products for the home (French lavender all-purpose cleanser, hand soap, etc.), and this product has only strengthened my love for the Method brand. I'd definitely recommend it to all parents.

title: Nice kit for beginners/parent child activity
text:
I purchased this for my 7 year olds birthday. We got around to doing it tonite, finally. Overall, we were very pleased with this kit. Make sure the water temp and oil temps are spot on, add them and mix. Let sit, mix, let sit, mix, let sit, mix, etc. I was surprised how simple it was. It's nice how they combine oils and make everything into convenient packets of mixtures. Not having to measure really helps you focus on making the actual product while still keeping my daughters attention. She enjoyed this very much and was so eager for us to be able to stop mixing it and bottling it up.
My only gripe is the amount of lotion. We wanted to play with scents, so we used flavor oils we found in our cupboards. But, because they are tiny 2 oz jars, it was difficult to experiment with different scents. We did end up just taking out 2 oz of lotion, scenting, bottling, repeat. But, it was kind of annoying. For double the price of this kit, I saw another kit that makes 4x this amount of lotion. But, I believe ingredient wise, this kit is better. I love that this company chooses a natural preservative and that they use essential oils for scent. (It only comes with 1 scent - lavender) To make this kit better, they should increase the amount of lotion this makes and maybe offer a variety of essential oils to make a few different scents. I also wasn't quite clear on if they used unrefined or refined mango butter, but considering the small amount, it's not a huge deal. For the first timer, this is a great intro to DIY AND THE BEST PART: the lotion is lovely!! Makes my hands so soft and isn't greasy. I'm going to try making more lotions on my own :) My daughter was so proud and just loved labeling her lotions and giving one to her brothers.

title: Good performance; no scent; slow to absorb
text:
This is a pretty good cream for dealing with ultra dry, cracked skin. I've used it with good results on my elbows -- it softens, soothes and helps with healing. There's only a small hint of a scent to it that is only noticeable if you smell the cream in the jar. Once it's applied there's no scent that I can detect, which is a major plus.

It's a soft cream that's easy to dispense and spread. That's also a plus since other intensive moisturizing creams I've tried tend to be more solid and harder to use. This has more of a whipped cream type of consistency that's easy to work with.

It does take time to soak in, and my skin remains greasy feeling for a while after using it. It's not a significant problem for elbows, knees, feet, etc., but is a issue when using it on my hands. The greasy feeling makes it not a great hand cream other than at night.

Not perfect, but a better than average intensive moisturizing cream. A solid 4 stars.

title: Powerful and light, but tough to reach the inside spots!

When I turned it on, I was surprised at how powerful the little tip was sonicating. I found it easy to use on the outside of my teeth, but it was awkward to get to the inside of my teeth. I think I will have to practice holding it differently, maybe. I bought this because I build up tartar on the inside of my bottom front teeth—directly where my tongue rests. I did mh best to clean there but saw only mild results after one use.

I will use it a couple more times and see if maybe I see better results and hopefully I will get used to how to hold it so I can access the inside of my teeth.

Now if someone did this for me, I think this little tool would work wonders!! It seems quite powerful. I will keep trying and update my return if I get better results.

title: A Winner!
text:
If you're looking for wooden paddle brush for long, fine hair, then this one may be just what you need.

This brush is well constructed. It's made entirely of bamboo (the handle, body & bristles). However, the bristles are smooth. This results in a very sturdy brush that can easily work through tough tangles, but without causing unnecessary breakage.

And the price is right (under $8.00 with Prime at the time of this review).

If there's any downside then it would probably not the best brush to use on wet hair with a blow dryer because it's not designed for air flow.

However, if you're looking for a good, sturdy paddle brush to use on dry hair, then this is the one for you.

title: Bummer.....
text:
Beautiful looking set and what you see is what you get.....for about two weeks and this is with very gentle use and no washing detergents or dishwasher machine clean.

I wanted this style angler for my long hair and saw it everywhere....decided to pay a bit extra and get the set. Arrived in a beautiful flawless condition and even my trendy daughter was impressed lol. She’s away at school and tends to borrow my makeup, hair products of all kinds, clothes, etc. Sigh! Lol

Normally, I would have attributed the damage to her as she is young and it’s easy to be roughshod on mom’s stuff when mom is pretty laid back minus a few clear things!

But, nope. Just me using it. Boyfriend skeptical but impressed by the detangler and decided the overall metallic “paint” rose gold was striking, yet pretty. He’s a die-hard boar bristle wooden brushes fan. Lovely but this was the detangler I needed (it works) and the case and other brush/comb were a splurge. A gift to myself. Nice!

Only I used it and never dropped it. Less than a month and the paint is flicking off and it’s night and day and looks....so cheap and damaged. I have supplies to patch up the chips and did fiddle with the chips but it was like an unraveling sweater.

Tired of picking the flecks off the bathroom floor and pitched it all in the garbage. It’s my fault for not seeking refund as the items were defective within the return window. Just darn irritating because none of the pieces were packed in a travel bag or a purse. Not once! I’d cleared an entire drawer for it.

I realized that I obviously had made a mistake and I do peruse reviews. I was too frustrated to do anything else other than leave this review.

It is a beautiful set. The paint shiny coating is glamorous and glossy and just too good to be true. I do not like chipped items, overall, so it all went in the bin.

Cannot recommend product

title: Be careful of the purple on your scalp
text:
The only thing I will say is that it immediately took out the brassy tone in my hair and has a nice smell.

Cons:
It left my scalp purple. I am not kidding when I say that I rinsed my hair 3 separate times and still found my hair/scalp purple. I don't have a mirror in my shower so I just kept rinsing out leaning over the tub. Finally after the third time, I said forget this and got back in the shower and washed my hair with my regular shampoo and conditioner. I still fee like there is a tiny bit in areas and my whiter blonde has a little purple tint. It was also very dry feeling after the three rinses. My hair felt like straw.
I am not sure if the scalp dying was because I used a shampoo brush and didn't have it immediately rinsed out as I was putting on a face mask. I had accidentally went to put in the conditioner and realized after I put it on the top of my scalp that it was the shampoo and waited till my face mask was done drying a few minutes later to rinse out.
It really was drying even after I used my regular sulfate-free shampoo and conditioner and put in my super moisturizing leave-in conditioner. I might try it again if I have a color that turns out horribly and I need to tone it down. I was just surprised it how much it toned it down and my darker blonde now looks too dark/dull, unless it is still got some purple in it.
So if you use it, I probably would not use a shampoo brush and I would not leave it in at all. Not even the conditioner which says to leave in a few minutes.

The padding is not excessive but really helps with snarled hair. I think this works BETTER than some of the detangle wet brushes you see in stores.

The handle is a nice silicone grip, the bristles feel light weight but solid - not breakable. Another plus - when brushing my daughters hair (she's 5) if I accidently snag her ear, she said it doesn't hurt as bad as the other brushes we've used before! I don't brush hard but some of the other brushes I've used before have been so rough on her ear that she has cried. :( This one does not! No more crying!!! It comes in a really nice clear box with a little thank you note from the seller - very nicely packaged. I would definitely purchase again!

title: It could be built better......... but it's still a good/great product
text:
This is not built very sturdy. T?he base of it, if only it had a metal piece to hold the bottom in place, it would be perfect...... but it has a plastic piece.......... and for this not to be sturdy, is pretty dangerous..

I bought it because I wanted to lay my mom under it as often as possible......... and it almost fell on her.............. and almost gave me a heart attack... she didn't even notice, but omg if it had fallen on her...........

Yes, that's a really big deal....... but...... I'm not properly set up over here either...... I just reallllllllyyyy think they need to do something about the bottom attachment piece to make this thing completely sturdy, because those lights get HOT!!!..........

Also when it showed up one of the lights was broken..... I never said anything to anyone about it though because it was for the night in the middle, and I don't really need that one........ But I probably should have just to get it replaced.

The last negative thing is that it makes a pretty loud humming noise while it's on. And depending on the brightness, it gets louder. (oddly it gets louder as the lights go dimmer....)

But on a bright note........ I can barely ever actually get my mom to get undressed to actually let the light shine on her skin....... (She doesn't know who I am most of the time, so I can't blame her....... ) but one time I was able to get her to....... we laid under it for probably 45 minutes........ and she was in such a bright and cheery mood after we got up.......... it was awesome.

So. Red light therapy really works.......... as far as this product goes.......... the fact that it's not totally sturdy, I think is dangerous, especially if you're in my situation with an older parent......... but it was the best one I could find. I don't regret buying it, but I hope that they replace the plastic piece at the bottom with metal.

title: Offers miniscule support
text:
I look at the other reviews here and I wonder if this is the same product I bought.

I have metatarsalgia from Morton's toe, so I need arch support to keep my feet from rolling inward and putting pressure on that second metatarsal bone. Additionally, my toes are very long, so I have to wear shoes 1/2-to-1 size bigger than I'm measured to, which means any built-in arch support is too far forward for my foot. As such, I have to buy inserts smaller than the shoes I wear, which means they tend to slide around.

I have had good luck with [[ASIN:B0033PSSJO Dr. Scholl's FOR HER Hidden Arch Supports, 1-pair Packages (Pack of 3)]], but wanted something that I could quickly wear with any shoe (as setting those sticky, in-shoe inserts takes a bit of time to get it positioned just right), as well as wear barefoot or with my slippers around the house.

Based on the rave reviews here, and that the image appeared to be of a product that has a wedge-shape and would push my insoles up and keep my feet from rotating inward, I ordered a pair of these. Unfortunately, when they arrived, I was sorely disappointed. Unlike the other inserts I have had luck with, these are a flat piece of gell-plastic. Yes, they have good adhesive and generally stay in place on my foot (after a few tries to get them in just the right place, which takes off a lot of dead skin each time I have to peel it off to try again, which makes them less sticky until I wash and let them dry), but they don't _support_. The fact that they are something extra on my arch offers the tiniest bit of support, but it is not nearly enough to keep my feet from rolling, and also wouldn't be enough for someone with fallen arches. I also found them to be uncomfortable to walk around in for more than 10 minutes, because they provide this lump in my shoes, as my feet start to roll over onto them.

I would try the extra thick version of this product, but since I know that they are just a flat piece of plastic, I know they still would not offer proper support and would probably provide even bigger lumps in my shoes. These should be a wedge shape, not a flat shape.

So, now that I've wasted $16, I'm going to go spend just as much to buy three pairs of the other inserts and just load up all of my shoes so it won't be a problem when I need to quickly slip on some shoes and go. And, so much for going barefoot or having support in my slippers.

Pros( I guess)-
It was delived with such speed so that was really nice, package and all was great. Product application was exactly how they stated, directions were actually really helpful as they prepared you so you know what to expect(and with the extreme drying of the mask I guess it's nice for them to prepare you in case you didn't know) and easy to follow instructions. Oh, I have had the steamer on and gone through the entire H (heating); S (steam) and W (warm) before I turn the machine off and then back on to redo the cycle.  We find this breaks the polish down quicker than if you put your nails in during the steam and warm only. title: Nice strong scent at first, but it disappears very quickly.
text:
I really loved the idea of this Boiess Baby Cologne "Les Enfants" in White Blossom, and thought it would be perfect for myself since I don't like loud fragrances. The description of the scent profile really enticed me, as I love all of the notes. I was able to try both the White Blossom and the Lavanda scents.
Both of the "Cologne" sprays smell identical to me. I can't say that I can tell them apart at all. They both have a very strong earthy, herbal, slightly floral scent that is heavily ladened with alcohol upon spraying. It stays very strong for several minutes, but then starts to dry down.
Sadly, once it dries down, the scent pretty much dissipates. If I don't spray it heavily at first, which is too much for my asthma to handle, the scent just goes away completely. I must spray it on me again. Once I spray it on a few times over an hour or so, I can smell the ever so slightest hint of it on my clothing later, if I put my nose right on it. That is a lot of spraying for very little payoff.
I know this is meant for kids mostly, but I would think the scent would and should last longer. Sure, my grandsons will like using it, maybe, as it is quite strong at first. But, I think it would just be more for the fun of it and very short lived. This is also very expensive "Cologne" to not be able to smell it after 30 minutes, and right at $28 is too expensive for me to buy just for the fun of it.  
For others this "Baby Cologne" may be something wonderful or maybe they can smell it more than I can. As I said, I really love the idea of a light fragrance, but not for babies. I do wish the scent stuck around more for me.

title: Semi-decent product, really crappy price
text:
I've used this shampoo about three months now and I have mixed feelings on the product.

I have very long, very thick hair that I get colored on a semi-regular basis (every four to six months or so). Coloring tends to dry and damage it, and it felt like I was pulling out a lot of hair every time I washed and brushed it. It could just be because it's so long it looks like a lot of hair, but I decided to take preventative measures, just in case.

I tried some other products before this one, but for the price they cost, I didn't think they worked well enough or did what they claimed to do. So I thought I'd try this product because it was cheaper than the others. It lasts surprisingly long time. I use about six or seven pumps per wash and it lathers well enough to get all of my hair. One bottle has lasted me about three months.

I have noticed that I seem to be pulling out less hair per wash, not the big clumps I used to, anyway. I can't tell whether there's any new growth or anything (honestly, I do NOT need it), but for the hair loss, it seems to work pretty well.

I have, however, noticed an increase in dandruff since using this product. I never suffered from dandruff before, so not so sure I like that. It cleans well but I don't like that it dries out my scalp badly enough to cause flakes. I've been searching for a good conditioner to counteract that problem.

Also, when I purchased this item, it was only around $18. Sometime in the last three months the price got jacked up to $35. I don't know why; I don't believe it's good enough to justify charging that amount of money. It lost a star for that and I think I'll look around a little more and try different products before committing to buy another bottle of this. Not unless they drop the price back to something way more reasonable.

title: Not as Strong As I Hoped
text:
I am relatively new to solid colognes. I own this sampler set, Oak City Beard's Sandalwood Bourbon, and a sample set from another company. The other company's set was my first venture into solid colognes. I liked the variety it offered, and their colognes usually lasted most of the day.

I expected the same from this set.

I will admit, I liked variety that this offered, which is why I ordered it. Now that I've had time to try out each one, here are my thoughts. (Please note, cologne can smell different on each person, so what didn't work for me, may work for you.)

Barista - I don't drink coffee, so the thought of smelling like coffee all day was not a selling point for me. I figured this would be my least favorite of the four. When I opened the tin, it smelled like a 30-year-old motel lobby. A powerful scent of cheap black coffee, with a hint of musty cigarettes and pleather couches. I was not impressed. Still, I put it on and the smell changed to more of a 1990s coffee shop. Fortunately, the cocoa smell came forward more once it was on me, and the coffee was not as strong. I don't hate it as much as I thought I would. In fact, I kind of like how it smells on me.

Woodland Ranger - My favorite out of the bunch. While you may think it would make you smell like a Christmas tree, it's more of a clean outdoors scent.

Snow Leopard - I love me some sandalwood, so this was the one I really bought the set for. It says there is peppermint in it, but I can't smell it. Also, I feel like the vanilla overpowers the sandalwood. Not as good as I had hoped. Not bad at all, just not what I expected. (This one also seems to dissipate quicker than the others.)

Uncle Jack - I smell the bourbon and a trace of tobacco, but once again, the vanilla is the stronger scent here. It's definitely not a bad smell, probably my second favorite of the pack.

As I mentioned in the headline, the colognes are just not as strong as I hoped for. I mean, I don't want to overpower everyone in my general vicinity, but I do like to smell the cologne throughout the day and none of these do that. Perhaps I'm not putting enough on. Like I said, I'm new to this whole solid cologne thing.

title: Took Care of My Brassy Hair the First Time I Used It!
text: A few weeks ago, I tried a different brand of purple conditioner. This was the first time I'd ever used any purple conditioner on my blond hair. To say that I"m pleased with this mask is an understatement. Its wonderful.  And I WILL continue to use it as needed.  Blonds, if you're dealing with brassy hair, give this mask a try. title: The All Natural way to remove nail polish!
text:
I'm puzzled by this product. I loved the idea of having a natural, non-toxic nail polish remover. I paint my own nails quite often, skipping the nail salon to save money and time. I've been giving myself manicures and pedicures since 6th grade, so I'm pretty good at it (if I do say so myself) and am well-versed in many of the products out there. I typically use a 100% acetone remover, which is AWESOME, but I hate that there are so many harmful chemicals, not only on my nails, but also in the fumes I'm breathing in every time I use it. So, when I saw this product, I was excited and motivated to try it and like it.

When it arrived, I was also pleased with the size. I had assumed it would be pretty small because of the way the dropper looks next to it in the picture, but it's actually a good sized bottle. Before using any product, I read the directions and particularly with a new type of product like this non-toxic, all-natural nail polish remover. That's when I saw that you have to leave the product on the nail for 2-5 minutes. I don't understand this because once you use the dropper to apply the product to the nail polish that's on the nail, it immediately starts dripping down the sides of the nails onto your hands and makes a bit of a mess. It's also pretty inconvenient to sit there for 5 minutes when I could use my regular nail polish remover and would have clean nails in 30 seconds to a minute. I decided instead to try pouring the product into a shallow bowl and soaking my nails in it instead. This did make it much easier and created less of a mess, but it also requires you to use a lot more of the product than you would just using the dropper.

I waited 2 minutes and took a cotton ball to swipe the nail to see if the polish would come off. It started to, but just the top layer. I re-soaked them in the product for 3 more minutes, and I was able to remove the polish from my nails. I should also mention that I use Orly bonding base coat, which helps the polish adhere to the nail. I also had 3 coats of polish, and a top coat, so that might be why the polish was so stubborn to come off. Plus, it was a deep red, which is difficult to remove no matter what you are using, and it usually dyes my nail beds a bit when I'm removing the polish anyway. As a positive, I did notice that this product was MUCH less harmful on my nails. My acetone remover immediately dries out my nails and strips all the healthy oils from the nails and nail beds. This did not do that. My nails had a nice, healthy shine to them and the nail beds retained their moisture, which is nice.

So, in summary, I love that this product is natural and non-toxic, but it's just not practical for me to spend 5 minutes soaking my nails to wait for the polish to come off. However, if you are super green and more willing to commit to being patient in order to be able to use something that has no chemicals and is good for your body and those around you (which I commend you for!), then this is a great substitute for chemical nail polish removers.

title: Does the job for me
text:
I use this clipper with no combs i.e. 'bald' settings.
I've been using hair clippers for a few years now on a weekly basis. I've come to the U.S. recently and I must say that this is the best one i've seen so far in the U.S. that is cordless. I used to have a Panasonic cordless clipper on European voltage that was (much) better but here this is the best one i've tried (two others have been returned).

A few points:
* charging time is long and there is no indication when the clipper is fully charged.
* power level is good although it tends to decrease already on the 2nd or 3rd use if not charged. This is not so great comparing to my previous one which lasted at least 4-5 uses before charged. This is a minor issue though because when it's to 'weak' it can be used as a corded device.
* cleaning is simple and the detachable knife is a nice feature
* if you don't use the combs, the '0' knife is not as close as I would want. However this is again a minor issue.

If you are like me, looking for a cordless clipper so you can easily and safely cut your hair in the shower, this is a very good option at a reasonable price. After some bad experience with a leading American brand I find this a very good clipper.

title: Quite happy with this! A great find.
text:
I had some reservations... I’ve seen the round wood ones around, but never made the leap. I was afraid the ceramic would make this too heavy and bulky, but it does not. It’s quite lightweight and because it’s vertical, saves some space. It comes with extensive directions - a nice change - but is really very easy to use and set up. It’s very hot and humid where I live, so I was also worried that adding more humidity to the air would be a bad thing, however, the air that comes out is quite cool, which seems to cool down the area around it (and by “it”, I mean me). I found it very comfortable.

I wasn’t sure how I felt about the colored lights option, but I love it! You can choose red, or a brighter red, and also green and a soft lavender blue with their corresponding brighter shades. You can choose to have your color, or opt to have the unit cycle through them all. It’s quite restful. You can, of course, just use the white light. You can set the steam for a continuous output or intermittent.

The until must be cleaned after 10 hours of use. It doesn’t hold a great deal of water, so I was wondering if that was going to be inconvenient. I ran it for two continuous hours and I could tell that filling the tank twice would be about 10 hours. So THAT’S easy to keep track of!

All in all, I couldn’t be happier with this unit! It checks all the boxes and I can enjoy my essential oils in an peaceful, comforting environment. Highly recommended!!

title: Affordable & Effective, But Has Pooped Out
text:
I had major dental work (extractions, jawbone surgery, grafting, dry socket, infection, implants) and needed something to help keep the area clean and emptied-out, given that my tissue didn't bond properly to the implants, thus allowing food in.

The unit has generally worked well for me and I like a lot about it, including how long it would go between charges.

Things I don't like:

1. It seems impossible not to taint the cleanliness of the water reservoir when opening its little door. I suggest filling the reservoir with hypochlorous acid (nature's germ killer) and letting the hypochlorous disinfect the door.
2. It is too easy to accidentally turn the unit off when using it, based on the location of the on/off button.
3. I wish the unit would default to the last-used power setting, but I have had to reset it each time.
4. My unit's battery appears to be failing. The unit will charge appropriately, but then only run for seconds. If I turn it back on, it will run another few seconds, then the process repeats. As far as I know, the unit can't be opened to replace the batteries, but correct me if I'm wrong.

title: Works and makes buying jewelry less of a guessing game
text: I just recently found out I have a Nickel allergy.  According to my dermatologist, both "real" and costume jewelry can have Nickel mixed into the metal (along with belt buckles and snaps on pants, etc), so he suggested I buy this to carry with me to test jewelry before I buy it.  I just whip this little test kit out of my purse and swab the jewelry before I commit to buying it.  The solutions fit into the provided prescription style bottle, along with a few Q-Tip cotton swabs (which you have to provide).  All you do is put 2 drops of Solution A and 2 drops of Solution B on the tip of a swab and wipe it across the metal for several seconds.  If the swab turns pink (it's not a bright pink, so be sure to look closely), it contains Nickel.  This sure beats breaking out into itchy blisters!

This is a kit that includes almost everything you need to remove gel nail polish. The springs on the nail clips were a little weak in my personal opinion, I prefer them to be a bit tighter so it doesn’t fall off easily.
