title: ADVANCED Moisturizer
text:
A few years ago, I was trying to decide if I could wear contacts after 30 years of just wearing glasses. I struggled through many different pairs and brands of contacts and they all just never felt right. My eyes just felt gritty and dry. My doctor finally just made this comment, and it is very true: At a certain age women just have less moisture in their bodies (in this case it was my eyes).

That phrase also applies to our skin, and of course the most visible is our face. This moisturizer is for those of us that need that extra little boost, as we might have "advanced" skin. Now in my late 40's I am noticing those fine lines, especially on my forehead, what I would call my furrowed brow lines. Will this moisturizer erase these lines? No. But it can help diminish appearance.

An added benefit of this moisturizer is it also provides a moisture barrier to protect your skin from the elements. As a child of the 80's, we all grew up loving the sun and getting tan. Now we know better and with better products are able to protect our skin from the elements.

title: These are not USDA certified oils. 2 stars ✨
text:
First, I will say these oils seem fine. They work well together or apart, mixed into other skincare products or alone. I use these types of oils to make my own facial oil mix or to add to my moisturizer.
The thing I absolutely hate that companies do to try to sell their products is to say things that aren't true. The USDA does not certify oils - food, cosmetic, or otherwise. The fact that the bottle says this product is USDA certified on one side, and the other side says not intended for ingestion should speak volumes. The USDA certifies and regulates the welfare and production of food products; meaning products that you ingest. So, why on earth would they certify a product you cannot ingest? The bottle also makes outright claims of known cures from using these oils. There is no disclaimer on either bottle that states that these claims have not been approved or proven by the FDA, or whatever the disclaimer is that is mandatory. There are ingredients listed, one ingredient for each product, the oil, and that's it. Nothing tells how these oils were extracted. Therefore, we do not know if they are refined or unrefined. They probably don't know either. So you see, therein lies the lies and deception.
These oils would be much better if they weren't tied to lies. Because you know what they say about lies... if you tell one you have to tell more to keep up with the first one. Is what they say in the bottle really what's in the bottle? Are they pure oils or mixed with a lesser oil? Oils are greasy. If they are unrefined, why aren't they greasy? When you refine oils, you take away a lot of their natural properties and their nutritive value, is that why they aren't greasy? Because of the lies and lack of important information, I really don't know for sure what these oils are.
Because of the deceptive practices and claims made, I would not recommend these or any of their other oils.

title: Banana Cream Pie Scent
text:
When I first tried this Marshmallow Vanishing Crème in a sampler kit, I purchased five more kits and then a 1.5 ounce glass container of this product. Can I say it is addictive? Yes, I guess it does have a banana scent and the texture is similar to a banana cream pie topped with whipped cream.

To say this is decadent is an understatement. You will be very tempted to slather your entire body in a good helping of this cream. Fortunately, it goes a long way and absorbs extremely well. In fact, that is why they call it "vanishing" crème. The ingredient list is impressive and contains rose water, mango butter, beeswax, grapeseed oil, rosehip seed oil, Vitamin E, marshmallow extract, willowbark extract, calendula flower extract, and a heady fragrance.

Grapeseed oil is one of the most powerful antioxidants and is high in proanthocyanidins, a group of bioflavonoids that are superior because they are water soluble. This ingredient also prevents skin cell damage caused by pollution and sun exposure.

"Marsh Mallow" is actually a pink flowering herb found in marshes and damp meadows. It has been used for centuries as a food and a medicine. The leaves and roots secrete an emollient fluid with healing properties for inflamed skin. In the past, people boiled the roots in wine to make a cough remedy.

I found this luscious creamy dreamy product to be healing for the body and mind. Not only will you feel comforted by nature, your skin will be baby soft and this product can be used for all-over body healing. The silver lid and glass jar have an unusually cute appeal. If you love this product, you might want to try the Pore-refining mask, Evening Primrose Overnight Crème and the very unique parsley blemish stick. To take luxury to the next level, try the Shea Butter Decollete Crème on your feet, hands or all over your entire body. What an amazing line of products. They heal, protect and soothe your mind.

I'm still trying all the Burt's Bees products, and love how these products make me feel. They add a level of protection to your skin care routine and the clay mask I recently tried cleaned my pores like a dream.

~The Rebecca Review

title: We'll see how long this lasts...
text:
Provides a decent shave, particularly after the beard has been moistened as it is immediately after a shower. The question is, for how long, considering the flimsy construction of some components and the already below-specified battery life.

Things they don't describe in the mostly worthless manual:

The charging indicator is a steady red AC plug symbol.

The LCD indication at full charge is 99. A RED (not a far more intuitive GREEN) battery full symbol is shown at when the charge reaches 99.

A low battery is indicated by a flashing red AC plug symbol when the charge number on the LCD reaches 10.

Charge time was tested and found to be 82 minutes. The manual claims 60 to 90 minutes, so they got that right.

Use time is specified in the manual as 50 to 60 minutes. The run time was tested and found to be only 30 minutes in 5 minute on, five minute off intervals, just free running and not being used to shave which should further reduce the run time slightly.

The charge indicator was at 52 after 25 minutes and then rapidly dropped from that to 10 only five minutes later causing the low battery indicator to flash, so I would definitely NOT trust the charge indicator to be an accurate indication of how much shaving time you have left. They are apparently not calculating percent charge remaining and displaying it on the LCD, they are simply and far less usefully displaying percent battery VOLTAGE which drops off rapidly at what is called the battery's discharge "knee." A cheap route to take revealing that the LCD display is nothing more useful than a gimmick.

The manual states that the razor should be unplugged from the charger (this razor package does not come with an AC to USB charge adapter) when the charge number reaches 99, so I suspect this charger might not have an intelligent charger which stops the battery charge process at full charge to avoid battery damage over the long term. So, I will not put this razor on charge and just forget about it until my next shave like I can with my Norelco with its intelligent charge system.

Other information:

The space under the heads which catches the beard shavings is very small. Cleaning often will be a must. We'll see how the hinge and head locking mechanism hold up.

When opening the shaving head to clean, put a finger on it to slow its opening, otherwise it will rapidly flip open and if a razor element isn't locked into its place by its flimsy and not very intuitive to correctly replace locking ring, as it wasn't in my case, the razor element and its parts will be vigorously projected into an alternate universe. Luckily, I found all of the parts. Had I been standing over a sink, some could easily have gone down the drain. We'll see how the razor element locking rings hold up.

title: Not worth the hassle
text:
At first I thought this was the greatest razor ever. It provides a smooth shave, probably the best shave I've ever encountered. I have very sensitive skin, so I have to be selective. First impressions: It is a very sleek and cool looking razor. It is so fancy, that I am afraid of breaking it every time I touch it. The problem with this razor is not its performance, rather it is the maintenance. The lotion is expensive, and to make things worse, it is nearly impossible to find, unless you are willing to spend lots of money and buy it online. But, the razor works, so I stuck it out.

Next problem: Norelco suggests that you replace the cartridge for sanitary reasons each time you refill the lotion. OK, but when I ordered the lotion (which is supposed to come with the cartridge), THERE WAS NO CARTRIDGE! So, I decided to stick it out anyway. Each time I replaced the lotion, I would just remove the cartridge and clean it myself. That seemed fine, until this morning when I accidentally broke a piece of this fragile cartridge. Now, I can't get the lotion to come out, so the razor is ineffective. I tried to buy a new lotion with cartridge at Target, and the lotion came without the cartridge, so I have to return it.

I know Phillips-Norelco has excellent customer service, so I called to see if they could help me. It turns out that the lotion does not always come with the cartridge (although it is advertised that way and I was told that it came with the cartridge by a customer service rep before I bought the razor). So, it's kind of like a little guessing game. Where can I find the lotion and cartridge together? Fun! I asked if they could just send me some cartridges, no lotion, just cartridges and I'd be happy. But they could not do that, so I am going to return this razor and get my money back.

I still have a previous Norelco shaver (dry) and I will try that again, although it is not as good. I think in the end I may have to resort back to the painful manual razor shave. I have been a Norelco customer for many years and up to this point I was always very pleased, this is disappointing.

To summarize: This is an excellent razor, but it is not worth the money or the hassle you have to go through to make it work effectively!

I welcome any shaving advice to help my sensitive skin!

title: Relatively strong water flosser but reservoir is attached which makes drying it nearly impossible
text:
I have used various countertop water flossers in the past such as the countertop WaterPik and the [[ASIN:B07HRNGS3Q Truwell Handheld Water Flosser]]. I love the idea of a hand held irrigator and this does work to remove most stuck debris from between the teeth. What is nice about this one over the other handheld I tried, is that there is very little splash back. However, I personally do not like that the reservoir is not removable for drying.

IN THE PACKAGE
- One reservoir attached to handheld flosser unit
- One USB cable (wall adapter NOT included)
- One instruction manual
- One standard jet nozzle
- One orthodontic nozzle (larger brush)
- One pocket nozzle (smaller brush)
- One tong scraping nozzle (what looks like a spoon)

I charged the unit fully before use. The white light on the side blinks when charging and remains steady when it is fully charged. Note the charging port is hidden behind a silicone nub below the grip dots on the top of the unit. Be careful to cover the charging port with this nub when the flosser is in use.

There is an on/off switch and a mode switch. The three water pressure modes are soft, standard, and massage can be cycled through using the mode switch prior to turning the unit on. The jet tip (or any of the other three tips) gets inserted into the top. Be careful to make sure it is seated with the notch in the groove as the first time I put it in the hole, I did not have it seated all the way. To eject, press the release button to the left side.

The reservoir IS NOT removable. Instead water enters through the small opening on bottom through which one has to fill the unit. I do not like that the reservoir is attached as I have to drain the remaining water out of that hole and leave the door open for drying. Also, the little button through which the water enters can easily break after lots of use. I personally would prefer not to have to use that hole.

I held my mouth almost totally closed during use and tried all three modes. I did not have splash back, which was very nice. Splash back is usually typical of almost any type of water flosser so to some extent I was surprised. This flosser does work to dislodge most debris between teeth but not everything because it is not super powerful but is powerful enough. I am also impressed that the manual is relatively well written; kudos to the manufacturer on this. Normally, I feel as if I am reading Pig Latin when I receive products from China or other countries.

In summary, my biggest disappointment with this unit is the attached reservoir that prevents me from drying this out easily.

title: Warped from Containing Polish Remover
text: After containing Mineral Fusion nail polish remover (one of the most popular, most effective removers on the market), this bottle stopped dispensing as well as it had. Upon inspection, we realized the acetone had started warping the all the parts so that the lid wouldn't totally close anymore, too much acetone started coming out per pump, and, most dangerously of all, the bottle itself had begun warping and starring. What's happening is it is liquifying the plastic and causing it to become molten, but on a very slow level, with the plastic molecules moving because of the organic chemistry of the acetone interacting with this particular type of plastic. It was only a matter of time before it bottomed out in my bathroom cabinet all over everything. Basically, this should be made of the same type of plastic as bottles that hold acetone and for long periods of time, at that. Furthermore, the straw should be of a sturdier material.

I gotta say I do love using sheet mask, they always provide my skin the extra glow and moisture it needs during the harsh winters. Each of the mask are individually wrapped so they're perfect to take on the go or in an overnight bag. All you need to do is open and unwrap the folded mask and align it with your face. Compared to many other sheet mask, these fit my face shape perfectly without having all these air bubbles. Leave it on your face for 15-20 minutes and then rub the additional juices and slap your face slightly so it absorbed completely. You don't need to wash your face again after using the mask.

title: Kiss has the best nails! Instructions on how to make them last 10-14 days!
text:
These nails are GORGEOUS!!

Do NOT use the sticky adhesive as they make the nails not last as long. Simply:
1. Push your cuticles back
2. File down your nails
3. Lightly file your nail bed so the glue has something a little rough to hang to, it’s always easier than putting glue and a nail on a smooth surface and makes them last much longer
4. Find the 10 nails that fit you and lay them down in the order of the fingers you will put them own (pink-ring-middle-index-thumb-thumb-index-middle-ring-pinky) - they have numbers on the underneath of the nail on the tip, remember those numbers or write them down because that’s likely your size in all Kiss nails (for example, I’m 12-10-7-8-3-3-8-7-10-12, the smaller the number the bigger the mail)
5. When you’re ready to apply, place glue on the bottom of the fake nail about 1/6 inch from the bottom to the middle of the nail and make sure it’s dispersed even - DO NOT put the glue directly on the nail bed, for longevity it works best to put it on the fake nail
6. Align with the appropriate finger and place down, holding for 5-10 seconds.
7. There may be a little glue that comes out on the sides. Be careful not to smudge that on the nail itself. Just take a paper towel and dab that little bit of glue up as you go
8. Once all nails are on, file how you need/want them and you are set for about 10 days.
9. I usually get a solid 2 weeks of wear out of mine! I use either these KGN10, the almond shaped wine, or I’ll do a French or natural French short length from Kiss.
10. Carry around an extra nail or two that may fit a couple different fingers for emergencies, the glue, and the nail file. If a nail pops off and it’s not a broken nail, simply file your nail bed again and apply glue to either a new nail that fits, or the one you popped off if it’s salvageable.

Enjoy!

I've purchased many sleeping masks which have a thin elastic band that is not adjustable at all. Those eventually get stretched out before the rest of the mask is worn out. This mask does a pretty good job of blocking the majority of the light. A little light can get through the area of the mask around the nose. title: Skeptical
text:
Ok sooo I don’t know about this one. Clear vitamin C means it is 100% potent, but having an ingredient list that potency is no longer 100%. So upon seeing clear thick serum I was skeptical. Soon as I opened the bottle I added several drops to a small old bottle I own and left it open exposing to air, lights and anything else that causes oxidizing to the vitamin c. It stayed clear. After one week straight no changes. I even popped into the microwave for 8 seconds still clear. Had it contained ferulic acid I would have been less skeptic because FA is a Vitamin C stabilizer. On its own Vitamin C (L-absorbic acid) is unstable and begins to oxidize once the seal is broken. Yes even pure vitamin C in water it will turn a slight yellow and begin to darken.

But my skin did not break out a good thing. Even if it doesn’t contain vitamin c the other ingredients are a plus especially glycerin as the second ingredient ... which is a natural humectant, anti microbial and antiviral all meaning moisturized skin that won’t get clogged and controls acne. I do get acne (thank the skin gurus) but I do chemical exfoliate with acids and use a retinol. Two things that cause dry skin. If I should break out from a product then it is pure trash and the PH is way off.

So it has it pluses and minuses.

text: I wanted to give this sunscreen a rating of 5 stars but I don't think that would be honest. The description sounds so appealing, gentle and pure, but there are several things that really bother me. First of all, this is definitely NOT a natural product. There are tons of ingredients in here that don't pass that test at all (read the label!).  Secondly, the two sunscreens that are listed as active ingredients don't protect against UVA rays, only UVB. Titanium dioxide which protects against UVA rays also is in here but not labeled as an active ingredient, and it doesn't give a percentage. Thirdly, if you research ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate you will see that it is not considered to be an entirely safe ingredient. With all that said, I do like the texture. It is light yet moisturizing, and it feels smooth and even a little silky because of the cyclopentasiloxane (synthetic silicone) in it. title: Like a Peach Bellini for your Face!
text:
Do you like champagne cocktails? This one smells like a combination of peach and champagne, and even looks like it!
It comes out like a gel. It's activated by water, so after washing your face, leave your face damp and put a thin layer of the gel quickly all over your face. Include your neck if you like.
Then with each passing moment, it's going to get foamier and foamier. That's why you have to have a very thin coat. You only need a small amount of product. If you use too much, your face is going to foam up like you have shaving cream all over!

After about 5 or 10 minutes, you massage a little bit with warm water and then rinse. After you dry your face it's going to feel squeaky clean. If you have dry skin, you're ready for a moisturizing serum and cream. If you have oily or acne prone skin, use the appropriate products for that skin type. I don't feel that this mask is drying, but it does leave you very clean.

So, in my opinion, this is good for all skin types, as long as you use it as a brightening mask as opposed to a hydrating mask.
This is just what your skin needs if you have overdosed on hot humid weather.please look at the ingredients to see if you have any sort of allergy or if any of them are a trigger for any skin issues. Because I have sensitive skin that can be triggered, but I only left it on for about 4 minutes. I had absolutely no irritation, but I think if I had left it on longer, I might have. That doesn't mean it's bad for you. If you leave a mild castile soap, which is so gentle, on your face for any length of time, skin will be irritated.
Made in the USA, from Tonica Skin in Marblehead Massachusetts.

I hope this review has helped you to make a decision about whether or not you'd like to try this fun mask. It really does leave your skin feeling and looking energized, but it's a bit of an investment. Nice splurge for a spa night, and because the product comes out via a pump, it's going to be sanitary for all the participants.
It's going to make for some really fun and Instagram worthy photos!

xxoo

PS, my 'spa night' pal doesn't look too impressed 😆

title: Best for Warm Toned Skin
text:
I am a makeup junkie, so I was really excited to try out a new contour pallette! I was slightly disappointed when it arrived though: the pictures on the box depict very cool toned contour and highlight shades, but the actual makeup is pretty warm toned. Unfortunately warm tones just don't work great for me. HOWEVER, if you are warm toned, then this would be a great introductory pallette. It's constructed well and pan size is generous (as pictured with a quarter for size reference). I applied using a synthetic contour brush and got decent color payoff and very little fallout from one swipe over my skin. It's a decently blendable powder formula; not the most bendable I've ever used, but it will blend out with a little patience. When I swatched the product I only did 2 passes to try to give an idea of what color payout will actually look like when used (as opposed to a thick swatch that looks like pan colors), but because I'm fairly pale, I had trouble capturing the 3 lightest shades on camera. The swatch picture shows the 3 darkest shades from the pallette. Overall I'd say that, for the price, this is a good starter contour pallette for warm toned people.

I received my contour pallette for free in order to review it here, but this is my unbiased opinion of the product.

text:
I love the look of this lamp. It almost looks like it came straight out of a salon from the 50s, but also manages to look very modern. It's relatively small and doesn't take up too much space among my other bathroom appliances beneath the sink. The plug isn't very long, maybe 4 feet, so wherever you do your nails you will need to be sitting near an outlet.

My daughter has sensitive skin, and when she stuck her hand under the lamp she said it bothered her hands a little because of the heat. I don't think the heat was too intense. I have a fresh burn on my finger that didn't feel bothered by the light so I'm attributing that to her being younger and more sensitive to heat, but I do think it's something to be aware of.

My fingernails weren't completely dry when I pulled them out, and I had to run them through twice as many cycles as the nail polish recommended, but honestly I think it was due more to the nail polish I used than it was a fault of the lamps (for reference, it was China Glaze brand Gelaze). The nail polish was really super runny and had a watery consistency with very thin coverage.

Two days later though (a record for two people who are hard on their nails) my daughter and I both have zero chips in our polish. I'm pretty happy to have received this and think it would make a great gift or be a good purchase for those who want to save a little money from getting a professional manicure.

Just one last note: I had to go to a beauty supply store to find a gel polish that needed a lamp. It seems like many gels these days advertise no lamp needed. Personally I feel like those aren't any better than regular polish, but it's something to consider.

title: Sketchy...  Ingredients?  Organic my eye!  For tea? - I don't think so
text:
First off for anything touting that they are Organic and then come in a non-descript bag - no ingredients, no country of origin or manufacture - no brand info, etc. that is SUPER sketchy. Seriously doubt these are Organic - no marking as such - but there is no info whatsoever anyway - so who knows what is truly in them.

I put a ball in my glass mug and poured boiling water anyway. There is no "flowering" like you may get from flowering tea balls. It just sort of filled the entire mug with flowers - petals and flowers. Like the entire mug. It was the consistency of a thick stew. You might get a few sips for the space that is left after the flowers expand. I was actually impressed with how much "flower" was there from that tiny and light ball.

I sipped it and was snot impressed with the flavor. Light at that and must have been chamomile as chamomile smells like chicken soup to me and I am not a fan of chamomile or this "tea". It was the consistency of soup, though... a hearty chowder. It was not fragrant in any way either so I think although you get plenty of flowers for a tub - you are defeating the purpose of adding fragrant flower petals to your bath. Plus no ingredients anyway. It seemed like all flowers - it really did - but I am not really sure what is in there. Plus some people are allergic to certain herbs and flowers anyway. This one is a bust...

I've had tape in hair extensions for quite some time now. This is by far the worst set I've ever purchased. The tape used on these is inferior and will begin separating within a week. I had these professionally placed, did not wash my hair for 5 days to allow the tape to really take hold and took excellent care of them, they still started to separate.
Now, two weeks after I've put them in, I'm going to have them removed and throw them away. I bought 4 bundles so this is a very expensive lesson - I'm writing this review in hopes of saving someone else the trouble - and the expense. I also noticed that when the hair arrived, there was quite a few "filler" hairs (synthetic) that are probably used for fullness but look extremely cheap.

title: Old adhesive
text:
The short version: the adhesive backing on these sucks and I think it's because they've been sitting a long time. I put them on and 20 minutes later they were falling off as I did simple things like put on clothes and pack a duffel bag for the weekend.

The long version: I have a feeling these are sold on Amazon because they are no longer sold in stores or on the website for the company- which means they're pretty old. Over time, press-on-nail-adhesive like this seems to get less effective. During isolation I stopped wearing Kiss Impress nails because I didn't need them, but my old stock is now broken out again and it seems like every pair I let sit for a year no longer sticks through a few days of use, let alone the two+ weeks I could get out of them before. New purchases have not let me down like this. I tried using Kiss liquid nail glue, but that didn't help at all, which is strange, since it's usually so effective for me.

title: Brilliant Idea, Great Clips, Needs More Colors
text: These are wonderful little containers for travel. They are very easy to fill and dispense from, when you are ready to use your lotion or shampoo or facial cleanser, but they are also the right size to give you enough for a trip. The bottles come in different colors, so you can sort of color-code your products, however, they don't include enough colors. As a result, there are really only four bottles that can be used for travel, without labeling. Given that three are the white color, all of those will be for hand lotion. They are really convenient for attaching to a hook on a bag, which is great for me because my hands dry out so easily. Since I know what color the original bottles are, for my products, I love that they are different colors, but, again, they need more colors. My shampoo is blue. My body wash is white. My facial cleanser is green. My lotion is orange. The list goes on. I am giving these five stars because they work very well, have a nice thick top portion to hold that clip, so that they don't break off, and the clips themselves are nice medium-duty clips that really hold the little bottles in place. These are high quality for a great price and made with food-grade silicone, so they are non-toxic and won't leach any chemicals into my products, which means I won't be putting anything bad on my skin. Even though you might have to separate them out, unless you use products with color additives like pink-colored strawberry scented shampoo, and only use four for travel, while the other two are for different use, they are still really well made and easy to fill and dispense and attach and carry around. I highly recommend these. I look forward to seeing more colors and more multi-color sets. That's basically what we all need isn't it, for everything to come in different sets with more choices as to customizing the variations in the sets that we purchase. Some would want all pink.  Some would want all blue. Some would want a rainbow. I need the rainbow, and still these are five stars, because they work so very well.

title: Not working out for me
text:
I was so excited to try these because I am not capable of applying the false eyelashes with glue and occasionally I want some extra flair. I know with most makeup you have to practice a few times before you can get it right, but I’ve tried these eyelashes many times and I cannot make them look good for the life of me.
If you are not good at applying liquid eyeliner then you definitely won’t be able to get the magnetic fluid across your eyes to look good. When you try to apply the eyelashes to it, you will still see a choppy line. If you don’t get that right the rest of it looks terrible. I had to watch a few different YouTube videos to see if I could get any tips or tricks.
One thing that did help was trimming the eyelashes. I could not figure out why my eyes kept watering every single time I applied the lashes and I found it was because the lashes were too wide. Once I did that, they did not irritate me as much. Before I trimmed them it felt like little metal pieces were scraping me. I’m using the smallest size which is 12 mm and they still look very exaggerated. There is no way that I would wear this for every day use as it suggests.
I’ve attempted to wear these about 5 times. They just don’t line up on my lashes and look horribly fake.
On top of all this, through my 5 attempts of trying to apply these, 2 of the 5 magnets have fallen off. The information in the item description says you can use them as regular falsies when the magnets fall off but that’s not going to happen for me.

title: Smells great, very intense scrub
text:
When you open the lid of this lava scrub, you'll think you just stepped off the plane landing in Hawaii. It smells so tropical, so dewy, and so tasty I almost tried it. And it's no wonder, with ingredients of coconut oil, papaya extract, and macadamia oil.
I tried it a few times on my face (mixed with soap, of course), and it was a little too strong for me. The sugar crystals are large and sturdy, requiring a vigorous scrub to dissolve. It didn't cause me to break out, but I did notice that the rest of the day and the following day, it looked like half my skin got taken off. Dips, discolorations, and small zits that were hiding beneath the surface were all visible - but after a couple of days everything went back to normal. Those of you who have tried chemical or acid peels on your face know what I mean.
I get it, if there are that many impurities on my skin, it's a good idea to scrub them away. But I don't really like looking at my face like that in the mirror. So... now I've switched it to a body scrub and use it in the tub. Perfect! Arms, legs, and chest are now totally smooth and smell great.

title: Damaged or do it yourself? Is it cruelty free....
text:
Feathers can be a little controversial. Rest assured that these are cruelty free! I used to have a peacock as a pet. He shed those beautiful tail feathers every year, and even though he is long gone I still have some of his gorgeous plumes. Peacock feathers are not harvested from the animal, you simply pick them up as they are naturally shed.
This set arrived in a plastic bag. When I pulled the pieces out, there were three peacock feather pieces and one headband. Each feather piece has a rhinestone accent at the bottom. One is all rhinestone, one is a pearl surrounded by rhinestones, and one is a London blue stone surrounded by rhinestones.
Of the two larger pieces, one has an alligator clip hot glued onto the felt backing, and one has a strip of grossgrain ribbon glued to the back. Although I'm not sure, I suspect that it was at one time glued to the headband, or they leave it to the consumer to glue it to the headband. I tried to push the end of the headband through the middle of the ribbon, thinking that perhaps it could slide on, but it is glued completely, you can't slide it onto the headband.
The smaller piece also has an alligator type clip of the same size as the larger clipped piece. They stay beautifully in your hair and are actually comfortable.

I wouldn't call this a glamor or fashion accessory set, it's definitely a costume set that would be great for a roaring twenties party. Each one would also be a fun addition to a hat. I wear a lot of hats and love to adorn them with scarves and feathers.

The following is not part of my review but it is a kind of funny peacock story. naturally, when guests came over they wanted to see him with his tail spread out in beautiful peacock glory. They only open up like that when they're trying to impress someone, and he certainly was never impressed by any of my guests. At the time I also had a miniature pig. That peacock was so in love with the pig that whenever she came near him he would spread out his feathers and shake them hoping she would notice and return his love. Of course that never happened, the pig could care less. But whenever we wanted to show him off to our friends, we would walk the pig over to him and he would immediately open his tail feathers with a great flourish! My friends and I were all impressed. Maggie the pig was not.

text:
Just tried the Sea Pearl White Shimmer on my nails, and if you are looking for just a "CLEAN LOOK" to your nails with a tad bit of opal shine on it, this is it.

2 coats of the polish is NOT opaque, NEITHER is 3 coats. BUT.. this is just a "shimmer" look. NO GLITTER. This did make my nails look clean and pretty, but really, it was just a hair over clear in my book.

I think it should have a bit more SHIMMER to it than it did. I ended up keeping only ONE accent nail per hand, and painting OVER the Sea Pearl, as I didn't like it much. You can see my nail under 3 coats quite clearly, so I tried to stamp it to add a bit more POP to it. This is the result (see pic)... all the others I painted over.

Anyhoo, I'll use it ONLY when I do not want a color and prefer a CLEAR WHITE SHIMMER CLEAN look. I used an LED light to cure, and it cured fast. Great if you want a simple CLEAN look, and see your natural nail underneath. Did add a tad bit of white to them and slight shimmer, but that is all I can recommend it for.

title: "Sea" Mist is a Misnomer
text:
*Sigh*
This product received rave reviews, so I was very excited to purchase and test it out.
My hair is naturally very wavy. If the wave doesn't have product, it isn't tame. So, most mornings I dry/straighten it to avoid looking like a wild banshee at work.
However, I recently moved to Florida and because of the humidity, my waves are being a bit more cooperative. That being said, a product like this that would help hold the wave throughout the day and tame the "wildness" is desirable. Unfortunately, this has not worked for me as it is advertised.
There isn't enough salt to hold the hair in place. Instead of a subtle stiffness to hold the 'beach wave', my hair appeared a droopy, greasy mess that looks like I'd slept in a frying pan (with leftover bacon grease) rather than the just-off-the-surf look that I was anticipating.
Everyone's hair is different, so perhaps this product works better for others. My hair is long and thick. I would think that this may work better for people with shorter hair where gravity isn't fighting with the product all day.
Okay, so why did I give this more than one star? IT SMELLS AMAZING! If anything, I'll be using this as a perfume rather than a hair product. Seriously, I can't get enough of the coconutty wonderfulness in the bottle.

title: Super soft skin, but oh so messy to use!!
text: This coffee scrub smells divine while dry, and leaves my skin smelling ever so subtly like coffee and cinnamon.  Oddly, I don’t really notice the smell in the shower.  I love the exfoliation and use it on my entire body.  Out of the shower, I feel a mild oil barrier on my skin that I don’t care for.  Once I add my normal body shaping cream (Clarins Body Fit), I’m in heaven!  The 2 products together leave my skin super cool and tingly for about an hour, followed by crazy soft skin.  I don’t actually have a lot of cellulite (thank you Clarins!), but what I do have is less noticeable after just 2 uses.  So, what’s not to like?  This scrub is so incredibly messy, it’s borderline impractical!  Most scrubs are made with sugar or salt crystals held together with some form of oil or gel, and dissolve in the shower.  Ground coffee doesn’t dissolve and this scrub is dry, so it literally gets everywhere...like sand from the beach!  And worse, I have a walk in shower with white tile floors...coffee stains if it sits too long!  As much as I like the way this product smells and improves my skin texture, it’s a pain in my cellulite free backside to clean up!  Mixing it with a little water and creating a paste before use helps a little, and thankfully I have a handheld shower to quickly rinse it off my tiled walls and shower door, but I’m constantly concerned it’s going to stain my floor grout.  Deep sigh...I soooooo wish this product weren’t so messy!

title: Get lash glue instead
text:
Well, I purchased these same lashes without the dandy little tool. I had such a bad experience, but I was determined to get those little ****s on my eyes. Well, the tool was of no help whatsoever. Those little lash pieces still fell and fluttered around. I could not even find one piece until I looked in the mirror and found it on my nose. I even watched YouTube to get tips. One model put hers on, claiming that it was easy after you get the hang of it... but even her lashes did not fit next to her eyelid. There was a space of about 1/16 of an inch. She said that they look really good "from a distance". Hey Hey Hey... from a distance??? You've got to be kidding. How many of us want to stay across the room to look good??

In addition, I really don't know whose eyes they are made for. These lashes do not follow the contour of anyone's eyes who I know. Who has straight eyelids??? These lashes look like wings on your eyes. They stick fly out at the edges and I could not find any way to get them to fit the lid, short of a lot of nail glue.... that sort of defeats the purpose of them.

Now I can look back at this experience and laugh. I'm quite certain that an observer would have found it to be hilarious to watch me. At the time, I saw no humor in it. This was funny enough to be on the "I love Lucy" show. I would have loved to see Lucy and Ethel trying these out.

The concept is great.... wow!! But, it makes me wonder if the developers did these to determine the lengths that we would go to for beauty.

In closing, I even tried to get ahold of the company.... and wouldn't you know, there was no contact number on their site. Amazon was gracious enough to receive them back from me. Thank goodness for Amazon's commitment to trying to ensure that we are satisfied.

Now do you see why I procrastinated in doing this review??? I have never submitted a review as negative as this. BTW, I finally admitted to some friends my experience with these.... and they confessed that they, too, returned their magnetic lashes.

title: WARNING!!!! This Color is Impossible to Remove!!! Use with caution!!!
text:
Summary: I loved the color, it's vibrant and fades to a rose pink on my ombre'd hair. However, I want to remove it now (after sporting the color for a year) and it won't come out!! Most google searches imply I'm screwed unless I bleach, cut, or color over it. This is a warning to all other potential buyers of Atomic Pink.

Intro: The reviews for this product and the photos are spectacular. I had tried a Manic Panic pink and it was an awful super blue pink with zero warmth/red. Upon seeing a lovely photo of a girl with rose gold hair when she added it to her brownish blonde hair, I wanted that on my ombre.

Pros:
-I mixed it to my desired shade with conditioner and it turned out amazing. I kept retouching the color since I expected this to be similar to Manic Panic. Manic Panic color would die with one wash; but this....this was so vibrant even after washing! It was amazing and I got more compliments when I went stronger on the color vs conditioner ratio.

Cons:
-Now, after a year, I've grown tired of pink and I want to go back to a natural color but the looooord baby jesus cannot exorcise this pink outta mah har. I've washed it with Suave clarifying shampoo/Head and Shoulders plus baking soda, left the mixture in for hours before rinsing, and there's still strands of pink remaining. There's a good portion that has been removed with this method, but about a third of the hue just won't die.
-Oh and my shower? It has permanent pink spots here and there. I moved to my bathtub in hopes that the bathtub would be easier to clean. Well it's not. Everything is pink now. Everything. I guess this is my life now.

title: Chemical burns under lip
text:
I would have posted a picture but it looked too graphic to post online.

I went back and forth for weeks debating whether or not to purchase this product. I had gotten my teeth professionally whitened at the dentist a few years ago and it worked beautifully; however, could not justify spending several hundred dollars on doing it again. In lieu of spending a ton of money on professional whitening, I researched at-home whitening kits. Glo seemed to rank high with at-home whitening kits and Amazon offered a coupon for it so I had finally decided to go for it.

I received the item pretty quickly and charged it right away. The first 2 days were fine, albeit tedious. On the 3rd day, I started to get a sensation on the underside of my top lip even though I applied the lip balm generously. By the 4th day, the burning sensation was intolerable but I pushed through it until I finished the session. By the end of that 4th day, the pain was enough for me to decide not to continue using the product. I flipped my top lip up and there is a long, white burn all the way across the length of my lip. It lines up exactly the way the gel would leak up out of the mouthpiece. All this for not even a slight change in the shade of my teeth.

I am returning this product and applying the money towards real professional teeth whitening at the dentist. I gave 2 stars for quick shipping, nice storage case, and the option to be able to return product.

title: Vintage GLAMOUR in RED
text:
From pin-up girls to starlets, from old Hollywood movie queen royalty to the girls at the automat, certain red lipsticks have dominated makeup counters for decades.
This is one of them.

Everything about this lipstick, except for the modern wearability, is vintage glamour. The shape of the tube and the shape of the lipstick itself harkens to another era. Perfect for making the ultimate Cupid's bow pout. It even has that slight fragrance that will remind you of vintage lipsticks.

I normally wear red that has a little more blue in it, so was surprised that this clear red was fine for me. To me that says that it will flatter a wide range of skin tones.
After swiping it on my wrist and then wiping it away, it left a nice stain. If you aren't interested in that drop dead gorgeous look and want something a little more subtle, it does double duty by leaving a pinky red stain when blotted. But go for the high voltage dramatic red if you want to be noticed.

Very comfortable lipstick, but I didn't have a problem with it bleeding. Non-drying and non-cracking. Opaque coverage with one swipe.
Another plus, it makes your teeth look super white.
I hope that this review as well as the photographs can help you to make a decision about this lipstick. It's really hard buying such things online, especially when it comes to luxury brands like this.

title: glowing glassy skin. NIACINAMIDE (2%), ADENOSINE (.04%) & PEARL EXTRACT
text:
I've only just begun using this, so this is a first impression review. I am fairly familiar with the active ingredients and understand how they work (and that they do work, so I expect this to continue that). The new part is the pearl extract, which has both immediate effect and longer term use benefit. I can attest to the immediacy, and it will be with using this for greater amount of time to determine if it a repurchase or not. As I learn more, I will share more. Here is a break down of what is in it and what to expect:

BLANCHET GLAM PEARL RADIANCE CAPSULE SERUM is a supremely light weight gel serum with hint of floral scent from lavender, geranium, rose, and sandalwood. Barely detectable. A little goes a long way. This weightless serum adds a mild level of healthy sheen. Korean Beauty emphasizes healthy skin, hydrated skin, supple skin, dewy, glowing skin. It is never matte. So while you could cover this with your foundation or powder, KB is all about letting natural skin shine through. The gentle, mild barely there sheen provides more of a glass look than a shiny look. Subtle. As for the rest... The primary active ingredients are NIACINAMIDE (2%) and ADENOSINE (.04%).

NIACINAMIDE is a skin care work horse. It provides a variety of benefit to all skin types, ages, and concerns. It is a water-soluble vitamin (B3) that works with the natural substances in your skin to help improve skin barrier, fix past damage, visibly minimize enlarged pores, tighten lax pores, improve uneven skin tone, soften fine lines and wrinkles, diminish dullness, and strengthen a weakened surface. As I hone in on ingredients that pack the greatest punch, niacinamide has stood out as a must have ingredient in my skin care routine. I especially like it for its ability to brighten pigmentation. It also is one of few ingredients that work well with other ingredients without concern for contraindication or nullification. Skin care can get tricky, and this ingredient is just so easy to work with- so go ahead and use it with retinol, peptides, acids, etc. Niacinamide simply helps skin be healthy and look healthy and radiant. As with most skin care, it can take several weeks to several months of consistent use to see changes. This serum will help over time, but other ingredients provide an instant radiant glow.

ADENOSINE is a rising star in anti aging products. There are studies that demonstrate that adenosine is an effective ingredient for improving the appearance of wrinkles, in both the eye and mouth area. Interestingly, adenosine directly affects the production of type I and type III collagen in the skin by binding to A2A receptors in fibroblast cells. So if it can help boost (or at least maintain) collagen, and help collagen from breaking down (collagen is what keeps our skin plump. Compare your 45 year old face to your 18 year old face, if your face now looks "thinner" despite no losing weight, it is the decrease of collagen that has produced that look). Since adenosine has been shown to stimulate the production of collagen, applying it topically can help to prevent (and somewhat even reverse) wrinkles. *thumbs up*

80% FERMENTED PEARL EXTRACT is rich in amino acids and trace minerals that are highly moisturizing, soothing, and brightening. I must say, this is something that is new to me. Before this product, I had no idea that there was a use for pearl extract. It is used in topical skin care products as well as for use internally. I really dont know much about any of this, but a cursory search led me to a few interesting bullet points:
-Increases skin's collagen production
-Helps repair skin's damaged cells
-Lightens skin's tone and improves blemishes
-Diminishes fine lines and wrinkles
-Controls oil and shine
-Reduces pores and promotes smoother skin
-It has soft hues which shift subtly from direct to side views

PURPOSE
Skin Brightening
Anti wrinkle

Uses
High-intensity brightening lotion with 80% of fermented pearl extract in capsule technology

First of all, the pictures show these straightened to make waves and the package of ones I received cannot be convinced to hold that shape. This wouldn't be a big deal, except they are difficult to put on as spirals. You have to thread the hook through first, but the tube is much longer than the hook. If I'd been capable of sprouting a third hand, putting these on would have been the moment it happened. And that's only the first hurdle.
It takes some extra work to get a good curl out of these. Make sure your hair is damp when they go on or it won't hold the curl (after a lot of success in my life using regular foam curlers on dry hair, this was the most disappointing thing). Keep a spray bottle handy, because they take long enough to put on that your hair will dry before you get done, at least the first couple of times. Make sure the hair isn't tangled or twisted or it won't curl properly. Don't snag your hair section with the hook or you'll find out.
A good curl cream is a must because these don't make a curl that holds as well as-- pick a standard type of curler. Make sure you have a God hair spray to set them with, too. If you don't have a quality product or three in your hair to force the curl to hold, they will fall within a few hours and then you've got whatever your hair texture is with too much brushing and a few weird bends.
Also, these pull your hair at the root pretty hard if you try to sleep on them loose, so make sure you have a good cap/bonnet/kerchief/babushka (whatever hair covering you use) to keep them arranged into something fairly comfortable.

title: Skin Feels Soft & Fairly Comfortable, No Greasy Residue-Moderately Strong Perfume & TEA (3.5 Stars)
text:
Spanature Olive Hand & Body Lotion comes with 4 travel size lotions (individually boxed for gifting) in a 2.53 oz size that’s more than twice the size of the tiny 1 oz hand creams I usually buy for my purse. I go through lotion and cream fast as I use it every time I wash my hands and more, so I like this bigger size as it lasts longer but is still a compact size for my purse. It’s also big enough for a long weekend away from home.

This is a lightweight mineral oil based lotion that absorbs quickly and doesn’t leave any greasy residue. It has a pleasant feel and adds just enough moisture to make my dry hands soft and fairly comfortable. I do prefer more hydration, but I also have dry rather than normal skin. The fragrance is moderately strong and sweet. It’s okay used just on my hands, but it would be too strong for me if used as an all over body lotion.

I dislike that this lotion has controversial Triethanolamine (TEA). The FDA designates it as safe for limited use (but bans it from hand sanitizer), but EWG rates it as a moderate health risk (allergen). And TEA can play a role in the formation of dangerous nitrosamines when combined with certain preservatives. I can’t assess that issue in this or any specific products, so I just try to avoid TEA. That aside, I like this lotion pretty well for limited use. 3.5 Stars.

Ingredients: Water, Mineral Oil, Propylene Glycol, Cetearyl Alcohol, Cetyl Ethylhexanoate, Polysorbate 60, Sorbitan Stearate, Stearic Acid, Olea Europaea (Olive), Phenoxyethanol, Caprylyl Glycol, Sodium Polyacrylate, Hydrogenated Polydecene, Trideceth-6, Dimethicone, Hydroxyethylcellulose, Carbomer, Triethanolamine, Sodium Hyaluronate, Disodium EDTA, Allantoin, Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E), Fragrance.

For the price, this is an excellent basic electric toothbrush and flosser. The two pieces lack the fancy features of more expensive pieces, but my dentist says all those extra features are not worth the money. The toothbrush works great and the only feature my dentist recommends is the 2 minute timer to make sure you give yourself enough time to brush all your teeth. I've always used string floss in the past, but this water flosser seems to work just as well most of the time. Sometimes there is some food stuck in my teeth that I still have to use the string for.

As I said, features are minimal. There is 1 charger for both devices, so you can't use the charger as a stand for both items. Instead of all the cardboard in the box, why not include a cheap plastic tray or stand? There also is no travel case, just a little cover for the toothbrush head. I would really prefer a full length hard case to be included instead of having to buy an aftermarket case that doesn't fit well. Also, you only get one tip each for both the flosser and the toothbrush and there is nowhere to easily store extras. This kit is probably designed for single people only, not couples or families.

I understand that there are differing opinions on this trimmer, but after using it back to back with the Remington Precision Pro MB-400 Titanium Vaccuum Mustache and Beard Trimmer, there is no comparison on the following counts:

1) quality of the trimming accessories - the Norelco has a flimsy cutting guide, and its all on the verge of breaking everytime you use it. Anyone who has had a previous Norelco product points this out.

2) a ridiculously designed sideburn trimmer - It is so hard to get the trimmer set-up! a poor design

3) A terrible cut - if you have even a medium beard, the trimmer is very uneven. you can certainly do better.

The Remington is superior in every way.

title: First (almost) electric razor
text:
Just had my first shave with this. I've used two electric razors in my life. One was an already ancient one that my dad had, about 40 years ago. Ripped each of the few hairs in my face out one by one. Then an early Norelco 3-head circular job, about 30 years ago that either sucked or I didn't know how to use. Very even stubble was the result of that. Hence my refusal to try one until my memories have faded.

This review reflects one shave - not a long term review.

I'm impressed. It's slower than I expected, I half-thought I could activate an app on my phone or something and I would be shaved (I'm joking!). It's pretty darn close to a manual 5-blade fresh razor.

Here are the conditions under which I'm reporting:
- I'm 62, so my skin isn't exactly taut on my face.
- Not a heavy beard, I need to shave every day now, but not until I was about 35.
- This shave was with 2 days of stubble.
- I usually shave in the shower, using Braille to tell when a patch is smooth.

I used the razor dry. The manual said to charge the razor before first use, but it came out of the box showing 100% charge so I went for it. The manual also says not to apply too much pressure, so I was tentative at first. It helps to apply fair pressure while moving the razor SLOWLY through that fungus that seems to grow constantly on our faces.

Stretching my skin with other-handed fingers in most spots helped. I used a mirror just to watch the progress, but you can use your sonic sensors, AKA ears, to tell when the blades are and aren't removing stubble. I don't think a mirror is at all necessary, YMMV.

While I've been writing this, I've used Braille again to check on the usual trouble spots - I can just grab the mower and run it over the rough bits while I'm doing this. You could do this easily while driving somewhere - no risk of a small knick, and the aural attention that it takes doesn't really distract from driving.

I didn't notice when I ordered this razor that it came with an extra foil. Nice detail, since the foil is easy to damage being thin (as it should be). The kit comes with a carrying bag, which is nice to keep everything together while traveling. I would find a small rigid container for the extra foil if I were to travel with that - it could easily get bent in the carrying bag knocking around with all the bits. The foil is too long for the old canisters from film cameras, but a cut-off from a roll of Xmas paper would suffice.

The grip is comfortable and makes the shaving head easy to maneuver. The carrying bag contains everything in a small package - I'm a Cardinal (Archbishops and above don't shave) in the Church of Small Luggage and I will happily carry this instead of a couple of manual razors on any trip.

Finally (applause erupts from the crowd), very nearly close shave as a manual razor, a little slower than a manual razor, works very well dry (absolutely unlike a manual razor, though I've tried that also and it does sort of work).

Buy it. Try it.

title: Very hard, mostly unusable stampers
text: I recently purchased a bunch of stampers to test, these included. These were among the worst I tested. All 3 of these are hard stampers with no squish to them. The green is the hardest, followed by white, then the red (the one I received was actually pink). When they're this hard, know that you need to roll the design on rather than press it on. Rolling, if not done carefully can lead to smudging. Also, hard stampers are not forgiving on curved nails. It will hit the highest part of your nail and miss the lower areas. I also found that the hard stampers do a bad job at filling in solid areas of designs, but only work well on designs with fine lines. The red (pink) one was the best of this bunch, very similar to the Konad double ended stamper. Although, I prefer the Konad because it is slightly larger. I made a full review of the stampers I tested here: https://nailstampingaddict.wordpress.com/2015/11/14/nail-stamper-trials/

text:
I don't really have any de-puffed areas. I do have a couple of odd spots around the corners of my lips that I am trying to figure out how to attend to. I have been successful with Easydew products, so I added this into the mix to see what more it can help me with.

-The texture is cool and gel like. It is clear.
-Very light scent
-Gentle feeling, non irritating on my dry, semi sensitive skin
-A little goes a long way, just use a little.. gently dab it on. Allow a minute to absorb before adding other products
-Key ingredients, benefits:
Epidermal Growth Factor (EGF) helps to repair skin, and Hyaluronic acid (HA) helps to attract and retain moisture.

I am currently using a variety of Easydew products, some of which contain EGF. I love how my skin feels and looks. I have only recently added this in, and I don't expect a quick change. I am using it around lips, and am considering using it around eye area. Since this can be used near eyes, I may keep it only for that area. I have their serum and moisturizer with EGF & HA. I would say from my experience with this line, is that this is more of a longer term use item. I see it says something about instant depuffing, but unless you have a real trouble spot, it may not be instantly noticeable. What I encourage is consistent use. Maybe add in their other fill up products or Repair Control EX, then use this for specific spots.

My skin: mid 40s, clear, semi dry, semi sensitive, Rosacea (redness/visible veins).

title: Not anti-fog, but you will breathe better/UPDATE: replaced with much worse
text:
I just reordered the same exact masks, but they sent me a totally different brand. The new brand is called "FRYLR" the old brand (the one in the photo of a working mask) was "TEMI". TEMI masks are great. FRYLR are simply awful. The first one on the top was already broken in the box. None of them look like they're going to hold up, even the ones that aren't broke. They're badly put together and not stuck on properly.

Since Amazon doesn't allow you to choose who you're getting them from, or tell you who you got them from last, it's all about luck when you order. 50/50 you get the good TEMI masks or the crappy unusuable FRYLR masks. It's the same purchase button. Either that or they replaced the good masks with bad ones. The "TEMI" mask is the one in the photo that contains a face.

If you're the gambling sort, here's the original 5 star reviews over the "TEMI":
TEMI
Positives:
1. You can breathe! Unlike with every cloth mask out there. It's still uncomfortable because you're still re-breathing your own exhale, but you won't pass out. So if you have health conditions, this type of mask is probably the best option you'll find.
2. You can see through it, allowing lipreading and ability to see a smile and so forth.
3. Comfortable on the ears
4. Keeps you from touching your face, which is part of the reason cloth and surgical masks are a bad idea.

Negatives:
1. Chin indent doesn't go away for a while and can irritate.
2. Touches the average sized nose.
3. It does fog up, but the fog disappears if the weather's not cold, so "fog resistant" might be a better description.

Wore this to the bus and the post office, and was allowed to ride and others seemed fine with it. It's an excellent way to go where you need to without being denied the ability to get necessities done, yet still breathe.

It comes in a pack of ten.

title: After 4 months No Longer Works
text:
At first I thought this was going to be the solution to the problem of the original rechargeable Sonicare toothbrush with batteries that can't be replaced (my original Sonicare stopped holding a charge).

However, after only four months (just long enough to waste money replacing the brush head!), the button began to only work erratically, and now it does not work at all (can't power the toothbrush on).

The reviews that state that the battery compartment does not keep water out are completely true. The battery compartment is always moist, and the batteries will begin to rust.

I was pleased that my Eneloop batteries worked well to power the toothbrush, so I could be using rechargeable batteries, however it doesn't matter if the toothbrush itself doesn't last past 6 months.

The batteries that came with the toothbrush lasted around a month. The Eneloops needed charged only once in the next three months.

Looks like the Sonicare brand just fails on too many levels, regardless of whether you are using the ultra-expensive rechargeable unit, or this unit with two AA batteries.

[Update] Flashlights have had "screw on" caps for nearly one hundred hears. The Sonicare toothbrush is the same form factor. I have no idea why someone at Philips thought a "clip on" cap (vs. a screw on) would be better, ESPECIALLY for something you use with water. I am still COMPLETELY BAFFLED by why they would use this design. The battery compartment will ALWAYS be moist. Being able to use rechargeable batteries is clearly superior to being stuck with the Philips Soincare charging station. However, the fact that your batteries get wet means you will eventually ruin your batteries. That said, I am about to purchase another one. Being able to use your own batteries makes it a when, both for the fact that you can replace the batteries and also so that the (much more expensive) toothbrush isn't useless when the internal batteries fail after a year or so. Unfortunately there is no better alternative at this pricep oint.

title: Fun Idea - Just Not Practical
text:
What you get - 10 horror style mouth covering temporary tattoos

Pros - the designs are fun and spooky - definitely fit the Halloween bill and look like they would be a great addition to many horror costumes.

Cons - they have to go over your whole mouth which firstly makes it almost impossible to apply well (you know how temporary tattoos can be tricky - this is that but more so because it's over your mouth. If by some miracle you DO manage to get it on and in a good placement you then can't move your mouth at all. No talking, eating, or drinking. I have seen suggestions about cutting a slit in the tattoo - but that just makes it move and fall apart so it's not worth it.

Overall - you get 10 for a cheap price - probably better to put them in a separate area other than the mouth and go for a weird look rather than use it like a mask.

title: This thing is absolute garbage.
text:
I don't like writing bad reviews, but I felt like this thing rates one. I really can't return it for a refund because it is what they said it is and it does what it says it does. It just does it really poorly. The different pads are a nice touch, but they're useless if the motor doesn't spin them effectively.

I put 4 brand new AA batteries in it, and got in the shower. I selected a pad, turned it on and it spins at probably 160 RPM - between 2 and 3 revolutions each second. Which isn't bad, except that it slows way down if you put the motor under a load (such as pressing it to your skin). It then bogs down so badly that I could easily cover the same area on my body with a 99¢ scrubbie and do a better job.

So this is going straight into a yard sale. Save your money and buy a scrubbie and a back brush - at least they don't eat batteries.

title: Nice power toothbrush!
text:
I bought a more expensive power toothbrush for my wife and thought I need one for myself. After doing some research, I pulled the trigger on this one.

For the money, you get
1. an Oral-B power toothbrush with good quality and water proofing
2. reasonable battery time per charge
3. a built in 'stutter' timer (stutter every 2 min)

It has most of the functionalities as the more expensive ones. There are a couple of weak points:
1. The timer does not reset itself after each use and has a memory effect. To be more specific, if you turned off the toothbrush at 1.5 mins, the next time you use it, it will stutter at 0.5min and recycle the timer.
2. The brush is not very durable. I am guessing the manufacturer intentionally makes it so that you will buy replacement more frequently.

To clean it now we just leave the head closed or risk fighting it trying to get it back on. Takes forever to dry that way and doesn't get very clean.

Yes, guys, my husband and I both use this razor! The women's versions (foil type) of a leg shaver are horrible! I'd bet most women don't use them because they don't have forever to shave their legs! Women's leg hair vs. men's facial hair...not much difference.

Other than the cheaply made head assembly falling off, this shaver worked very well, except on longer hairs. If you repeatedly missed one and it gets longer than say 1/4 to 1/3 inch, be prepared to have it yanked out...painfully! My husband also noticed this when he got too close to his sideburns. Our advice: use the long hair attachment first.

title: Cheap Shaver is Cheap
text:
I picked one of these up on sale last fall in order to be able to cut my own hair. The price was right, especially on sale, and it performed adequately for my needs - touching up a crew cut once a month or so. However the tabs which allow the guides (which Conair inexplicably calls "combs") to clip on to the main unit are flimsy and in roughly nine months of infrequent use I have broken the tabs on all three attachments, meaning that the unit can no longer adjust to trim hair at any length greater than bald skin.

This is a real flaw, but I was willing to put up with it, right up until I tried to order replacement "combs" and found that while they will sell you replacements, it's totally impossible to order such replacements online. The manufacturer has an online store and there's a separate website dedicated specifically to this product - but neither website has current pricing nor ordering info for replacement parts. If you want to order replacement parts, you have to do it by phone.

And that's why I'm buying a different brand of trimmer for next month's haircut.

text:
My skin is dry, totally clear (no acne) save for some redness & visible veins from Type 1 rosacea. This sunscreen feels quite gentle and does not seem to irritate my skin at all. It adds a light but effective level of hydration without feeling heavy. It is a chemical sunscreen, so zero white cast. It is thin, and goes on like a light lotion. Typical viscosity among my other K-beauty brands.

I have a wide assortment of sunscreen, of various formulations and types. It is my #1 skin care product as I use it daily all year long. It is a habit. I avoid the sun for a few reasons, so sunscreen is vital to my well being. I live in a variable climate (from dry, freezing temps to humid hot) and I have sunscreen preference depending on season and situation. I tend to prefer mineral (my fair skin can handle any white cast) but do utilize chemical sunscreen often.

I am going to like this for basic daily summer use. I tend to reduce my morning skin care routine down to a basic wash or splash of water and a moisturizing sunscreen. Since this offers SPF 50 (P++++), I know my skin is going to be pretty well protected. Since it feels like a moisturizer and goes on clear, I can skip my other skin care if I want. I tend to skip morning skin care in the summer because I am likely to just sweat it off anyway (I have a more involved night time routine to make up for it). So a sunscreen such as this is easy to use, makes my skin feel good, and easy to reapply throughout the day. I dont wear make up usually, but for sake of review I used it under a light foundation tint. Seems to play well- I didnt notice any rolling/pilling. I'll use it up. I have also used it over other skin care (hydrating toner, serum, light moisturizer) and it worked well on top of all that too.

Not sure yet if it will be repurchase. I do like Fascy Lab products, so it's a contender. Worth trying anyway

title: This vs. Clarisonic Uplift?
text:
I haven't been using this item long enough to report on any discernible difference in my face but I can speak to a couple of other interesting tidbits.

I know that these have been in use for generations and they must work because people swear by them. If that weren't proof enough, I use my Clarisonic Uplift daily, and it comes with an attachment that does the exact same thing that this roller does, only with using technology. The instructions on this roller is to use it for 5-10 minutes a day, 2-3 times a day. That's a lot and I don't know of many people who care to carve out time to do this, but if you're sitting quietly watching TV or even reading, you can do it absentmindedly. With the Clarisonic, you're supposed to use it with a moisturizer or a serum but with this, you use it on a dry face. With or without a lotion, the massaging affect is exactly the same.

The jade roller feels cool across the skin (even if mine does squeak a little) and it feels wonderful. I'm not sure it does anything if you're rolling it on your chest, but it feels amazing if done with a bit of pressure. It comes in a nice little Asian-inspired embroidered bag, so it doesn't look bad if you want to leave it on your bedside for easy access. I'm going to continue to use the Uplift each night but this item doesn't require a battery and I can whip it out anytime.

title: SHORT handle, WEIRD neck angle, BAD loofa positioning
text:
The brush is very soft, soft enough to use on your face or your more sensitive spots, but still stiff enough to clean those callouses on your feet. It won't remove all the callous, but it will get them clean LOL. The loofa side is soft enough not to be irritating on the skin, but it is very small AND someone thought it was a good idea to put a rope loop sticking through the loofa so you actually end up trying to scrub your body with the rope instead of the loofa. VERY annoying. They should have found a better place for that rope loop - like attached to the back of the handle. And the neck of the handle is built at a pretty severe curve, makes it so that if you try to scrub yourself with the loofa you will just smack yourself with the bent part of the plastic handle instead.

The brush side is pretty good and the plastic handle is comfortable and solid, but I'm tall and also disabled with limited range of motion in my shoulders... so for me the handle is too short by almost a foot. That, combined with the bad design decisions they made on the loofa side... this is one of the worst shower sticks I've seen.

title: Worth it!
text:
Ingredients:
Miracle Oil® Ingredients:

Olive Oil, Canola Oil, Wheat Germ Oil, Sweet Almond Oil, Sesame Seed Oil, Castor Oil, Safflower Oil, Dimethicone, Vitamins E, A & D, Burdock Root, Chamomile, Hyssop, Henna, Alfalfa, Sage, Goldenseal, Jaborandi, Slippery Elm Bark, Sheep Sorrell, Wheat Germ, Cherry Bark, Comfrey, Black Walnut, Yarrow, Fragrance

This product contains no animal fat or oils and is a cruelty free product.

***
I have used this for 20 years. I can not smell any fragrance with this at all,
this is best used in light applications for body and hair- a little goes along way! Its NOT gloppy like olive oil/almond/canola, seems lighter than grape seed oil even.
Worth the $. I lightly apply it through my hair the day I need to wash it- lightly oil all hair, twist up/clip, time it like a light hot oil treatment so it can soak in and work. It is a God send for unruley eyebrows. It washes right out no residue. I do this 2 times a week. I live in the desert/New Mexico/hard water/50 yrs/unprocessed thick semi curly hair. My hair shines but its not oily looking after washing, it semi tames and makes it so much better...it looks alive and healthy. My beautican is astounded. I have found its so much cheaper and works far much better than high scale salon items. It feeds your hair and body.
How I apply this I squeaze a small amount (pea size) onto one palm then rub my hands/palms quickly together till oil is warm- then lay my hands on area and massage in-it sinks right into dry scaley elbows, chapped lips, wind burned knees- etc. it does leave a light very fine oil film if it doesnt soak in 100%. If that happens it doesnt stain my clothes.
Oddly I have found for some reason it heals skin/cuts/wind burn more quickly than salves.
I keep my oil bottle on the (metal) end of an old frozen OJ tube style container- making a tiny saucer in case a drop oil seeps out.
Just my 2 cents....

If you've ever tried to apply a goopy face mask with just your fingers (looking at you gold-infused charcoal paste), then you know the struggle that often comes with scooping up products and then trying to spread them evenly before they start to dry in place. These bendy silicone-tipped spatula brush sticks and paddles streamline the entire process!

All of the tools are lightweight, easy to clean, and they seem to be fairly durable! I love the candy-colored palette of pastel hues, and the various textures and tips offer plenty of versatility and flexibility. They are also great for hygienically scooping up globs and dollops of various creams and moisturizers that need to be kept as sanitary as possible for repeated applications. I'd definitely recommend this tool set to others!

title: the BEST for anything from subtle shimmer to hard chrome
text:
This palette has become one of my favorite nail tools. I've been using it mostly on acrylic dip powder, but have also used it on top of traditional polish with a clear coat on top. if you apply a light/thin layer (or on dip powder base that has NOT been buffed), it adds a subtle shimmer. If you apply it more thickly AND buff it with the eyeshadow-type applicator, you can achieve a solid chrome look that's really fun as well. I enjoy putting it on all my nails, or just on one nail for a fun accent look that still matches my overall color scheme. I've also enjoyed using it on a relatively plain nail for a fine-textured glitter look while other nails have full-texture glitter. It's really a lot of fun and goes a super long way (basically as far as a comparable eyeshadow palette would go). Strongly recommended

UPDATE: I've ditched my acrylic powders (long story - I kayak too much) but couldn't let go of this shimmer. Turns out it works on traditional nail polish as well. You can apply it directly on top for a chrome effect, or BUFF (not file) the surface gently then apply for a soft shimmer. In both cases top with clearcoat. I still love this palette!

title: Poor Overall Performance and Longevity
text:
I bought this in July and began using it in early September. It seemed like it would be easy to use, as well as clean and maintain. The extra features included a beard trimmer, a nose-hair trimmer, and a face brush. There was also a charging cord but no actual charger.

I ended up using this every day for about 100 days before the lid broke for the cutter housing. It broke right where you would expect at the hinge after normal opening and closing for cleaning per the instructions. For what I paid for the shaver, it didn't seem worth it to try and find a replacement cutter housing.

The shave itself is by far the worst I've ever gotten from an electric shaver. I did use it consecutively for more than several weeks to allow my face to adjust. This wasn't the issue as my face was already used to using electric shavers and I had no adjustment period issues with my face. The issue was that the cutters were just plain dull and ineffective. Even with three heads I would say I spent at least twice as long shaving with this shaver as compared to my last one. Though it has three cutting heads, I would sometimes have to make a half a dozen passes over the same area before the stubble was cut flush with my skin.

The shaver seemed to use a lot of charge for a single shave. Enough of a charge that it typically took 4+ hours to fully recharge after a single shave. I'm not sure if it was the battery or the charging cord but the charger was actually the same one I used with the previous shaver with much better results.

The nose hair trimmer worked well. I never used the beard trimmer or facial brush.

After cheaping out on this unit, I ended up buying a Panasonic Arc4 for 3 times more than what I spent for this one but so far it is absolutely worth the extra money. Do yourself a favor and don't cheap out and buy this like I did.
