title: Effective Moisturizer!
text:
[[ASIN:B00VXEQ0WO Retinol 2.5% Cream From Majestic Pure for Face and Eye Area Will Nourish Your Skin, Potent Anti Aging Formula Reduces the Appearances of Wrinkles, Stretch Marks & Redness, 50ml]]

I purchased Majestic Pure Retinol Cream because I am always looking for something that will help give my skin a more youthful appearance. After all, no one wants to look older or tired. I try all kinds of skin care products and really work hard at keeping my skin in good shape, so I decided I'd give this a try.I was speaking to a friend of mine recently whose skin always looks gorgeous. I asked her what she did to look so good? She is considerably older than me, but has no wrinkling and very pretty skin. She told me that she visits a dermatologist regularly and that she uses a retinol cream and that she pays 60.00 for just a small tube, plus the cost of the doctor visit. Now I am not sure of the strength of the retinoI cream she is using is, and I noticed this is 2.5% so I think that's a pretty effective dosage.The product came in a 1.7 fluid ounce moisturizer. I noticed that the retinol moisturizer also had Vitamin E & B5, Green Tea, Jojoba Oil, Propolis and shea butter. So I thought about Vitamin A or retinol and what it does for the skin. Vitamin A stimulates and thickens the dermis where collagen, blood vessels and elastin are thereby reducing wrinkles and increasing blood flow to the surface of your skin. Vitamin A actually expands the deposit of collagen in the skin; therefore slowing down the normal aging breakdown of your collagen and elastin. I've also read when studying skin care (and I really researched it) that Vitamin A increases blood flow and reduces the symptoms of rosacea, helps heal wounds more quickly, repairs cells in the skin and optimizes UV protection, exfoliates to make the skin more smooth, supple and even and even decreases melanin granules reducing brown spots and pigmentation. Vitamin A decreases sebum (oil) thereby treating acne very well and even helps with the eradication of precancerous lesions of the skin and improves hydration. Skins miracle healer!My mother has always used vitamin E. She is in her 70's and still has beautiful skin and is very selective about what she puts on her skin. I've read that Vitamin E has been used in skincare for so long that it sometimes gets passed over for newer, more exotic-sounding ingredients that are sometimes advertised or added to products. But Vitamin E is a highly beneficial ingredient, a strong defense against free radicals and the damage the environment does to the skin. When it’s combined with other antioxidants, It is an exceptional line of defense for your skin.The product is very good quality with no redness, burning itching or negative side effects. It doesn't leave your face shiny or greasy and seems to absorb within just a couple of minutes. I notice an immediate firming of the skin but no discomfort or a feeling of being too tight. There is no build up or product residue. This product has a nice smell, light and soothing, and is quite easy to use. It's good that the items come in a pump, because exposure to air effects good quality ingredients. A little goes a long way, and the product seems to be lasting a good long time. I use many of Majestic Pure products, and I have had excellent luck with them all and no issues. This moisturizer already is reducing fine line and wrinkles in my skin. It really helps to keep down oiliness and shine off my face. I use this moisturizer on clean skin and I let it soak in, and use under the the throat and jaw line for added firmness. While I am applying my eye makeup, I let the cream soak in. This anti aging skin cream keeps your skin supple and moisturized. So far no complaints or problems and all the products I've tried and it works well for me. I am not affiliated with any supplier or manufacturer of goods.

title: Good product, bad customer service (Almay not the seller).
text: I really want this on subscribe and save but Amazon only has a couple shades available. :( anyways a few years ago my skin became super sensitive and Almay consistently puts out products that don't bother my skin. This has pretty good coverage and you can build it up. I am rather happy with it. That is the only reason I am not giving it 3 stars. Here is my problem. I am colorblind and finding makeup that matches my skin by myself is a nightmare. For those of you who do not know colorblind is where we have a cone that is low in color which also affects other colors. We do not see in black and white. My green is low sometimes making certain greens look like a light version of goldenrod copy paper or as I say 1970's gold. Yuck... Anyways this affects how I view other colors and I cannot match makeup well. Certain shades will appear the same leading me to believe I have a match until someone (usually my cousin) points out my makeup looks ridiculous. Let me mention my cousins call me "educated" colorblind because most of the time I know how to compensate for color deficiency. I know color theory well. I wrote Almay about the problem because my only alternative was to drag my cousin to the store and have her "sample" shades. I am sure other customers and the store does not appreciate this so in the end I have tons of money wasted on the wrong shades. I know this happens to people with normal color vision but multiple that by 5-10 times you have done that and that describes my experience. Anyways I thought I'd write them and ask as Covergirl used to sell a 3 pack sampler of similar colors so you could find your perfect shade. The reply was to purchase full size products. I thought this lacked empathy as I wasn't writing to get free products. I was writing to find a resolution that would result in me being a long time customer. I don't think them going the extra mile to send something mini even if I had to pay was asking too much from such a large corporation. This leaves me felling like I should rate them 3 stars. While I remain a loyal customer they don't care about me. :( I wouldn't have minded paying for some sort of samples, but I guess they rather keep taking my money while I experienced trial and error finding a shade. Now while my cousins have not compared my makeup to mud since using this shade I haven't exactly had them inspect it closely for me after applied. I will ask to get a final opinion. The smart shade does not provide adequate coverage or I would go that route. I have that product also for lazy days. I rate the product a solid 4 stars for being a good product especially on super sensitive skin, but I rate the company 0 stars for not even considering people like me. They got my money so I guess they're happy. Still let wondering if this is the right shade for me.. *sigh* still holding on to the heap of bottles because I paid good money for it. Anyways I am leaving this review here because this is where I am going to order and the price looks very reasonable. Now if I could find the perfect powder... Btw their concealer sucks. Just use the foundation to build coverage and save your money. I will update after I get some more opinions on if this shade is for me. Gawd I hope it is. I can't keep spending all this money, and because of my skin conditions I absolutey have to wear makeup when going out so I don't feel like people are staring at me.

title: Glad Honest for Men finally got it sorted out and offers two varieties - one exfoliating and one not
text:
Gotta take a moment to write a review because this is my favorite soap. The other kind they make (the non-exfoliating kind) went through phases - first it was exfoliating, then they got bad reviews because it was TOO exfoliating (which I absolutely loved about it), then they removed ALL of the exfoliation and got bad reviews because there wasn't any exfoliation any more... and finally they got it together to have two varieties, one without any exfoliation, and one with exfoliation - this one. And the other one is now stuck with a 3 star review average just because of that mix-up.

At first I was nervous that even with the exfoliation back (this one), it would not be as good as it was before when it had the exfoliation originally, because it used to be oatmeal for the exfoliation, and now it is coffee grounds. I even sent them a note asking why they didn't use oatmeal any more, and they said it was because the oatmeal version would fall apart in the Amazon warehouses. But I tried the coffee ground exfoliation - and even though it isn't quite as good - it's still great. This soap beats any other I've tried to purchase, and I have purchased about 10 brands through Amazon that all said they were exfoliating. Only one of them was exfoliating enough, and I like this one better. (I forget the name of that other brand right now; I'm at my computer. If someone really wants to know, add a comment and I'll dig it up.) I really need a very strong exfoliating soap, and this one actually is strong enough. It also happens to be a brown bar with a decent hearty soap material, as well - not phony - so it is all I need.

Just wanted to post this review to start to bring back some 5 stars for this company now that they've gotten things sorted out and have two varieties, one exfoliating and one that isn't.

text: I tried this on thick curly 3c hair. The results were quite decent. You first wash your hair with the pre-treatment shampoo to clarify the hair and remove dirt and oils. At this point, make sure to detangle the hair well and section it into smaller parts so that you can apply the keratin treatment. The hair should be 80% towel dried. You then comb in the keratin treatment to each section of hair. I recommend wearing gloves. Allow it time to process and then blow dry and finish with a flat iron. The hair came out quite silky and smooth, but it began to revert into fluffiness as the day went on. Adding a bit of hair oil helped to restrain the humidity. For an at home kit, it is decent, but it is not as strong as salon treatments.

title: Wow!  Don't Buy This!
text: Edit May 16, 2019:  I just sent the second brush cleaning machine back to Amazon for a refund.  The first unit I had stopped working not long after writing this review.  It just stopped working.  It would not charge.  I sent it back and decided to give the product a second chance.  The same thing happened.  And before it died, after the first use, it held the charge for a shorter time, each time.  After fully charging it would die after cleaning maybe five brushes.  I'd rather use a brush cleaner that takes batteries.  I am going to get some rechargeable batteries and shop for a new cleaner not made by this company!!  I have had a similar makeup brush cleaner but I think the motor may be going on it and one of the rubber attachments is tearing and it eats batteries like crazy, so I decided to get this one.  Oh wow!  My other one had one speed and this has three.  The highest setting is crazy, in a good way.  It dries brushes so fast; less than 10 seconds easily.  The attachments handle all my face and eye brushes without a problem: even the ones with oddly shaped handles.  There's only one brush that it doesn't do well with, which is a large, thick facial fan brush.  The brush shampoo I used was ecotools shampoo.  You just need a drop in the water bowl.  If you add more you'll have the bowl overflowing in foam.  It also did all my brushes (a lot) without running out of power on me and it charges quickly via the USB port.  Yeah, no more going through all those batteries!

title: Not Recommended At All
text:
This iron is mediocre in performance and quality. The iron is very heavy to hold and has a semi long heat up time. This isn't an iron I'd honestly recommend and the price the company charges full price is outrageous for the quality of this iron.

My hair texture is 3C/4A and it is relaxer free. It requires high heats to lay flat. All of my irons is set to 450 degrees when in use. Before any flat ironing can begin I start with clean freshly shampooed and conditioned hair. I then blow dry, prestreching it so that it is easier to iron out. I use a blow out cream which also protects my hair from heat damage and a vented brush when blow drying. After I'll apply a argon oil serum and a frizz busting serum to my hair. These oils aide in getting my hair to lay flat with out any frizz.

Iron snagged my hair upon first use. I thought that maybe it was user error but it wasn't as the second time I ran the iron across a different section of hair it was snagged. I also had issues with my iron staying on. The placement of the on and off switch makes it very easy to turn this iron on and off while in use. The iron didn't even stay plugged in when I was using it. I was constantly giggling the cord to get it to turn back in. This iron doesn't glide down a section of hair well. It is very choppy thus leading to the snagged hair I spoke of earlier. The iron does swivel while in use making it easy to use. It goes up to 450 degrees but it's very difficult to maintain any temperature selected on this iron.

I don't recommend this iron simply due to the fact it snags at hair. It does work to smooth down hair but it doesn't work well as it cannot guide down smoothly. The only good thing about this iron is the fact it is very attractive to look at. I'm happy to say that I didn't pay full price as I received this for a promotional price. Had I paid full price I would have promptly returned this iron.

*** In exchange for my unbiased and honest review I received this iron for a promotional price.

text:
I wasn't really sure what dermaplaning involved before I ordered this product. I watched a couple of youtube clips and decided to give it a try. These tools are bladed scrapers that are used to gently scrape away dead skin and tiny hairs to give your face a fresh, clean, healthy look. In the videos I watched, there was a considerable amount of icky skin removed- literally piles of it! My experience has been much less dramatic. A whole face application resulted in just a tiny amount of "dust" to be removed. I applied a bit too much pressure at first and gave myself a little scratch, so do be cautious. These blades are sharp!
I feel that my skin does look brighter and more healthy. Those videos of dermaplaning likely feature models who had been tanning and not washing their faces so the dirt and oil really built up, and skin was ready to peel.
This product removes tiny "peach fuzz" hairs but I also tried it on a small patch of coarser leg hair that I had missed while shaving. It took it off neatly with no irritation.

title: Great for psoriasis
text:
I buy everything I review. To receive FIVE stars, a product must meet >90% of the manufacturer's claims. I don’t subtract because I don’ t like the color or appearance (too subjective and personal). I review form, function, ease of use, and construction quality. Please forgive typos: I’m an evidence-based scientist, NOT a typist. If you find my review helpful, please click "YES". This helps me improve future evaluations (which I do for free to help people make more informed decisions).

Their Claim: Controls the itch of psoriasis

My Verdict (details below): True for most people

As a physician, I know how itchy this condition can be on your scalp. I recommend coal tar shampoo to all my patients. Most dandruff shampoos use salicylic acid (which is aspirin) for the itching, which is NOT very good at stopping the itch. My wife has tried that with NO success. Coal tar is much better at controlling it and is the active ingredient in most topical creams for psoriasis of the skin. It's available in higher strengths by prescription, but this product at 2.5% is sufficient for most scalps.

Just use it 3x/week for adequate control. Let it sit in the scalp for five minutes, which means apply immediately upon entering the shower, then do your stuff. Just before exiting, wash it out. It's okay to leave some in the scalp; it won't hurt you. You may wish to use shampoo after, but this has shampoo/conditioner in it and in my experience, using other hair products is counterproductive.

This tingles, so you know it's working. The only problem? It's nearly impossible to find in stores, and is often sold out at Amazon. Other companies make similar products. Just type COAL TAR SHAMPOO in the search bar to find others. They all have 2.5-3% coal tar. You need a script for 5% for some idiotic reason. What, you're going to get addicted to the stuff and overdose? The FDA is a real killer sometimes.

If you itch, here's the product for you if you can find it. Denorex does a lousy job of marketing this product.

title: Not as good as supplied mount
text:
I had a Beltronics radar detector and had an Arkon mount that's similar to this one. I never had any problems with the Arkon mount but cannot say the same for this mount. After the Beltronics was stolen, I purchased a Cobra replacement and this mount to replace the Arkon windshield mount because it would not work with the Cobra, but this mount is nowhere near as good as the Arkon mount was. Specifically, the differences between this and the Arkon are two:

1. I have to reattach the mount to the windshield weekly because it eventually loses its hold and falls off.
2. I have to retighten the leveling screw often because it loosens with vibration and the detector doesn't stay level.

You're better off using the mount that comes with the detector than spending extra money for this one. There also may be others sold on Amazon that are better than this one.

title: Don’t Be Afraid, Just Give it a Try!
text:
At first, I was excited to get this micro-needling device, but then I started to look into micro needling. Dermatologists said to take Vitamin C 2 for weeks before use, and avoid sunlight; avoid makeup; your skin may peel afterward. So, I was afraid to try it out. It turns out, that using this is not painful at all. But when used on my forehead, it looks like it has more pores. So, I decided to start taking vitamins, and planned out when to try this out, but I avoided trying it out before times when I planned to expose it to sunlight, along with one week before my (wife’s) period.

Finally, I had the right time to try it out, and it had no obvious side effects...no pain, no skin flushing, no damage, no problems with sunlight or wearing makeup. Because this is a device made for home use, it is much more mild than professional devices. You may be able to use this every other day.

The device is light weight, and rechargeable, but comes with batteries, so you don’t have to charge before use; this makes it easy to bring on travel. I wish I had tried it much earlier.

The head is supposed to be replaced every three months at a current cost of $35. You are supposed to use a new cleaning pad before every use, and it came with 5 pads; the replacement skin prep pads are $35 for 30 pads which will last you two months, using it two to three times a week, which is what the manufacturer recommends. The minimum monthly cost of supplies is about $38 per month. You also need to have isopropyl (rubbing) alcohol to use with the provided spray bottle to sanitize the micro-needling head.

I would recommend using sun screen after use, to protect your skin.

After the first few uses, I haven’t seen much effect, but my husband thinks my face’s skin looks better.

title: Worth a try!
text: This kit is a great deal!  I've been a devoted user of Korean skin care products.  For a while, I have preferred, out of several brands and types of sheet mask, the Benton Bee and Snail sheet mask.  Fantastic product!!!!  Firms, smooths, soothes.  It's great.  However, that's not why I purchased this set.  I have combo skin that leans towards oily in the heat.  Super oily T-zone.  After doing a ton of research, I decided to give the Benton Aloe Gel moisturizer a try.  I'd also heard great things about this foam cleanser.  I'm really enjoying the cleanser so far.  I wet my hands and face, use only a pea sized amount, rub my hands together to create the foam (not a soapy lather, but a thick and creamy foam), and work over my face.  I do this after oil cleansing.  This does a great job of picking up any oil residue and dirt, while leaving my face soft and refreshed.  Never tight and dry, which is the sign of an awful cleanser.  The gel moisturizer is okay.  Just okay.  I don't get as oily as I did with lotion moisturizers, which is great.  However, I don't have that supple, smooth feel that I'm used to and prefer.  I've actually noticed flaking around my nose, which is something I never dealt with after moisturizing.  A pea sized amount covers my entire face, it leaves a slightly tacky finish until absorbed ( I always let each of my products absorb for around 90 seconds before applying the next step), and is completely colorless.  Will I repurchase?  No, but I do suggest that you give this a try if your research and needs point you this direction.  Everyone's skin care needs can vary on several levels.  There are universal musts for good skin health, like cleansing daily, moisturizing, and using a good sunscreen.  There a a ton a variations of those products, though.  Finding the right routine and products can be a trial and error process.  The main thing is to stick to it.  The results are worth it!

title: More silicone than argan oil. Actual ingredients not clearly listed.
text:
I bought this because the seller listed the main ingredients as argan oil and resvesterol, when in fact the product is full of silicon and demethicone is listed before argan oil. I can see why there are rave reviews from other users. This will give your hair a great TEMPORARY shine and silky soft feel but will end up robbing it of shine shortly and prevent your hair from absorbing moisture. You are not coating your hair with Arian oil but a rubber derivative. So th cuticle lays down short term but never gets the moisture that is causing the damage and frizz to begin with. I think someone who has science in their name would know that. Long term demethicone use will cause more drying and damage and is not good for your hair.

I had actually wanted to use this product on my face, not hair because of the resvesterol. But it has an extremely strong scent of sandalwood that is overpowering and I would never be able to use it on my face.

The bottle arrived in a box but leaked all over. I would have returned anyway because of the demethicone and smell. I bought pure cold pressed argan oil to use instead. It smells naturally like poo as all of them do but the smell dissipates in a few minutes.

I do think the seller should make its ingredients clear to prospective buyers and not just list the deceptive "main ingredients" omitting the ingredients that are listed first when the package actually arrives and therefore are really the main ingredients.

title: Beautiful But Need to Be Cautious When Using
text:
This is, for less than $10, a lovely comb.

Can function at a wedding or other event. However, the cons outweigh the beauty.

Given how delicate this is, there is NO storage box or bag. So, after use – where does one put it? That is an issue for me. Even a simple velvet type bag would be a good idea.

Second? The comb itself.

While absolutely stunning in design – function is a bit questionable because of the construction. The combs are “OPEN” design – thus loose hairs can weave in, particularly those with thick and curly hair. This makes removal or readjusting a bit difficult if not a tad uncomfortable.

This is also for thicker hair, not thin, and thus circles back to the issue I just presented.

While pretty, it isn’t something I am particularly pleased with. It isn’t something I would get for myself again. I also wouldn’t give it as a gift.

I like that it has very gentle ingredients and not some of the harsher ones that are found in most acne products. I am giving this 4 stars instead of 5 because I think it's misleading to claim there are only natural ingredients in here. Lauryl glucoside, decyl glucoside, and sodium cocoyl glutamate aren't truly 100% natural ingredients, although they are gentle and safe, and personally I would actually prefer a face wash with cleansing agents like this included rather than not. Some people might be might be sensitive to the essential oils in here but the majority of people most likely aren't, and again personally I'd SO much rather see things like chamomile extract, lavendar oil, and tea tree oil than a long list of chemicals!!! I'm super happy I found this for my son Peter and would most definitely order it again at the full price if it continues to work well for him. title: Arrived ahead of time which was super cool! I was incredibly excited to try this ...
text:
Arrived ahead of time which was super cool! I was incredibly excited to try this product out after seeing the buzzfeed video with them using it.
When I first opened the package, I was a bit shocked at how big of a bottle it was but how it seemed like barely half was full. When attempting to squeeze is out it was very much like trying to get the last of a product out of a container just as you're about to run out of it. All air, very little inside.
I did a small test area just to see if there was any kind of crazy reaction and I didn't have any issues. Goes on, peels off, wash away any little flakes that don't peel with it. However, when I went back to do a full mask I noticed that even though I had totally sealed it up tight, within about 20 minutes a massive amount of the product had leaked into the lid. I cleaned it up so it didn't solidify and placed the bottle upside down, so the lid was facing up instead.
The full mask itself went on nice and easy, just like the test. When I peeled it off, I did notice my skin felt fresher but it didn't really pull anything out. I checked the peeled off mask itself and while it had plenty of little itty bitty hairs from my face, nothing really noticeable. I checked out problem areas in the mirror and they looked basically the same, maybe with some blackheads and things closer to the surface and drawn up so they could be removed. The effect was minimal though and pretty disappointing.
I'll finish it off since there isn't much left and there is no point in not using it, but I won't be buying any more after this.

title: Cute with a couple issues
text:
This wig looks really cute, and I was able to get it to mostly blend with my natural gray hair around my face and with my widow's peak, which is pretty hard to blend in with a lot of wigs. I don't like to use any kind of glue or tape, so I depend on a wig grip and bobby pins to hold everything in place. This fit my head pretty well, and I have an average size head, but I think slightly larger heads would fit too. I'm not sure it would do too well if you have really long and thick hair, as it might take up too much space in the cap. When I had it on, I didn't notice the tracks, but when it was off I thought they were pretty noticable, and I was a little worried. Also you know how on some wigs, they add those short annoying hairs that inevitably end up poking through the longer ones and looking weird? Yep, I noticed the hair towards the back of the cap does that. Coincidentally, that's the place where the tracks are most visible as well.
The thing I like about it, is the actual hair, and the color, the texture, and the ability to flip it from side to side (even though it's parted in the middle. The style of it is most like my natural hair of any wig that I've purchased so far. I did add some dry shampoo. The color looks really awesome indoors. Outside in the daylight, it is a little much. It looks pretty white outdoors, but has a nice silvery-gray color indoors. So there are some negatives, but I could see wearing this as a daily wear wig. It didn't tangle too badly after a full day of wear... even with me running my fingers through it and flipping it like I do. I was easily able to tidy it up by finger combing at the end of the day. I wish the back side was slightly longer because the front that frames your face is longer and the waves in the back can look a little shaggy compared to the slightly curlier waves in the front. Overall, it's still cute, but I think the price is too much for this short wig. It should be closer to the $20 range. I'd love to own a 22-24" version of this in the same color or even a slightly darker gray or gray mix.

title: calms my skin, redness reduction with my rosacea, lightweight and hydrating
text:
I have tried several Easydew products, and they have all been great for my skin. I always want to touch my skin in awe, and have to remind myself to keep hands away. I am pleased with this Easydew EX Repair Control Renewal Intensive Moisture; it has been good for my mid 40s, dry, clear, semi sensitive skin that has type 1 rosacea (redness, visible veins- "telangiectasias").

It has ingredients to help repair skin, to build and maintain skin barrier, to help brighten skin, to calm the skin, to hydrate the skin. My skin is always well moisturized, feels dewy and supple, and never ever as a problem with being irritated. I like how it feels when I first put it on, and I like how my skin looks and feels come morning after having put it on the night before.

I like it for day time or night time use. It is surprisingly hydrating. Works well under my sunscreens. Works well over other serums. While I prefer a heavier cream at night, this is instantly moisturizing enough that I don't need to add anything else on top. Perhaps once the extra dry cold weather comes in, then I will add something on top. However, when paired with their hydra toner, it may be enough no matter the humidity.

It has a light fragrance (has fragrance as an added ingredient, for those who refrain). Not great but not bad. Fortunately it is light and doesn't linger.

Any alcohols used in this are fatty acid alcohols and are highly beneficial to the skin, especially dry skin.

Using medical grade EGF, it contains 10ppm of EGF, which means that it contains the maximum amount of EGF allowed for a cosmetic product to give you maximum results.

title: Upgrading from a T900
text:
Ok, here's my summary review of this trimmer.

I've had a T900 trimmer for a few years now and wanted to upgrade to a new and hopefully better trimmer. I've had it now for two weeks and here's what I think...

* The vacuum is great, period. When shaving with my Norelco T900, the shavings would fly all over the place --- in the sink, behind the faucet, in between the handles of the faucet, and on the floor. With the vacuum set on low, I barely see any clippings now! Now, my wife doesn't get mad any more!

* The height adjustment can be easily set, and unlike other reviews mention, I haven't accidentally changed the setting without knowing.

* The clipper works great and easily cuts/trims without any effort. This is an upgrade from my T900.

* Battery holds its charge pretty well. You can use it with a power cord also when the battery is low.

* The smaller trimmer is a now a separate attachment. My T900 has it attached to the trimmer, and it can be popped up or down when needed. To me, this is a downgrade as it is not as convenient.

* The parts seem somewhat delicate. I try to be careful as to not cause damage.

Overall, the price is good, it works well, and I'm glad I purchased it, and would recommend it to all.

title: Excellent concealer; just beware that when they say 'light', they mean LIGHT!
text:
I had a small bruise on my face from a cosmetic procedure, and it was driving me crazy that none of my concealers or foundations would cover it. Several friends had gotten the Boo-Boo concealer in a beauty box, and highly recommended it, so I grabbed it when I saw Amazon had it on sale.

I'm very fair, so I got the light version. Ummm, I guess I'm not as fair as I thought; they aren't kidding when they say 'fair'! This is Caspar white!

No matter. I mixed a bit of foundation in a more human shade in with the Boo-Boo, and my bruise was history (or at least until I washed my makeup off.) Very nice cover-up, no creasing, no caking, and it didn't move all day. The only issue I had, aside from how light the lightest shade was, is that it did such a good job of covering up the bruise it made the surrounding skin look naked (this is a VERY full coverage item.) Just be aware of that when you buy it.

And take them at their word for the color! I'm probably somewhere between light and medium in the Boo-Boo universe. You can always add a drop or two of your foundation to make the color more your shade.

title: lightweight, natural coverage, dewy, has goodly amount of sunscreen
text:
#21 light neutral beige, and it is a pretty good match to my fair, cool skin.

My skin: fair, dry, mid 40s, pink cheeks from Rosacea (visible veins, zero acne). I find that this has light natural coverage using a foundation brush. It tones down my redness with ease. It can be built up, especially if allowed to semi dry between applications. I really like that it has SPF (PA++++) 50. I always use sunscreen, so adding this on top of my sunscreen base is just added protection. Also perfect for reapplication & touch ups through day.

I also find that it is hydrating on my dry skin. Has a dewy finish. My natural skin comes through but looks better- more spruced up and put together looking. I do notice that the finish depends on what I use before hand. When I have used this on bare skin, it has a more mattifying appearance. When I use on top of my moisturizer and/or moisturizing sunscreen, then it has a more dewy radiant look. I prefer the latter.

Seems to stay in place. I applied some to my forearm, and it is still in place a couple hours later. I have taken my finger to try to wipe it off, and it is still there.

4 stars. I prefer it for light coverage. When it is built up, it seems to take on a grayish cast on me.

title: Great Idea, Needs Some Fine Tuning
text:
I own a foot filer (Amope-style) already and was intrigued by an electric nail filer. The product came well-packaged and with some toe seperators, which was a nice bonus. I also appreciated that it comes in a plastic, TSA-type storage pouch.

As for the product itself, there is still some work to do before it's a great product. Firstly, the fact that they do not offer refills yet is a huge deterrent. I've only used mine a few times and the heads are still functioning adequately, but soon I'm sure they won't (particularly the filer) and then it will be useless until they offer refill file heads.

Secondly, the file head itself could be of better quality, in terms of filing power. The buff and shine ones are pretty good, but not amazing, as it still takes a little longer than I'd expect to get great results.

Finally, because everything just work "okay", the end result is perfectly fine. Fine is not bad, but I can achieve a better, more fine tuned result with a quality multi-way filing block in only slightly more time. Changing the file heads vs using 1 block for my hands, it's a no brainer I'm better off just using the block. I have found the buff & shine heads useful on my toes, though, for a quick shine boost when I'm in-between polish and letting my toenails breathe. For my toes, the speed of the machine is a little helpful to be bent over lslghtly less long.

All in all it is a pretty okay little device, but for the price it's not quite "ready for prime time". I can only see this being beneficial to those with hand problems, such as carpal tunnel, arthritis, etc, because then not having to grip a block and make a repeated motion for so long would be helpful.

I did receive a discount on my purchase, but my review is honest & unbiased.

It really did neither for me. The only benefit I found for this tool was that it helped my hair look more 'relaxed' the day I washed it (if I'm not careful, it can look on the dry side).

I don't know if it is the thickness of my hair, the length of my hair or just the fact that I've almost mastered my hair maintenance but sadly this Brush Styler does not work for me (I've been trying it for a few weeks now).

Side note, I showed this tool to my stylist and he said it is a knockoff of a $300 Dyson version.

title: Something doesn't have to be expensive in order to be effective
text:
I'm in my early 60s, with slight rosacea under my eyes and a couple of red spidery veins around my nose. My spouse is on blood thinners, and bruises easily.
The small amount I show on my hand is the amount I need for my rosacea and around my nose. Not very much at all. It did not happen overnight but it did calm the rosacea down, and while they have not all disappeared, the tiniest of the tiny red lines are gone. Gone!
This cream has also helped those pesky bruises disappear more quickly.

The product contains all of the wonderful herbal and botanical ingredients well-known for healing skin, such as arnica Montana flower, green tea, and chamomile extracts.
The flip cap opens easily, just in case you have any hand difficulties and are curious about that. You need to unscrew the flip cap and remove the safety seal, then screw the cap back on. I can't say this enough, I love a product with a safety seal!
I even like the packaging. Various plants and flowers on a celadon background.

title: Great smell and great lather, not so sure about the ingredients.
text:
This body wash not only smells great but provides a thick silky lather. I generally don't enjoy using foaming body washes because they don't foam up enough to get a good lather going so I have to use more of it than I want to; that is not a problem when using this! Two squirts of foam and I can really work up a respectable lather all while basking in the wonderful scent of rosemary and water mint!

With that being said, I don't think I'll be purchasing this after using my current bottle just because the ingredients are VERY questionable. I'm very conscientious about what I put on and into my body and I try to stay as natural as possible. There are some very questionable ingredients in this body wash you should watch out for including butane, isopropyl palmitate, propane, sodium hydroxide, and benzyl alcohol, all of which I'd rather not have going on my skin and into my body. I understand that isopropyl palmitate is what causes that rich lather I spoke so highly about earlier but be aware it can problematic for some people. I'm also not sure what the purpose of butane and propane is in this product...maybe for aerosolization purposes? If that's the case I'd much rather see a pump used on this product to create and propel the foam like some other foaming washes.

title: Great Razor, But doesn't last...
text:
I bought this for my husband just under a year ago (and might I add it was about $35 less back then too, how dare they increase the price for the same older product?) and he loved it. He used it to shave his beard everyday and had a close enough shave to make both myself and his Air Force career happy. The only problem is that the battery charger will not charge the battery any longer, and obviously he can't use it without the battery. The charger will not even register that the shaver is on there anymore and it has been well cared for. Such a shame. I can't find a replacement charger, so it looks like it's back to the old three blade disposable razor and cream for us. I can't afford to spend $100 for something that won't last even a year when $4 pack of disposables lasts him two months. Very dissapointed with the quality of this product.

Other than that, it's a great razor with smooth, clean results almost as close as a regular razor, but there is a slight difference and someone who has fast growth and/or a coarse beard may have to shave more often. The main advantage is that it is a lot quicker and can be used in or out of the shower. But if you want something that will last longer than 10 months, be wary of this product.

title: Easy to apply
text:
One of my favorite beauty YouTubers wears false lashes and I have always been so envious of how much they make her eyes pop. I have tried regular strip lashes before that you glue in and I can never seem to get them on or if I do it takes several attempts.

I saw the YouTuber try out some magnetic ones so I thought I would give them a shot. I didn't want to invest a ton of money in case they were a total flop.

I decided on these and glad I did. The case the come in is really cute and I like how there is a mirror inside.

At first I thought there were no instructions so I was like "what the heck". However once I pulled up the plastic insert to remove the magnetic eyeliner, I saw them underneath.

I do recommend doing your eye makeup as normal and if you wear black eyeliner, put that on first and then put a small amount of the magnetic liner on top of that. Let it dry and out them on. BAM! Lashes were easy to apply and I didn't feel like they would fall off. I do think they might be a little too wide for my eye because I could feel them quite a bit in my inner corner. I might try trimming them, but not sure yet.

text:
[[VIDEOID:e487d57bdd82c5405085efb372c8fecd]]

The power button should be pressed to start setting the temperature and then when the LCD stops flashing, it has reached that temperature. Then the power button has to be pressed again so that the light in the middle of the plate lights up.

The plates have some space between them and they are offset a bit from each other which is the biggest annoyance to me. I guess this is why it straightened my hair only so much. This is not a bad flat iron but it is not perfect either.

title: HUGE WARNING: It Contains DMDM Hydantoin
text:
It contains DMDM Hydantoin. This is a cancer causing ingredient. I encourage you to read about DMDM Hydantoin. It is basically an unnecessary ingredient, which you will find in some shampoos, conditioners, body wash, lotions and other cosmetics. It is added as preservative (as if you need to preserve lotions/creams). It's not necessary to add to cosmetics; hence, not all brands use it. This ingredient turns into FORMALDEHYDE in liquids, which is classified as "known human carcinogen" by the IARC (International Agency for Research on Cancer).
I always check for this ingredient before I buy any cosmetics. Had I known it is used in this facial cream, I wouldn't have bought it. So the cream came out of the shipping package and went right into my trash. This was a waste of money.

title: Desktop Pro 2019 works great; upgrading an existing payroll subscription is awful
text:
Desktop Pro 2019 upgraded smoothly and easily with absolutely no issues. I began by backing up my QuickBooks desktop Pro 2018, and then began the installation process. It went smoothly and quickly and didn't take very long. I used the express installation which was recommended, and the whole thing was very easily done, retaining all of my previous settings and information.

The part that was awful was that I have an existing payroll subscription and had to call into tech-support to upgrade that portion of things. Luckily I was aware of this so when simply entering the information into QuickBooks didn't work, I knew that I was in for a phone call. About 45 minutes later of being on hold and trying to be up sold on QuickBooks online by an Indian tech-support person (hey guys, I just got desktop Pro 2019 upgraded, please don't sell me on QuickBooks online), I was good to go.

I think it's absolutely offensive that after you've purchased a software product like this they make you call in as a matter of course to activate. Anybody using this product is either being paid by the hour or runs a business and does not have that kind of spare time to sit around wasting on a process that should be 30 seconds of data entry.

I have multiple employees and so end up paying an additional 4 to 8 dollars per month for the subscription to add additional employees. It's another two dollars a month per employee after the first one. Also, be aware that the setting is set to subscribe you to an annual payroll subscription, which if done through QuickBooks will cost you about $420. Purchasing the new upgrade of desktop Pro 2019 with the payroll for a year costs less than that, so being automatically billed such a high amount for just the payroll is offensive and ridiculous.

I would really like QuickBooks as a company to reconsider how they deal with their payroll subscriptions and activation of payroll that has already been purchased, because this is a huge problem that is been garnering them poor reviews and lots of bad press for some time. I personally have considered many times changing to a more congenial company just to avoid this particular dance every single year. Do I pay $420 to avoid being on the phone for 45 minutes with somebody from India who act like I've done something terribly wrong by purchasing my payroll upgrade on Amazon along with the software upgrade? Or do I do as I have done most years and purchase the yearly upgrade that comes with the enhanced payroll.

As an FYI, the enhanced payroll really does make it very easy to run your quarterly reports and do your e-filing. I did it myself for many years, but now hand the file back and forth to my bookkeeper via email as a portable file.

I looked up DIPEPTIDE-3 AMINOHEXANOATE on DuckDuckGo & I guess it's a new skin ingredient. It might be why it & ACETYL ETHYLHEXYLGLYCERIN are not on EWG as they haven't been evaluated for safety. I really don't know though, it's just speculation on my part. As for safety, who knows? I rely on EWG to let me know. This is frustrating.

I've used this several evenings as a night cream & I like it, but I don't love it. I heat my home exclusively with a wood stove. Even running humidifiers & essential oil diffusers 24/7, the air is painfully dry. So far this cream seems pretty good on my middle aged skin. The funny thing is, out of all the various brands I've tried on my face, a little known handmade brand has by far served me best. It's a brand called Eruzile or Progress in Health. They have two names. I don't know why. It's really annoying. They are on Etsy & last I checked, have their own website but for some foolish reason, it seems to be more expensive to shop at their website. And to be clear, I am not affiliated with them, I'm just a long time customer. Another brand I like but it is ridiculously expensive, so I hardly ever buy it is Juice Beauty Stem Cellular. You can get it right here on amazon.

Okay, back to this brand. It is a light/thin feeling cream. Not greasy. It seems to absorb well. My skin does feel a tiny bit tight when I get up in the morning. I find a few spritz with rose water helps. This is packaged in a glass pot that you use your fingers to apply. A little plastic in the lid, so not Zero Waste, but not bad. It is not scented. It does have a smell as is normal because the ingredients will have their own smell to them, but when applying I don't notice the smell, so calling it unscented or fragrance free is more than reasonable. I only notice its smell if I'm practically sticking my nose in the pot & inhaling deeply.

For me, this isn't moisturizing enough for the dead of winter, but for spring & fall I expect it will serve me fine.

Overall, I would have rated this higher if not for the ingredient concerns.

title: Pleasant Enough, Not Much Scent, Need a Lot of Product To Shower
text:
Like all too many organic soaps, this example ends up being a bit too subtle and bland in scent and power to justify its price point. I love vetiver but even with a generous dollop on the loofah, I get only the faintest scent of that fragrance here. The hemp / vetiver combo smells pleasant in a mild sort of way, but this is not what I expected at the price point and given the product name. If I wanted "fragrance free", I'd buy it!

Besides the really mild non-especially vetiverish scent, NH IH&V body wash also needs a lot of soap to generate any lather, and even needs a lot just to get through a whole body wash. Lather may or may not be to your liking, but having to reload the loofah halfway through your shower is no one's idea of fun. At the rate of product usage, I would be amazed if this 13 oz bottle lasts me for more than 2-3 weeks.

Ultimately, even if you want to stay organic, there are better choices with more prominent scents and better product consumption rates. EOs Cedar & Mint for Men works well enough and can even be used as a shampoo and shave cream for the undemanding. My personal favorite semi-organic products are from Every Man Jack. Their cedar and sandalwood (two separate types there) body wash have great smells and give adequate lather and cleaning duration with roughly half the product needed to get similar effects from NH IH&V wash. (I call Every Man Jack semi-organic as I haven't bothered to assess all the ingredients on their label, but they have no parabens or SLS derivatives, so they pass my personal screening standard.) Both of these product lines are much cheaper than Nubian Heritage.

For vetiver lovers who want that scent in their bath ritual, Provence Sante makes a good vetiver beauty bar soap, and also a rather expensive vetiver body wash. which I have not tried due to its high cost. I have tried the beauty bar, and though not cheap, it does indeed give the user a noticeable vetiver smell when applied, which is always a good thing when buying a vetiver named product!

title: Made my bathroom smell good
text:
I specifically bought this brand because customer reviews said they didn't smell strongly. I have asthma and strong smells give me an asthma attack, but it's nice to have a smell-good in the shower. I've used bath bombs, but shower bombs had never occurred to me until I saw them on amazon. What a nice treat! They came nicely packed and none of the bombs were broken.

As soon as they came, I jumped in the shower to try one out. Let me just say that I take super looooong showers. Like until the hot water runs out lol. The bomb lasted my whole shower and didn't leave a trace when it was all gone. I couldn't even tell where it was, so it didn't mark or stain my shower at all.

Other reviewers complained about the scent being too weak, but I thought the strength of the scent was just right. If it were any stronger, I'd have had an asthma attack and that would've sucked. It was enough scent that I felt like I was treating myself, but not strong enough to bother my lungs. Even an hour later, I could still smell the scent of the shower bomb in the bathroom. Beats the heck out of the usual Hints de Kitty Litter lol

Anyway, I think these shower bombs are lovely and I have no problem recommending them to my friends. Even my asthmatic friends lol

title: Pleasant But Feels More Clarifying Than Hydrating To My Dry Skin-Has Risky Ingredient TEA
text:
I have dry, sensitive and mature (55+) skin and used this Reboncel Aqua Rich Foaming Cleanser daily for about a week. This cleanser has fragrance that smells relatively light to me, though fragrance is an ingredient that poses health risks. I generally avoid foaming face cleansers as they tend to make my skin overly dry, but this has a pleasing creaminess and initially made my skin feel good. It cleaned my skin well yet left it feeling refreshed, soft and comfortable after use.

After using this wash more than a few days in a row, it felt more clarifying (better for oily skin) than hydrating to my skin. While it didn’t strip my skin or make it visibly irritated, by the end of the week my skin just didn’t feel as comfortable as it did at first and it felt like my skin would end up too dry if I continued daily use. So I switched back to my creamy, hydrating cleansers, but felt this cleanser would still be good to use as needed as a clarifying cleanser.

However, while this wash has some good ingredients such as Centella Asiatica, Aloe Extract and Sodium Hyaluronate, this has controversial Triethanolamine (“TEA”) high on the ingredient list. It’s on my personal list of ingredients to avoid after reading many articles about it and seeing it on lists of risky chemical by many sources. Some sources say it’s safe in amounts we get thru cosmetics, but I’m concerned about the cumulative effect of risky chemicals.

TEA is a nitrosamine used to generate foam and adjust pH and is likely a hormone disrupter and irritant. But the bigger issue for me is that TEA gets absorbed through the skin and reacts with other chemicals to form the carcinogen NDEA. While less risky in rinse off products, it still poses more risk than I’m comfortable with. The problem is that I have no way to know if this cleanser or any product I’m using with it has chemicals that react with TEA.

So, for me, I find it best to avoid all products with TEA, especially since so many alternative products are available that don’t have it. I also dislike that this has so much Cocamidopropyl Betaine (second ingredient), which I generally avoid mostly due contamination concerns. Fragrance also poses health risks, though it’s a common ingredient I don’t avoid altogether (but I do try and minimize use). All things considered, this is just okay for me. 3 stars.

title: Excellent Epilator With A Price Premium for the Exfoliation Brush
text:
My wife has used a number of Braun Epilators over the years. Her most recent one was a Braun Series 7- 7181 [[ASIN:B0077PLNB6 Braun Series 7-7181 Silk Epil Wet & Dry Epilator 1 Count]] that proved to be a 5 star product. This Braun Se7921 is identical to the 7181 except that it comes with a brush head attachment for exfoliation. The price is about $20-30 dollars more than the 7181. So is the extra cost worth it? While the brush attachment does leave the skin on her legs looking more smooth, it really does not seem to be worth the price premium. The Se7921 is an excellent epilator that is worthy of 5 stars but the extra price for the Brush attachment brings this down to 4 stars. Save the money and get the 7181 instead.

*** Positive Points: ***

- Excellent Epilator that is worthy of 5 stars
- The 40 tweezer system and sonic massage really do lead to less painful epilation
- Built in light is a great additional
- Battery lasts a very long time between charges
- True Wet/Dry system
- Fast recharge time

*** Negative Points: ***

- Exfoliation brush is not worth the $20-30 premium over the 7181 model
- Epilation truly is more painful than shaving (though some say less than waxing)

title: Patience and a Little Luck Required!
text:
Before purchasing I had read the reviews and believed any issues were isolated and decided to purchase. Unfortunately I was only able to get 4 small tattoos out of the entire pack. Printing was relatively simple and the ink did not run or bleed out. I used photo quality and matte paper for my settings.

The issue is with the adhesive. For the tattoos to work you have to first print the item on the paper; then using the clear adhesive sheet cover the tattoo. All the clear sheet is used for is a transfer medium to move the adhesive onto the image. Where I ran into the problem was getting the adhesive film to release from the plastic sheet and remain on the image. Separating the image side and the clear plastic sheeting resulted in varied degrees of torn images, half the adhesive sticking, or the entire image sticking to the clear sheet

One tip would be to have someone hold down the adhesive/image side as you remove the clear backing. This has its own set of problems since the adhesive side sticks to your hand and gets stretched out or bubbles up.

In summary the idea is great but the adhesive needs to release from its medium easier to make the product more user friendly.

title: Paraben free, silicone free, sulfate free but not EWG verified
text:
I searched the EWG website for this company and product and in many spelling varieties and came up empty handed. If this product was indeed EWG verified, it would not only be on the website but it would have the EWG logo on the product plus it wouldn’t have linalool which is high on the allergy list.

Other than the linalool, this has decent ingredients. It is silicone free, paraben free, sulfate free and alcohol free. I would stay away from this product if you have malassezia (fungal) acne as olive and japonica may be triggers and/or pore clogging.

Like all natural bar shampoos, it won’t lather like traditional synthetic shampoos but it does clean. It takes some getting use too and a period of detoxing for your hair to get use to the change in chemicals if you are switching from synthetic to natural but it is worth it!

I would recommend this shampoo bar however I am rather concerned about the EWG verified claim.

text:
The item is not worth getting. The first 2-3 shaves were okay but after that, it takes foreverrrrrr to trim your head. The angled foils seem like a perk, but it really does not make everything easier or faster because in essence, the unit is really just separating the foils from each other, resulting in a slower shave. My traditional foil shaver (the ones with two sets of parallel foils) actually trimmed my head faster. But even then, that took a long time. I really only got this device because I wanted to avoid the bloody mess of shaving with a razor.

Here's the truth... there is really no device that can provide short-cuts or easier methods when it comes shaving your head bald. Nothing will ever beat the results of a traditional straight edge, or double edge razor. I would suggest investing some time to practice the art of shaving with a straight edge, single edge, or double edge razor. Over time, you will actually learn techniques to shave your head faster.

Or..... you can buy this unit, and spend more than an hour shaving your head. lol

I noticed the head is lighter, probably because you can rinse the head in water; therefore, most parts are plastic. I did not expect the rinse indicator to light up each time I use it.

The closeness setting has three modes. My previous model had 9. It did not matter; I use the closes setting all the time.

The head has more coverage; however, I think the multi opening is too complex (holds and line opening to cut closer). I find that parts of my chin/throat area has a few strands that are difficult to cut. I tried different angles and push even harder to the face and it does not work well. I had to use the trimmer to trim down the few.

I was tempted to return it since it has a 60 days money back. My old one is "DEAD" does not charge nor does it work with outlet (7 yrs). So I decided to push forward with this model. Maybe this one will last me just as long as the previous model.

Tom (NYC)

title: This is a gommage. It is meant to clump/form bits. Apply to dry face, massage, rinse. SOFTNESS!
text:
This is a gommage!!! The most gentle of all the physical exfoliation out there. If you haven't tried it, I highly recommend. I also highly recommend anything by Easydew. Good stuff! Know that this is meant to clump! Not supposed to have lather or creaminess. I had looked at the ingredients and some of the description and I suspected a gommage. The directions on box say to use on wet face and that it will lather. It doesn't. There is some clumps, but not as much as if it were used on a dry face, which is what is expected from a gommage. We want glorious clumps! For best results use on a clean dry face, not a wet face. I have tried it both ways, definitely use on dry face. Works but not as good on wet face.

So use a generous amount. Just pat it in all over. Let it sit a moment, then massage it in in gentle circular motion. As you do so, small clumps will form. This is a combination of product and grime and dead skin cells. Basically, a "gommage" is like an eraser on a pencil, and your skin is paper. The graphite marks are dirt and dead skin cells. The product once applied is like that eraser-- it is removing those "marks". What happens when you use an erase? You start to see balled up pieces of eraser mixed with the graphite/pencil marks. That is more or less what is happening here. Those balled up pieces are a mix of product, dirt, and cells. Rinse, and carry on with rest of your routine. It is a very gentle "peel". And quite effective. But less so when used on wet skin-- the ingredients just can't grab the gunk on face as well. I'm surprised there is such a discrepancy in instructions.

Instructions on container:
"How to use:
Apply desired amount of peeling gel and work into a rich lather by wet hands.
Gently cleanse by massaging thoroughly over face in circles, avoiding eye contour.
Rinse off with lukewarm water."

But the pictures clearly show what is expected--balled up bits/clumps.

SO, it it may be a matter of terminology/language. Easydew has some wonderful products, and this is a good product that I will use maybe 2x a week. I love how smooth my skin feels and that it doesnt feel parched afterward.

FULL INGREDIENTS
Water. Glycerin, Cellulose, Butylene Glycol, Dipropylene Glycol, Pentylene Glycol, 1,2-Hexanediol, Carbomer, Tromethamine, Caprylyl Glycol, Polysorbate 20, Betaine, Fragrance(Parfum), Disodium EDTA, Glycine Soja (Soybean) Seed Extract, Dipotassium Glycyrrhizate, Alcohol, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Hydrogenated Lecithin, Octanediol, Ethylhexylglycerin, Sodium Stearoyl Glutamate, Ceramide NP, Panthenol, Theanine, Milk Lipids, Sodium Ascorbyl Phosphate, Glutathione, sh-Oligopeptide-1, Capryloyl Salicylic Acid, Protease, Phenoxyethanol

title: Adheres well to file and fog is easily dealt with
text:
It's adhered to the tiles in my shower for months, and that's exactly what I wanted. It's easy to adjust so long as you are moving it when the tiles are dry. It's obviously not a genuine mirror as a heavy glass mirror would not work. I run a hot shower and I don't see the mirror getting foggy with any consistency. When it does, I find that I can swipe it with my hand and it's fine. I use a squeegee on my shower tile when I'm done and this has a low-enough profile that I can just lightly graze it while I'm squeegeeing the tile and not have much disruption.
Update: after about a year, I couldn't clean the haze that built up on it. Because it adheres directly to the wall, you have to do some occasional cleaning to keep mold at bay. text: My jar is almost empty and I can honestly evaluate it, according to my personal experience.  First of all, I love the smell....so light. title: Good but not what it appears to be
text: Ok, first of all, there is no such thing as a pure aloe vera gel with no additives.  Mainly because pure aloe vera extract isn't a gel, it's a thin liquid.  Therefore, despite the vendor's claims, a gelling agent like Carbomer or something else has been added - guarenteed. That aside, it is a very nice product.  Silky smooth, absorbs easily, no fragrances added (that I can detect).  But if you want real pure aloe vera, buy the freeze dried powder and add water.  It won't be a pure aloe vera 'gel', because there is no such thing, but it will be pure aloe vera extract.  But if you want an aloe vera gel, this is a good product.  Just don't be fooled by the label claiming that's all that's in it...

text:
I bought this for use in the shower as a body scrubber. Overall I was very disappointed.

Handle: There were burrs along both sides of the handle that made it very uncomfortable to hold. The length was great but the odd bend near the end essentially make the handle 3" shorter. The thickness of the brush made it easy to get into the cracks and crevices of the undercarriage - just protect your boys from the stiff bristles.

Overall I think this brush is better suited to toilet cleaning then body cleaning.

Lately though the BE makeup just hasn't been agreeing with my skin. I'm getting older and my skin is a bit more sensitive these days apparently. The one thing I never cared for with the BE makeup was their use of bismuth. Anything with bismuth it just makes my skin itch. I've been reading about the negatives of parabens too, and I decided I wanted to get away from that as much as I could.

BE doesn't have that but it does use bismuth, at least they did as of the last time I ordered a big kit. After perusing Amazon and reading ingredient lists I chose to try this kit. Mainly because of the fact that this makeup doesn't have any of that and reviews here already are mostly positive. Also because I liked the eye shadow colors in the trial kit. These are colors I'd use a lot so I didn't feel like I was wasting money on colors I'd never use just to get trials on everything else. The jars are about the size of a BE eyeshadow, a little smaller maybe. The brushes weren't bad but they are small. I put them in my purse kit. They're useful for that, but not for much else. But they're sturdy. They're not losing bristles and they seem fairly soft.

For the most part I like this makeup. It's about the same grind as the BE mineral makeup, feels a bit silkier to me actually. It smells about the same seems maybe a bit less noticeable, the smell. It blends as well, but doesn't feel quite as heavy. The finishing veil is good. I have combination skin and oil in my t-zone and it did a good job of keeping me matte all day. The foundation covers well and doesn't make my face itch at all. The bisque is okay but I don't think it's got quite the coverage of the BE bisque. I did have to use more of it to cover things the same way. I kind of wish this kit had come with sample jars of the colored concealers as I would have liked to have tried those combined with their bisque. I think it might have worked better with that combo. I'm admittedly at a point where a simple bisque concealer is probably not enough for me. I'm getting dark under eye areas and have some red I need to cover now and again.

Their "glow" mixed with the pink blush is my new blush. It's too much for me as a bronzer. I have very pale ivory skin and it just does not work for me all over. Just a little too much orange, a little too dark but it did work okay as blusher over the pink they send you. Combining both that gave me a blusher that worked well for me. The pink blush they give you is just way too light and frosted for me. It just doesn't show up at all. It was the one product in the kit I just did not care much for. I would definitely want a darker more mauve or cinnamon toned blush rather than this one. The pink on it's own is pretty useless. I had to combine the two or forget it. It didn't even look like I had any color on my cheeks.

The foundation colors are decent. Their Fair #1 is actually a near perfect match for me but I'd probably never use the Fair #2 unless it was combined with the Fair #1 maybe. My skin is never that dark, not even in Summer. But Fair #1 I must admit I like that one. It's hard for me to find a foundation that's fair enough that's not too yellow, but Fair #1 works well. Fair #2 is just a tad too dark and just a bit yellow for me.

Overall I'd have to say this kit was a positive experience except for a couple of colors being slightly off for me. I do plan on ordering a big kit but I'm also going to email them and ask if they might send a slightly darker blush and just the Fair #1 x2 instead since they're supposedly picking the cosmetics as they pack for you. Can't hurt to ask, and if they do then their "Fair" kit will work very well for me and I can see myself becoming a regular with this one. I did not expect this product to be as good as it is actually. It was a very pleasant surprise. I'm used to spending a lot more on the BE product. This is much less expensive and in some ways I think I actually like it better than BE so I probably won't be a BE customer much now that I've discovered this.

title: Best toothbrush made.
text:
A great alternative to the expensive plug in version. It has just as much power - maybe more. Reliability is about the same. You end up spending more for batteries, but the unit is much cheaper to begin with. I'm not sure how much electricity costs are for the plug in model. I subtract a star from both this one and the plug in model because of reliability. Over the years I have had almost everything go wrong from dead batteries to bad switches to corroded wires to just plain dead. The first one I had lasted 4 years. None have since. These units are not repairable. Expect them to last a year, maybe two.

This unit has the exact same mechanism as the expensive plug in model and uses the same replacement heads and is about the same size. The batteries come out the bottom and there is an O ring seal there. If moisture is allowed to enter it will mess up the battery compartment. If you stand it vertically after use rather than laying it down it will last much much longer because the water drains off it. I get a month, sometimes two, out of a set of batteries.

Do not buy the suggested newer model of this for $15. It's not the same as the others. It a motor driven thing with a huge head that is hard to use and doesn't do near as good of a job. It's small and cheap. Junk.

After that first week my skin adjusted. I really enjoy using this serum, I love that it doesn't go on greasy and it dries very fast and does not react with my foundation so I can wear it under my daily make up with no issue. I'm glad that I was able to try this product for free in exchange for my honest review of it.

I took a shower and used the product last night. The smell of it is something to get used to. Not bad, but not the best smelling thing in the world, lol. It's very smooth (and a tad greasy, but not in a gross way) and left my skin feeling very soft. Went to bed and (knowing not to expect any sudden changes) saw a dramatic reduction in dimpling in the morning! Maybe because I haven't really had cellulite until very recently, but I was very happy and surprised at how my skin looked and felt this morning. Even if it didn't help with cellulite (which it obviously did), I would use it for the simple fact of how awesome it makes my skin feel. This is better than Sally Hanson rasp, any sanding block, battery operated "diamond" rotary sander, pumice stone, sanding paddle... You get the idea. It has a variable speed which I have only used on high. It plugs into the wall so no worries about batteries and low power. The sanding pads are inexpensive and replaceable. I get at least a week of daily use out of each one. In the morning I gently sand my feet before I shower. I make sure to soap my feet good. Then I apply the Heel-Tastic just before I put on socks. title: Not too convinced about claims after use for a few days.
text:
Usually a serum is immediately effective at deep hydration, fine line and dryness management even if temporary. Usually the under eye area darkness, under eye wrinkles, puffiness, and crows feet are treated and diminished within minutes of first application and improves the look of make up in those areas as well. Perhaps over time the texture of the skin improves with continued use but can backslide if product use is discontinued.

I have not seen much improvement, immediate or over the few days with use twice daily while using this product, unfortunately. Also, I'm not sure when we are supposed to use this product. Perhaps over night? The reason why I mention this is that the product doesn't absorb into the skin cleanly, but rather is tacky to the touch and feels heavy. I didn't notice any fragrance, but I make candles and am probably nose blind at the moment. The product feels like a watery jelly, because it is mostly water and aloe gel. It does have gold flecks in it and they seem to break up and disappear when on the skin, massaged. I haven't seen any help for fine lines or skin texture. This is a photo taken right now. Un-retouched The left side of the photo is the 24k serum side, after three days and after recent application. The right side is immediate results of another product I use applied within a half hour of the photo. It works so fast, even I couldn't believe the photo. The lines on the other side are pretty bad actually, which means I've back slid over the last few days and have more trouble. I've been using the 24K serum on half of my face, the right side of my face only. As to the right side of the photo and left side of my face, I'm not pulling on it or doing anything to make the skin look better, less wrinkled or tighter, I just put the serum on and wrote for a bit and then took the photo to complete this review. The right side serum is from a farmer's market made by a local person, Julia's. This roll on was only 15 dollars and I've been using it for under eye area on days when I wear makeup, for a few months. I felt I should offer a photo, although not a great photo and it's not flattering at all. I'll continue to try it, but at my age I need all the help I can get and don't want to backslide.

title: sharp, long plade, short handle, slices hair off easily
text:
WOW!! These are good. They are very similar in style to all the other dermaplaning razors out there, but they are longer than any I have used. The blade is just a hair under 2". Pun intended. One of the popular blades among beauty conscious people (pictured) is around 1.5". Many are 1" or less. SO, keep this in mind for where you want to use this and if you are comfortable with that length of blade. Otherwise it is all very similar.

I like that this 5 pack is contained within a box. Many are on a flat piece of cardboard with molded plastic around them. Makes it too easy to lose one, misplace one.. they just fall out of package when opened. This box will nicely store the remainder. I won't lose these among my other beauty goodies.

I have no idea what it says on the box. The sticker on the box says Made in China. The box says, Made in Japan. I can't read anything else.

Handle is short- I think adds to precision of use. The longer blade makes it harder to get the eyebrow area. For that, I would go with a smaller, angled razor. For larger areas of face (or other body areas), this large blade is nice. As with any blade, BE CAREFUL. And don't over use it- a dull blade can be as dangerous and damaging as a sharp blade.

The blade is indeed sharp. I usually use a regular razor (like for shaving legs) to shave my face. I have pale skin and dark hair, so I have always preferred to just shave off my hair. No, it doesn't grow back thicker or darker. But it sure makes the face nice and smooth- great for make up looking good, for skin care setting in nicely, for exfoliation- for overall health of skin. A leg razor is fine, less likely to cut.. but a straight razor provides an extra close shave (if careful). I love these for taking care of upper lip area, and for eyebrow area.. but is taking some getting used to since it is a longer blade than others I use.

This shaver lasts much longer on a charge and, if the spec is to be believed, can last 90 minutes on continuous use. That's incredible and means you'll likely never need to charge it away from home.  One less charger to carry and one fewer thing to worry about while packing are good things!  And if it does run out on you, there's a quick charge feature that let's you get one shave in with only a min. or two charge. Impressive. Lastly, like many electrics, it's a wet/dry shaver so for those needing that feature it's as versatile as competitive brands.  I doubt that any electric razor really will shave as close as a (good) blade and no product is every going to please everyone but I'm impressed that I don't see any reviews below three stars. title: Peppermint and coffee scrub that I like the smell and on some of my dry areas
text:
Rub a Dub Scrub! A delightful shower treat. This organic body polish is nicely scented with coffee and peppermint. Typically I make my own from organic ingredients, so I am picky and compare. I was very happy with the Alexa coffee body scrub. The package is a nice size at 8 oz. It also would make a wonderful gift if you are needing a quality pampering for someone.

You can just get your feet wet if you are doing a pedicure with it. All you have to do is get your body wet, or the particular area you are using it on. I put a smidgen between my fingers and only use it on key body dry areas. If you want to slather it all over that is ok too! I just like to make it last because it is nice on my skin. I have several dry eczema areas and dry areas on my feet.

I have used other brands and had to transfer it into another container of my own, I love that with this one I didn't have to! It is not to cumbersome in the shower, the package is easy to open and close. The Alexa brand is made in the USA with organic all natural moisturizers. My skin is soft silky smooth with the combination of the great ingredients of dead sea salt, organic oils, organic coffee and organic shea butter. I used the scrub on my hands, feet, upper arms and legs. The scrub doesn't leave behind an oily residue, just a nice soft skin feeling. It's great for light exfoliating. Scrub, rub and rinse! I received this product at a discount in return for a review and my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: Excellent electric toothbrush for sensitive teeth and gums
text:
I really put a lot of effort into taking care of my teeth and gums but for some reason I've always been plagued by sensitive teeth and due to bruxism have receding gums that are also sensitive. My dentist is excellent and has always told me that since I take such good care manually the effect would always be better and more thorough than with an electric toothbrush. Till the Oral B Smartseries 4000 Professional Care electric brush that is. When I saw this brush I showed all the info on it to my dentist and he told me I should take a try with this one.

And thank God I did. Other electric toothbrushes I have used were painful for me and not effective. This one is so easy to maneuver for deep and thourough cleaning. Whether using the deep clean mode or the one for sensitive teeth both have improved my oral hygiene greatly. I was very impressed that the deep clean mode wasn't too intense. My dentist is thrilled. My gums have come back to new life a healthy pink and are no longer sensitive. And my teeth? The plaque removal here is superb and my sensitive teeth have improved more with this brush than with any desensitizing paste I have used. My dentist said it is because the brush is doing what it needs to do and not stressing the teeth by using a faster speed that is just not necessary.

Everything else about this electric toothbrush I found to be very user friendly as well. Both my dentist and I are very impressed with this 4000 Professional care product. I give it my highest recommendation and for people with sensitive teeth and gums finding a product that really works and helps means a lot.
