title: 50/50 Chance you get a good bottle
text:
Doesn't matter where you buy them, who you buy from, etc. There is a 50% chance you get a good bottle of polish and a 50% chance you get a bad one. I have 3 bottles from 3 different places, 3 different colors (blue white and black) and the blue one is good, the white one is meh, and the black one is completely useless. The white and black have bent brushes, and the white polish is a bit dried out but not the worst, kind of reminds me of using white-out before they changed the formula and it got all watery and they changed to a sponge applicator from a brush. The black one is awful - it's literally just clumps of dried out polish with some occasional damp spots. The blue one is okay, the polish is alright, but I wouldn't recommend using the brushes that came with these but buying a separate skinny brush for line work or whatever it is you want to do.

I should mention I have been using them to fix an enameled piece of jewelry as opposed to doing nails, as that's what the jeweler recommended (nobody local repairs enamel resin and buying enamel is very expensive and you end up with a ton leftover), so a jeweler I trust recommended nail polish with a good resin sealant and that's what I've been doing. Initially I had used an X-Acto knife to cut painter's tape around the shapes of different colors and metal but switched to this pink-colored liquid latex paint I saw on a youtube video for nail designs and it's much easier.

title: Love! Easy, affordable, effective.
text:
This is, I think, my third order of Rio De Keratin. I'm able to get 3-4 treatments out of each kit with my hair ranging from super short to just below my shoulders. I usually still iron my hair, but it stays flat, even in Alabama's subtropical humidity. Otherwise, it doesn't matter what I do: by the time I walk from my house to the car, my hair is frizztastic. But with a keratin treatment, I can even just blow dry my hair and it look fantastic. This saves so much more time and it makes styling last for days. I also hike and get sweaty and my hair still looks great after it dries. Once, after a day of kayaking, I rode in the back of a friend's truck back to the marina, and my hair still looked terrific. This of all things has given me the hair I've dreamed of. And at $10-$15 per treatment, this price is right.

Of course, it does smell terrible. And the fumes can sting your eyes, both as you apply it to your hair and as you iron it out. I like to open the back door and aim a cyclonic fan into the bathroom while I use this stuff so I don't choke on the fumes.

It also comes with a small bag, but I'm slightly worried about putting the straightener in the bag if it's even slightly warm, as it's the type of material that could melt easily.

title: Works great if you want a frizzy mess
text:
I should have listened to the negative reviews. I just figured the people that didn't like this curling iron didn't know what they were doing, didn't follow the directions, etc. and that was why they didn't get the results they desired. After all, if you look at all the videos on youtube, it looks so easy to get beautiful spiral curls. I'm not the most skilled at styling my hair, but I can do a pretty decent job with a blow dryer, hot rollers or a regular curling iron, so I figured I'd be able to manage this Bed Head curler just fine with a little practice.

Boy, was I wrong! Despite following all the instructions on various youtube videos, all I got was a frizzy mess. Remember that episode of Friends where Monica went on vacation and there was so much humidity that her hair kept getting bigger and frizzier? That's what my hair ended up looking like (and my hair is naturally stick straight). Also, the glove did very little to protect against the heat - after just a couple seconds, it was too hot for me to touch the curling iron.

I will go back to using a regular curling iron or hot rollers when I want to add a little curl. I'm sorry I wasted my money on this thing.

title: Great for orthopedic use - see UPDATE
text:
These work very well for my application. My orthopedic surgeon recommended I buy shoes with heels to counter a problem I have flexing my foot upwards at the front. This makes it painful walking uphill and on steep hills I have to go up on tiptoe. Although many shoes have 'heels', they do not raise the heel much above the toe of the shoe. By attaching these to a standard pair of hiking shoes I am now able to walk much easier and without any pain.

They are advertised as size 14 (US) but they are actually slightly small on my size 13 shoes. Overall, they measure 3.4" wide, 3.5" long and give a lift of 3/4". They don't exactly conform to the shape of my shoe heel, but they work fine. They are easily attached using the nails provided and Shoe Goo, or similar adhesive. I used two G-clamps to hold them while the glue set. Several pairs of these heels have now stayed firmly attached and outlasted the shoes.

UPDATE (Sept 2021): Please be aware that the new supplier of these does not ship nails with them. The old supplier, Leather Care Supply used to ship a pack of the correct nails with the heels. The nails are hard to obtain elsewhere,

title: 99J, How to use as top piece

I have now managed to cover that awful seam, transformed it from stiff, flat & boring to full, natural-looking & silky with no seams showing anywhere.
I may order another one to color a little lighter to wear when my red shade fades. I will take a pic of what it first looks like. I have colored many hair pieces, sometimes lightening them first with a color remover like color zap. I also curl them to match my own hair. Will attach styled pics of front, top, back, & underneath. title: excellent sunscreen with skin loving ingredients, broad spectrum, great little container
text:
The "Drop the Bomb" BBOSONG Suns stick uses one of THEE best UVA/UVB sunscreen ingredients on the planet: "Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine"! Say that 5 times fast. Or once. lol. It is a broad spectrum, highly photo stable, chemical sunscreen. Chemical sunscreens mean that they absorb rays and disperse as heat before they can reach skin and do damage. The SPF rating of 50+ and PA++++ means that it offers the highest amount of protection that a sunscreen can offer.

Korean skin care, particularly sunscreens, can use super effective ingredients that products made in (or for) USA can not have because the governing bodies have not approved it. It is not because they are unsafe, but because there is a significant amount of bureaucracy involved. No new sunscreen ingredients have been approved in the USA in over 15 years, sad since there are so many wonderful innovations in the rest of the world. We lag greatly behind. Fortunately, we can still buy these products.

The other sunscreen used in this product is, Ethylhexyl Methoxycinnamate (Octinoxate)- a less stellar chemical sunscreen that has mixed thoughts on its efficacy, safety, and desirability. It protects only against UVB rays and breaks down when exposed to light (10% per 30-40 minutes). However, when combined with another broad spectrum sunscreen, it compliments it very well.

The third sunscreen component is, Octocrylene. Screens out the UVB and somewhat in the UVA II range. It is quite photostable (loses 10% of SPF protection in 95 mins) and is often used to stabilize other photo-unstable UV-filters (octinoxate) It is also often used to improve the water resistance of the products.

As for all the other ingredients- primarily stabilizers, viscosity controlling ingredients, hardeners-- basically all ingredients that make it a STICK than can glide onto the skin. It is formulated to melt into the skin on contact, and yet absorb thoroughly. Basically, you won't even know it is there.

And like so many other Korean skin care items, there are ingredients that go above and beyond the basic sunscreen-- included are skin loving ingredients (emollients, skin conditioners, soothers) such as Japanese knotweed, water lily, gotu kola (centella asiatica), camellia japonica, Lespedeza Capitata Extract (anti inflammatory), scutellaria (ie scullcap/mint), green tea, licorice, rosemary, chamomile

Has a super mild scent- clean, fresh almost like a deodorant, but subtle.

Happens to be a in a container that reminds me of deodorant. Super small, cute. Stick in a pocket or purse. I happen to love using it on my hands. I am in my 40s, and while I have been using SPF most of my life on my face, I figured it was high time to remember to put some on my hands. I like keeping this in my purse or my car, and applying it when I go to drive. That seems to be the time that my hands are most consistently exposed to the sun. Figure, hands on the steering wheel and in front of a big window. So yeh, this is perfect for that.

I have no problem using this on my face. Doesn't grab skin when used over a moisturizer. If need be can be applied/emulsified in palms then patted on. I prefer it as my "reapply" SPF rather than my first application product (I am used to a cream style). When I do apply it to my face, I always run it over my lips. It is very silky, doesnt have a sunscreen flavor or feel, and it is adding much needed hydration and protection from the sun.

Again, I am in my 40s.. clear fair skin but with Rosacea (non acne- just redness and visible veins). Leans dry. Loves Korean skin care.

This is so clear, so clean feeling, and so incredibly light that I wish I could show you how it doesn't even feel like anything is on. Not greasy, not even dewy. My skin feels bare.

If I have any complaints, it is the use of fragrance. While it smells nice and doesn't really linger.. it would not make a top choice for use on my face. I do however like it for everywhere else and rather enjoy the light scent before it dissipates fully.

Even so, it is a really good product, so far. If I experience anything else, I will be back to say so.

For all the other ingredients, the each rate 1-2 (very low in terms of hazard to self or environment) on EWG Skin Deep Database.

title: Best adhesive ever; worst mirror ever.
text:
I've had this hanging in my shower for nearly two years now, and I am *completely* sold on the adhesive. My shower wall is square tiles, and this overhangs one tile by an inch or two on each side. But it doesn't seem to matter, because it just sticks and stays there. Unlike suction-cup systems, this has NEVER fallen. It hasn't become brittle. It isn't nearly as limited in the places you can find to get it to stick. In short, it is perfect!!

Except for the mirror itself. The mirror is a very thin piece of clear plastic, with a reflective surface glued to the back. When it flexes, it distorts the reflection. But the largest problem is that it is almost impossible to clean. Unlike a glass mirror, the plastic is prey to terrible scratches. Pretty much any sort of scrubbing will scratch the plastic and reduce it to uselessness. The ability to get a replacement would be greatly appreciated, but alas it appears that buying a whole new mirror is your only option.

So, while this is quite honestly the best mirror I've ever used in my shower, I'm still looking for something else...

title: Sheer formula, builds well.
text: This is a nice Nautical gift set with 4 pretty polishes.  They are 13.5 ml each, and made in the U.S.A.  Initially I thought I would love Stay Nude the most, but it ended up being my least favorite of the set, only because it is pearl and streaks are unavoidable due to the type of finish it is.  All 4 have a shiny topcoat built into the formula.  The 3 cremes are all very sheer formulas, not super opaque.  The thickness of the formula for all of these is good.  If you like a sheer formula, where you can see your nail bed thru the polish, then these are your jam.  I did several manicures with each of them, and found that if I wanted a sheer look then 1 coat worked perfectly, otherwise 2 or 3 coats for full coverage and less peek thru of your natural nail and smile line.  I did 2 easy coats for each of my manicures.  The blue (Hypnosis) seemed to have the best coverage, and the formula for that was my favorite of the 4, it dried the fastest at 8 minutes to the touch.  They all go on easily, with a regular round brush (not flat) and they dry fairly well, in about 10-15 minutes each layer.  I did find that using my own quick drying topcoat that these wore much better, but from the manufacturer neither base nor top coat are required.  I did not get any staining from these, which I love.  The pink and white will both be really good polishes for doing either French tip or pond manicures when you just want a sheer base, where you do a layer, do art over it, then cover it again, and more art on that layer-it gives a layered effect that is fun to do.  The color palate is a fun one, with lots of options for artwork.  These are not quick drying-more of the typical 10 minutes per layer, and I expected them to be hardened on their own, without the help of a quick drying topcoat, but that was not the case with them.

title: Very small salt crystals, but smells good!
text:
The best way to describe the scent of this exfoliating scrub is to say it smells like you just walked into a day spa. It's a truly lovely smell, light, fresh, salty, and luxurious. I've actually tried using it as a lotion instead because the fragrance is so nice, but it didn't really work out. It's very creamy, though, and when you put a dollop in your hand, it might seem like there aren't any salt crystals in it, because the cream is thick like lotion.
There was quite a bit of settling in the packaging when I opened the jar, and since I ended up using quite a bit in the shower, I don't think it'll last very long--perhaps a month. The salt crystals are very small, and when I tried to vigorously scrub, it washed away before I could properly exfoliate.
How I recommend using it, in order to get the best use out of the Himalayan salt is to wet your leg before you step unto the shower, so it's a little more than damp. Then take a dollop and scrub your leg, and when you're done with whatever appendages you wanted to exfoliate, hop in the shower and rinse it off. Somehow, when my legs and arms were really drenched, the scrub just slid right off. Less moisture helped it adhere better. The smell really is great and refreshing, and once I've figured out how to use it, I've started enjoying it more.

title: Pretty good.
text:
I bought this to upgrade my lotion dispensing Norelco that's now 5 years old. The battery on it barely lasted one shave and it lived in its charging cradle except when drying.

Since I was so used to the old cradle and how it always was in it, I liked the little clock on this. But once I noticed it lasts < month the cradle is now a relic in my junk drawer! It seriously only needs about an hour to charge fully so there is not any need for the cradle. The tiny (not a huge brick that sticks in the wall) will fit inside the cradle or the razor.

When I first used my 9160XL I really irratated my skin, even being a long time Norelco user. But it went away in about a week. I still get red spots from irratation some times but heres my trick: wait until BEFORE you shower because soap strips all the oils off your face, making it hard to glide or try using a TINY amount of shaving cream, spread so thin you can barely notice it and then go over with a splash of water. If you use alot the Norelco could choke on all the extra cream and become less effective. I hardly notice any differences in irritation when using the <S N> dial (sensitive or normal skin)

The trimer is neat but I only use it to shave my unibrow when I am too lazy to actually pluck the hairs out. The trimer + the head array pop up with a flick of a finger. I was used to pulling open the head like my old Norelco but this is spring loaded. Some how when I was store drying it (the recommend to leave it wide open to air dry out the insides) the head came off. I was frightend! But it is designed to snap on and off easily.

The plastic head cover is working like it should. I just prefer my old head cover more because it was easier to tell which side is going on the top. But it is getting easier the top nub is alot smaller the my old one. The travel case is awesome, fits it like a glove and zippers up. Be sure to leave the cover on for double protection.

Be sure to look for a brush to clean the heads before you throw away the box. The packaging is so complex it took me a while to extract all of it's contents.

More cons:
- I don't like how the heads are unprotected during air drying... I wish the cover would fit while its opened.
- Orange? Bold color for something thats mainly blue, silver and gray.
- Maybe my drain needs draino but when washing out the chamber and heads alot of my hair gets stuck to the side of my sink, requiring splashing until it all goes. But it's kinda cool filling my sink the top then start draining and look up close at all tiny hairs it cuts.

I am been using this for 4 months now.

edit, now it's been 5 years and the battery still holds a pretty decent charge. Still working really well too. Only replaced the blades once so I'd say I got my monies worth.

title: Works with a little elbow grease, FAINT results
text:
You really have to work at this to make sure you get a result, and you must be careful that you got equal amounts of each solution on the cotton swab. I accidentally got too much of Solution B, and got a negative result on something I knew had nickel. Also, you have to really rub hard for 15+ seconds, and then you see a FAINT, faint pink on the cotton swab. It's very subtle.

It would have been helpful if the makers included something to use as a "positive control", something that contained nickel so you could see what a positive test looks like and know what you're looking for while testing unknown items. I highly suggest that users find their own positive control - find something you know has nickel, and test that to see the pink and know you're doing it right.

Also, this seems to release ammonia gas when the solutions are mixed, so use in a well-ventilated area, and don't put your face right over the swab or item being tested or you'll get a whiff of ammonia in your nose/eyes.

As it turns out, real surgical grade stainless steel does test NEGATIVE for nickel! (And I tried really, really hard to get a result on that one!) I was using this test kit to double-check my earring-making components to make sure there was no nickel content for making hypoallergenic earrings. Again, I HIGHLY recommend using a positive control (and perhaps a negative non-nickel control as well) to make sure your results are real and valid.

title: Sharp Shears for Healthy Looking Hair
text:
I learned some things when I was looking for hair cutting shears. Mostly that you can pay around $200 for the best ones,used by professionals,and,that you need very sharp scissors or shears to cut or trim hair.

I've been trimming and shaping my own hair for a long time and am usually happy with the results,considering too many times,when I would go to a salon to have it cut or shaped or trimmed,they did a job I was almost always disappointed with. I decided a long time ago,if someone was going to screw up my hair,it might as well be me. At least I have a good idea on when to stop cutting it and I actually care what the final result looks like.

I also have fine,wavy hair. Not the easiest to cut.

I have noticed,and maybe it was from using whatever scissors were around at the time,that sometimes the ends do look a bit frazzled;and in researching shears,I found out that unless the blades are very sharp,the ends can break,or result in split ends. I don't have split ends and never noticed them,except for a long,long time ago when I was a teenager;but,I have used these once to do some light trimming and shaping;with wavy hair you are always shaping,cutting with the wave and not cutting against the wave. And,these shears have produced a nice result. And I don't see the somewhat frazzled or lightningbolt effect at the ends of my hair,that I sometimes get.

I've used these just once,I only trim my hair to maintain healthy looking ends,and I did it a few weeks ago,and I like these and I'm glad I looked for something better than "any old scissors" that I have on hand.

title: So far I am pleased with this set, having sensitive skin, it works for me
text: First, this Beard Growth Kit, 10 In 1 Beard Kit For Men with Beard Oil, Beard Balm, Beard Conditioner set offers a nice number of items if you are considering a gift this holiday season (or any time). It’s a nice box, again, offers a good number of items for a gift, and is done nicely enough in box set up and presentation it would be well received. Second, the items in it are a good range of “quality” so I think it’ll be appreciated. What I am saying: the brush, comb, bag, scissors, and guard are decent, but not great quality. You can get better quality, but for working needs and for a gift, this is pretty good. But, for example the scissors feel a bit cheaper. But they will get use as long as they cut well enough. I’m not big into using a guard, but this one is like others I’ve had. The included bag is decent, but I’d never use it; if traveling or moving my stuff I’d use a toiletry bag. The brush is not as nice as others I have, but it’s useable and gets the job done. Same with the comb. That brings us to the shampoo, Conditioner, and oil. NOTE: I have extremely sensitive skin, so this review is based on my experience from that standpoint. I like a range of scents or items to keep my beard in good shape, but I have a far more difficult time finding things that work and are okay on my skin. I have only used these items once, but that’s all it takes to know. I come away happy - they all worked and NO reaction. I used the shampoo and conditioner in the shower today and they not only had a nice, light scent, but I was bale to let it sit on the beard for a few minutes each, having no issues with skin and liking the smell. The beard felt soft following and I liked how they worked overall. Next, the oil. I believe it is claimed to be used for “beard growth,” and maybe it’ll help with that. My beard is decent, but I do have spots that could use thickening, so again, I keep an eye open for options. However, there is no way to know if it’ll work for that for a few weeks if not months. So until then, it again did fine on my skin - not a single ounce of negative reaction. The sect is light, so it’s nice to smell, but one (my wife) has to get up close to smell it. I do like it that way, so it doesn’t bug my sinuses or overwhelm. In the end I’m very happy so far with this Beard Growth Kit, 10 In 1 Beard Kit For Men with Beard Oil, Beard Balm, Beard Conditioner set and happy I grabbed it. I’ll use it and if all stays well, would consider getting it again.

I was surprised because when I opened it I felt like there was no way it would work on my hair but it was so easy to use!

If your hair is damaged I would 1000% reccomend this to help keep your ends from looking fried.

It's as affordable as most traditional straighteners and works so much better!

Get it.

title: Packaging is a bit misleading
text:
It's tough to find actual lip oil for a reasonable price. First I got a tinted lip "oil" that ended up being a pretty much a lip gloss. Sticky and annoying (squeezy tubes ... why does ANYONE think those containers are acceptable for liquid/semi liquid lip products I'll never understand). Needless to say I was disappointed as that was NOT what I was looking for! And I'm not interested in buying high end stuff where the name and packaging makes up most of the price.

So I found this, it sounded perfect (though annoying that it's a 2-pack at $22). Well, it's a lip oil, not a gloss, which is great. But it has no flavor/fruit scent and no tint. The packaging makes you think it's red, but see pics, it's just plain ol refined oil. Given that castor oil (not pomegranate) is the first ingredient, it smells and tastes like castor oil. Not the most pleasant scent, but after you apply you don't really smell it.

I believe that it will condition my lips with time but to be honest, just buy a roller ball container, some cosmetic-grade oils and melt down a lip gloss/lipstick and mix it in and make your own. This wasn't worth $22.

title: Some tips
text:
I got this thing when I was working retail, a lot of long shifts standing stock still wih only a single 15 minute lunch break can kinda kill your feet especially when you're heavy. I got this thing to help me deal with the calluses and just oiverall roughness of my feet. By itself it does a great job but even using the black tip if you have feet like mine won't do you much good especially since that low grit means it tends to catch and stop itself due to thesafety feature built in to the device.

So some tips I found are:
Use this once or twice a week. It feels like it's made for that especially with the high grit white tip for fine filing and polishing

Use with a cheap dust mask and away from electronics. Trust me while most dust is dead skin as it is, this thing doesn't so much grind away deadskin and calluses as it vaporizes them. Nothing worse than having to dust a computer or going to check your phone and just realise the horror you've created.

Don't use pressure, the machine does the work for you and applying any pressure, especially witha black tip, will just flat out stop the machine.

And lastly and probably the most important, NEVER STOP MOVING. Even if it's a particurally rough spot or calluses, even if it's on low if you leave it in the same place too long you will give yourself a friction burn or, even worse, take of too much and leave your foot raw. Instead if you want to focus on the same area just rapidly tap the machine aagainst the problem area giving it a second or two to cool off in beteween. For the rest of the areas making sweepng, brushing, or lazy cricular motions work the best

text:
... The self cleaning feature is designed for lazy people. I like it because the cleaning fluid lubricates the blades. Refills are five a pop and supposed to last 30 days. Lets see 5x12=60 Thats a new shaver a year. Heres what I do...and not out of cheapness either, after every shave pop the screen off and give it and the blades one good blow, pop screen back on. Every other time, clean it.
Every 6th time charge it. By blowing every shave and cleaning every other....... you get 90 days out of a fluid refill, not 30.
The base detects how much [stuff] is in the fluid, and when it gets too much ,forces you to change cartridges or it will not work.(clean) To make your batteries last an extra year.. once a month let them run down completely, then charge. Theres a difference between being cheap and throwing money away. I just get to buy more toys. Aint that whats its about? Closest shave ever? Not really, but fuctional enough to be worth it. Overall> Nice shaver.

So back to this first try, my 3 day old hair was frizzy and after a few sprays it reduced that by 60-70%. The scent is light and my hair never felt heavy or looked oily. So after washing my hair I applied the product to damp hair. My hair looked very nice and never looked oily or felt heavy. It helped keep my wavy hair from getting frizzy all the way to my next wash day. This product is not as "green" as I would like but it is a good product that works well. title: Proven ingredients, but a poor value
text:
I’m not all that impressed with these products. Neither container lists the ingredients on the label, instead providing the ingredient list on a card that’s in the box. It shows that the cleaner is a 2% salicylic acid wash, which is a pretty tried and true formulation for treating acne. It is a low-lather, but still effective cleaner, but I didn’t experience any difference with this compared with other 2% salicylic cleaners that cost far less. It’s a fine cleaner, but way overpriced for such a tiny (0.51 oz) container.

The repairing night cream is a combination of retinol (0.05%), niacinamide (3%), and hyaluronic acid (2%). All are proven performers, but again, it’s quite overpriced considering how low of a percentage of retinol is in the formulation. It does a decent job of moisturizing and did not cause any skin irritation. I am a fan of retinol, but the concentration in this cream (0.05%) is well below what I usually use (either 0.1% or 0.5%).

While this product combo is on the right track, the value is just not there considering the amount in the container (one-half an ounce for each). While I would certainly recommend a salicylic acid wash and a retinol-based cream, there are many other options that provide these options at a far lower cost. Four stars for performance; 1 star for value; overall rating of 2.5 stars.

text:
I hate shaving. I have a beard for this reason, but you still have to do minimal shaving. I have used just about every razor under the sun, but recently I have had a lot of trouble with cuts on my neck. As a last resort, I decided to give a "power" razor a try, and I went with this one over the Fusion because replacement blades are much less expensive.

I was a little apprehensive about the power razor as I thought it might just be a source of faster cuts and nicks. However, I am happy to report that not only did I not cut myself, but I also got a closer shave as a bonus. Knowing that these have been out for years, I am now kicking myself for waiting this long to give it a try. Can you ask for a lot more than a closer shave and no cuts? If you are frustrated with your non-powered razor, give this a try. Hopefully you'll have a pleasant surprise like I did.

title: Nice salon-quality cuticle pusher with nail cleaner tool, with a minor caveat.
text:
I have been looking for a stainless steel cuticle pusher to use for home manicures - this one is nearly identical to the one used by my manicurist, it has a nice weight to it, is comfortable to use, and is salon-quality. I use it with the CND CuticleAway Cuticle Remover gel, and it works just as expected. The nail cleaner end is a nice touch - I prefer this style to the ones that have flat or split trimmer blade ends.

One caveat - the edge on the pusher end is sharp - you need to be careful of the pressure and angle used which pushing your cuticles back, as holding the tool at the wrong angle and/or using too much pressure may result in damage to the top layer of your nail (e.g. the tool may shave a slight bit off). I used my Dremel with a fine sanding bit to dull the edge on the pusher end; this resolved the issue for me. If you don't have a Dremel, I suggest taking an emery board to smooth the sharp end before use in order to avoid damaging your nail.

I paid FULL price for this cuticle pusher, and did not receive any incentives or discounts in exchange for this review.

title: Great Price, Some Decent Ingredients, but Some Bad Ingredients as Well
text:
I really like products that contain Retinol. They work really well on my oily, acne prone skin. They also work great for combatting fine lines and wrinkles in between Botox injections. Yes, I do like my Botox twice a year.

I like the jar dispenser. It keeps things nice and clean and sanitary and I can control how much product I dispense. This 1.7 oz jar will last a very long time.

I use it at night only for fear of drying my face out, but on rare occasion I have used it in the am and it is a nice cream that glides on smoothly, quickly absorbs and doesn't leave my skin feeling greasy. I am a stickler for that. I won't use a product that makes my face feel greasy, sticky, or tacky.

The amount of Retinol is consistent with that on the market. It also contains Vit B5 and E which are great for repairing damage to the skin and Green Tea.

What I don't like about this product is that while it is 71% organic, it contains Cetyl Alcohol (can dry out the face), Xanthan Gum (a filler) and Phenoxyethanol, which is a very controversial ingredient. It is said to disrupt hormone imbalance amongst other issues. This is very important to me because I am a Breast Cancer Survivor. While I tested negative for hormone receptors and hormone driven cancer, I still proceed with caution. My ob won't even put me on Birth Control because of the hormones. So for me, the ingredients would make me steer away from this product in the future.

I had another Norelco shaver for the last 5 (or more) years. The difference in the shaves is striking. Both less pain when my stubble is a little long and closer.

However, the reason this shaver is cheaper is that there is 1 battery inside it instead of 2. I know this because I took it in to be "repaired" because I only got 8 shaves to a charge. I talked (online) with Norelco and they said my shaver was broken. So, I looked up on the Norelco site a local authorized repair shop. I took it in and the guy opened it up. He said it was one of the "cheap" versions that has 1 instead of 2 batteries.

My old shaver, over most of its life, gave me 25 or so shaves before needing to be recharged. That's quite a difference.

title: Highly recommend this company'S products.
text:
First, I want to say I bought this at full price....period!

I've been very lax over years, at any kind of skin care routine. My skin isn't really showing any effects of bad skin care, because I was blessed with really good skin, but....I'm 52 now and decided I really shouldn't push it any longer. So; I purchased Tree of Life Beauty Vitamin C wash first. I was very impressed with the ingredient list, the amount used to wash my face (neck, chest, and shoulders as well), and the way my skin felt afterwards.

So when I saw the toner was 93% organic, I decided buy the Tree of life Beauty Toner, to go along with the wash. First of all, I really am impressed with the ingredients this company uses. I grow all organics herbs, berries, vegetables, etc. and use as many organic ingredients that I can. I would love to be a purist, but my budget says "NO!" This company doesn't use a lot of needless filler ingredients to stretch the product. So when you think of the product being only 8 oz, you can be assured that 8 oz (when used properly), is a good amount of product that will last. I can't say how long yet, as I've only been using it a week.

Secondly, being an herbalist has taught me that your skin is your largest organ! You should be careful what you put on it. Your pores soak up every last drop of whatever you put on your skin. Parabens are absolute poison and should be avoided like the plague! (Sorry all of you Vicks and vasaline lovers out there) From what I've read about Tree of life Beauty, we're on the same page and I don't feel I need to be concerned about them hiding any in their products.

And finally, Vitamin C is essential to your body in too many ways to go into. But I take a vitamin C daily to help with the absorption of Collagen 1&3 (Which is important for hair, skin, nails, bones, joints, etc). I had not realized the benefits of vitamin C for your face. I absolutely love the way my skin feels after using the cleanser and toner. I let it dry well, then follow up with moisturizer both morning and evening.

So far, I'm quite happy with Tree of Life Beauty products and will probably transition to more of their products as I use up what I already have. We'll see how it goes after using these items for 30 days.

title: So disappointed
text: So I bought the hair steamer and it arrived pretty quick.  The first problem was there were no instructions.  I contacted the company via amazon and they quickly e-mailed me apologizing and giving me some instructions on how to put it together and how to use it.  I then wrote a mixed review rating them a 3.  I was then contacted and offered a $25 refund to remove the mixed review.  I decided that I would remove the review but only after making sure the steamer worked properly.  Once I did follow the instructions they gave me the plastic hanging down in the catch cup between the metal heating device started to melt.  The steamer never started to steam even after 15 to 20 minutes.  I again contacted the company and they immediately responded with different instructions from the original one and when that didn't work they told me to ship it back to them and once they received it they would ship me another one.  They also offered to issue a full refund.  I opted for the shipment of the replacement product but I explained if I got another bad product I would not only be contacting Amazon but I'd contact BBB and FTC Bureau of Consumer Protection.  Once I sent the e-mail I got a response stating that it would be in the best interest of both parties to issue a full refund at this time.  I think that says a lot.  I would not use this company going forward.  The customer service was polite and quick but their products are garbage and they don't stand behind their product or distributors apparently.  If they did they would have shipped me out a new product maybe even an upgrade to make up for the inconvenience.  Instead they told me I didn't have to ship it back I could just discard it.  If you do chose to do business with them I would definitely do all correspondence via e-mail so that when you have to file your complaint, you have adequate documentation.

text:
I give this shampoo two stars only because the first time I liked how my hair felt after using it.
I purchased the first bottle as a lightning deal. I only bought the shampoo. I liked how my hair felt after washing it, it had a nice fragrance, and even though the bottle came broken and the shampoo spilled I used whatever was left in it.
The second time I bought this product I bought the conditioner too. I was surprised to see that in the second bottle I received clear shampoo with no fragrance at all. Totally different from the first one. But the labels are the exact same with the same ingredients. How can a creamy white shampoo with fragrance have the same ingredients as a clear shampoo without any fragrance at all?
I can't return this product because I used it already but I'm sure I will never buy it again. I don't even know which bottle is the real one.
Before posting this review I asked other amazon customers and their feedback was inconsistent too. Some received creamy shampoo some clear shampoo. You can see their answers in the product questions and answers section.

title: Truly some wonderful stuff to fight "winter hands"
text:
I hate winter for a lot of reasons, but one of them is that my hands get so dry that I get cracks at my fingertips. It’s annoying and painful, especially at night. I’ve tried all sorts of moisturizers without much success. The best results (if you can call it that) have been from using petroleum jelly, but that’s messy and it still doesn’t work well.

This argan oil, however, has been hugely effective. It gave me results right from the first day, and over the course of just a few days I can see noticeable healing of the skin cracks. No more pain and my hands feel far better than any other treatment I’ve tried.

The product comes very nicely packaged, with a nice box filled with shredded packing material to keep the glass bottle safe in transit. It also makes for a very nice presentation should you want to give this as a gift. The bottle comes with a dropper and a “spritz” head. The latter is my only quibble – the spray head didn’t work well at all, and made sort of a mess when using it to dispense the oil. I replaced it with the dropper and had much better results.

The oil itself has little or no scent. You need very, very little for results – I use about 1-2 small drops per hand, and that’s more than enough. It spreads easily (as expected given that it’s oil). It does take a few minutes to soak in – my hands are very greasy when I first apply it, but after a few minutes the greasiness goes away. The sheen from the oil stays around longer, but that too dissipates after 30 minutes or so.

This can be used for a wide range of applications including face, body and even hair. It comes with a good amount of information to help explain how/where to use it, and how the oil was processed.

I’m very impressed with this oil – it’s the only product I’ve ever tried that totally worked to solve my dry/cracked hands. It’s not cheap, but well worth the price if you need a highly effective moisturizer. Highly recommend.

According to its Amazon listing, this serum is supposed to restore skin elasticity, reduce the look of fine lines, firm skin, replenish lost collagen, and reveal younger looking skin. title: Confusing marketing.....
text:
The seller really should change their description of this hair dryer.

First, the pictures make it look as if you can use the concentrators in either the vertical or horizontal position and this isn't true at all. In the horizontal position, the concentrator will fall off because it will not lock.....see promotion picture and my uploaded photo.

****This may not seem like a big deal until you start using it and have to adjust the direction with your wrist.****

Second, the description states the wattage is between 1800 to 2000 but the label says 1800 watts only....see description paragraph and my uploaded photo.

While the blow dryer is cute and an obvious design copy from the Dyson blow dryer (seems China has been copying Dyson these days but can't match the superior quality of Dyson), it's kinda heavy and gets too hot, even on the medium heat setting. I had to turn on the cool shot to offset the heat.

If you have hand arthritis, carpal tunnel, shoulder arthritis, etc, this will give you some trouble due to the heaviness, along with the inability to switch the concentrator into the horizontal position.

2 star deduction for the deceptive advertising, lack of concentrator versatility and heaviness.

I also took me a minute to figure out how to get it completely open and attach the dispensing top that came with it.  After you pop the top of the vial you have to carefully removed all the metal around the rubber stopper without hurting yourself and then pull off the rubber top and pull over the top the dispenser.  It is a very poor design concept.  As for the serum itself, it is good.  It hydrates without being greasy or oily.  It goes on really smooth and you don't have to use much of it.  It doesn't come in a very large container so it doesn't take up a lot of space but I was really disappointed when I opened the box (which is much bigger than what is inside) and pulled out a small medicine vial.  Hyaluronic acid serum works like it should if you are familiar with it.  If you are not then I would avoid this product as a first time choice so you don't waste too much product and you receive directions that you can read.  I did receive this product at a discounted rate for my honest, unbiased review....I have given just that and my review has not been influenced by anything other than how I liked the product itself.

title: These bandages have many uses; sticks to itself and not to skin or fur; not only tattoo grip tape
text:
These bandages have many uses. There are 16 black rolls that are individually wrapped and each roll is 5 yards apiece and 2 inches tall. These self-adhere as the bandage is wrapped around a hand, leg, arm, etc. These stick well. The stretch allows this to be used like kinesiology tape with the exception that one cannot shower with this successfully and each wrap is for one-time use.

The entire roll does not have to be used at once as it depends on the amount needed. When used where joints open and close, such as a knee or elbow, the wrap may bunch up in the crease as expected. However, this is perfect to use as a lightweight version of a carpal tunnel brace by wrapping it around a bad wrist, hand, and thumb. It does not stick to my skin nor to a pet's fur, which is wonderful.

This is versatile enough to wrap around the handle of a tennis racquet to get a good grip or an umbrella or cane handle. There are just so many useful possibilities besides medical reasons.

In summary, because the wraps are two inches wide and are not designed to stick to the skin, it does have a tendency to bunch up if wrapped around a knee or elbow, so it is not perfect for everything. I feel these are great bandages to have in one's medicine cabinet. At the current price of $15.19 ($15.99 minus 5%) it comes to $.95 cents per roll which is on the high side of competitively priced. These are self-adhesive bandages rebranded as tattoo grip tape.

title: More of a Novelty
text:
Beurer Foot Bath Massager, Water Tempering, Relaxing Vibration Massage and Bubble Massage Functions for Tired Feet, Includes 3 Pedicure Attachments, FB21 by Beurer North America. Of course, our feet play an important role throughout our lives as they have to bear our full weight: and each foot has 26 bones, 22 joints and 107 ligaments that may all need care. Beurer North America says that this foot bath will be a simple and convenient solution for sore and tired feet. The bath has three setting functions (water heating, vibration and bubble massage), an integrated water heater. The infrared light points will support the soothing effect of the foot massage. The three exchangeable pedicure tip can deliver a cleansing foot care treatment. The massage-assisted foot bed, Beurer states, will stimulate the feet; the detachable roller attachments will give a soothing foot reflexology massage; the double-walled housing ensures better thermal insulation. It includes a removable splash protection guard, convenient draining outlet, infrared light points to support the soothing effect of the foot massage.

I expect Beurer North America is a branch of a German company, and I am as awed by German engineering and technology as anyone else. But Beurer’s claims that this device can deliver a professional quality luxury spa experience are, frankly, silly. The item is more of a novelty than anything else. To begin with, I know nothing about German bathrooms, but in this country, any electrical outlets in bathrooms seem inevitably to be near the sink. The cord provided is not long enough to allow the item’s use in the tub without an extension cord, which, considering the well-known risks of mixing electricity and water, adds an unnecessary element of risk. So you will probably end up sitting on the toilet seat, or may have to bring in a chair. And the gadget is messy; you’d better put it on a towel. That being said, it did make my feet feel marginally better after a long tough day. Will you find it useful? That depends on how much you’re willing to spend on it, and whether you have room for one more bathroom gadget of limited utility.

The first results in even trimming; the second allows the vacuum to work best. Yes, a few hairs will show up in the sink, but with one swipe with a damp tissue they're gone. The adjustable comb trims beard, mustache, goatee, etc., to any length a user might want. In addition to the trimmer, the mustache and sideburn clipper gives a precise and neat edge; to use it, just remove the comb.

Taking the T770 apart to clean the blades is easy; getting it back together properly requires careful assembly in good lighting and some patience. I wish Norelco would simplify the re-assembly mechanisms and process. But even that, since I have now mastered it, does not truly lessen my liking of this product. Nor does its charging time; the T770 holds its charge for around two months (and I use the trimmer 2-3 times a week).

Should I drop and break this trimmer, as I did with a previously owned Remington, I will replace it with another Norelco. It's been great to have said good-bye to scissors.

title: Wash them well before using 💀
text:
A spray bottle is a spray bottle, right? 🤔 Lol, nope!

So, here we are... shopping on Amazon, presented with a thousand options for something as simple as a bottle that sprays. 😰

My selection criteria was this: (a) The plastic must be able to handle liquid sanitizer made with a base of 60% alcohol (the 91% ISP variety), *without suffering undesirable changes* and (b) Have a good spray nozzle capable of producing a fine, even mist *without getting clogged*.

This set of bottles from MOSTOF checks both of those boxes. ✔ I tested them specifically against 2 different types of liquid (not gel) sanitizer. Initially, I chose this particular set for the larger sized funnels that are also included, and the fact that it comes with (10) travel sized bottles.

None of my bottles leak and they spray a fine, even mist without leaving droplets. After seeing the spray function in action, I decided to use a couple of these for facial mists and essences. I don't know (yet) whether they'll spray every last drop, but the sprayer feed wraps all the way around the bottom of the bottle, which does look promising. 🤞 So far, every liquid I've put in them has been fine; the plastic didn't change and the sprays perform the same.

Ultimately, I had to dock a star from my rating because the bottles came filthy inside, 😬 every one of them is heavily scratched up, and one of the bottles I received doesn't sit evenly. ➡️(see photos 3&4: defect (warped) bottle is on the right)⬅️

PRO'S:
+ Contains everything you need to package liquids immediately
+ Includes larger sized funnels = quick flow in filling
+ Spray nozzles produce fine, even mist without leaving droplets
+ Sprayer feed goes all the way around the bottom of the bottle
+ No leaking from the bottle necks or spray nozzles
+ Spray nozzles have not clogged
+ Caps fit tightly
+ No adverse reactions to the plastic (re: high alcohol content)
+ Airline approved carry-on size
+ Excellent price for ten bottles (and two funnels!)
+ Convenient PRIME shipping
+ Bonus sheet of labels (they're small, but they work)

CONS:
- Bottles came really scratched up and very dirty
- One of the ten bottles I received doesn't sit evenly

SUMMARY:
Ultimately, I think there's some quality control issues that the manufacturer could improve upon. As long as you're not an Etsy seller, or someone that's gonna be gifting these, you may not mind the scratches or the possibility of uneven bottom(s). Provided you wash them out really good, they still do the job! 👍🏼 Should anything happen to change with these as time goes on, I will update this review. Thanks for reading! Stay safe. 😷

title: Good and bad - But I have notes to increase success.
text:
I applied this to my 5 year olds blonde hair. I did not want to spend a future at a salon because.... she is five!
She DOES love the end result but I will say, if you want a successful process I have several important notes.
1. I can NOT speak to the bleach because we did NOT use it. I hear BAD things about it.... so, read other reviews if applicable.
2. Product is messy! That said; count on the NEED for 2 person application. Do NOT attempt to self apply this product. Will absolutely regret it and ruin your home and clothes.
3. Count on purchasing extra items AND plan for 3 hours from prep start to finish. I will explain why.
EXTRA ITEMS: This product will ABSOLUTELY stain hand, face and scalp. Purchase: extra gloves, vaseline, and hair dye removal!
GLOVES: It only comes with one crappy pair of gloves. For best result, swing by Sally's beauty and buy SEVERAL good pairs of gloves. OR buy some of those thick bathroom cleaning gloves that come to your elbows. this way you can use them and take them off and on easily to both apply AND rinse hair.
VASELINE: COMPLETELY coat ears, forehead, neck, etc with a THICK coat of vaseline to avoid staining
DYE REMOVAL: Swing by sally's and buy a bottle of hair dye remover BEFORE you start. This will get on skin and you will NOT get it off otherwise.
EXTRA TIME TO APPLY: I have applied this product in 4 different colors to both my own hair and others hair. I have NEVER gotten good coverage without having to apply it TWICE. (including this application. pictures attached are product of applying BOTH colors twice for an hour each time) For the vibrant color you will want, count on applying, waiting an hour to rinse. Blow dry and reapply for ANOTHER hour. Do not think you will "quickly" apply this product like a box of normal 20 minute color. You will be disappointed.

Overall, as I said, my daughter is happy with the turn out and I saved money so in my case, it worked out.
However, I have experience with this product so it was successful based on ALL the above notes.
Also, I DID experience severe staining to her scalp and it will NOT come off so far even with the hair dye remover. I did not apply it close to scalp but she is young and her hair is so thin, it bleed right through and left big nasty looking spots all over her little head. That said, I ONLY applied this to the underneath of her hair as an ombre look... so I can keep working on getting it off in the next few days.
I would be much more upset if I had this all over her head.

title: A favorite childhood snack!
text:
I grew up eating Taro Fish Snacks in Thailand, and they're still one of my favorite snacks. For someone not used to them, they can seem a bit strange. Maybe it's a bit of an acquired taste, but I really enjoy the chewy leathery texture of them as well. Something I discovered with these years ago is to spread them in a thin layer on a cookie sheet and stick them under the broiler for just a few minutes.. no more than it takes for them to just barely start to get a hint of brown. The texture completely changes to something crispy instead of chewy. Watch it though, they go from brown to black in the blink of an eye! Toasted up this way they also make for an unusual topping to a salad or a bowl of noodle soup.

The original while package taro are my favorites, flavor wise, though sometimes I like the yellow and orange package ones too - they tend to be spicier, which I have to be in the mood for.

title: Promising Moisturizer For Oily Skin
text:
My face skin is weird. It can be so dry but can also be so oily. I hate it when my face is so greasy and shiny. It makes my face look awful during a video call or even at a photo shoot. So I am always on the lookout for something that may help.

This Cell Fusion C moisturizing gel is promising. The product came in a tube enclosed in a small box. The box around it is sprinkled with instructions. English instruction at the right side and equivalent Korean at the back. There are no leaflets inside regarding the product. I guess the manufacturer believes the pieces of information provided around the box are more than enough.

To use, I uncapped the translucent plastic hinged cap. There is a foil safety seal at the tube’s mouth I need to remove. I love the smell of this. It is flowery with a hint of Philippine Jasmine (Sampaguita) and Perfume Tree (Ilang-Ilang). There is also a teeny-tiny hint of lavender and citrus. It is made in Korea so I guess they use Asian flowers. The fragrance is subtle and not overpowering. It is light and not greasy. My skin did not complain, no irritation, no tingling sensation, and it just felt relaxed. This would be good to use during summer when my face becomes oily, and breakout may occur due to clogged pores.

title: Good Basic Oil
text:
3.5/5 Rating

I have sensitive, dry, acne prone skin with occasional bouts of plaque psoriasis. My main concerns/wants are products that are gentle, don't strip my skin and cleanse well.

This was my first foray into oil cleansing and the double cleanse method. I used [[ASIN:B004RRGXKI Neutrogena Fresh Foaming Cleanser, 4 Count]] in conjecture with this cleansing oil. This oil is a great, basic, no frills cleanser. I usually needed 2-3 pumps because my dry skin would soak up the oil and I needed extra to actually cleanse. It has a flora scent which while I didn't feel over powered by, I didn't love either. The oil does a great job taking off daily sunblock and makeup. I did not use it to take off eye makeup but micellar water instead because I found it did not take off mascara well at all.

I never broke out when using it and always felt clean after washing with it. It didn't strip my skin but it didn't appear to help it either. After finishing the bottle I eventually went to [[ASIN:B00EJ9RUKQ The Face Shop Rice Water Bright Cleansing Milk]] which serves my ultra dry skin better. I would recommend this to someone new to oil cleansing or someone wanting a good, basic oil.

title: Works!  Looks great!  Eyebrows! Yay!
text:
So, after being chemo eyebrow bald (and everywhere else bald too) for almost a year due to breast cancer chemotherapy treatments, when my eye brows finally grew back they were mostly white instead of my natural dark brown. Augh!! Since I am a second time breast cancer warrior with bigger fish to fry — I ignored my mostly white eye brows for about nine months — hoping they would eventually recover their natural dark brown color after my body recovered from all the chemo poison. Nope. Not happening. No such luck.

The mostly white eyebrows bothered me even more than the flat chest double mastectomy— because well a flat chest can be padded but having invisible brows left me feeling washed out and old. So, I decided to fix my brows because that seemed like a doable relatively easy DIY thing. I read lots of articles on home dying eye brows. Then, based on article recommendations, I found this Godfey product on Amazon and after much research and watching DIY “dye your eyebrows at home” videos, I gave it a go and dyed my eyebrows at home exactly one week ago. The results: Yay!!!! As everyone suggested, I put vaseline around my eyebrows to protect my skin. I did one eyebrow at a time rather than both at once. Also, due to my super sensitive skin, I only left the dye on for two minutes per brow. Still, it worked perfectly. My eyebrow hairs are still dark brown — one week after I dyed them. Success!!!

I love having my dark eyebrows back, and sort of feel like me again.

This item is very durable and very easy to hang up, as all that is required is simply removing the glossy sheet that covers the back of the stainless steel hanger and applying it to the wall with pressure. You would have to make sure you are precise, i.e. it is leveled––straight, as the adhesive on the back is REALLY strong.

That being said, you would have to make sure the wall is not made of cheap materials. I had no problem having this item on my bathroom wall for over a year. There was no need for concern that it would fall. However, the moment I needed to get it off, it was as though it was going to take the wall with it. Paint and parts of the wall came off and caused damage. So I had to take off the black sheet that had the adhesive from both stainless steel pieces and keep them. It's possible to find some other form of adhesive (like Command hanging strips) to reapply them to the wall.

title: Very high quality and professional set
text:
There are so many uses for tweezers, and I am used to having some from brands like Revlon and such that are okay, but they are not very high quality. The ends are usually dull and they have a hard time grabbing anything. I was extremely happy when I opened this pack of 3. They are a sturdy stainless steel metal, no plastic or cheap aluminum. The ends of the silver one are extremely pointy, perfect for pulling out things like splinters and anything that might get stuck in the skin. My husband was working and ended up with a large splinter under his finger nail. Since you can't exactly get it from the top, we decided to use the silver sharp pair of tweezers and were able to extract the splinter from under his nail. They also work very well for removing hair. I pluck from time to time and the black and pink pair are really nice for that. The silver is easy to get out any ingrown hairs. Overall the set is very high quality and very professional.

*I RECEIVED THIS ITEM TO TRY IN EXCHANGE FOR AN HONEST AND UNBIASED REVIEW. THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE A GOOD REVIEW, SO IF I GIVE THE PRODUCT ONE, IT MEANS I TRULY BELIEVE IT DESERVES IT. EVERYTHING IN THIS REVIEW IS 100% MY OWN AND HAS NOT BEEN INFLUENCED OR ALTERED IN ANY WAY

text: The black pins are nearly identical to the Goody brand I have been an unwavering fan of for at least ten years. It can be difficult to find the Goody brand so I figured I would try Amazon. I chose this color & number of pins configuration b'c the black pins most closely match the Goody product. I also loved the look of the bright gold, rose gold and silver varieties of this product but the small balls on the ends of the shiny metal ones are too large and actually prevent me from being able to get them out. I have never tried a knock-off version of these so I have never experienced the tangles' issues until now. I chose & ordered this brand by visually estimating the similarities with the ones that are $7.85 at Walmart for a package of two pins (if you are lucky enough to find them in stock). So...long story longer, the size of the comfort covered wire end is critical for this product to work, but all of the pins are pretty, appear to be well made and have stood up to the shower and strenuous activity for hours. If you have curly hair however, I would gently test the removal of the pins immediately after placing them before you go a whole day. The tangles are not apparent until you try to take them out. Putting them in seems to be exactly the same as the original pins.

title: Good for a gentle exfoliation or those with already good skin.
text:
If you need a mild chemical exfoliant and want to cut out products from your routine, this might be the serum for you. It's a weaker concentration of retinol but with that trade, you get a less harsh serum that still keeps your skin hydrated and has a lesser chance of causing irritation. You can most likely use this as a serum/cream combo. Likely a big bonus for those with sensitive skin.

I've taken a break from my usual Tretinoin cream due to the extreme sun in my area but I do still need to keep up with chemical exfoliants and retinol has the added bonus of fighting acne like Tret does. My skin is definitely smoothing out again and looks more even, but it's a very very subtle improvement so I'm not sure if those that have significant texture issues or need a lot of brightening or fading will be pleased with this as it most likely would take a while to see visible results.

It's not a bad product but with such a low retinol percentage it is quite expensive compared to other retinol serums/creams on the market and also comes in a small bottle. I do like it but I don't think it's something I'd purchase myself if only because of that.

title: it might be fun to pay a little more than I would if ...
text:
I got this set because I was curious about the spiral thingies and figured, for the price, it might be fun to pay a little more than I would if I was just buying the spirals elsewhere and have some stuff to play around with. Most of the items turned out to be pretty meh, so now I'm the proud owner of spiral thingies and some clutter.

Pros:
The spiral bun holders are great - both for holding my hair up in a neat bun and for putting my hair in before bed. If I wear them to bed (on not totally dry hair), I'll have nice waves when I take them out in the morning.

I like the medium size donut hair thing too. These are super easy to make out of an extra sock. So... maybe not worth buying.

Cons:
I ended up getting excited about the the 'topsy tail' things - but they both broke. I put my hair in a pony tail, wrapped some of my hair around the elastic to hide it, and was using the little topsy tail thing to pull that bit of hair back through the elastic / pony tail holder when it snapped. So I tried doing the same thing with the bigger one and it snapped too. There's always room for user error, but it seems like these guys should have been able to withstand pulling some hair through a pony tail / pony tail holder.

The rest of the set is pretty meh and/or useless.

title: Ingredients identical to Dr. Bronner's liquid soap, but price is double or higher
text:
So, this product is natural and works well to clean brushes. It is a super basic soap without unwanted chemicals, which is great. However, the ingredients are pretty much identical to Dr. Bronner's Pure Castille Liquid Soap, which costs half as much or less, and does the exact same thing. Dr. B's also comes in numerous scents (all organic) and even unscented. Also, I think Dr. B's is more concentrated, so it takes less soap to clean each brush, making it even more economical.

Bottom line, this "Makeup Brush Cleansing Shampoo" is a perfectly good product, but you can get essentially the same thing for a much lower price by buying Dr. Bronner's Liquid Soap instead.

title: NOT REAL GEMSTONE
text:
If you do your research, Opalite is not a real gemstone!! I didn't know that and bought this soap thinking I'd have a nice gemstone after using such a cool soap. Opalite is man-made glass. I knew something was up after holding the "real gemstone" up to the light and finding bubbles in it. It's a hunk of pretty glass.

I still enjoyed the soap though, it's pretty and smelly lightly minty - although it doesn't last long as it is glycerin-based. It's nice to give as a gift or use when guests come around although it's rather expensive for almost $10 a pop to use in your shower and not a great deal or value...especially since you are not getting a real gemstone!

I tried to take a photo with my phone but it was hard to get a good picture due to light bouncing off the milky white glass.

If I could grade this, it would get an "A" for appearance and gift-ability, "C" for long lasting, "F" for advertising it as a real gemstone, and an overall "C-" for value.

title: TSA-approved clear quart bag - sturdy and surprisingly roomy!
text:

My family used these during a recent trip to Europe - they zip open and closed easily, are made of heavy plastic, and the gusset design allows one to fit a large amount of travel-sized bottles! Much better than a zip-lock sandwich bag. Highly recommend, especially for anyone who wants to use only carry-on luggage instead of checking their bags.

Liquid prescription/OTC medications and other prescription items, such as contact lenses (and lens solution) are generally exempt from the TSA's 3-1-1 liquids rule for liquids, gels, aerosols, creams and pastes (3.4 oz bottle or less; 1 quart-sized, clear, plastic, zip-top bag; 1 bag per passenger), and can be packed in a separate bag; you just have to pull them out for inspection with your quart-sized bag. Check the TSA's website for more information.

text:
﻿I’ve been using the NIRA Skincare Laser & Hyaluronic Acid Serum for a couple weeks and can’t yet gauge whether the laser is effective at increasing collagen production and smoothing wrinkles as a long term benefit. I get good results from the hyaluronic acid (HA) serum as it gives quick but temporary plumping and smoothing of wrinkles, as do other good HA serums. I also suspect the warmth created by Nira laser may increase absorption of the HA serum and boost its short term benefits (though I can’t say for sure).

I assume it will take regular use for at least 60 days (and likely 90 days) to judge Nira‘s benefits beyond the temporary HA plumping. Nira’s own before and after photos are from the 90-day mark. While I’ll continue use of the Nira laser to see if it helps, I question the extent of any long term benefits based on Nira’s own photos that show a smiling before photo and a rather solemn after photo; clearly, we more lines are evident when smiling so I feel photos would be more credible if they showed someone with the same or similar expression in the before and after photos.

Still, I like the Nira laser as it holds a charge well and is quick and easy to use. It gives feedback via beeps. Nira states it has FDA clearance (which I haven’t verified) for wrinkle treatment around the eyes. I’m cautious about the eye area, so I’m initially trying Nira on less sensitive skin between my eyebrows where I have fine lines and slight sagging and also on my neck where I have a weird wrinkle likely from looking down at my tablet. I started using Nira on fine lines around my mouth, but I may hold off until I feel confident it won’t exacerbate existing pigmentation issues.

Nira is painless and I only feel warming on setting 2 or 3 (depending on area). The skin around my mouth is drier and only tolerates a 2, and it turns red temporarily. I’ve tried a 4 between the eyebrows and it stings, so I’ll need to work up. I use the HA serum after use, and it’s a clear gel like serum that’s calming and my redness goes away quickly. I get a quick plumping effect that temporarily helps smooths lines, but I can’t say if Nira will provide a long term benefit over time. I do like using it with the serum, so I’m rating it 4 stars. I’ll update as appropriate.

title: Better than the loofa one I have.
text:
I recently started using one of these with loofa on it. It works for me, even if loofa does take a while to break in. However, it also absorbs quite a bit of soap. I like this one much better.

I was a little hesitant to order it. How would silicone feel against my back? It turns out that it feels fine and works well. I like that it needs much less soap since it doesn't absorb it. Instead of spreading it all over the thing - I like the side with little bristles like a brush - all you need is to put some in the center. Moving the brush over your back spreads the soap out nicely and does the job without a lot of waste. It squeaks a bit on un-soaped skin, but that's pretty easy to get over and doesn't last long. It was just a surprise, initially. It feels like a gentle scrub, and that's the important part. It also rinses off easily and dries quickly, an important point here in our humid climate. The interior relative humidity in our house hovers around 55% in the summer, so things can get moldy fast. That's what usually happens if a loofa or any other kind of absorbent surface isn't dried properly. I just hang this up on the thoughtfully provided suction hooks and forget about it. It's great, and I'm really glad I gave this a try!

title: Works on every level...
text:
So, for a man who thinks his looks strike a resemblance to that of Anderson Cooper.. (bc, of the devilishly handsome silver fox short crew cut) mixed with a longer (3/4”) faux-hawk frontal vibe.. this is a great product to work with this style as it complements the cut really well! As one who’s always used hair gel (daily x30+ yrs!) it’s hard to find one we have not tried. Bold Men casual- sold just under $20 for 3.3oz. Is a higher price point so, the expectations were high and happy to say, this came through impressively.

This gel has an ability to last thru the day without becoming razor sharp quills nor, a crusty-crumbly flake after a full day of wear in tear. Being one who prefers a touchable hold (the hardest combo to find btw!!) this gives that to you.. We found, unlike cheaper store bought brands- less is more! (too much will weigh down the hair) **A trick of the trade for any who want to accomplish short spikes- use less product!!

Best results came from using no more than a nickel size amount onto towel (50%) dried hair.. and finger combing into place. The hold stays movably put.. performing better then ever expected- yay!! TBH, this may take getting used too.. IF, you’re norm is the “frozen gel look!” Hack: one can finger style hair into place with this- then, use blow dryer on a lower setting for just a moment.. it will expedite the setting process- giving specific direction to the final look. (A convertible would do the same but.. not sure It’s feasible in winter ha ha!)

Product is thick yet, offers just enough slip to give you pliability to style before it settles. Note: color is clear… It’s just the container that is black! After hair is set, this absorbs vs. shellacs to the hair- letting hair have movement and touchable texture.. The scent is nice with a masculine appeal And after 3wks. of daily application we’ve used approx. a tad over 1/4 of content (to give you an idea how long it will last..) thus far, washing daily we’ve noticed no unwanted build up.. which is also a big deal- as this can lead to flakes/Dandruff..!! A good shampoo scrub removes product easily enough.. and paired with daily conditioner, it’s not over-drying to the hair. Making the $ seem worth all the quality benefits.

This is a top quality higher end product that best fits those who have a moveable set style they like their hair to maintain throughout the day.. this can achieve the desired look and look fantastic- and does so, without all the unwanted side effects that can come with daily use of hair gel.. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!

title: Electrolysis... FOR WHENEVER YOU NEED IT
text:
Love being able to access electrolysis at home! I have been going to a professional for months now and when the 2020 pandemic began and all service providers closed up shop, I wasn't sure how I would deal with unwanted facial hair. Where other methods of hair removal can encourage stronger hair regrowth I did not want to regress. Then I found this! I have had this product several weeks now and am very happy with it. I wish I had found this earlier. Not only can I do a treatment whenever I want, I am able to target hairs when they first appear as opposed to waiting for an appointment. It is very easy to use. I was afraid I would be unable to target the follicle in the right spot but that has not been a problem. It has a high pitch buzz when the current is delivered to the follicle. Most of the time the sound is my only indication that anything is happening. I do not find this painful. I can tell it is working because when I go to remove the hair it comes out with no effort. I do keep the power at the highest setting except for the delicate area above the upper lip. That can be a painful area at home or at the salon.

My only complaint with the product is that the tweezers included are useless. Just use your own.
I bent the stylist at first so I did order extras to have in case that happens again... so far so good as I haven't ruined another. I don't think that is a product flaw as it must be very delicate to do the job right... just be careful.

If you are unfamiliar with electrolysis, do not expect that one shot will forever kill a hair. I suggest reading articles on the subject as this can be a long term process. But considering other methods are a FOREVER process... go for it !

title: Lovely pampering skincare, frustrating packaging
text:
This product is a perfect example of a good product compromised by packaging. Each of the four pampering products was lovely: the body butter was rich and moisturizing without leaving the skin feeling greasy, the scrub had a good texture that never scratched or left skin dried out; the body wash felt great and cleansing, and even the bath salts, the weakest offering in the bunch, left the water pleasantly scented with a fresh, sparkling pineapple scent. Indeed, if you are a pineapple fan the combination of all these products is heavenly.

But the creams and potions are difficult to extract from their packaging! Instead of bottles or pots, a sealed envelope is used, similar to the ones you might purchase loose tea in. It takes up less room and weighs less than traditional packaging, so this option is very environmentally friendly. I was able to squeeze the body cream and body wash out in a manner similar to pushing toothpaste out of a tube, but I wasn’t able to get everything. The bath salts shook right out, so that wasn’t bad. But oh, the scrub! I loved the texture of the scrub but it was impossible to get out. It wouldn’t squeeze out and it was too sticky to pour, so I had to try and reach in and scoop it out with my fingertips. I gave up after using less than half of it because so much of the scrub got pushed into the deep corners of the envelope that I couldn’t get to it.

I recommend skipping this travel option and buying full-sized products instead. They’re great to use and very moisturizing for the skin - I would rate most of them 4 or 5 stars if not for the travel packaging.

Overall, I am pleasantly surprised & generally happy with it.

What I don't particularly care for is, with usage, my hair has to be washed every other day or it ends up looking greasy, limp and stringy. Also, the smell is definitely a medicinal odor with the Taila. But the results outweigh my complaints: Considerably less flaking of my very dry scalp, less shedding (yeah, I lose hair like a Husky), receding hairline seems less so, and sometimes I have to actually search for my small truly bald spot at the back of my crown rather than it displaying itself at every opportunity. A pleasant surprise this second time around is that some of the new growth is coming in my natural black rather than silver or white as it had been. This was totally unexpected at my age, although I did read it might stem greying. Makes it look like I have more hair at my hairline with the darker strands growing in. So ignore my complaints. title: Neutral
text:
I bought this product to use on my daughter's hair. She's 7, her hair is super thick and cannot seem to decide whether it wants to be straight or curly!
Pros: Lightweight enough.
Bristles glide easily (I do brush out her hair first).
Gets pretty hot, but you really would have to be trying to burn yourself. Pretty safe.
Keeps the volume in the hair that would normally be flattened out with a 2-sided iron.
Cons: Takes FOREVER to heat up. They say 30 seconds up in the description, but like a full 5 minutes to reach 200C.
It's display is Celsius. I had to do some math to figure out what to set it on. Call me a dumb American or whatever, but every other hair tool I own is Fahrenheit.
You have to provide some real tension in the hair to get both the roots and the ends straight. This may work better with a glove when you get to the ends to hold them there, but I didn't have one handy and had to go over the ends several times.
So, I would pretty well recommend this for someone my daughter's age where she's going to be safe using it on her own. I don't think I would use it on my own hair unless for some reason I found myself without my other styling tools. It's a good way for her to learn how to take care of her hair though.

title: Great moisturizer for most skin types

I love a more lightweight moisturizer that doesn’t look greasy and this fits the bill.  It absorbs completely and makes your skin feel hydrated and plump.  I wear a lot of foundation and it goes over this moisturizer nicely without causing any weird texture or breakage.  Unfortunately with the cold weather now upon us, it still isn’t quite enough to keep my skin hydrated all day and I do start to feel tight after a few hours.  For me, this will be great in the warmer months but I just need a little bit more out of a cream in the winter.  I think it is a great moisturizer for most people, just maybe not enough for those of us with desert dry skin.
