title: Nicest organizer of this type I have seen has clear attention to detail
text:
Plastic and/or acrylic organizers come in all sizes, shapes, configurations and qualities. MelodySusie® has blown me away with this three part, multiple sectioned organizer with drawers. Just so you're clear, you get a base with four drawers, each with an flattened oval shaped pull, each lined with a black textile that can be removed or used as you choose. The edges of the drawers are beveled, giving this an aura of elegance, but most importantly, each drawer slides in and out with ease, regardless of whether or not the drawer is packed or empty. The bottom of the base has a little strip in the form which raises this organizer from sitting directly on the counter, so if it is used in a bathroom, air can circulate around the entire piece and grungy mildew and such is reduced from forming. Don't forget to dust, though. The exterior edges are beveled, giving them a very finished appearance, unlike those sharp edges on many similar products in the marketplace.

Included with this organizer are two additional pieces, each is the same dimension as the interior of the top ridge of the chest organizer, so you can decide which one you want to put on top and which one you want to put next to the main component. Or you can separate them entirely and use the top of the organizer to put items and use the two multi-sectioned components separately. You could line them up side by side along a dresser top and have more width rather than extended height.

I love the assorted sizes of the sections and the angles top of the shorter of the two pieces. I also love the rounded design in the sections of the taller component. Every aspect of this trio is outstanding, high quality, and it makes quite the impression in addition to comfortably storing whatever you like in each compartment. Each edge is finished, every detail has been considered, and it is even practical in that it can quickly be cleaned with no harsh detergents. This lovely item was made in China and it is clear that quality control is important to the manufacturer because I saw no defect even after intense examination. Be prepared for a weightier set than you might expect, because there was no skimping on the materials. It is perfectly packed for protection and is ideal for presenting as a gift. It is well worth its price point. A sample was provided for review.

title: Some nice items, but disappointing quality for toenail clippers
text:
This is a comprehensive set of nail cutting/trimming/maintaining tools. The standard clipper is very nice -- solid, sharp, and well up to the task of handling fingernails and lighter toenails. The various tools are also of decent quality.

What's not so good is the toenail clippers. It has a rather lightweight feel to it compared with other clippers I've used. The short handles make it less comfortable to use than other clippers. More importantly, the spring mechanism failed within the first couple of minutes of use. It uses two leaf style springs that push the jaws apart. The problem is with how they attach to the handle. There are two little prongs for each spring that fit into two little holes in the handle. For mine, the pins are too short to make a solid connection, so one falls (or rather, jumps) out no matter how many times I've tried to seat it properly into the handle (see photo). It can be used without the spring, but it's quite cumbersome to do so. Given the importance of the toenail clipper to the overall usefulness of the kit, I see this as a 2 star product.

If the springs were better it would be 4 stars since, even when properly functioning, the clippers are not as easy to use as others, but warrant 4 stars given the low cost compared with better quality clippers.

I don't like the glue because it always takes my real lashes off. So magnetic liner "YES Please"! I did watch some YouTube videos prior to buying to see how to put them on properly. I put a thin line on first with no luck, so I put a thicker (much thicker) line on and waited a bit before putting my lashes on. I'm not sure if it is truly magnets that hold them in place or just the goo/glue substance of the liner? I will say that with magnets you feel a "pull" sensation where the magnets are drawn together, I never got that feeling with this liner so my guess is... it is more the goo of the liner that holds them on (still better than glue). Either way, I have them on and I hope the goo holds up for the entire day! :)

UPDATE: After wearing these eyelashes for a full day they stayed on without any issues! Be it magnets or goo, I'm thrilled with using this product again and again!

title: Made an impressionable impact.. great for teen boys!
text:
This was a lifesaver for our son with an acne issue! Being a 17yr. old boy who was feeling the high school inferiority angst at a time in life thats rough enough.. bc duh, it’s High School!! He hoped for a solution to improve his condition and give a boost to his confidence. We ended at a dermatologist who gave us a regiment of:
1. wipe the counter clean of all gimmicks/products
2. use a dye/scent free soap and water x2 daily
3. follow up with clindamycin 1% to dab on larger
trouble spots ONLY..!!
So, on our way to where we wanted to go... improvement was ours in leaps and bounds. Then, Covid... Then, the mask mandate!! Soon after we developed a sort of acne/rash on bridge of nose and around mouth 2” due to synthetic material where the mask touches the face. Dr. said mask was compromising the skins ability to breathe and would subside after mandate lifted. Only, attending school x5 days a week 100% fully masked- didn't give skin any reprieve and with no end in sight, I went seeking help for acne irritation.

As of now, we’re on the 25th day of Geologie’s 30 day regiment and I am so grateful we found this product. TBH, I personally didn't realize the extent of red, blotchy and puffiness this irritation had brought his poor skin.. until after using approx. 5 days- when we noticed a decrease in the puffy/red that had gradually appeared. Over the last 2wks- it has been clearing things up a little at a time and things seem less inflamed and aggravated. What I’m most impressed with- this hasn’t caused excess breakout like many other products in the past had done and I’m sure it’s bc, of the compound. Nor, has it left skin overly dry.. and both of these are huge!! I’m not even sure how it does it, maybe it’s witchcraft?! For comparison: a BFF uses Proactiv (as seen on TV!) with her 2 son’s for past x3 months and I’m actually surprised the results we had seem similar but, in a lot less time!?

The 2 bottles of product are easily identified and instructions are simple easy and straightforward- x1 AM/PM. I applaud the packaging as it doesn’t have a feminine vibe, nothing “fu-fu-“ to turn teen boys away from using “girl stuff!” Trust me, I’ve gone this route before- and it does matter to some! This is a non offensive clean smell and the product itself dissipates/absorbs into the skin easily after application. A few suggestions I have: leave out on bathroom counter to remind one to use daily, use fresh pillowcase every few days to keep any excess bacteria away, wash mask daily if poss. while this mandate applies.. and most of all- keep your hands away! Easier for adults- harder for teens.

As with any product there are many factors to it success.. and for obvious reasons. I can’t promise it will cure all issues but, I feel confident in saying you can expect improvement (if not extinct..) end results. I’m so happy to have found this and will be looking into the entire product line for future maintenance use. Sorry so long winded.. I wanted to include details for any in a similar situation- I am hoping this info. may be helpful to someone else in need.. Be safe.

title: It works.... Just not how it claims too.
text:
After reading the reviews about nail bed damage and how well this helps the soak off I ended up getting it.

Firstly, it does peel a little nail bed up, so the damage thing is accurate. I wouldn't suggest using it "as advertised". However, after nudging off one nail I dis the standard coarse board, polish remover soaked cotton balls, wrap my fingers in foil thing. The soak off is MUCH easier with this as the base coat. They come off faster, more cleanly and leave behind no damage.

I'm only giving it three stars for a few reasons. It doesn't do what it says it should do. It does lift. On my second try, after the first experiment, I did my nails again. Several nails lifted and peeled. Some came completely free with no damage. Usually my gels outlast my level of interest, and I soak them off before I even go the full two weeks. These definitely have a gripping problem. That's not a negative for me. It makes polish changes easier. However, it mean that they don't do what they're supposed to do.

Bottom line, the things about this product that make it convenient for me are counter to what the product is advertised as doing. I imagine that would make it a poor buy for many a gel lover.

As others have mentioned, this trimmer suffers from a bad stand design; you cannot charge it while it's in the stand. Frankly I don't bother with the stand at all; the trimmer and accessories stay in a drawer in my bathroom where they can't gather dust.
I mostly use the G250 for nose and ear hair removal. It does a decent job at trimming with this attachment. Other reviewers have mentioned problems with the battery. I'll have to consider myself lucky in this department. I've gotten very good charge retention, with several weekly trimming sessions on each charge.
Bottom line: It's got some flaws, but the G250 has worked well for me.

title: Well made, leak-free bottles for a healthier, greener lifestyle
text:
Since becoming a mom, I've been trying to live a greener, less toxic lifestyle. I've started cloth diapering & using un-paper towels. I've switched to natural body & laundry products. However, for some reason, I had been holding out on switching to chemical free cleaning and fabric/air fresheners. I'm not exactly sure why I was so hesitant. These bottles made making the switch fun and easy!

These bottles have both a mist and a stream spray option, as well as an option to turn off the spraying mechanism. Currently, I have one bottle filled with a 1:1 ratio of water to vinegar for use as glass cleaner. The mist option works well on my mirrors and shower doors. The mist option also works very well for both my homemade room/linen spray and my pest repellent spray. (Peppermint essential oil diluted with water and sprayed on the baseboards/around door and windows.) I use the direct stream option for my tub and tile cleaner. It works very well for spraying directly onto the grout.

At 16oz, the bottles are substantial but are not heavy in hand. The trigger is easy to squeeze, yet not flimsy. The glass itself is a gorgeous, deep cobalt blue. I keep my homemade air freshener in one of these bottles on the bathroom counter and have been asked multiple times about where I got it. They really are just so very pretty. Too pretty to be hidden under the sink like most other air freshener or cleaning supply bottles.

Often times, when you purchase cleaners from the store in inexpensive plastic bottles with these same mechanisms, the spray head tends to leak after a week or two of use. It never fails. These, however, are sturdy and seem to be much more heavy duty. I've used these bottles nearly daily and have not had any leaks whatsoever. As beautiful as these bottles are, this is what impressed me most. I'm extremely happy with this product and would highly recommend them!

*I received a discount for this product in exchange for my honest and unbiased opinion.*

title: Best for a newbie with patience
text:
First time ever doing this. I bought it for my daughters they couldn’t do it so I wanted to try it out for myself to see if I got ripped off. After trying it out I realized the reason they had trouble was bc they don’t have any nails to grip the fake nails to and they have the tiniest fingers which makes a difference. So I tried it out and I had a lot of trouble at first but once I got the hang of it it wasn’t hard. Tips i can give a newbie :
1) use the nails they provide. At first I thought to speed it up I would just apply the gel to my nails and I never got length. So I did it the way it tells u to and it made a huge difference literally lol
2) to make it easier to spread the gel use rubbing alcohol. In a small bowl put some rubbing alcohol and before u apply the gel to the nail dip ur brush into the alcohol wipe some off then apply the gel onto the nail. That’s the slip it gives and makes it less thick and goopy to work with
3)bc the nail setter is not that many watts u will have to set it several times to get it to actually set. I did it at least 5-7 times but I guess it also depends on how much gel you use
Overall I think it’s not bad for a newbie and will def use again but I will buy a drill for next time. The drill will help with removing the gel later and makes it much easier when u have to fix mistakes One of the gel tubes did pop broke I don’t know if it was my error but but just something to add in this review. I loved the fact it came in a cute portable box to contain everything together. I would buy again but it was tricky to learn and u definitely need patience. The first 2 hours we’re trying to figure it out and I only finished my right hand. Once I got to my left hand forget it i lost my patience ( I was tired) and all the nails popped off. I gave up and tried the next morning and got it done in 45 minutes.

title: Magnets are too weak!!
text:
Update: The top pair in the 234 was my favorite because it's the most natural looking but after 2 uses, one of the magnets fell off! This brand has quality issues. I decided to order many other brands of magnetic lashes (Newcally, LAMIX, Coolours) and I found that the magnets for the Yiwamica's lashes are considerably weaker. The other brands lashes would pop on and when pulled off would pull my skin a little. This brand's magnets do not do that. I have to press the eyelashes on and then corners would dislodge. I thought it was due to the liner but no, it's the magnets! Between the magnets falling off completely and the weak magnets, I'm downgrading from 4 to 2 stars.

As for the styles, I bought 3 sets from this listing: 230, 231, and 234. See my photo.

The 234 is a set of 3 with a natural pair, a denser natural pair same length, and a longest natural pair. The length difference is probably 1mm, very hard to tell on the tray (I didn’t measure with ruler or anything) but you can tell in person when wearing them. I think only the first pair looks truly natural on me for everyday use because I have small Asian hooded eyes. The other two in the 234 tray are sort of natural but I would not use them for day time use.

The 231 has 2 pairs that looked the same as the longest pair in the 234 set...again not natural enough for small eyes for day time use.

The 230 has crisscrossed lashes where it is longer towards the outer corners and shorter towards the inner. These lashes are longer than those in the 231 and 234.

I ended up returning 231 because it was a repeat of my least favorite pair in the 234 set.

The 230 box had quality issues. One of the lash strands was super long on one of the lashes. The 230 set was also glued to the plastic holder instead of magnetized to strips on the tray like the other two sets. When I removed the lashes from the holder, the middle magnet fell off 2 of the lashes!

I also got a eyeliner and 2 lash pair set from the same company. You can see in my photo. That eye liner turned out to be really bad so I returned that.

Instead, I use the Aroama brand of magnetic liner also sold on Amazon (the one with over 1,000 reviews) with these lashes. The magnetics in these lashes are sorta big but since I have to draw the liner really thick for them to stay at all, it’s tough to even notice the magnets. The thick liner could also contribute to the lashes not looking as natural.

I want to mention the magnet spacing is inconsistent across this brand. There are always 5 magnets but some are gapped evenly while others you get 2 magnets on each end and one in the middle with a huge gap on each side. The ends of the lashes do tend to detach from the eye easily for me as compared to the middle so the configuration with 2 magnets on the ends helps me. The spacing is purely up to your preference though. Pay attention to the product photos to see which magnet spacing you would get.

title: I highly advise that you stay away from this kit if you want to keep the hair on your head
text:
Although I didn't purchase this kit on Amazon, I'm writing this review so that others who are looking up reviews on this product will have a point of reference. At this point in time there are no reviews on Amazon for this product. I purchased this at Big Lots a few days ago and decided to try it out tonight. It is a 17 piece set that includes 6 rollers, 3 of one size and 3 of another, one really tiny detangler comb, and the rest of the kit are bobby pins. I washed my hair and upon trying to be detangler comb I found it was completely useless so I used my own full sized comb and sectioned a portion of the top of my hair and rolled it in one of the smaller rollers. I didn't feel like it was sitting properly so I tried to unroll it to reposition it, which is something that you can easily do with any other roller I have ever tried, and yet this kit has self adhesive rollers that completely grabbed onto my hair and I could not unroll it. I ended up having to rip hair out of my head in order to get the roller off of my head. I am just going to throw this kir awat because I cannot lose hair just to get some beach waves. I have no idea what kind of hair goody used to test this product out, but it's completely useless. I've been a fan of most of their other products but definitely not of this one.

Just for reference I have medium length, thin, straight, fine brown hair. I wasn't working with any kind of strange textures (coarse, thick, unruly, curly, crimped, etc) that typically would grab on to rollers.

title: Very hydrating, but left my face sticky. 4 stars ✨
text:
This is only my second time using a face mask, and this one was a much better experience than the last. I chose the morning to do the mask while I was having my morning coffee, checking the computer, and using my LED White light therapy lamp. The Mask itself is made of a very durable fabric like material that does not tear. The serum is nice and silky feeling without any scent, that I could tell. I appreciate that, as I have a sensitivity to certain smells.
For me, the mask was a little bit short on the forehead and not wide enough on the cheeks. I don't have a large face at all, and I had quite a bit of skin left to cover around the sides and top.
There's an ample amount of serum left in the package that I was able to keep re-wetting the mask with, as it seemed to dry fairly quickly. I also rubbed some on my neck and decollete. I left it on for about an hour, so that my skin could soak in as much as possible. I then used the mask to rub the rest on my neck, decollete, and the backs of my hands. I wanted to make use of every bit I could. I use Retin-A on my face, and had done a treatment the night before, so my skin really needed the hydration and nourishment. It looked and felt very hydrated and nourished afterwards.
The only thing I did not care for was that my skin was very sticky after removing the mask, and it stayed that way. I ended up having to take a damp cloth and blotting it off. After that, my face felt a bit greasy, and I had to keep blotting it until it was time for my bedtime skincare routine.
Overall, I really enjoyed using this mask and will be using it at least once a week. It is very hydrating and nourishing, I just wish it didn't leave the sticky and greasy feeling behind. Maybe, I left it on too long, as I do have combination normal to oily skin. Next time I will only leave it on for about 15 minutes, as I think that may work much better for me. I would definitely recommend this mask, but would also recommend starting with less time than I did if you have combination to oily skin.

title: Might be the best out there for the $, but not terribly impressed
text:
I purchased this unit to replace a 7-year old Norelco trimmer (that had an integral main blade and an integral mini pop-up blade, but no vacuum).

Good Points: Comfortable, not too noisy, even on "Turbo" setting. Strong blades clip everything in sight. Mini trimmer blade is sharp and precise. Guide pops off easily. Comfortable to hold. Vacuum does pick up lots of beard/stache clippings and it's easy to empty clippings,too. Easy to change lengths. Nice travel bag. Battery life excellent (but do NOT overcharge and obey the drain-to-zero recommendations).

Bad Points: Vacuum not strong enough to suck up all clippings...you'll still need to trim over a sink or trash container, which really takes away from the advantage of having the vacuum (even on the Turbo setting). Length indicator needs a stronger click-and-hold ratchet mechanism -- too easy to accidentally change length settings. I miss the pop-up mini trimmer: Having to manually swap out blades is a pain. The trimmer can't stand up, even temporarily...it can only be stored in the bag or lying down.

Summary:
This trimmer might be the best compromise of cost / features / functionality out there, but was disappointed with the vacuum capabilities even on Turbo. I was very impressed by the cutting quality.

title: Excellent hand cream
text:
UPDATE - 09/30/16 ========================================
Still loving this moisturizer and just ordered another package. This stuff goes on well, absorbs quickly into the skin and doesn't leave a greasy feeling! My skin feels truly moisturized. I love using it on my hands and feet before bedtime, this way it really absorbs into my skin overnight.
Love it, love it, love it!

========================================================
Not many people know this, or give it another thought sometimes - anything you put on your skin gets absorbed through the skin and ends up in the blood stream. This is why I am rather careful when picking my skin care products. I have been staying away from most hand creams for a while now just because for the most part there's at least a few potential carcinogens lurking among the ingredients. Even though the big famous brand creams make your skin feel wonderful the question is if the trade off is worth it.

Unfortunately, even so called organic products aren't always that safe. Provided, manufacturers of this goodness are disclosing all the ingredients on the label (and not hiding anything) this cream looks safe enough to eat. Therefore, I have been happily slathering it all over my hands (and any other body parts needing additional moisture) in the past few weeks and I am quite pleased with the results.

This white fluffy goodness feels surprisingly light and absorbs quickly into the skin. I must admit, it is a tad thinner in texture than I had expected but on the other hand this lightness ensures there's no oily residue left on your hands. The cream has no scent whatsoever which is a definite positive for those who are sensitive or don't particularly appreciate scented products. I'm adding a drop of essential oil of my choice (whatever I feel like that day) when I apply the cream if I feel like smelling something nice. Basically this cream is your blank canvas and leaves much room for creativity.

One thing I would probably change about this product is the packaging. (At least maybe as an option for buyers to choose from) I really think that tubes are better for hand creams - way easier to dispense and so much more hygienic (sticking your fingers into the container doesn't really help keep it germ free). Other than that I am happy to give this product my approval.

I purchased this product at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review, all opinions are based on my own personal experience with the product.

title: Permanent lightening with consistent use
text:
This product is intended for permanent skin lightening and will require weeks to take effect. So if you are looking for immediate results, I recommend Shouvy's BB whitening cream with SPF30; it is a cosmetic lotion which gives instant whitening but does not physically alter skin tone.

This is a blend of effective natural whitening agents with additional properties beneficial for skin. These ingredients have been demonstrated to even skin tone, lighten hyperpigmentation, build collagen and inhibit the production of melanin. The skin lightening agents in this product are as follows. Google each for further information, but in brief summary:

Glutathione has been called the mother of all anti-oxidants. Clinical research has shown glutathione significantly lowers the skin's melanin content in as little as 10 weeks.

Kojic acid is derived from mushrooms, used as a skin lightening agent because it inhibits the protein tyrosinase from producing melanin. Kojic acid alone has shown effects faster than most other lightening agents, beginning at about 6 weeks.

Even faster is Artocarpus Lakoocha Heartwood extract. Used alone, it has shown significant whitening effect after only 4 weeks of application.

Coenzyme Q10 aka ubiquinone is a chemical substance naturally produced by our own cells. Applied topically, it can help lighten freckles, age spots, acne scars, and other discolourations. Q10 may also help enhance regeneration of skin cells, thereby reducing the appearance of wrinkles.

Vitamin C provides surprisingly high level lightening and increased UV protection while helping to fade sun/age spots and freckles. Vitamin C is also proven to boost glutathione levels which further helps lighten skin. It also enhances collagen synthesis and increases cell turnover, which makes it a popular ingredient in anti-aging serums.

All together this should be effective in treating melasma (dark pigmentation), acne scars, freckles and age spots. The company does not mention SPF but the inclusion of titanium dioxide, coenzyme Q10 and vitamin C would be expected to provide some degree of UV protection.

Before applying whitening lotion, you should perform a patch test. This is a good practice before using any skin care product, but especially those containing parabens. (common allergen) Just dab a little on your wrist or inner elbow and wait a few minutes. If you experience any signs of irritation such as redness, itch, or swelling, of course discontinue use.

My skin is somewhat pale, but tans easily, so I always have one arm darker than the other simply from being exposed to sunlight in the car. I will conduct an experiment using this lotion on the one arm only, and report my findings. Whitening creams do require several weeks to produce results, and the effect increases over time. For now I can only say that it goes on smooth and silky and has a pleasant scent.

***EDIT - I've now been using this product for several months, and just raised my rating from 3 stars to 4. Yes this lotion actually does work. Not surprising, with those ingredients. If you don't mind using a product that physically alters your skin's production of melanin, and are willing to use this daily, it will absolutely lighten your complexion a shade or two. Just be patient and give it two or three months to achieve full lightening potential.

Where this stuff really excels is over any kind of nail art (decals, rhinestones, striping tape, loose glitter, etc). It seals it down perfectly and seamlessly, helped in part by its thick formula. This easily adds a pastel color to my lighter hair with a smallish amount of product.  I could see that to change up dark hair or to get a strong/intense color tone, you'd need to pile this stuff on, and I think that's where this gets a bad rap. Yes, you can glob this on to higher opacity and change your dark colored hair to the color shown in the jar. BUT, you need a lot to do this, and you may not like the sticky, waxy result -it is wax, after all. If you are using a little bit (about a quarter sized blob) and adding this through your washed and wet hair and then blow dry, your hair will still move naturally and have the lighter tone of the product, provided your hair was fairly light to begin with-- just my two cents.

title: Works great!
text:
Top it off (gloss) is a big hit. It does a great job with sealing your gel manicure and lasting a long time. I appreciate that isn’t too thick and gloppy.

The matte top coat is an odd duck. It’s not suuuuper-matte, but it works really well for my purposes. I have a crazy nail (after a little accident) with a thin vertical strip that constantly splits. If you imagine that would be painful, you would be correct, so I cover that nail in clear gel polish. The matte-ness is pretty close to the sheen of a natural nail so it’s not immediately obvious unless you look super close (and even then). So I don’t have to wear nail polish if I don’t want to, but if I do, I can just paint regular polish over this. And if you use a non-acetone polish remover, you can even switch shades without this coming off.

The only reason I knock off a star is because the matte isn’t impervious, and it will pick up fabric dyes and other colorants fairly easily. Sometimes I’ll look down and notice that one nail is looking pretty grey (like the lenses on sunglasses), which is frustrating.

Take off is not too bad. Those crazy clips that hold cotton pads to your fingertips and some acetone will make short work of this in about 15 minutes with no scratching that damages your nail plate. People whine that gel is bad for your nails, but if I remove it properly, it doesn’t hurt them a bit, at least not in my experience. In fact, my nails grow pretty long and strong with this on.

title: Fairly inexpensive 100% remy hair, however, they don't really last more than two-weeks.
text:
I've been purchasing these extensions for the past year. I continued purchasing them after the first time because they ARE 100% remy hair and I've paid more than what these cost with other sellers claiming that their extensions were 100% remy hair when actually they appeared to be part Barbie hair and real hair. This is the reason I am giving this seller a 4 star. However, after a year of purchasing these, I am trying out a new seller (even lower price and 62% 5 star rating) because of the following reasons:

1. These extensions are very thin at the ends.
2. The ends require trimming as they appear to already be splitting when you receive them (so you have to make certain you order a length longer than you want to leave room for trimming).
3. The tape is really bad. However, this is not a reason I would never order from this seller again. I typically take the original tape off and replace them with better tape before I put them in.
4. No matter what type of shampoo/conditioner I use (sulfate free) or how often I wash my hair (twice a week), these extensions get dry/brittle/frizzy very quickly. And I do use Chi heat protectant prior to blow drying & flat ironing.
5. I consider myself in the mid-stages of DIY (I watch YouTube videos to find out how other DIY hair extension users prolong the use of the hair extensions, etc.), however, no matter what measures I take to keep them in my hair for more than two-weeks, I am still spending too much time and effort on the upkeep and replacing the tapes and putting them back in.
6. According to the description, these extensions are treated with a shed-free treatment to keep them from shedding, however, these extensions shed a lot. Obviously, if they are brittle/frizzy, they are going to break off.

I wanted to wait until I had purchased these extensions multiple times before writing my review so that I would be able to post a fair and honest review. Also, when I first started purchasing these, I was a newby at putting in and replacing hair extensions. And this review does not mean that I will never purchase these extensions from this seller again. They do have a good return policy that I could have used. Prior to purchasing from this seller, I had purchased hair extensions that were very expensive that I will never purchase from again. I do appreciate that this seller is not overpriced.

title: Thrilled with this mask!!
text:
I love this product! It comes in a small container so I was kind of bummed at first, but what little product is in here packs a powerful punch. I highly recommend this if you're looking for a clay or mud type of mask to clarify and clear your skin. I suffer from deep cystic acne and broke out earlier this week. I put on this mud mask and I could not believe how great the results were. Within one day my pimples had disappeared and even my damage spots seem to be less noticeable. My skin felt super soft and clear.

I have a pretty sensitive skin but I didn't have any irritation from this whatsoever. The package says to leave the mask on for 10 or 15 to 20 minutes but I noticed that even after 20 minutes, the mask still was not dried so I did leave it on for longer. It is a bit of a drying mask so if you already have dry skin, you will want to use a moisturizer following the mask. I found that when I combined it with my acne medication that contains benzoyl peroxide and salicylic acid, it was just to drying for my skin. Therefore, I would recommend maybe skipping a day of other chemical products when you use this mask.

The mask it goes on really nice and smooth. I used a Q-tip to mix up the mask material as the directions say to stir it each time you're going to use it. Then I just used the Q-tip to apply the mask and I from layer on my face. The mask has a cooling a fact and isn't a dry or itchy at all. It was a very pleasant experience overall. It wasn't messy at all to use either.

I posted some pictures below of the material in the jar as well as when it was on my face. That way, you can see how quickly I put the mask on my face. I hope the photos are helpful.

Again, I recognize that this is a smaller container than I had previously thought, but you don't need much to cover your entire face. Although I can't say for sure, I am guessing that I would get at least 10 to 15 masks with this product. That is quite a bit considering how much is charged for mud mask facials at spas. Do you make sure that you see all the container tightly and store it in a cool or dark place as it will dry out quickly if you leave it open.

title: NOT Unscented.
text:
I constantly use moisturizer, both on my face and all over. Huge fan of keeping my skin moist and soft. This product had all the right ingredients, plus that enticing "fragrance free."

But this product definitely has a scent to it; perhaps they just mean there's no added fragrance when they designate the product as "fragrance free." That scent might be due to the plum extract, but I'm a plum fan, and the smell was a bit dank and musty for that (although this is my super-sensitive sense of smell doing an interpretation).

Like 2 billion people (in 2021), I suffer from chronic migraine headaches, and like 95% of those, I'm sensitive to smells. Very sensitive. Too much laundry soap is untenable. I can handle most essential oils, but manufactured scents may actually trigger a migraine. I can't have such a smell anywhere close to my nose, like, say, on my skin (or especially on my face).

Although the initial application felt wonderful on my arm, where I test products, the smell was intolerable for me, and I had to wipe it off. I'm really bummed - it felt exceptionally good, but I just couldn't cope with the scent. That's definitely a me thing - not everyone is so scent-sensitive, and it may work great for you...just not for me.

title: Nice mirror for make up
text:
I have never been the type of girl to stand in front of a mirror and do make up for long periods of time. I have used a hand mirror for years, I prefer to sit somewhere like a bed or couch and do my make up. Using a hand mirror is harder though because you then only have one hand to work with the make up. While I don't do a ton, opening things like mascara or doing eye liner is a lot harder when you only have one hand.

This mirror stands up on it's own, so you don't have to hold it. It has a pretty red exterior and it even lights up. The light is not a really bright one, but enough to light up your face if you are in a room that is not as bright as you would like. The rim lights up on both sides, the regular mirror side and on the zoomed in mirror side. There is a place to plug it in, but no plug, so you can choose that option if you have a plug. I used the 3 AAA batteries that it came with. It works well for me to be able to do my make up without having to stand in the bathroom and I don't have to hang onto a hand mirror.

title: Definitely not universal, but great if you have a dryer that it fits
text:
I don't think this item should be marketed as a "universal diffuser." I tried it with a mid-range Remington, a high end T3, a mid-range Conair, and a low end generic dryer. The only one this diffuser worked with was the Conair. Unless you have a BIO IONIC dryer you run the risk that this item will not fit your dryer.

When I finally found a dryer that worked with this diffuser, the diffuser worked well. This diffuser is very well made compared to the diffusers that come with most dryers. First, it's larger than typical diffusers. Second, it swivels to open and close the air vents. I find that it's best used when my hair is nearly dry to put the finishing touches on. I was a bit skeptical of what a diffuser would offer at this price point, but I think the build quality warrants the price.

Overall, I proceed with caution when ordering this product unless you have the BIO IONIC. If you do own the BIO IONIC, this item is fantastic and I highly recommend it.

title: Smooth long curls
text: Keratin’s make the hair smoother (NOT STRAIGHT), shinier, and frizzy free for up to 8 months depending on the strength of the product. Keratin treatments rebound the keratin in your hair so that they are all put back into place. There are a lot of steps but don’t get discouraged because they’re quiet simple. To start of give 2 good shampoos with a clarifying shampoo (specifically the keratin complex one, then towel dry and blow dry the unconditioned hair. Once fully dry, make small sections and apply the treatment from roots to ends and comb through with a fine tooth comb to make sure hair is fully saturated. Let that sit for 30 minutes then blow dry again without washing out the product. Once fully dry the final step will be to straighten the hair with a flatiron so the keratin will set in your hair. After you’re completely done you won’t be able to wash your hair for up to 3 days depending on the strength in the solution.

title: Great for DIY...
text:
Not only are these sheets good for do-it-yourself masks, but they're fabulous at making any good serum a high-end mask.
What I like to do is open one of the individual packets and pull out the tablet, which is a compressed mask. And then, I take very hot water in order to get it to open up. After cleansing my face, I will load it with serum, and then put the warm mask over my face. It's easy to pat it into your skin to make it stay.
Lean back and relax, I generally do it for half an hour.
Remove the mask and gently massage the remaining serum into your face, and continue with your facial routine of moisturizer, sunscreen, whatever you use next.
So, whether you dip them in pineapple juice, apple cider vinegar, or whatever your DIY routine is, or you use a prepared serum from your favorite brand, these are convenient, easy to use, and relatively inexpensive.
I especially like the individual packaging because they stay sanitary. I can pop a couple of them in my makeup bag and always be ready to go on any adventure that requires an overnight stay.
Thanks for reading.

title: I liked the idea better than the product
text:
With four cats and a large dog, I am always looking for good grooming tools. I liked the idea of this brush, but the actual product really wasn't all that. First of all, this thing is much larger than any other slicker style brush I have. This is a great feature for my large dog, but it was just ridiculous trying to groom my cats with this large, unyielding wire brush. So, not a good choice for the cats.

Unfortunately, not a good choice for my dog either, as she has a short coat with little to no undercoat and she was really uncomfortable with wires dragging on her skin. She's more of a rubber curry comb type gal, I guess. Besides the size and wire bristle problems, the plastic itself felt a little brittle and cheap and when you add in the mechanics of retractable bristles... I think higher quality material would have been a better choice because that slider for the bristles is very basic. Finally, while I loved the idea of the easy-to-clean retractable bristles, they really aren't necessary and if those wires become crooked or bent it will cause all kinds of problems with the retraction. I've made it decades by just pulling the fur out of my slicker brushes-- it literally takes 2-3 seconds-- and while the thought of retractable bristles is nice, it totally isn't necessary. It's not a practical tool for me and doesn't work for any of my animals due to its size and the wire bristles. It also doesn't seem terribly well-made nor is it made of high-quality materials, and for the price it should be.

title: Not good if looking for neat, piecey and textured-wavy/curly hair look
text:
First things first - I'm a guy with short thick wavy/curly hair (I think somwhere between 2/3a).

The look I go for is wavy but neat and piecey-looking curls and a strong gel hold which often makes my hair feel crunchy but looking good.

Regarding this particular product:

- It has a decent hold - definitely above medium - but I would not describe as "max hold"
- It does leave the hair feeling crunchy but I think that this is dependent on how much product you add to your hair
- It did an 'ok' job controlling frizz but did not provide the neat, piecey/wavy curl look I go for and have obtained with other products
- It curled my hair more than when it is dry
- It smells good but it's not overpowering
- It is MUCH better than a similar product - Garnier Fructis Style Curl Scrunch Gel, 6.80 Ounce - regarding it's gel hold and frizz control

What I have used in the past that has worked perfectly is for my specific need/look has been:

1. L'oreal Studioline Grab, Extreme Texture & Structure, Instant Texture (discontinued)

2. Sexy Hair Short Sexy Hair Hard Up and Slept In-Hard Holding Gel and Texture Crème (costs more than I want to spend and the pump bottle craps out after half way through it).

3. Garnier Fructis' mess maker hair putty + power gel disorder (ultra strong hold). This does the job but the hair putty doesn't seem to be available in stores anymore and it's too expensive on amazon. Axe seems to have two products very similar to these two by Garnier that I will likely try.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
These plates are just cheaper (price-wise and quality) versions of Konad plates. You get 21 plates for about $18, and shipping is free, so that's quite an irresistible deal, but I have to say, these plates CANNOT compare to the Konad plates.
First of all, there is no safety backing on the plates, as many people have written already; the plates are very thin, and can be very sharp. I resorted to pasting the plates to index cards so it's less likely to slice into my fingers, and to prevent the plates from scratching each other.
Secondly, the designs of the plates are not as intricate and well done as the Konad plates. I have a bunch of Konad plates, and the BM designs definitely don't come close. The BM designs are not as detailed, and just are not as "pretty" as the Konad designs (but of course, you get what you pay for). Also, some of the plates I got, seems like there were manufacturing flaws. The designs on the plates appear smeared, or smudged, and when I tried to stamp them, the images do not transfer properly, if at all.
Thridly, the full nail designs don't actually fit on your whole nail (unless you have really small hands, or are a child). I learned that if I'm very precise on how I stamp, I can get away with stamping the "full nail" designs from my index to my pinky. Thumb is definitely out of the question, lest you end up with a half stamped thumb, or you're good enough to stamp in two halves (you have to really match up the designs). I've never had this problem with Konad designs.
Fourthly, some of my plates arrived with water and rust stains. I don't understand how this happens, since there is a thin Saran type film ontop the plates when you first get them. This must mean that the plates have somehow gotten wet during manufacturing process, but before the packaging process. This doens't interfere with the stamping process, but I just find it annoying to have rust and water marks on my plates.
Overall, these plates are dirt cheap (under a dollar for each plate), compared to Konad which are between $4-7 per plate, but you get what you pay for, and Bundle Monster plates definitely do NOT compare to the quality of Konad's.

Yet isn't a big bulbous excess of material either. But I am definitely pushing max space available (again, I have a large head).

I simply dont wash my hair every day, but I do hop in the shower. I dont notice my hair getting wet at all, but I dont put my head in the water even with this on. I have a spray nozzle for washing and rinsing, so I guess I am able to control where the water reaches better.

The fit is surprisingly good. The rear has an elastic portion to provide a nice fit. The spacing left over once in place is reasonable for my large head and mane of hair. I really was skeptical, but am glad I went ahead and got this. I have some cute shower caps, but none as nice as this. The little bow on top makes me feel like I went back in time to the 50s or something. Adorbs!

I dont use it for keeping my hair out of face for make up or skin care, but it would certainly do well for that too. Also, if I had pool.. while it isnt a pool cap, if I just wanted something to help keep excess water off my hair while casually wading in a pool, this very well could work for that too.

title: Painful and kind of flawed
text:
Pros
• Sturdy and durable – The tweezers themselves are aluminum, but surprisingly sturdy.
• Great carrying case – Tweezers fit inside tube, just like a lipstick!
• Convenient mirror – Located inside of plastic tube that stores the tweezers.
• Easy to understand – Push a button and use.
• Light – Bright blue, useful in a way.
• Packaging – The packaging is honestly one of the best I’ve received a beauty product in. The bag is sheer with a ribbon in place for the draw string. It’s already filled with my other beauty products. The carrying case is what makes it though! It looks like a tube of lipstick, and when you remove the tweezers there’s a little mirror inside.
• Bellabe-esque spring wand – It works! It hurts like anything but man, it gets the job done. Beware areas with high density hair, it will nearly bring tears. Also, I didn’t find it effective on the outer lying hairs of my eyebrow, I believe the skin is too loose.

Cons
• Light – The button is flimsy and seems like it may break eventually. Also, when I attempted to turn the light off the first time I accidentally held down the button which actually made the light strobe. Also, it may seem silly but I felt like the light was a little too bright and washed out the area of my skin I was attacking. Finally, the light takes 3 of those watch like batteries, and I’m sorry to say that the odds of me taking time out of my day to go get these things once it dies are very slim. It does come with them included though, so for now that’s not an issue.
• Mirror – The mirror is definitely a convenience and the placement is a great idea, however, I feel like it would be more useful if the mirror was a magnifying one so I didn’t need to hold it so close to my face.
• Tweezers – The ends are not as slanted as I would like, and while I may be just tweezer challenged, I found myself chasing the same strand of hair for minutes at a time. It would be great if you could switch the tweezers that the light attaches to, but that doesn’t seem possible.

title: Horrible Flavor, Non-Existent Results
text:
Being a tea and coffee drinker, my teeth have a tendency to stain from time to time. I have used OTC whitening products in the past with a lot of success. I was originally looking at the Colgate pen, but saw very mixed reviews and decided to go with this one.

Packaging, top notch. The colors, construction, and branding are all on point. However, that's where, for me, the good news ends.

To start the pen, be prepared to click 30-40 times to get the first bit of gel to come out. After that, sometimes just opening the pen is enough to cause it to ooze... other times, you are going to be clicking 5-10 times to get it to dispense the gel.

To prepare the teeth, I use a Kleenex to wipe the teeth down so they are dry. I apply a generous coating of the gel to all the teeth in front (top and bottom)... Once applied, I leave the mouth open and teeth exposed to allow the coating to dry (suggested was 30 seconds... I went up to 1.5 minutes with no difference). Once you close your mouth, the product immediately starts foaming (H2O2). The flavor is not good... I know this is subjective... but it is like dropping cinnamon red hots into Vanilla Coke... letting it set until flat and then watering down to almost no flavor... [in short, back wash.]

After 9 days, there has been no change in the color of my teeth. I have used a color guide from my dentist to follow the process, and I have stayed right around a 6.

Horrible taste, ineffective whitening, more than $20... Yeah, not for me.

title: Avoid. Buy a 'true' Sonicare
text:
The lifespan of this device seems to be quite limited. A couple of years ago, I bought 2 of these for my 2 boys. One of them stopped working after a couple of weeks - was able to return it to Amazon and get a replacement - and the other stopped after a little over one month. The replacement stopped working after about one month as well.

The big problem with this toothbrush is the battery compartment. Since it's using 'throw away' batteries, a bad thing by itself, there is a need for a lid to allow removal/insertion of batteries. At this price, the lid does not close tightly and water creeps in. Eventually, the entire thing stops working.

Pros for this toothbrush:
- low price.

Cons:
- short life due to almost inevitable water damage
- use of 'throw away' batteries

My recommendation: avoid.

Spend a few more and get a true Sonicare. You won't regret it. I've been using Sonicare tooth brushes for almost 10 years now. My first one was replaced after more than 5 years, mostly because I wanted a new one. My current is alive and kicking and it's likely to last for many more years if I don't choose to replace it.

4. Slip foot into a gallon size Ziplock bag to avoid spills
5. Sit with feet on the ground to avoid spills or tearing the bags for 1 to 2 hours

7. To speed up the peeling process, do not moisturize feet the first day

My 7yr old, and I were so excited to get these to hold her many, many large Jo Jo Siwa bows. I was expecting the ribbon to be a little thicker, and longer. It holds 4 large 8 inch bows comfortably. Possibly 5, however because the ribbon is really thin, it doesn't hang straight when holding, organizing, or using. The ribbon twists around, and doesn't hang straight at all. There just isn't enough space for what we need either. I think these would be great for smaller bows, tho. They look just as pictured. I'm just now learning about the different types of ribbon out there to hold the larger bows more stable. I have not found or purchased a new set, yet. I think if these were longer, it might not have been a complete miss for what I was looking for. The set with the crowns and the ribbon rings as the hooks, do fit over my daughter's dresser draw knobs, which I was hoping, and looking for when ordering. I'm still giving them a 3 star review, because they would be nice for other's needs as I've mentioned. A suggestion would be to make much longer ones. I'm not upset with the product itself, as much as I am upset that I didn't realize that these are not ideal for a lot of large bows. They are pretty!

title: Great sheet masks that works wonders for your face
text:
In this pack you get 3 masks for $18, so this is one on the more expensive face sheet masks that I have tried. I like that it is biodegradable since we really should do more for our environment so I find this to me a big plus. This mask has some very nice ingredients in it like Vitamin C that is from pineapple and others. It is free of parabens, phthalates, mineral oil, gluten, formaldehyde and vegan friendly.

You use this mask like you use most. Clean your face and apply it to the cleaned face. Then leave it on for about 15 to 20 minutes and after you removed it gently massage In the remaining serum. This mask has a good amount of serum on it so you can easily leave it on for 20 minutes without having to worry that it will dry out, you could probably go longer yet. My face was a bit sticky afterwards but that feeling did go away after about minutes or so. The serum in the mask had a pleasant smell that I did like a lot. My face felt nicely moisturized when I used this mask and looked great. All in all this is a great mask I just wish it was not as expensive to be honest since it is not on the cheap sice to be used weekly.

title: Mediocre effort to create a cheap sonic brush, better options available
text:
This product attempts to bring sonic toothbrush technology to the sub-$20 price bracket. It does not entirely suceed, and though nicely designed, it is not very effective at its job.

The Sonic toothbrush as invented by Philips uses a high speed pulsing (> 30,000 rpm) to use fluid below the gumline to help vibrate dirt and plack off the teeth. This process is gentle, effective, and leaves the teeth feeling and looking very clean. I've used these brushes and they are great.

The downside to this marvel is that Philips charges roughly $80-$130 for their Sonicare brushes. Oral B has their own latecomer Sonic Complete model (which costs about $100) and a number of lower cost designs that use a more conventional oscillating mechanical head to clean teeth.

The problem here is the corners Oral B cut to bring you a $20 sonic brush. The brush vibrates at a much lower speed (20,000 rpm) and though it uses the same brush head as the more expensive Sonic Complete, it does not clean teeth anywhere near as well as a faster sonic brush. The 1/3 speed difference evidently is very significant in the ability of the brush to get the ol chompers clean.

If you want a sonic brush, spend more money than this. If you want a cheaper brush that is fairly effective at cleaning your teeth, try the Oral B Vitality Dual Action ($18) or the Oral B Cross Action Power Max ($12).

The dual power head action of these designs, though not sonic, is a reasonable compromise in getting teeth clean while also keeping price low. The Vitality Sonic just spins its wheels without doing much.

The design and function of the Vitality Sonic is ergonomic and reasonably high quality, but for a low cost cleaning solution, buy something else, and if you want the high-tech sonic experience, then spend more.

The few that comment say it looks nice since my beard has blacks, several shades of dark brown but it annoys me! The Grizzly natural beard color works pretty good for me but I was wanting something to completely wipe out the gray hair. I tried this Godefroy Tint Kit and was very disappointed with it. After testing it and finding the right mixture (wife helped), I applied it to 4 areas that have graying. Both cheeks have a little strip of gray and at the top of my sideburns where they connect with my hair (I'm bald so taking a guess). I left it on for the directed time, started washing it off and one sideburn started burning. It wasn't a terrible burn but it was bad enough to speed me up. When I got out of the shower, I had a red mark about 2 inches long right beside the top of my sideburn. I put some aloe on it and went to bed. The next morning, I got up and the red spot was peeling like it was sunburn! It had burnt me to some extent. What color did go on wasn't that good. Maybe I should have used black. I might try it again in the future and try to be more careful about letting it get on unprotected, no hair, areas of my skin but for now, I would only recommend it if you're comfortable in your ability to keep it on the hair.

title: Excellent lather, performance and scent; fussy bottle
text:
I'm impressed with this face soap. It's very thick and silky, and only a very small amount is needed to get good results. That's especially welcome to find out given the price for a pretty small bottle. It lathers up well and does a good job of cleaning without leaving my skin overly dry. It is a bit more intensive than other face soaps, so my face does feel a little 'tight' after using it. However, it's not excessive, and well worth it given how well this soap cleans if you have an oily complexation. The charcoal makes the soap dark, but it's not as jet-black as other charcoal soaps I've used. It's more of a deep gray.

The scent is also quite nice. It's a medium/light intensity and has sort of an after-shave smell to it. The scent does not linger much at all after rinsing. While I tend to prefer unscented soaps, this scent is pleasant and enjoyable.

The only con is the bottle. Getting the pump nozzle to pop up was a chore since the retaining ring the pump head screws into also rotates, making it a struggle to get the nozzle to pop up. I eventually got it working, but have noticed that the pump leaks at the stem. It's a small leak, but it adds up over a few days to make a mess on the bottle and waste soap. Given the price, the pump mechanism should have been of better quality.

One star down for the bottle issues, but otherwise, it's a very enjoyable soap to use.

title: Cheap, but Cheaply Made.
text:
I've had these for almost a year but I haven't used them that much--there are a select few designs that I use regularly, but the majority have remained untouched. Here's why:
-A lot of my plates came damaged; maybe I'm just the unlucky one in a thousand, but many had imperfections in the metal that ruined the images. Other than that, the undamaged plates worked decently. You might run the risk of having damaged plates like me, but I'm guessing this was just my bad luck. Can't really blame the company since I never made the effort to return them, and it's been waaay past 30 days (at the time I was just happy I got them).
-I liked that there were themed and matching stamps, but to be honest I just don't like a lot of the images enough to actually use them. There is an unnecessary amount of tribal/swirly images, and what were they thinking with the ambiguous pair of chili peppers? Take a good look at the individual images and take that into account more than the sheer number of plates. Will you actually use them?
-Unless you have child's hands, the full-nail plates are waay too small--it's most noticeable on the thumbs and middle fingers, but they can barely fit over any of my nails (in terms of width, not length--I don't have crazy-long nails). To avoid awkward-looking nails, I haven't used many of the full nail stamps. Images like the polka-dots are easy to align and restamp, but others not so much.
-They come off a little blurrier than Konads, but nothing too horrible
-Some of the images are nice in theory, but don't show up that well once stamped. For example, there's a cute lace french tip that I just couldn't get to work because it was impossible to pick up the full image.

On the plus side:
-they're cheap, and most of the images are pretty crisp
-A lot of the full-nail designs have matching french tips
-The french tips will definitely (probably) fit over all your nails, including thumbs.
-I like the themed plates--for example, there's a Christmas one and a Halloween one.
-I've heard complaints that these plates were too sharp, but I don't see how you could accidentally hurt yourself with them--maybe they've updated their plate design?

Although I haven't used many of the images, those I do use make the bundle worth it. The total price for all 21 image plates--damaged and unattractive though some may be--is the price of 3 Konad stamps. It's definitely worth the price, but I can't guarantee amazing quality.

title: The line of silver dye we've needed!
text:
I want to start by saying that most of the poor reviews of the SilverWhite line are written by people who clearly don't know what they're doing. This is for light hair, as in WHITE or platinum blonde. If your hair is not light enough, you won't get the results you're looking for, and that isn't the product's fault. With that in mind, these colors are a wonderful alternative to custom silver formulas that require mixing many shades!

I've been dyeing my hair silver for years and I've tried just about every brand of "silver" dye out there with various amounts of success. My hair is naturally a cool dark blonde (ranging from level 7 to 8) and I have to bleach my roots twice to get them light enough for a proper, no brassiness silver. I currently use the Wella T18 toner + 050 for the length of my hair, and do my newly bleached roots with Schwartzkopf Slate Grey + E-1, which fades and blends nicely as new roots grow out. I use Fanola No Yellow shampoo to maintain it. This is a 1:1 dye, meaning you should use the same amount of developer as dye. The great thing about this line is that the dye truly doesn't have any warm undertones (with the exception of the dove grey, which is still cooler than most silvers). I like to add a little E-1 to the slate grey because as with every dye, no matter what brand you use, the cool pigment is the first to fade and adding this extra purple gives it a little more staying power.

I've found that the slate grey does fade more quickly than you would expect from a permanent dye, as it is meant for hair that is naturally grey and has a transparent quality that helps match new grow out; this transparency will also make it VERY obvious if you have any brassy areas or your hair isn't light enough to begin with. Using 20 vol. developer instead of 10 (as is recommended) helps with permanency. The lilac shade also seems to last longer than the other three.

As for being true to color, the slate grey tends to come out darker than shown, and you have to pay close attention to processing time with the silver, which does lean slightly blue and can really take over if you leave it on too long. The dye is relatively gentle since you're using 10 or 20 vol, but don't be tempted to let it process for more than twenty minutes. Both of these color issues will fade within a couple washes if you do though.

TLDR:
These are really great cool shades with little to no warmth and stay true to that as they fade, but
- You MUST have white or near white hair
- Most SilverWhite shades fade quickly, so use 20 vol. developer
- Slate grey is dark and silver leans blue; don't over-process unless you want that

"Dad's" razor had a clam-shell arrangement that accepted blades easily and held them straight when the "doors" were closed with a turn of the handle.  This one has to be dissembled to change blades. Then when the blade is inserted and the blade cover put in place, the blade is free to wobble around in it's "bed", resulting in a potentially dangerous triangle of blade sticking out from the razor.  I was disappointed- glad I spent only $10 on this device.  Serves me right to buy cheap foreign-made stuff.  however, with a new blade properly seated, it shaved well.

title: Short lived, not the best shave
text:
On the plus side, like most mid-line Norelco shavers, it delivers a decent shave, is fairly quiet, and deals with longer hairs fairly well. I've been a loyal Norelco rotary fan for close to 20 years.

Times have changed since Philips bought Norelco. The early Norelcos were the best shavers I could find and lasted a long time. The last several Norelco shavers I've bought, however, have either gone dull and/or the batteries have grown week within a year of buying them. I honestly believe Philips/Norelco is doing this on purpose to sell more expensive replacement blades and shavers? The sad thing is you buy a $70 shaver and the replacement blades run about $40. And, in my experience, the batteries (which cannot be replaced) die before the second set of blades wear out. So you're out $110 in about 18 months and have to buy a new shaver.

Fed up spending a small fortune these last several years on Norelco products that just don't last I tried the latest Braun "360 Complete" shaver and so far am very pleased. To my surprise it shaves MUCH closer than my 8140XL and with less irritation. I don't know how long it will last, but based on the quality of the shave, and their short life, I'm done with Norelco.

title: My skin's holy graile
text: I decided to go the whole 9 yards and try the foaming face wash + 12% souffle + the moisturizer. Just so you know, my skin problems are: Excessively oily skin (need two blotter sheets every hour); uneven skin tone; and clogged pores (disgusting little oil plugs peaking out, some enlarged pores and then those tiny little bumps where the oil plug hasn't hardened yet). I saw immediate results with these products in term of the oiliness and clogged pores. I've only had to blot my face once a day since I started using this stuff - big difference over having to blot every hour.  The enlarge pores and the tiny bumps were greatly minimized. My skin looks  much smoother. I usually use Biore pore strips to remove the plugs so, it is hard to say exactly how effective Alpha Hydros is at getting rid of these. But I don't seem to be developing them as quickly as I was before. Within a week, I saw a noticeable difference in my complexion - much brighter. I don't have wrinkles or zits, so I can't comment on that. But those tiny little clogged pores have been spreading over my face since I was 10! This is the only thing I've used that immediately and consistently improved the condition and appearance of my skin (and the my oiliness) without over drying my face. My skin is actually very supple. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because it's only been a week. I still have yet to see what the ultimate result will be--but looks promising so far.

As someone with very sensitive skin, I have always had problems with razor burn after shaving. Dry electric shavers tend to butcher my skin. Traditional multi-blade razors (like the Mach 3) are easier on my skin, but as sensitive as my skin is, cuts are not uncommon. A few months ago I received a Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a gift and gave it a try. Thanks to the shaving gel that can be applied to the skin at the touch of a button while shaving, it provides a very close shave that doesn't cut my skin like a traditional razor, and there's very little skin irritation afterwards. As for closeness, I'd say that it's almost as good as a Mach 3 razor.

One aspect about this shaver that I like is that it operates from a rechargeable battery so that there's no electric cord to get in the way while shaving. Also, the shaving gel packets are easy to replace, it comes with a charger stand, it's easy to clean the rotating blades and it takes up little bathroom counter space. Further, it takes less time to shave and clean-up afterwards than with a traditional razor & shaving cream.

Overall, I regard the Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a very good shaver and rate it with 5 out of 5 stars. Granted, it is somewhat expensive, but if you have very sensitive skin like me, you might be as pleasantly surprised as I was with its performance.

title: Good. (w/pics)
text:
I like at home spa treatments and have enjoyed most I've tried. I was offered this Molequle Glow & Go mask and thought I would try them out. At time of review 3 masks cost $24.99.

The masks come well sealed as a set inside another bag. My set did not come with instructions for use. The back of the packet only has ingredient information. I had to look on the Amazon product page and with my phone I could not read the instructions on the one picture they have of it- as it was blurry. So from what I think I read you use these masks daily for 20-30 minutes. 1 star was taken off for lack of instructions- there's no real reason it couldn't have been on the packet itself. I'll say when I buy these at home treatments I tend to lean more towards mud masks, gels, and lotions, the biocellulose masks are never very comfortable or fit my oval face well. The eye holes are never big enough and the masks never sit right. This is sadly no exception, I would keep pushing on it while I wore it so another star taken there. Now, the effects: they were pretty good, my face definitely had a glow about it when I removed them. Likely over time and with extended use my skin would lighten more. So at least what they said is very true. They are pricey but if they do what they say and this is the result you want they would be worth the cost. The solution had no smell, absorbed nicely, and felt good, no irritation to speak of. I'd be interested in trying their other masks or more of these even with my small gripes.

title: OMG! I'm in LOVE!!!
text:
Ok...I'm going to try to not write a novel here, but I am sooo in love with these polishes!!! I read a ton on reviews on these peel off polishes and finally chose these not expecting a whole lot. I have 100% no complaints!!! But I will say that I guess it all depends on what you are wanting out of your nail polish. If you are wanting it to last like it lasts on artificial nails... this is not for you. If you are wanting options and to not have to deal with nail polish remover...THIS IS FOR YOU!!!

I have loved painting my nails and having polished nails since a kid. I've always hated nail polish remover. I have thin nails and can't change my polish often because nail polish remover dries my nails out and makes them even weaker and it stinks...even nail polish stinks for that matter.
To make the polish last I've always added a top coat about every day or two and I've learned how to do touch ups that hardly show when the polish on tip of the nail (natural nails) chipped or wore away, so that I didn't have to use acetone any more often than necessary. But it was really self defeating because the more polish I had on, the more acetone I had to use to remove it.
So anyway...I got these little gems in...they are small....but then again, when you compare the price to buying regular polish ( I buy OPI normally ) and the fact that you are getting several colors of these for the price you'd pay for 1 or 2 bottles of decent regular polish, it's not a bad deal at all.
I tried them right away and
#1...they are hardly smell at all! I don't smell them unless I actually hold my nails or the bottle to my nose to smell them.
#2...the polish went on fine. It's a little thick, but it settles down smooth as it dries.
#3 I love some of the colors and some will be just for having fun, but they are fun t play with. 5 colors are opaque and 4 are transparent, so they are fun mixing and matching. I like using the transparent ones as top coats on the opaque ones.
#4 They lasted about 3 days with no chips and very very little edge wear (with the daily addition of a top coat for shine) until I couldn't stand it any longer and had to try to peel them off. Some of the reviews said they were hard to peel off, but I had no problem at all. And all but one came off in one full piece! Amazing!!! So easy and NO ACETONE!!! And the other thing I like is that with regular polish, I would sometimes try and peel of as much as I could before using the acetone and some would come off but my nail always seemed super dry under the polish even when it was peeled off. That is not the case with these at all. My nails were not dry at all. They were still healthy and not dry at all!!!
Oh and the BONUS ....since they peel off, any polish that gets on to your skin peels off easy too after it dries. :)

title: So far this is working well for my sensitive skin; will see how it goes in the long run
text:
First off, I have extremely sensitive skin overall, but especially on my face. To that end, I must be very carefully about what I put on. I do tend towards lighter or no scents, but have found some that work alright for me. But with or without scent, I can still have issues. In the end, it’s how my skin handles anything that is the bottom line for me. In this case, this Provence Beauty Beard Oil - All Natural Fragrance Free Olive, Sunflower & Jojoba Oils works well for me and so far, I’m very pleased.

I use a derma roller a couple times a week to help with hair in my beard and front of my head. At this point I then add a beard oil to these locations to help stimulate growth. Without doing major testing with all the elements, like a control group (area) of my head, it’s hard to say what works and what doesn’t. I feel like the derma roller has a large part in how well growth or at least slowing of loss goes. But, I have also come to believe some of these oils available do play a supportive role. To that point, I won’t be able to speak about this Provence Beauty Beard Oil - All Natural Fragrance Free Olive, Sunflower & Jojoba Oils for awhile. I have only just begun to use it - as a replacement for another oil.

But I do like that 1. it’s not too oily on my hair or skin, 2. has little to no real scent, 3. feels fine and is not a problem on my skin, and 4. that it washes off my hands easily post application. Right now I like it as an oil providing at least some softening to my beard. Will it aide growth? We shall see...

title: Whoa, not what I expected
text:
I can't believe all the high mark reviews for these: These clips are a mess! For reference, I purchased the 20 PCS 19" set (2 @ 10 pack). Let me outline what the issues are:
- First thing is trying to squeeze to open - the outside rubber is highly oiled, loose, and therefore just rotates around and one can't grip on the clip to open. I tried to stabilize with my other hand and the inside clip just rotates away instead of opening even with 2 hands. Almost impossible to open! I am not clumsy or incompetent and tout myself as pretty handy and capable yet these things are flawed right from the start. I wrestle with just trying to use a simple alligator clip and it floors me that the main purpose of these do not work right.
- Some of the clips just don't close properly. The springs are cheap and so forget clipping on a fine wire like a resistor with the ones that won't close properly. I use the flawed ones that don't close all the way on a larger item like my multimeter leads. See photo
- None of these are soldered like many other reviews state. They are crimped. See photo
- The jaws are rough cut and work fine (when you finally get them opened) for larger items but for smaller and very thin items (think resistors) they are not what you want. See photo where I had to bend the resistor wire to get it to stay in the jaws.

While these are inexpensive and fine for the non-discerning use they are by no means competent and have serious flaws that prevent one from using these on many fine and detailed projects. Since there are so many 5 star reviews I can only think the use case would be not for electronics projects and perhaps a set once and forget use?!?

title: Lightweight and well-made
text:
This bag would be PERFECT if it had mesh pockets in the main compartment. I love this style of bag, with the two additional outside pockets, but there aren't a lot of bags in this style and they're all missing something. This one is missing inside pockets. I hope Veckle will add pockets in the future. A slightly smaller everyday bag with a similar design would be great as well.

Anyway, this bag seems very well made. It has SBS zippers which all my Gonex bags have as well, and they've all been excellent. I have like 10 Gonex packing cubes that I've stuffed beyond reason, and the zippers are still perfect. So these zippers should last, too. The top zipper has two sliders so you can open it in either direction.

The bag is made with lightweight materials without any padding or rigid structure, so you can flatten it. If you pack only a little bit of stuff, it stays small. If you pack a lot, it gets bigger. I love that. The main pocket is just for dumping stuff. There's no organization, which I need, so I won't be able to use this bag as a toiletry kit. There is one outside pocket with mesh so you can put your toothbrush or razor in there while it's wet. The other outside pocket has three little elasticized mesh pockets inside to hold things like eye drops or travel contact solution, or little pill cases. Those are the only sub-organization features in the bag. They're nice just not enough for my stuff.

The bag has one closed loop handle that you can hang from a hook. Most of the hotel rooms I've been in recently have one or no hooks, so I learned from my mom to bring a rubber coated S hook with me on trips. They're for holding scarves or whatever on your closet rod. You can hang one from a shower or towel rod and keep your stuff off the tiny hotel room counter.

Anyway really nice bag, just needs more organization for me.

Second, after prepping my skin with an alcohol prep pad (just in case), I taped a very-low-necked top to wear on a moderately warm day. I was out in an air conditioned car for about 20 minutes. When I got home, the tape was still stuck to the fabric like a trooper, but not at all to my skin. In fact, I had to work a little to get the tape off of the fabric.

In the future, I'll try to stick fabric only to fabric, but that may not always be possible depending on the garment, and don't think that is the way this stuff is supposed to work. {Edit: I did try this and, again, the tape stuck to the top garment but not the garment beneath it. Drat.}

I do have sensitive skin and the tape didn't bother me, so 5 stars for that.
