title: I'm allergic to some of the chemicals in this, so it's not for me.
text:
I'm a lip balm addict. Rarely do anything that I don't have a lip balm ready to use at any moment. It's sitting all over the house, at least three varieties in my purse, extras in my travel make up kit--it's EVERYWHERE. While I'd gotten to the point where I only bought the more natural products either from the "health food store" type companies, or online, boutique type companies, Even bought lip oil that comes in a small roller bottle. Have hated some and I haven't loved any of them a lot. Started doing aromatherapy last April. Took two online courses from a reputable aromatherapy company--Natural Living and Butters & Balms. Started making a lot of my skincare products. Even made some of my own herb infused oils as a base for my homemade lip balms and oils. Hadn't love any of those, either. Actually took everything and added beeswax to it to make my own "Healing Lip Balm." I like it a lot, but will never be able to replicate it:)

I had recently bought a natural lip balm that I just loved; however, it didn't have an SPF factor. When I saw the Cal Pharma SPF 30 Mango Lip Balm at a discount for an honest review, I thought I'd try it. I must not have looked at the ingredients when I ordered it (which is VERY unusual for me) because I would have noticed the active ingredients: Avobenzone 3 %, Homosalate 7.5%, Octisalate 5%, Octocrylene 2.75%, Oxybenzone 6%. I have sensitive, allergic, reactive, rosacea skin and am allergic to most commercial sunscreens. In addition to these ingredients, the SPF 30 Mango Lip Balm contains Undecylcrylene Dimethicone. The only one of these chemicals that I could confirm was natural was the Homosalate. Not sure how they call this a natural product. My only excuse is that I'm going to Florida in a few weeks to visit my mother and wanted a lip balm with an SPF factor.

Aside from the issue with the chemicals, I've tried this a few times. For one, the texture is very waxy--too much beeswax. I also feel a tingle on my lips and an itch in my throat, so suspect I'm having an allergic reaction to the SPF 30 Mango Lip Balm. This product is not for me. If you don't have allergic/sensitive skin, and don't care as much about ingredients, this product might be for you. Your other choice is physical blockers--like zinc or titanium oxide. And they give you that whitish cast. Not real desirable, either.

I did receive a discount on this product with the expectation that I provide an honest review. This has no bearing on my rating and I review all products as if I had paid full price. My opinions are from my own personal experience with the product and I have no affiliation with the seller.

title: Thank you Prairie Rose!
text:
Review for: Cocoa Butter Cream Peppermint Body Butter - Mint Cocoa Whipped Body Cream

I love this body cream for so many reasons. To begin with, it arrived inside a clear bag with a silver tie, making me smile at the nice presentation. Being impressed with the packaging was nothing compared to the wonderful aroma that I was treated to when I peeked under the seal and looked at the product. It looked like whipped cream cheese and smelled good enough to eat! The scent is a combination of chocolate and mint. Taking just a tiny bit of the cream in my hands to feel it let me know why it is called velvet body cream. It truly does feel velvety, silky and soft.

I was able to appreciate all of the above before I even tried the product. However, using the product is the real treat. This soft and silky cream is just fun to use. Getting out of the shower and dealing with dry skin in the winter is a pain and this product changes that. Instead of being in a hurry to get some lotion slathered on my skin so I can get dressed, I look forward to pampering myself with this product. I feels so good on my hands while I am applying it to my arms and legs. Of course it smells wonderful too but the really great part is how well it absorbs and leaves my skin feeling hydrated.

If you are looking for a gift for a friend that complains of dry skin in the winter, look no further. Your gift will be appreciated!

Even if it would stick with a thinner line, the magnetic base of the eyelashes is pretty thick so it gives the impression of a thick eyeliner. I think you would have to draw the actual eyeliner thicker than the base so you can control the shape. But I recognize that this is more a makeup style preference than a default of the product.

And then I went to remove the eyeliner. Holy mother of fire demons did that burn so bad! My eyes and skin can be a little sensitive so I'm always extremely careful with what I use to remove makeup and how I remove it. I was being extra careful not to rub as I didn't want to risk getting in my eyes but it still hurt so much. And it was not easy to get off! I always use waterproof mascara and eyeliner so I'm used to that but this was a whole other level of stubborn. And it took a while for the pain to fade completely and my eyes were red for the rest of the day. So yeah, never putting that stuff back on.

Looking at the other reviews, this doesn't seem to be a super common reaction but if you have sensitive skin or eyes, I would pass.

title: take good care of the internal battery
text:
I bought this trimmer two months ago. I use it to keep my hair very short. I have not gone to a barber ever since I bought this. I simply turn the dial to set the guard to level 5 and cut all of my hair the same lenght. Definitely easy to use. On my short hair, I can probably get four complete haircuts in one charge. This is a good trimmer for those men who like to keep their hair very short all the way around. Use it two times and it would have paid for itself due to the fact that you were able to avoid going to a barber.
This is my second Norelco trimmer. My first one was a T6000 that I bought back in February of 2001. The battery stopped taking a charge four months ago, after almost 3 years of use. I called Norelco to have the battery replaced, and I was then informed that they do not replace the batteries on these trimmers since replacing the battery would cost as much as buying a newer unit. So, I ordered the newer T860 from Amazon. The T860 functions just like the older T6000. In addition, the T860 can also function as a corded trimmer, in the event the battery stops taking a charge. The service life of the trimmer can extend beyond the life of the rechargeable battery by using the cord. I am satisfied with it.
By the way, the reason why the battery got damaged in my older T6000 was that I kept the unit plugged in the charger stand for very long periods of time. I later learned not to do that, as that practice will damage the battery over time. Overcharging even a little seems to damage the battery over time. It's best to read the directions so you will know how to properly care for the battery. The battery basically will determine the life of the unit. The cutters do not wear out, from what I can tell. The motor seems durable. So the life of the unit is really how long you can keep the internal rechargeable battery working. Norelco's internal rechargeable Ni-Cad batteries can last a long time, if given proper care. They seem to be of good quality.
I had a Norelco 885 razor, and the battery was still taking a charge after nine years. The razor had the advantage of having a five level battery meter that tells you how much charge is left in the internal batteries. Basically, you want to wait until there is only a little charge left before you put the unit in the charger. It seems this trimmer is a bit different though. The instructions on the T860 unit say to completely drain the battery. Which would be a bit inconvenient. With the T860 trimmer, it takes 10 hours for a full charge. Recharge fully. That way, you can minimize the dreaded "memory effect" or voltage depression and extend the useful life of the rechargeable batteries. The rechargeable batteries are permanently soldered inside the unit. This trimmer unit, T860, does not have a charge meter. I refrained from getting the pricier unit with a charge meter in order to economize. However, my advice to you, if you're not too cost-sensitive, is to get a unit with a charge meter. That way, you will know when to charge the unit and when to remove the unit from the charger. That precise practice should help extend the life of the battery, and hence, the unit.

title: Get a spa quality treatment in 20 minutes.
text:
I love to pamper myself with deep hydrating/anti-aging facial masks. After all, why do I need to spend a fortune on spa treatments when I can have that spa experience in the comfort and privacy of my own home. I received this particular mask at a special price for the purposes of product testing and reviewing. Everything contained in this review is my own personal experience using this mask.
First I made sure my face was freshly washed and found a quiet area where I could apply the mask and lay back and relax for 20 minutes. By quiet area, I mean I made sure I was home alone so no one would bother me, I turned the television off and played some soft soothing music to relax myself and to really give myself that spa experience.
Applying the mask was super simple and it completely fit all the contours of my face evenly. Thereby giving my face all the wonderful benefits of this rich hydrating formula. Then I just relaxed and let the mask do all the work. I have sensitive skin and was pleased that the all natural ingredients in this mask did not irritate my sensitive skin what so ever. In fact, it actually helped improve the look and feel of my skin after just one use. After the 20 minutes were up, I was amazed at how soft and hydrated my skin felt. I had no idea I had let my skin get that dry. I plan on taking time out for myself at least once a week to give myself a deep hydrating, anti-aging mask. After all, the key to younger looking skin, is keeping it well hydrated. I love these masks and would also recommend them. They make you feel great afterward!

title: Ok brush at this price point.
text:
I noticed some other reviews talking about the brush being dirty when they received it. Mine didn't seem to be although I did shampoo it once before I used it. I have a couple other brushes in this price range. The brush head seems to be the same size and consistency of my other two brushes. The handle is a little shorter than one (same length as the other) and narrower/thinner than the handle on both my other brushes. Not horrible but just a little smaller than I was used to. The first couple times I used the brush it did shed maybe 5-6 bristles each time. But that number dropped off drastically and after a couple weeks of use it might loose a bristle every second or third use.
One thing I was happy about was that the complete brush not seems well seated/anchored in the handle. Every other brush i have bought the whole brush head loosened almost immediately and within a couple weeks came out. So i'd have to break out the Gorilla Glue and repair. But this brush seems solid.
The brush works up a decent lather although it is not as easy or as voluminous a lather as my favorite brush and i'm not sure why. The brushes seem very similar. My best guess is the Beau Brummell doesn't seem to retain moisture as well as my other brush.
All in all it is a good brush and a great brush for the price.
Please note that I received this brush at about an 85% discount with the stipulation that I write a review.

UPDATE Nov 19, 2015: So its now been about two months of using this brush about 3-5 times per week. And lately it has been shedding like crazy. Every time I use it I end up with 5-10 loose brush hairs stuck in my shave cream jar or on my face. At this rate it will need rogaine soon. Downgrading my original 4 stars to 3.

title: Better than shaving/nair
text:
I have very long legs and very sensitive skin. I hate shaving because it takes to much time in the shower and I always cut myself. All the nair like products that basicaly burn your hair off make my skin really irritated and I develope a painful rash because you can never wash off all the chemical residue.
Nads is a great alternitive to other hair removal methods, altough it does take some practice to get it right. It takes me maybe 15 min to do both legs and clean up, rinsing the strips etc. You have to apply the gel SUPER THIN (the thiner the better) to get the best results. I know it seems a bit backwards but the thinner you make the gel the more hair it can remove. My legs stay smooth and stubble free for at least 2 weeks and I dont have the annoyance of razorburn and I get far fewer ingrown hairs. Love this stuff, it really works. :*)

title: Not sure I'm doing it right
text:
Starting off this is my first experience with magnetic lashes and false lashes in general. Never liked the idea of glue but wanted to try these.
No clue if I'm doing it right, I followed these instructions, multiple YouTube tutorials, tons of trial and error.
I like that there's a variety of different styles but I can't tell which are supposed to be on what eye. They are idental on both ends on both lashes in each pair.
The tweezers honestly seem useless to me as they're metal so the lashes stick to them which complicates all this lol.
The eyeliners provided aren't ideal (I do felt tip) but usable. I tried thin line, thick line. Didn't seem to matter when putting them on. There's no way to adjust them once they're placed though, the liner comes off with the lashes which kinda sucks for a newbie like me. It also makes them hard to clean and reapply so I've moved onto different ones if I have to take it off.
Not sure if I'm doing it wrong. They don't seem to adhere as well to the outer corners. Also possibly they're too long for me but not exactly sure these kind can be trimmed as they only have 5 long magnets (2 being at the ends)
One magnet came off one pair and stayed stuck on the packaging base they come on. Kinda bummed because those were the least extreme ones. (Wanted to get used to the simple ones before going bigger/fluffier/longer).

Overall the cost was not bad for experimenting. Am gonna look at ones in stores closer to see if any maybe have more/smaller magnets.

title: I was a little disappointed to realize when I opened it that it plugs ...
text:
I was a little disappointed to realize when I opened it that it plugs directly into the wall as a wall-wart -- I didn't realize it when I placed the order. I thought it was like the 5 and 6-port chargers that have a separate power cord. It limits the outlets that I can plug it into. I did ultimately make it work where I wanted it, it's just not as perfect as I was hoping.
I bought this to replace another Quick Charge 2.0 5-port charger with separate power cable - to keep by my bedside. I used to stick the 5-port charger alongside the bed rail - next to the box spring, with ports sticking up. Now I have this in the wall a foot or two further away, but still next to the bedside table (just means I had to use longer cables). For bedtime charging, 3 ports is more than enough - enough for me to have my fitbit charge cable sitting on the bedside table, cable leading to bed for my phone, and a spare port for charging my Anker battery if perchance I want it near the bed (normally I have it in a hanging pocketed 6-port charge station for all our household Anker batteries and other devices like kindles and tablets). Works as advertised. Quick Charge 2.0 works to charge my phone quite fast.

title: Awesome if you do a lot of outdoor/sweaty activities
text:
I've been using this product for about five years. So very worth it.

I naturally have zero pigment in my eyebrows. I apply the dye once every ~4-6 weeks, and leave it on for 2 hours since dye does not take to my hair very easily. For more accurate results and less skin dying, I use an old mascara brush that I've cleaned off with rubbing alcohol - no vaseline needed. My eyebrows are also tattooed which I cannot recommend highly enough.

They say no eyelashes but I do mine very carefully with the mascara wand, again leaving on for about 2 hours. Between the dyed brows and lashes I don't usually wear makeup.

When you mix the tint with the developer, put the developer in the mixing cup first! If you do it the other way around, the air blown out by the developer bottle will blow some of your dye out, and it'll dye your bathroom sink in an instant.

Included a pic; forgive the grim face, it was taken just following the 2016 election.

title: There Are Better Norelcos
text:
Since this model seems to be discontinued there probably isn't much chance of you finding one for sale. But just in case you do, don't get it.

I've had this shaver for years now, buying it as a replacement for my previous Norelco that I dearly loved. But I had put so many years on that one, and when it was time to replace the battery and heads (about $80.00 total), I figured it was time to just get a new one.

This was the first frustrating part of the process, finding a replacement. Norelco makes so many models. I was looking for one on sale as to limited funds. I soon found out a lot of things I didn't like. These shavers are no longer made in Holland, to fine exacting standards, but are now made in China. They are of varying quality, even within the same model, so you get the luck of the draw. This new model, for twice the money, did not have a battery charge indicator on it, and they no longer have the head height adjustment. And it was LOUD! All for TWICE the price of my old Norelco shaver that was made in Holland, had the battery indicator, and the adjustable heads.

So right away, I considered rebuilding the old one. I should have. This shaver grabbed my hair (still does), gives me razor burn, is made out of a more flimsy plastic, doesn't hold a charge nearly as long as with past models, and is just all around a poor replacement, for, did I mention, TWICE THE MONEY!

So I've put up with it for years now and am at the same place again. The heads and battery need replacing for a cost of over $80.00 and I'm sure not going to put that into this shaver. So it's off to the reviews again to find a new shaver. I understand that now that Philips has purchased Norelco that their quality has begun to come back up while their prices have stayed the same or even gone done some. I hope this is true as the alternatives don't exist.

In a word, you get what you pay for and with the 6843XL Reflex Plus, you don't get much!

text: And also - where has this been all my life? I have long, very thick, wavy, mostly frizzy hair. I hated washing it because it took. So. Long. To wash it, and then rinse it and then condition it and rinse it again. Sigh. Hair washing days means 30 min showers. Anyway, I often got flakes, not dandruff, just flakes that I always chalked up to the tons of products I need to tame my mane. After using this little scrubby I now realize it was because I was never getting my scalp and the hair closest to my scalp completely clean. Lathering up and then using this to massage my scalp, my hair is so much cleaner and TBH behaves a bit better. And I'm now down to washing it only 2x a week because it's now so clean, it takes longer to show build up from all my products. I read some folks don't like this because they say it tangles their hair. Not true. I can speak from experience, they are not getting their hair wet enough. In order to get a good cleaning - with or without this - you must SOAK your head completely and lather completely. This little scrubby will glide through the shampoo. And if you don't want to wash your hair every time you want a little scalp massage, then just soak and put a little conditioner in your hair. This works and it works well.

title: Takes a lot of work to look good...
text:
3.5 stars

I have many thoughts on this wig. We ordered this to compliment my daughter's Mad Hatter Halloween costume and honestly, it looked like a hot mess when it arrived. The bangs were going everywhere, the curls were tangled, there was no part...it was awful.

My daughter, who is 12, has long, VERY thick blonde hair. When the wig arrived, we tried it on with her hair down to make sure it fit. It did. Fast forward to Halloween...I braided her hair and pulled it into a knot at the back of her head. Lo and behold, the wig wouldn't fit...it just kept sliding off her head. That was my mistake...I should have tested it with a bun when it arrived. Having said that, my daughter is incredibly petite...her doctor predicts she won't surpass 5' when she's full grown Obviously, her head isn't that large. My point? If you're an adult or are purchasing this for a teen or big child, it likely won't fit. I finally had to put her hair in a low bun at the nape of her neck to make it work.

Unfortunately, because her natural hair was so low, we couldn't do the up-do we had planned because her bun showed if we did. We ended up leaving it down, brushing it out, putting bobby pins in strategic places to help it frame her face and to contain it, and then I hair sprayed it in place. Styling was especially difficult because the wig is sparse. It's a lot of work to hide the netting underneath. The netting is a yellow-beige color and stands out like bright white against the purple and teal. We finally got it looking decent though, and she actually got many compliments on it throughout the evening, hence the higher star rating despite all the complaints.

Once the wig was brushed and styled, the waves looked beautiful. Just don't buy this expecting it to look great out of the box. It won't. It takes work.

title: Nice improvement
text:
This is a nice improvement to the Sonicare line of brushes. It appears to be their response to the Oral-B Floss Action line of brushes that have a "paddle" to help get between teeth. This accomplishes that goal with an plastic insert in the middle that helps direct the toothpaste between your teeth.

I use both the Sonicare (Healthy White) and the Oral B 5000. Both have their pluses and minuses, so switching between the two gives me the best of both worlds.

The Oral-B arrangement of paddles does a better job in getting at the gum line without discomfort. The Sonicare Hydroclean's bristles are stiffer and I find that they irritate my gums when used several times in a row.

But, the Sonicare does a better job in cleaning stains between teeth. I'm a tea drinker and getting the stains out between my front teeth has always been a chore. The Hydroclean works very well - noticeable improvement over the Sonicare ProResults and the Oral-B.

These only come in the standard size. The ProResults has a smaller version that is great for getting at the tight spots. But, I assume that a smaller version of this would not function well since the plastic insert would have to be very small.

If you're a ProResults user these are well worth trying out. If you have tender gums you may want to alternate between the HydroClean and the ProResults (or, as I do, with the Oral-B. The Oral-B also makes a super soft brush if you have very sensitive gums. Hard to find, but works very well).

Keep in mind that nothing takes the place of flossing. No matter what you use, you still need to break out the floss to keep your teeth healthy!

title: An Inexpensive Way to Whiter Teeth
text:
Crest Whitestrips are one of the most popular among the store brand tooth whitening products. They were introduced to the public in 2001 and they have been satisfying customers ever since. They work by concentrating special whitening ingredients like peroxide directly against the teeth where they can penetrate the surface for a full thirty minutes. Repeated usage for fourteen days should result in significantly whiter teeth.

Crest Whitestrips claim that these strips can be worn and used any time and that, once in place, you can go on with your normal daily routine for 30 minutes while the strips have the opportunity to work. It is true that you can do what you want, but there are certain activities that are not easy to do with one of these strips in place. I'm one of those people who has a tendency to want to move my tongue around when a have some type of dental object against my teeth and more than once, I have accidentally pushed the strips out of place. The gel helps to hold them in place but they can still be moved with little effort. Also, if you start talking with a Whitestrip in place there is a chance that some of your words will come out a little funny- like someone who has had a little too much to drink. I have found that, for best results, I try to do nothing at all when wearing Crest Whitestrips. The best thing to do is read a book. The time goes by quickly and it makes it easy to forget the strips are in place.

Waiting for fourteen days is frustrating and it is possible that you may need a second treatment after the first, depending on how well you stick to your 30 minute per day schedule and how well the Whitestrips stayed in place. But the results should make you happy. At first I avoided Crest Whitestips because of the price and because of the product itself. Spreading liquid gel on the teeth seemed much simpler than having to wear an object against one's teeth. I didn't like the idea of hassling with strips so I avoided buying Crest Whitestrips and tried the liquid variety in its various forms first. I finally gave in and purchased Crest Whitestrips because I got tired of waiting for satisfactory results. And I did get good results with these strips. I followed the advice on the package and used the upper strips twice per day first, then the lower strips twice per day for the next seven days. This is a good idea because you can compare the shade of the top teeth with the bottom, right after the upper treatment is completed. I could see a significant difference as all those years of soda pop, coffee, tea, and other staining drinks were suddenly washed away.

Crest Whitestrips use the same chemicals that dentist's use to clean and whiten teeth, so they are safe if used as directed. They are designed to keep teeth white for six months after each fourteen day period of usage. They also come with a money back guarantee. In order to get the guarantee. If you are not satisfied with the results, you can get a full refund of the purchase price provided you have followed the correct procedure for a refund.

Crest Whitestrips work well, but like other over the counter whitening products, they only work on natural tooth enamel. They will not whiten dentures, caps, crowns, or other artificial dental material. If you have teeth with artificial surfaces that are badly stained, you will need to seek the help of a dentist or other professional to get rid of the problem.

Crest Whitestrips are a little more expensive than the liquid whitening formulas but Crest Whitestrips are also more effective. I am satisfied with Crest Whitestrips and I recommend buying a box for effective treatment of discolored teeth. They are not as thorough as the treatment provided by a dentist but all things considered, these strips are a good buy. They eliminate stains and return your teeth to a more youthful appearance in only two weeks if used as directed.

title: Painful for tender headed-curly hair types

But nearly every other section pulled her hair. The hooks kept getting stuck and wrapping around her hair during the install. I would not recommend these if you are tender headed. It did not rip her hair out, but she is tender headed and since her hair is thick I had to put some elbow grease into getting the hair through the wave former and she cried. She also said it's uncomfortable to sleep on, about the same as the typical curling rods. I gave it 3.5 stars because it definitely does what it says. It's not the same as braiding your 3C type hair and leaving it for a few days, despite what some reviews say. I would have to leave braids in for a week for this same over-night effect. title: Only after 1st use, wow!!

I am an avid coffee drinker and I smoke every once in a while, so my teeth tend to stay yellow unfortunately. It is a TERRIBLE mess in my sink, but its so worth it. This picture was my first try at the charcoal stuff. Instant results. It will leave your gums a little tender, so don't brush vigorously like normal toothpaste. I use the charcoal stuff for 2 minutes, wash it out with water, brush my teeth, then use mouth wash. I'd definitely recommend this to my coworkers and friends. However, if you still drink coffee everyday, the whitening will not stay. If you give up smoking or tinted drinks, you'll fall in love with the long term results.

title: Using this cleanser with Clarasonic
text:
For the price, I have to wonder why this item is not listed under Amazon's "luxury beauty" line. Like many reviewers, I was put off by the sheer amount of packaging that came along with this item. It wouldn't be so bad if they didn't tout how conscious they were of environmental issues, but I've purchased Chanel with less packing, come on!

All of the beauty and skin care products I consume are luxury, at the moment I've been using Dr. Gross's skin care line but until I could get back to Sephora, I've been using Purity cleanser. I was hoping this product would be a suitable replacement but I'm not convinced so let me tell you about the photos.

Each night I cleanse my face with Purity using Clarasonic's Uplift with the Revitalizing brush. I follow this with micellar water (by Borghese) and then a serum and moisturizer. The whole thing takes about 7 minutes (it's therapy, don't judge!).

Upon waking, I swabbed my face with the micellar water and then took a picture of the cotton ball along with an untouched cotton ball for comparison. And by the way for the uninitiated, micellar water is the best skincare product to come out since mascara was invented. I was sure that my $349 Clarasonic erased all traces of dirt no matter the soap, but the micellar water never lies.

On the second morning, first thing, I used the Clarasonic with the Radiance brush and three pumps of LaClaire Foaming Botanical Facial Cleanser. Two pumps did not create a bit of lather. Then using micellar water, I swabbed my face again and there you have the picture of both -- no cleanser and cleanser.

You can see that there is still a lot of dirt left behind after using this cleanser, certainly less than no cleanser at all but there is still some there. There is less dirt left after washing with Purity so I wouldn't call it a miracle cleanser, it's really just "okay."

title: dry soft granular "scrub"/mask, just add water/hydrosol. Directions for use on Face
text:
This Juicy Chemistry face & body scrub is a very mild, and seemingly gentle "scrub" chock full of great ingredients. For rating, I am right in the middle of neither really liking it nor really disliking it (ok, maybe leaning a more toward dislike for me). The "3 stars" include the fact the company (and their ingredient selections) seems of high quality and may be worthwhile to check out.

I have mixed thoughts on this, so please bear with me as I try to explain.

At first glance, the small container is packed to the brim with a dark brown, dry, granular looking substance. This is primarily a combo of coffee powder and cocoa powder. I thought it was going to be a rough scrub, and immediately thought that there is no way I would use that on my face. Since it says, "for face AND body" my plan changed to use it on my body in the shower. However, the directions say to apply TO FACE, and allow to sit for 10 minutes/until dry. That isn't happening as a body scrub. In the shower.

So now I am back to trying it on my face. It did not come with a spatula or spoon, so plan to use your own. Or scoop out with a finger.I have tried it by spooning out a bit of product and adding water, adding a hydrosol, and adding an oil. The latter makes it easiest to use through I do not know if it impeded the other ingredients. Also, it wouldn't dry with oil. But it did stay in place with oil.

Any granular feeling quickly melted down, so I felt better about using it on my face. But still, not a fan of anything granular on face. Overall, I don't like it for my face- I only tried it once because that is all I could handle. . It felt like it left some powder behind. I felt compelled to rewash my face to get any remnants off. Meh.

Body is fine (and is why I selected it for use). When used with all bases I mentioned, the result was a slightly oily feel. Not heavy, not greasy. Definitely a little bit of hydration/moisture. Ultimately not a fan of it for my face, but do like it enough for use on body. HOWEVER, I do not "keep it on until it dries" while I am using it.. in the shower. I just use it like a regular body scrub. I either add water to it, or oil. OR use a basic creamy body wash as the vehicle. Now that I think of it, even a body lotion would work (especially if you have one you dont love and want to use up). Once again, the oil (or body wash/ lotion) is easier to worth- I can work it all over body, massage it in, and as it rinses away once again that slightly oily feel is left behind (not greasy, not heavy, rather soft and light; rather nice). Make sure to rinse shower as this will splatter brown all over.

I like that the product is packed into a small jar container, and that it needs a base (water, hydrosol, etc) which can be good or bad depending on your preference. By needing to add your own, the product is more concentrated (not paying for added water,etc), but it lends just a tiny bit of inconvenience. Use in the shower is awkward. Use as a scrub mask is going to come down to preference. If you like a more granular feeling physical scrub/exfoliator this may not be for you. If you use more, you may get more of a scrub feel (I guess you could add sugar). I use less as I do not want a harsh physical scrub. For the shower, I prefer a greater scrub feel, so I use more. I am thinking now I may add this to another jar, add some cream or oil, and some added sugar for an easier to use shower scrub experience.

Packaging is nice, and pleasant to look at. Could be worthy as a gift if this seems like something someone would like.

Full Ingredient List:
Sucrose*, Coffea Arabica Seed (Coffee)Powder*, Theobroma Cacao(Cocoa)Powder*, Theobroma cacao (Cocoa) Seed Butter*, Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter*, Citrus Sinensis (Sweet Orange) Essential Oil*, Vanilla Planifolia (Vanilla) powder*, Simmondsia Chinensis(Jojoba Oil)*, Corylus Avellana (Hazel) Oil*, Coffee Infused Oil*, Tocopherol^, Helianthus annuus Seed Oil, Rosmarinus officinalis(Rose Mary Antioxidant) Leaf Extract.

"Formulated especially for dry skin, this scrub brings together the classic combination of Coffee and Cocoa with a hint of Sweet Orange.

Cocoa has powerful antioxidant properties that help to heal damaged skin and other skin ailments. It helps renew and promote healthy cell development. Ground coffee beans gently exfoliate the skin and also reduce the appearance of cellulite and stimulate skin cells.

The fatty acids and Vitamin E content of Hazelnut oil help create a natural oil barrier that helps skin retain water and avoid drying out. It also contains tannins, a powerful antioxidant that help cleanse and shrink pores. Vitamin E also helps with collagen synthesis and reduce the appearance of scars.

High Vitamin C content in Orange makes skin radiant and also helps in collagen production resulting in supple, hydrated and age-less skin.

Sugar acts as a natural exfoliator and helps to gently remove dead skin and impurities making it radiant and softer.

Rich in fatty acids and natural vitamins, Shea Butter moisturizes the skin to relieve dryness. A super-hydrating blend of Cocoa Butter, Natural Vitamin E, Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Jojoba Oil, and Sweet Almond Oil makes skin softer and smoother."

title: Better than other electric shavers
text:
My first impression of the razor was that it was overly packaged. In a day and age in which we're becoming aware of environmental hazards, I don't think there's a need for an outer box enclosing a couple layers of thick hard-to-open plastic wrapping. A strong pair of scissors cut through the lot, and eventually I got to the razor itself.

I was pleased to see that it comes with a hard-shell case for travel. This is definitely a good thing to have, though I would have preferred it were only one piece that swivels open and shut, rather than two pieces that have to be separated to open it.

The instructions indicate that the charging pod should be unplugged when the razor is fully charged (which takes about an hour). While hardly the worst thing in the world, I don't see why they couldn't have designed it so that it could remain plugged it but turned off. In general, I prefer not to have plugs lying around exposed, especially in the bathroom, where I think most people would tend to keep it. It does have a very clear indicator, though, telling how much longer it needs to charge before reaching the full 65 minutes, and, after a couple weeks of usage, it still did not need to be recharged, so it definitely holds the charge well.

The razor itself is stylish and comfortable to hold, and it has a trimmer on the back, which is good for sideburns and the awkward just-under-the-nostrils area.

My first shave felt like it took ages, and, half-way through, I seriously considered giving up and getting out my old blade and shaving cream. I decided to stick with it, and, eventually, I figured out that you can't just press it to your face, but press it rather firmly. With more pressure, it eventually got the job done. Subsequent shaves went much easier, and as I got used to using the shaver, the shave-time got less and less. It does a significantly better and faster job on only one day's growth rather than two or three, so it's much more ideal for everyday use than if you tend to go a few days between shaves.

Clean-up is easy and fast. Just flip the three razor bits up and rinse with hot water. I'm a little suspicous about using water to clean it each day - I would tend to think it'll rust - but time will tell.

After shaving, my face sometimes feels less comfortable than had I used a regular blade and shaving cream, but usually it feels all right. This is the third electric shaver I've owned, and it has been the case with all three that the shave is not as close as even the worst blade I've used. There's really no getting around it: you'll always get a closer shave using a real blade. I'd say this is easily the best of the three electric razors I've used, though, and did a significantly better job on the chin, due to its swiveling head.

Overall, I find myself liking this shaver, particularly for the traveling and the cold winter months, when I don't really want to deal with a wet shave in the morning.

title: One of the most unappealing facial products I have used
text:
I try to avoid reviews for products before I try them myself, but I was kinda shocked to see a low rating so I peaked. Other reviews mentioned things like how watery the product was and how yellow-y the color was, and I'll admit, I was worried. But just because one person has a bad product, doesn't mean that I would have the same experience.

Turns out, I did.

When I opened the container, I saw the same runny, milky yellow gloop (this is NOT a cream by any stretch of the imagination) as I saw in the other reviews. There is a sparkle also, which I'm sure is meant as cosmetic, to make it more appealing. I almost didn't want to dip my finger in it, but I did. It was a very thin product left on my finger. Then I sniffed it. It was a horrid scent; I cannot quite describe it, as it's (fortunately) not strong enough to really kick in, but the scent is unpleasant and just "wrong".

Right there, I probably could have enough justification to not use the product. But I wanted to attempt to be thorough, so I did. I dabbed my finger into the jar of liquid shimmery gloop, ignored the scent and rubbed it on my face. And I was fine - it was pretty moisturizing (my skin tends to be dry so that is good for me), soaking through pretty quickly and leaving my skin soft.

This isn't a cream; this is a liquid. And everything about the liquid sets off alarm bells, from the thickness to the texture to the color to the smell. Fortunately, the product itself seems to work - I'd need to use it longer to see if it does long term. But I don't know if I can manage to use it that long - couple that with the EXORBITANT price of $49, I will definitely NOT be repurchasing.

title: you will see results if you commit to it
text:
I've been using this for 3 months now and I do think this works with longterm use. You obviously aren't going to see overnight results but if you keep at it you will notice a difference on your wrinkles. Luckily I don't have too many yet but I did use it on the little areas where I'm starting to see wrinkles. I noticed a tightening of the areas I used the laser on for the past 3 months. I really liked the hyaluronic acid serum that was included in the set - the serum felt gentle and has no smell (fragrance free). On some days where I didn't use the laser I would still use the serum to moisturize my face. I looked into purchasing just the serum, which they do have for sale, as I really like the product. The laser is easy to operate and charge (usb). I didn't use this daily as I wanted to give my skin a rest, but I think if you used this religiously then you would see results at a much faster rate. It isn't painful, but you feel a little zap. I would equate it to the same level of "pain" as a derma roller, that spikey/zappy feeling - not painful, not super uncomfortable. That of course, will depend on your skin sensitivity. I recommend using the lowest setting first then working your way up as your skin sensitivity will allow. Don't force your skin into what it cannot handle - listen to your body's reaction!

I've seen so many of these laser type products for the skin/body, and never tried it because I didn't trust it. Nira is the first at home laser product that I decided to give a chance to, as I trust it. Overall I am not disappointed but do know that you need to commit to it if you want to see results. If you are going to use it once every few weeks then it will be a while before you see results, if ever. I plan to keep using this to stimulate my skin.

title: good soap, disappointing variety
text:
I've loved Primal Elements soap since I was a kid, but it's expensive to try by buying full bars, and they keep raising the price of this sampler, which they used to call a grab bag and charge a bargain price for (since it's the end slabs they can't sell as full bars), and they keep filling them with a grossly disproportionate number of Christmas soaps.

I ordered 3 samplers direct from their website when they offered a special in mid October, and 10 out of 23 soaps that came were Christmas-themed, and 2 of those were duplicates (2 each of Rudy and Skyward). Another 2 of the non-Christmas soaps were also duplicates (2 each of Primal IPA and Paw Prints). The Primal IPAs weren't even in different boxes - they were stuck together, right next to each other, in the same box. (If you're going to bill this as a sampler rather than a bargain pack, and as gift-worthy, at least make sure the soaps within a box are distinct!) Though it's early-mid autumn, there was not a single autumn scent.

When I've ordered in the past (whether through them, or Amazon, or RockinGifts), there was a similarly disproportionate amount of Christmas soap, except when I ordered in mid-late spring and got floral stuff instead of Christmas. I've never had luck getting autumn or "oriental" soaps in these packs no matter when in the year I order. This is probably the last time I buy a sample pack unless they add an option to pick the scents included.

title: Let's just call it a heat protectant, not a "Flat Iron Lotion"...
text:
I previously used the FHI Hot Sauce heat protectant, which I loved and has been discontinued. UGH. I didn't really like the CHI one and I saw a flatiron review on natural hair that used this and decided to try it. Pros: It protects my hair. I didn't have noticeable heat damage after washing. My curls came back and my hair didn't feel fried while straightened. CONS: It's heavy. You don't "NEED" to use a lot, but it's hard not to because it's very, very viscous. It comes out thick and is therefore fairly difficult to distribute evenly through your hair. My hair is 3C/4A curly with a patch of DRY coarse-ish hair right on top in my cowlick area. Even with my hair very wet, I had to apply extra to feel safe with this product.but once the blow dry was completed, my hair felt "coated". Overall, it's better than most sprays I've tried, but my recommendations are to use it on damp, not wet hair. Towel (t-shirt for the naturals) hair to the point where it's barely damp, section into 4-8 sections (depending on tightness of curl), and rub about a dime sized amount through your palms until it's as moist as possible before applying to hair. Apply on middle to ends and come (Denman brush) through prior to blow drying. I'd also try to completely dry your hair before flatironing. I tried using this product only for the flat-iron only once, after allowing my hair to air dry overnight, and it was just NOT a good life plan. I'd use a different cream if you don't blow dry. It made my hair feel kind of like a protein treatment that hasn't been fully rinsed out --crunchy, hard and a little fragile. I just didn't like the texture of my hair using this at the flatiron only stage, even though it's called a flat-iron lotion.

Overall, my hair doesn't break off after heat styling so it does it's "job" but it's called a flat-iron lotion and maybe it's just my hair (so I'm not saying don't try it) but I can't just use it for flat-ironing.

title: Good for travel
text:
I've had water flossers before - they're honestly pretty fantastic since they can get in places and in pockets where regular floss can't. If you get the right one and know how to use it, it's a lot like having your own dental assistant to help clean your teeth. My last water flosser gave up the ghost after I dropped it while moving (RIP water flosser!) so this seemed like it'd be good to try out.

Upon using this I immediately noticed that the lowest setting wasn't shooting out water hard enough for me, so I turned it up to the max. That worked better, but it still didn't have the oomph that its larger counterparts did. So if you're looking for a particularly intense water flosser, this isn't really going to be it. On the other hand, this would probably do well with people who want lower pressure.

The fact that this is handheld is pretty nice, although it does take a while to get used to since I'm used to the smaller water flosser nozzles. It's a bit like holding a really huge toothbrush in some aspects, if that makes any sense. The water being in the unit is an OK feature but if you like being very thorough and doing several passes, you'll more than likely need to refill at some point. That part isn't a big hardship as filling this up is a breeze and one of the nicest aspects of it. It's insanely easy to do and isn't needlessly complicated.

In the end the main draw for this would be that I can take it with me on trips, which I almost certainly will. It's far easier to pack into a travel bag or throw into a suitcase than a standard water flosser with a huge tank would be. I just don't think that I'd prefer this for daily use over a more traditional unit, especially since I like my water pressure a lot higher than that. Still, for what it is, it's not bad and it'd be a good little gadget for travelers.

title: A lot of conflicting reviews for thick hair...
text:
This probably won't help ; )
I don't normally write negative reviews. Its just that this brush had so many conflicting reviews regarding thick hair (which I have in spades), that I decided to put my experience here. I also have to say that another reason to look for a new brush is because I have pain in my hands almost daily. Right now in use a wet brush. It's not too bad.
On to this...I like the shape of the handle, I just think that it could be bigger. Others in my family didn't like it at all.
Now for my hair. It was awful. The texture of the bristles seems ever so slightly rubbery-ish maybe? Still plastic, but it couldn't even get through my hair AT ALL. I mean, I could take a very small strand of hair, put the brush toward the end of the strand and the brush would kind of pick at it. What resulted was a nest of tiny knots where the brush left the hair.
I still kept trying to see how it would go. It took a ridiculous amount of time and patience to finish that strand. I have a feeling that I could have (and probably did) break much of my hair if I tried to go faster, got distracted, was impatient (which happens often), or if my hands started having pain.
I hope this helps people with thick hair.

title: Not a real human hair
text:
Here is my honest review:
I wanted to add some length to my short and damaged hair so after some research decided to purchase tape in extensions. I scheduled an appointment with the professional who could install these. My first mistake was that I didn't read those negative reviews for these tape-ins. Wish I did. Hair looked good at first, soft and the color was matching mine. It came with some extra tape-ins. After the appointment, I loved the hair. However, my stylist said this was not real human hair but quality synthetic hair. I didn't believe her.
As recommended I used 1 pack of 100 grams and 2 packs of 30 so the total was 160 grams and I have tin hair. Waited 4 days and washed my hair. It wasn't as hard as expected. One extension came off. I replaced a tape in and reinstalled myself. Wasn't hard. The first two days I had a headache I guess because of the extra weight. It went away on the third day. After I dried my hair, the extensions were dry and curly. I purchased straight hair. Used an iron to straighten it out. After 7 days my scalp was itchy and the bumps were all over the scalp due to the glue in the tape-ins. At that point, I just wanted them out. Thank God I was able to find a good tape in remover. Ladies these are not real human hair extensions. Save your money. I attached the picture for reference.

title: love, love, love this!
text: I bought this oil after using their avocado oil. Life-Flo is a great brand. I've never had issues with any of their products. This oil is food grade, cold pressed. It is a lighter weight than their avocado oil, but it works just as well. I use this on my son who is two to help his skin retain moisture (he has severe eczema). I put a cap full in his bath and apply it all over after his bath while he is still damp. His skin is soft and his eczema spots are softer, not as rough, but I still have to apply a layer of Vaseline to his rough patches to keep him from scratching and to keep his spots super moisturized. I use it on his scalp also once a week. I massage it through his hair and let it soak in while he's playing in the tub and I follow it put by shampooing his hair like normal. It absorbs quickly, and I do apply it throughout the day when I change his diaper. It doesn't have a scent to it really, which is a plus since I have to be careful with perfumes with him. It does make your tub slippery if you add it to your bath water, I always clean the tub after his bath to be on the safe side. We usually go through a 12 oz bottle every six months so it lasts a while compared to a gel baby oil (we go through one of them a month if we use it).  A little bit goes a long way. This oil used in conjunction with Vaseline and his prescription meds helps keeps his eczema in check, and I have discovered that we are using his prescription med less since we swapped over to this oil. For us this oil is more effective than coconut, avocado, baby oil, ceteaphil, or aveeno.  If it's for eczema we have tried it. He's had eczema since he was 3 months old and I feel like we finally found a product that I know is safe to use, it's all natural, no chemicals, and it's within budget.

title: Definitely Not For Oily Skin
text:
The first thing I noticed about this product was the scent. It's a strong, earthy scent, much like I would expect from a pile of pulled-up weeds that had been sitting around for a few days. The scent lingered to the point that I've had to use scented moisturizer to cover up the smell.

For me, the texture was a bit odd considering it's dispensed through a dropper. I'm guessing that's so you get the right amount and so that you don't end up using too much. For me, though, because it's a bit thick, I felt like a bottle where I could squirt the product out would make more sense.

One good thing is that a little bit of this product does go a long way. When you squirt the product out of the dropper, you might think that it wouldn't be enough to cover your whole face. Fortunately, it is. That means that even though there is only one ounce of product in the container, it will likely last for a while.

I have dry skin. While it's not too bad during the summer, I do use moisturizers specifically for dry skin most of the winter. Yet, this felt a little greasy on my face. It was like it didn't quite seep into my skin. Even a few hours later, my face felt slightly greasy. I tried it without using a moisturizer after putting it on, and it still felt greasier than expected. I think that come winter, when my skin is really dry, this might work without feeling too greasy, but I would definitely not suggest this for anyone with oily skin.

While some people may love the smell, that combined with the greasy feeling and a price tag of $62 for an ounce, makes this a product that I would not get again or suggest to someone else.

The lotion is a good size bottle of 8.5 ounces and is a very army green color when dispensed. Be sure to wear a disposable glove when applying or yes, your palms will turn bronzed.

title: 🚫Contains synthetic perfumes and colors 🚫
text:
The list of ingredients isn’t in English which is a big thing for me as I am sensitive to certain products. The ones that are in English, Solanum Melongena which is an eggplant extract, EDTA which is a chelating agent and not good for you at all, Camellia Sinensis Leaf which is a skin conditioner and perfume and CI 77492 which is a synthetic cosmetic colorant. There is a -20 which typically is a PEG which Polyethylene Glycol and can cause health issues if used in excess.

The application of the product itself is a neat concept and makes applying a mask much easier. There are unnecessary perfumes and colors in this product along with EDTA and possibly PEG which I stay away from.

Learn your skin and what it can handle also what you are looking for in a skin. This is not a natural product by any stretch of the imagination.

title: Strong fragrance
text:
This was my first time trying shampoo or conditioner in bar form, and I had the opportunity to try both from this company's line of products. My first impressions were very positive - the ingredients looked clean and natural, as well as being cruelty-free and vegan, I love that it’s plastic free (both the lack of bottle and the packaging), and that the scent options were relatively gender neutral. The bars were a little smaller than I expected, but ergonomically they fit comfortably in the palm of my hand and don't seem to be shrinking too fast after a week or so of use. I'm glad that they have different colors, so that I can differentiate between my bar soap, shampoo, and conditioner!

My experience using them was pretty good. It felt odd at first as I've only ever used bottled products, but quickly got used to it and could definitely see myself using more bars in the future. I tried both running the conditioner bar down my hair and lathering it up a little in my hand and applying that way. Between the two, I felt that I got pretty good coverage and results. My hair felt less tangled and I was able to work a brush through pretty easily once I got out the shower. When my hair dried, it seemed softer and healthier looking than it had previously, and my curls had a little more life to them.

I only have two concerns - the first is that I'm struggling to find a place to put the bars in my shower where they won't get misted by water and disintegrate more quickly that way. The second is the smell. Although it's not unpleasant, it reminded me a little of a scented candle, and was very strong. Three different people commented on the smell of my hair that week, which is not something that usually happens to me. My husband thought that I smelled like cologne! I could see this being a pro or a con depending on how you feel about fragrances. Personally, I found it overwhelming as I'm more on the sensitive side to smells.

Overall, I would consider trying this or a similar product again in the future, but only with a less intense scent.

title: More you apply, longer it lasts
text:
This glittery eyeliner is reasonably effective. However, the title of this review really says it all. The more eyeliner you apply the more glittery it will look and it tends to last longer as well. While this is obvious, it does highlight a small limitation in the use of this eyeliner. And that limitation is that you have to apply it multiple times to have the glitter take effect. That's not particularly a bad thing though.

The other good thing about these eyeliners is that the tip is fine enough to give it a level of precision that is absolutely required in case you want to get the fine lines shine through.

Another good thing about these eyeliners is the variety of colors that you get which makes this overall package quite versatile and allows these eyeliners to be used with really any attire.

So overall quite happy with this set of eyeliners, it is also priced reasonably low for it to offer very good value for money. The tip is durable too and stays good for it to be used multiple times. Do recommend this product.

title: Best electric shaver I've ever had
text:
I agree with most of the other reviews. This is the best electric shaver I've ever had--lightyears better than the Braun Syncro I was using before. I don't expect to get as close a shave with an electric as with a blade, so I don't think it's fair to judge them by that standard; the only thing that makes sense is to compare them to other electrics, and this one is outstanding. It's quiet, it charges quickly, and it shaves your beard. I like products I don't have to think about.

I'm not pleased by the fact that this model doesn't have a low-battery indicator. That's a demerit. The stand is a little gimmicky. You can charge the unit without using the stand; the stand just makes the product look a bit more pretentious. (My shaver came with a free "personal groomer" for beards as well as ear and nose hair; this was a nice addition, but not enough to make or break the sale.)

Lastly, to the guy who had a hassle at Target: don't blame the product for the fact that you don't like Target's return policy.

title: Good product after you learn how to get the oil out of the tube
text:
At first I had trouble getting anything at all out of the tube. There was a problem with my cap that prevented anything from coming out. But after taking the cap off the product flowed out. By reading other reviews I learned that the tube must be submerged in hot water for some time to liquify the mixture of oil. Otherwise you get a pebbly mixture. And unless you live in a subtropical climate, one of the oils in the mixture comes out in a semi-solid state and must be rolled between your palms to liquify it as well. Once that is done, your hands will be pretty thoroughly coated on both sides and between the fingers. Then you must work it into your beard. It did a pretty good job of softening my scruffy beard. But now its time to clean the oils off my hands using the sink full of hot water I soaked the tube in. An oily film can be seen in the water, but my hands still feel oily. No worries. The remaining oil get absorbed into my hands.
The instructions say to use a "manly amount." But that begs the question, how much is a manly amount? It really doesn't require as much as I initially thought. I guess the fragrance could be described as manly.

title: Low iron fixes bent wings
text:
This review is for the DARKLATER Butterfly Hair Clips.

Extremely cute and beautiful butterfly clips! I'm an adult and bought these for myself — I like to wear a small flower or pretty barrette on the side of my hair most days. These clips are very ethereal, with a delicate fluttering effect while wearing. They have beautiful detail on the wings, and sparkly bodies that thankfully do not shed glitter. The metal clips are covered in grosgrain ribbon, which is more comfortable and makes them look extra polished.

The only downside is that these clips need better packaging. Mine arrived completely strewn about inside the bubble mailer — their flimsy plastic bag had busted open during shipping — and several butterfly wings were bent askance. The wings are, I'm guessing, a polyester satin fabric (not feathers or nylon stockings with wire), so I used my iron on low heat to straighten out the bent wings. It worked perfectly.

title: Halloween Or Messing Around Okay, But Serious Wear, Not So Much
text:
I have been working with wigs for quite a few years now. One thing I know is a good quality vs not so great quality wig. Let's take a look at this one.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?

HAIR
This wig has some great hair. the colors are definitely platinum white and what I would call light auburn base hairs. The white hairs are about 1/3 or so longer than the auburn hairs. There is a nice kink to the hairs.

THICKNESS
That is where this wig is sadly lacking. At the top, the wefts of hair are way too far apart. The lace in the cap is a very light butter colored yellow. The hair is not too thin, but it is not quite thick enough to cover hair below. Yes, this comes with a nylon cap, but it just is not comfortable with those. If you have dark hair it will definitely show the bright colored lace and elastics through the wig when the wind blows.

BANGS/STYLE
That is where this wig is just not practical unless you don't mind looking stupid for a party or Halloween. The bangs are WAY too long for anyone to wear. That usually would not be a problem, but what you will get instead of the cool light ends on the entire head is chopped bang that is bland looking and then these white cool looking ends around the head. The bangs are best cut painstakingly so that the auburn is cut way shorter (about 2/3) than the white hairs. That takes a lot of time but worth the effort. Then you have to cut them at a staggered manner.

Other than the bangs being hard to trim so you can at least function with this wig on, the overall style is fabulous. I love how it falls and looks while on the head.

ELASTIC BANDS
Inside the wig, there are elastic bands with hooks to help hold the wig on the head. You might want to take them down to the spot you like it in as the hooks have a tendency to come undone during wearing.

WHAT I WANT IN A WIG
Believe it or not, I would actually wear a wig like this with the right outfit, and not to be silly either. I prefer wigs that look authentic,, and can be worn realistically as well as for fun.

1. I have to be able to see out of it
2. I have to be able to wear it comfortably without fussing
3. I want it to not have my real hair showing
4. I want it to look realistic
5. I want it to last for quite a few wearings

DOES THIS WIG PASS THE TEST?
I am giving this wig THREE stars because it is hard to wear and see. In order to trim this in a realistic manner, I have to take a LOT of time and that takes stars off for me. I happen to love the style and coloring, so I am wiling to put the work into it, but honestly, I think it should be a bit shorter in the bangs area since it is so hard to trim and keep it looking real. Also, the wefting on the top is just a bit too widely spaced. I wish also that the cap was made with light auburn lace and elastic instead of the icy yellow colors.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to wear this for fun, it will be hard to see and hard to trim and not look silly in this. It is comfortable and the style is epic, but there will be work required. You can bandana it to help, but it still will look a bit floppy unless trimmed a little bit in the bangs/fringe area. I like this, but it takes work to wear and not look silly for me.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. The trimming of the bangs is VERY time consuming since we only have one shot at it and if it is screwed up, then the wig is toast. I wish there was more hair on top and that the lace cap did not show as easily. A darker cap underneath (light auburn color) would have been much nicer with this. I will still use this, but it could have been a bit nicer with small inexpensive changes.

title: This is the greatest invention I've stumbled upon
text:
Even with various gloves and pads, washing makeup brushes is always a pain. You always get your hands wet and prune-y.

This is the greatest invention I've stumbled upon. It's very easy to choose a boot, insert your brush, and spin wash. I used this to clean ALL of my makeup brushes and it worked well for almost every single one. Each brush needs to be positioned a little differently for optimal cleaning depending on the shape and length of fibers. The only brushes that didn't work well were bulky face brushes with heavy handles that the machine did not spin well and small eyeshadow and detailing brushes that couldn't fan out. I recommend two rounds of rinsing. The first in soapy bubbly water to clean the brushes and the second in clean water only to rinse out any bubbles and residue.

Even with two cycles, the process was quicker and less intensive than washing by hand and the drying time was cut down to almost nothing for nearly all my brushes, including dense synthetics.

I highly recommend!

title: Nice balance between soft and firm; some fitment issues
text:
This is a good middle ground between the standard Oral-B brand brushes and the Ultra Soft Oral-B brand brushes. I find the standard brush to be a bit too firm and, while I like the softness of the Ultra Soft, sometimes I'd like just a bit more firmness to the bristles. This is a good compromise. It's softer than the standard but firmer than the Ultra Soft.

On the downside, it does not fit as well as the authentic Oral-B brushes. It's a little bit loose, which causes it to be noisier in operation than an authentic brush. It still works fine and stays on firm enough so there's no danger of it coming off in use, but there's enough play in the fit that it's more buzzy than an authentic.

Even with the fit issue, this is a decent alternative to the Oral-B brand brushes and a solid 4-star brush.

title: Beautiful finish and wear time
text:
This is a beautiful foundation. I tried applying this both with a flocked powder puff and a foundation brush. I did prefer the powder puff, which did a better job of picking up the powder through the elasticated net dispenser. The finish is what I would call a "luminous matte" or "lit from within"---it definitely wasn't flat but didn't look dewy or greasy, either. It applied very smoothly over some very textured spots on my skin and covered blemishes well.

Unfortunately, the shade range sucks. I typically need a shade described as "very fair", which are harder to find in mineral foundations. The 100 Light shade is too dark for me unless I also cover my whole neck and chest with it, but the finish is beautiful and I honestly would wear it out on days I'm wear a scarf, for example. I would describe this shade as fair-light or light with a neutral peach undertone.

If you are familiar with the Tarte loose powder foundation, this seems very similar but without the clay that tends to oxidize. They have the same style of packaging (elasticated net + stopper lid), same luminous matte finish, and similar longevity.

I have used both wunder brow and this product and here is what I think:

Pros:This product has a much better applicator brush. For wunder brow, I had to buy a brush separately because I didn't like the one it came with.

title: Average soap bar - mix of natural ingredients and harsher surfactants...
text:
I have kind of mixed feelings about this soap. I love neem and I love natural essential oil based soaps. The design of this soap was actually really cool and I wasn't expecting it. It has a cool floral print with a lot of neem bark bits (I think so anyway?) that really help with exfoliation. The smell is a bit funky but it also is clear to me that it's only using neem and those essential oils listed, neem is a funky smell. I do feel like the feel was nice and it lathered and cleaned well.

However I think for the price the ingredients are kind of junky. You can see that they make a big deal about it having shea butter, etc, but that's way down on the list of ingredients. This is mainly a glycerin based soap with a harsh surfactant/foaming agent in it, Sodium Stearate, as well as a lot of other ingredients that I haven't seen in a long time in a natural soap bar. I didn't have a bad reaction to it and it doesn't have sulfates but I try to stay away from foaming agents and given the price I don't understand why they are trying to play both sides by acting like this is an "all natural" soap when it's a more traditional soap with shea butter, neem, and other stuff added. It's true though that glycerin based soaps can be less harsh on the skin but even the glycerin based soaps I've used don't have all these extra ingredients in them.

I don't think I'd buy this again, although my husband had no problem with it - check out Neem Tree Farms for legit neem soap.

title: Cute MOM gift but not as fragrant or impressive as I expected
text:
[[VIDEOID:f77804a8088c40dfbef6fdcfacf8b15a]] There are three individually wrapped bath bombs in this set along with one bar of hand soap and a package of dried rose petals. In total there are five items. The bath bombs spell MOM with the heart substituting for the letter O.

The outside packaging looks giftable but the inside is just an ordinary uninspiring throw-away box. The fragrance of the bombs and soap is hardly noticeable. It has a whisper of rose aroma and I detect no lavender at all. I did try the letter M bomb in a hand bath and it dissolved in 5 minutes in lukewarm water and a nice foam of suds lasted about 10 minutes. The results initially felt moisturizing because my hands felt a little oily after the hand bath; however, eventually I needed to moisturize my hands with lotion.

With regard to the dried petals, one has to like something like that in their bath because it requires straining the water so that they don't go down the drain. For me, I would never use petals in a bath, so keep the recipient in mind when ordering this.

The bar of soap is the only item that would be used by most people.

One thing I love is that the color of the dissolved bomb did not adhere to my skin, my hand bath, or my towel. That is not always the case with bath bombs today.

The current price of $9.74 ($12.99 minus 25%) comes to $1.95 per item which is reasonable.

title: Epilator works very well but only has one head
text:
I have previously used the Braun 7181 WD (orange colored) and was disappointed in it because I got a lot of ingrown hairs and the charge didn't last long. I wasn't expecting much from this epilator because I figured they are pretty much going to be the same, except this one has the exfoliating head.

Well, I was pleasantly surprised. The battery seems to last much, much longer on this one. I don't know how that's possible because I figured they were the same. I use the brush before epilating and the day after and my skin is even smoother than usual with no ingrown hairs. At first I was annoyed that this one doesn't come with the efficiancy cap for experienced users, but ended up finding that the included one works great. This one seems to work best with only water, but make sure you use the brush with soap before so the area is very clean. Overall I am pleased with this epilator and will continue to use it.

There are only a few small cons to the product. This only comes with one head and the exfoliating brush. For the price, they just include a few different heads. For some reason though, Braun has decided to make multiple epilators that seem to be the same, but each comes with a different head, rather than just making one product that comes with all the different choices. In my opinion they are just doing this to make more money.

The other cons were things that Braun has always done and doesn't seem to want to change. For the life of me I can't figure out why braun refuses to make a cap for their epilators. They even made a cap for the brush, but not the epilator. They also give you a drawstring bag, rather than one with a zipper.

title: Great Resin Decorating Sampler and Tools
text:
I am happy with my order of the Resin Decorative Accessories Set. This was packaged well and arrived in great condition. What I really like is that this set of tools and inclusions comes in a multi-level box that is transparent. It is easy to see what inclusions are inside, which is very easy to use while working on a project. Pipettes are really great to remove bubbles and also to apply very small amounts of resin into detailed areas. The silicone mat is essential to protect a working surface and the tweezers are very useful to add small items into a poured resin piece. There are also extra 30ml mixing cups, tiny spoons and wooden sticks.

These inclusions are great to use with other materials besides resin like nail art, decoupage glues, acrylic paint and polymer clay. This makes the set versatile for working with different mediums and for different projects. There are full round hole-less beads and also half beads. I really like the tiny seashells, my set also includes a tiny starfish. I am putting these into a resin painting with some sand I saved from a recent beach vacation. The only thing included with this set that is not useful to me are the finger cots, as I prefer to wear gloves when working with resin. The only negative aspect is very small, but some glitter was loose. I did not find this to be bothersome, but did want to mention that. There is a lot of supplies in this kit and I consider it to be a really great value for all that is included. I hope that my experience is helpful as you kindly click the button below.

title: Absolutely love this oil!!!!
text:
This Kardashian dry black seed oil is by far the best shining/straightening oil I have ever used in my life. I am on 2 different types of chemo drugs and it has played havoc on my long hair. Kim Kardashian knows her stuff for sure! I have tried at least 30 different products to help with the frizz in my hair. I received a small sample bottle of this in a monthly subscription box I get. A small bottle of this lasted me about 4 months of daily use. I used it right after a wash while my hair was still wet and then right after blow drying and using the straightening iron and then a tiny bit to give my hair that shiny finished, sleek look. Let me tell you, my hair looks and feels like silk after using this. First off, the tangles fall right out. The heat from my iron doesn't damage my hair any longer and my husband says my hair feels like spun silk! This is also a dry oil so there is no oily build up or feel at all. Also, look at the AMAZING price that this is offered at! Wow! I will be heartbroken if they ever stop selling this stuff!
Now, there is only one con to this dry black seed oil. It has a small aroma that to me smells like pencil shavings. Almost like when you were in elementary school standing at the pencil sharpener getting your pencils all sharpened up for your tests! The good news is that the smell doesn't stay in your hair but for a few minutes. Other than that, you can't go wrong with this product!

title: Great, versatile builder’s gel!
text: I was concerned this builder gel would be difficult to work with based only on how runny it looks in the product pix.  In real life it looks runny and sticky, but is surprisingly easy to work with.  After applying a long bead of the gel with the included brush, I pushed the gel to my desired shape, and then let it self level to smooth itself out.  On both thick and thin layers very little effort was required on my part.  In fact, if I tried to get the shape perfect with the brush, the gel got stickier and messier, so I quickly learned to let the gel smooth itself out.  Tip: once you get your shape all smoothed out, turn your nail upside down and let gravity create a natural apex before popping it under the lamp. So far I’ve only used the clear gel.  I created on extension (not shown), attached rhinestones to several pride nails, and fully encapsulated a fully covered rhinestone nail.  1 thick layer of this hard gel and a have encased rhinestones that fully cured in just over 2 minutes!  I also plan to use this for simple overlays when my nail need additional support.  The sticker nail forms work well, the slip solution is good for clean up work (not shaping the gel), and the brush/spatula tool work as expected.  The tiny buffer and file are silly...why include tools that won’t last a day?  Best off all, the gel containers are pretty big... these will last me awhile!

title: I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers
text:
I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers, but I ran into some problems with it for my Halloween costume (Daenerys Targaryen). Don't get me wrong, it helpped me execute my costume wonderfully, but fell short in my opinion in three categories.
First, when I initially opened the wig, the fibers at the part/crown were for lack of better words bent in a strange way that could not be corrected, even with light heat from my flat iron (luckily for me this was a non-issue for my costume because I needed to pull the front pieces of hair back into braids, but re-wear is going to look a little strange). Second, because you are purchasing a light colored fiber wig that is woven on to a nude headpiece, some of your natural hair/the wig cap is bound to show through. My issue was that you could starkly see the edging of my nude wig cap through the wig. Lucky for me, I naturally have very light blonde hair, but I couldn't imagine what show through would look like with someone with dark hair (just something to keep in mind). Third, thank the lord I remembered my brush. This thing got crazy tangled, now I knew some would come because of the length I went with, but I was brushing at least once an hour to keep a "fresh look."
With all that being said, I would purchase this wig again (just hopefully ending up with one that has a better crown/part). It looks 10X better and more realistic than anything I could have picked up at a Halloween store for my costume, especially keeping cost in mind at $43.
