I have always been a fan of Taya hair products. I found though that this duo is not one of my favorites. In this pack you get a shampoo and conditioner that are basically travel size for $14. They are a bit bigger than you would get at a hotel for example so you get quite a few applications out of them, but for $14 I find this to be rather expensive to be honest.

The bottles are pretty cute and look nice. When I used the shampoo I have to say I was disappointed by the fragrance. Usually this line has a fantastic fragrance but this one just wasn’t it. It produced a decent lather and rinsed out with ease. The conditioner had a similar fragrance in line with the shampoo. It was nice and soft and I did leave it in my hair for about 3 minutes I would say. It was easy to rinse out and left no residue on my hair. My hair overall looked ok once it was dry and was pretty soft but nothing impressive that would warrant spending $14 on this. I am sorry I just wasn’t impressed with this set, especially since you can get the full sized ones for a similar price really.

title: My cellulite looks less pronounced.
text:
When I start using instaNatural Cellulite Cream, my cellulite wasn’t too bad. But I still want to get rid of them completely, if possible, for sure.

I’ve used topical lotion to get rid of cellulite in the past and some worked and others no so much. So, I wasn't sure what kind of results this cream will deliver. Most of the review shows awesome results and I wanted to try this cream.

It's been a month since I start to use this. I am pretty sure every skin/body types react to cream differently and some may show results sooner and others may take longer. Unfortunately, I have skin type that takes while to get used to the product. As expected, this cellulite cream does work, but not as fast as some reviewers indicated.

On 3rd week of using this cream, my cellulite does look less noticeable. I did what I call "pinch test" (pinch my skin and see if skin dimples, how the dimple looks - pronounced, slight or none, etc) and skin looks much smoother. I believe it would get rid of them if I continue using this cream.

This is very thick cream. Even if it isn't for the cellulite, it smells good and it make my skin soft.
Also, I didn’t shower or bath at least hour after I applied cream. I think I have body type that takes longer to see the results than other people. I still have about 1/3 left in the jar, so I will keep using it until it is gone.

text: I got these to give to my husband to try, as I don't think he has ever used a face scrub before. His skin isn't bad but everyone's skin could do with a little scrub every once in a while to brighten and freshen things up. I tested it out before giving it to him as i wanted to make sure these didn't have any off putting smells or texture. Scent wise, these are nice - not too overpowering, a gender neutral scent. I was expecting the typical masculine scent you find in men's skincare but I was pleasantly surprised that it is more gender neutral. After using the scrub my face felt clean. It isn't a super strong, gritty scrub but more on the gentler side. I think this could be a good scrub to use 3 times a week because it isn't super gritty but I would also rotate this with another face scrub that is grittier. This scrub didn't leave my skin with the softest, smoothest feeling afterwards like with some other scrubs but it isn't bad. This is a good one for someone that wants a gentler, less harsh scrub. Good ingredients.

title: Grandma Agafia Shampoos are GREAT.
text:
Have been using the "Grandma Agafia" product lines for a few years - they are superb.
The aromas are not overpowering or objectionable, and all of the ingredients are natural.
I am an over-60 male with advanced male-pattern baldness. If it were not for these products, I am sure I would be slick-bald by now.
When I started on the propolis formula almost ten years ago, I WAS slick bald on top. A month of using the shampoo and my scalp started sprouting "peach fuzz" hair - not a full recovered hairline by any means, but it showed that the shampoo was doing its job of cleaning the scalp and supporting follicle health.
I have much less breakage, and the hair I have left retains its thickness and diameter.

title: High Molecular Weight is the Real King!
text:
I had been using High Molecular Weight HA for a couple of weeks on my face/ hair with nice moisturizing results. But at some point I read on beauty blogs and publications that since Low Molecular Weight HA is better absorbed through the skin, that it was a much better option for the face. Made sense to me. Because of this I bought a LMW HA serum to put on my skin. This serum felt differently, watery yet more drying that the HMW HA (HMW can initially feel a bit drying on the skin). My face also felt irritated ( I have acne-prone skin) after the first days of using it. I still decided to buy this powder and the results very similar to the serum I bought.

So I decided to do some research on the difference between both, the HMW and the LMW, because I could not understand why the LMW, which is supposed to be a far better option for the skin (according to the beauty industry) , did not give me the good results I have with the HMW. Interestingly enough I found this: "Transepidermal water loss increased by 55.5% with low-molecular weight , and was reduced by 28% with crosslinked resilient , and by 16% with HMW". So more water loss with LMW? Not good.

I also noted this: "There is abundant experimental evidence from the human physiology and biochemistry literature to support the basic notion that LMW-HA is inflammatory, pro-fibrotic, and associated with adult scarring phenotypes rather than fetus-like, scar-free, truly regenerative healing. The latter is what we want in an any aesthetic procedure, or topical adjunct to a procedure, or just for topical use." This part here may explain why my face felt irritated and even got a mild breakout after using the LMW HA. More info on this on Barefacedtruth. They have detailed explanation and comments on this.

I did give this product a 3-star because it is nicely packaged, has the detailed info on the product, etc. 2 stars down for being marketed as a potent moisturizer.

Remember, whenever you use retinol you want to make sure to protect your skin from the sun since retinol makes your skin more sensitive to the sun. However retinol is very good for your skin.

This face oil is very light and absorbs quickly into the skin. It does leave your skin slightly oily but to me that is ok since I am using a face oil. I prefer to use this at night for two reasons, one because my face is a bit oily for a while when using it and also because retinol containing products do make your skin more sensitive to the sun. When I use this product my skin feels always super soft and smooth and looks nicely moisturized. There are little specs in it that look like gold and I am not sure if it is that or something else but when I use this facial oil my skin has this natural glow to it that I really like. This oil is fantastic and is quickly becoming one of my go to facial oils.

title: Just got an amazing shave!
text:
I have about 10 razors. I have been in search of better and better shaves. My Feather AS-D2 is awesome and smooth but perhaps a bit too mild. I fine even the Merkur 34C a little too aggressive for my skin. The Merkur Futur is horrible for me and is a paperweight for anyone who prefers mild razors. The iKon B1 slant is a perfect balance. Not too aggressive, and with a light touch it gave me a very smooth shave. I normally do 3 passes and then touch up areas that need it. I had 5 days growth when I shaved with this razor head today. I was amazed when I finished my first pass. It looked like I had done two passes with my other razors. I normally do with the grain, cross-grain, and then lightly against the grain.
With the B1 I did a with-the-grain pass and one very light across-the-grain pass and it looked like I was done shaving. I did a touch-up in one or two spots and I called it good. An against the grain pass would have left me absolutely BBS but that usually gives me ingrown hairs. Oh, by the way, no nicks, weepers, or irritation at all. The head is shaped very weird with the slant design but I was able to shave under my nostrils with ease; much better than most, actually! I really am impressed with this head.
I can't wait to do another shave tomorrow.
My shave:
iKon B1 head
iKon OSS handle from my 101
Persona Lab Blue blade (2nd shave on the blade)
Stirling Soap Co. British Leather shaving soap
Stirling Soap Co. Coniferous Pre-Shave oil

Unlike the fake reviews already submitted, this is a real review from a real buyer. I bought these to spritz the dogs when they bark. They looked like they would be perfect for that except you can't adjust the sprayer. It ONLY does a fine mist. This would be perfect for misting your plants and other uses where you would want something very fine. For the dogs, however, I'd like to adjust the sprayer so it can shoot further.
I think I'm going to keep them, though, and use them outside when it's hot and we need to spritz ourselves to cool down.
The tube is about 3.5 inches longer than the bottle. At first, I thought this would be too long but it curls nicely along the bottom of the bottle, so it should get all the liquid better than other sprayers.
Also, the description says it can be used for shampoo or as a soap dispenser - that's not going to work with these bottles and spray head unless your shampoo or soap has the consistency of water!

title: has to be lengthening and make it look like I have eye lashes
text:
I am picky about my mascara. It has to be waterproof, has to be lengthening and make it look like I have eye lashes. It can't cause irritation when I wear contacts. The reason I tried this product was because I was out of mascara and was being adventurous in trying a new product. This product was dark, made it look like I had lashes, and made them look longer. I don't remember seeing anything about being waterproof but I wore it my first day when it was hot and I didn't have black eyes by the end of the day! I don't see much "thickening" going on with this product though. My lashes are very thin and minimal due to wearing mascara for so many years. I feel this product helped in making them stand out, but not so much making them look thick and perhaps fake-ish. I began layering this on with my other go to mascara and it definitely helps. Not a bad product by any means, just not your product if your main purpose is thickening.

I did receive this product at a discounted price for my honest opinion. No matter the price I paid for it, all statements are truly my own and are no way altered. People rely on reviews before trying a product and I believe in giving my honest opinion to help others make their decision. Just remember, what works for some may not always work for others. We are all different after all.

title: IF your blowdryer is a match for this diffuser, you are going to want it for lift and volume. Nothing else compares.
text:
Several years ago I had purchased a blowdryer with a similar attachment. I absolutely adored that thing - you could use it on the top of your hair or the sides to give lift so your hair had volume without using any product or doing any backbrushing. The thing was a miracle worker!

Then we entered the era of pin straight hair, and volume and body were out. Thank God, we seem to be passing that era, but hairstyling implements seem to be lagging behind. I was dying to try this diffuser to see if it emulated the gizmo from long ago, and it does. Well made hair styling tool that gives lift and volume to your hair, I love it. Well, kinda.

I'm not sure how 'universal' this is. I tried it on my current blowdryer, and it didn't fit. I had to go digging around until I finally found a Conair dryer upon which it fit, and the funny thing is that it fit like it was MADE for the dryer. The odd thing is that the Conair looks to have the same kind of nozzle the other blowdryer had, so go figger.

IF you have a blowdryer that marries this diffuser well, this is definitely something you're going to want in your hair arsenal. It'd almost be worth getting a new dryer just to use this, it's that good (one star off for the weirdess of the 'universal' claim.)

title: The best razor ever!
text:
I had a Norelco years ago, then I went through three Brauns (the micro-foil ones that a straight instead of having three circular blades like this one). All my razors were expensive, they were all the best in the bunch. This is the best by far.

This razor shaves close, I have never felt my skin so smooth except when I used to use a blade. It conforms to your skin, even my neck comes out smooth (about 4 minutes to completely shave smooth, or I'll usually shave for less than a minute and get a shave that lasts until I get home from work). It has a timer that not only tells you exactly how many minutes of battery are left, but it also tells you how many minutes you shaved for (which comes in handy more than I thought it would). The best feature is that you can pop the top up and rinse it in water! My brauns cleaned with refil cartridges that were hard to find and expensive and a hassel; whereas my old Norelco cleaned with a brush and never got really clean. This one cleans easily and quickly, and even beeps to tell you when to clean it! Also, this razor doesn't give me razor burn like my Brauns did!!

If you are a first time shaver, or an expierenced shaver looking for a better shave from an electric razor, this is the one for you! I will never buy any other brand of razor again and I'll probably have this one for years to come...

title: I counted the days I was without it...
text:
My original Sonicare died after about 2 years. My wife spent [...] bucks on it and needless to say I was not happy to see it go. You would think a $[...] toothbrush would last pretty much forever... Anyway, I replaced it with this much cheaper model and am very pleased so far. In addition to being a lot less expensive it has a much simplified design which should last longer, and has a user replaceable battery.

On the negative side, it seems to chew through batteries. In fact I actually reported the first one Amazon shipped as defective as it stopped working after 5 days. Turns out the batteries I swapped were dead too and there was nothing wrong with the toothbrush after all. My bad. The fresh batteries I installed only lasted maybe 3 weeks or so. I'm going to use rechargeables from now on, but just be forewarned that this thing gobbles batteries.

But in terms of the operation of the toothbrush I love it. In the short time I had to use a regular toothbrush waiting for this to arrive I felt like I had trench mouth. No matter how long or how vigorously I would brush my teeth just never felt clean, and by 10AM if felt like I hadn't brushed in days. The commercial is a cliche but it's true - Sonicare makes you feel like you just walked out of the dentist office.

title: Very strong scent at first, but it disappears very quickly.
text:
I really loved the idea of this Boiess Baby Cologne "Les Enfants" in White Blossom. Not because I think it is a good idea for a baby, because boy, is it not. I actually thought it would be perfect for myself since I don't like loud fragrances. The description of the scent profile really enticed me, as I love all of the notes. I was able to try both the Lavanda and the White Blossom scents.
Both of the "Cologne" sprays smell identical to me. I can't say that I can tell them apart at all. They both have a very strong earthy, herbal, slightly floral scent that is heavily ladened with alcohol upon spraying. It stays very strong for several minutes, but then starts to dry down.
Sadly, once it dries down, the scent pretty much dissipates. If I don't spray it heavily at first, which is too much for my asthma to handle, much less any baby, the scent just goes away completely. I must spray it on me again. If I spray it on a few times over an hour or so, I can smell the ever so slightest hint of it on my clothing later, if I put my nose right on it. That is a lot of spraying for very little payoff.
I know this is meant for kids mostly, but I would think the scent would and should last longer. Sure, my grandsons will like using it, maybe or not, as it is quite strong at first. But, I think it would just be more for the fun of it and very short lived. This is also very expensive "Cologne" to not be able to smell it after 30 minutes, and right at $28 is too expensive for me to buy just for the fun of it.  
For others this "Baby Cologne" may be something wonderful or maybe they can smell it more than I can. As I said, I really love the idea of a light fragrance, but not for babies. I do wish the scent stuck around more for me.

title: Pretty nice quality hair for the price.
text:
I've been using extensions since 2006, due to health issues causing extreme hair thinning. I used to get the fused extensions at the salon, 1500 dollars back in the day. They broke off from the weight of the extensions because my hair was so fine and thin. The fused glob of hair was just too much and so many fell out. I started buying the clip in hair, taking the clips off and using them as weft hair. I use salon pro white glue, much like eyelash glue but used for weft hair. It is a wonderful solution and I still alternate between tape in hair and the clip in wefts. I also buy closures and custom color, to make my own toppers. What a job! But, I'm happy with the results. I have more control over the color and style, and I feel 'normal'.

This hair is a medium to coarse texture, thick, and has a really nice body wave. The is soft and smooth and doesn't feel damaged. It will blend with fine hair. You can use a straightening iron, just be sure that you can control the temperature. Once you burn this hair, it will stink and it will be ruined. However, if you control the temperature and use care, the hair looks great straight and shiny. You can also curl the hair. I have used felted hot rollers, and those work really well. They are safer, and not as damaging, and the curls last so long.

These 16" extensions are very nice. Although the ad isn't quite accurate. The color is a darker caramel blond, and a reddish brown. This is not piano keys, but close. The wefts are not in the ombre style, they are bold and varied high lights. If you look at the ad images, the photos showing the people aren't shown with this product in their hair. The wefts laying on a surface showing the color differences between the offered colors is the most accurate. I've offered some images that show the color more accurately. You can custom color most of the wefted hair, but adding color is easier. Typically the hair has so much red in it that it is impossible to cover or remove, and the dye can be hard to remove. You can add a longer root to eliminate the chunky roots. My hair is so fine, the sewn edge can be obvious, so have a good match to my natural blonde ash tone roots helps. Any coloring will add to the damage and potentially shorten the life of the hair, but for me it makes me happier to have an exact match to what I want, and I am hard to match for color.

The weight of the hair is shown in a photo in ounces. In grams, we get a little over 104 grams, far less than the advertised 120grams, and I would complain about this and have, just not for this brand. That being said, the fullness and the weight is still good, and the wefts seem to feel average when compared to what I usually order. If you order the longer options, the hair will be thinner, as most hair is sold by weight. 120 would be better, of course. This weight is significantly lower than 120grams.

Shedding. Over the last 7 years or so, shedding has become a real problem. It never used to be this bad. There is a weft glue that is meant to slow or prevent shedding and I always use it. It makes the weft more stiff, but if you use the weft the way I use them, you need to do something to protect your weft hair. You can find it online. If you are using this hair for special occasions and clipping to thick strong hair and are simply making your hair more full, wild and glamorous, then you may not need to worry about shedding. I did finger comb this hair once out of the packaging, and there was significant shedding. Again, I say, this is a common issue now, and unique to this particular brand. I have no idea what changed but the wefts should not shed this much, but they all do this with most brands. I have to say that if the wefts didn't shed so much, they would last for a couple of years or longer. Also, keep in mind I use the wefts differently, so clipping, as intended, may offer longer life and far less shedding.

The length is 16" and the hair hangs nicely, with a gentle, natural taper. There is a very nice body wave. It's not a blunt edge finish, which is nice.

The clips are the same type that I see on most clip in kits. They are small, and hold nicely even on fine hair.

Over all, I think this is a great value and will require the extra effort to keep them looking great over a year or more. To keep human hair looking good and tangle free, I use the sleep and shine shampoo and conditioner. It keeps the hair fresher and mat free longer. There are a lot of youtube videos that can help you with application and care, and give you tips and tricks.

4 stars.

GLO Science Teeth Whitening Pen 35 Aplications, Safe and Efective, No Sensitivity, Easy to Use Dentist Invented Whitening Treatment, Travel-Friendly

Are my teeth whiter? Yes. It's not so white that anyone will see me and be like 'wow your teeth are so white!' but it is whiter and I notice it, which I prefer. I have very sensitive teeth and almost no enamel. The pen is a click pen, and you have click quite a lot to get it started. I thought mine was faulty at first, and the clicker even got stuck half way down but I smacked it and it popped back and I kept clicking. The silicone tip has little bristles and it does a good job of coming off on your teeth - I was worried the gel wouldn't grip onto my teeth and would slide, but it didn't. It does have a cinnamon taste, and it does dry in 30 seconds, it was easy enough to smile for 30 seconds and it was on there. Truly I forgot about it after that (don't eat or drink for 30 min if you can). Are my teeth whiter? I couldn't tell after 1 use, but after two, I also couldn't tell... BUT I took a before and after photo (which I'll save you from because my lips look awful right now) and my teeth are definitely visibly whiter! I'm happy with this, it's easy to put on, doesn't make my teeth sensitive, works for whitening, dries quickly, and you don't even have to spit it out.

title: easy use, comfortable, could have longer nozzle
text:
I use a larger plug in water flosser unit in my full bathroom (on upper level of house) which has a large capacity water reservoir. I typically take my time and use it at night before bed. However, I wanted a unit on my main floor bathroom for quick use during the day without having to go back upstairs, or for use if I am going to be gone all day and want to take it with me. Therefor I have been keen on getting a portable chargeable flosser. That, and my first floor bathroom is super tiny with nowhere to put a typical flossing unit nor anywhere to plug it in. This is perfect for me!

Nice unit, right out of the box. It is attractive, feels comfortable in the hand, as is easy to get it going. While it comes with instructions, it is easy to figure out- very intuitive. USB cord is good length. The port that plugs into the unit has a pop-in cover ("anti-fouling rubber stopper"). It doesn't come attached, and I wish it did since I'd rather not have that area exposed to water. I sense that I will lose that cap soon enough, or just forget to use it. We'll see.

The unit comes with four attachments, all for doing different jobs- so unless someone has a need for this unit and for an attachment for something different than what you need, I would say this is for solo use. Good sized water reservoir, too.

Unlike my main unit, this one has a fairly straight nozzle in comparison. This makes it a challenge to get behind the rear most molars. If the nozzles were a little longer, with slightly more curve than it has, I would consider this a perfect product.

title: Wheels broke, base broke, rebuilt using other parts because the seat itself is very comfortable.
text:
Purchased this chair a year ago. I use it exclusively to roll around my small kitchen cooking. This is the fourth saddle chair I have owned, and they all eventually broke because I weigh 400 pounds. Of the four styles, this is by far the most comfortable seat for a big man. The seat is in great condition, and I have combined parts in order to continue using it.
The wheels broke within six months. Replaced them with "rollerblade" wheels and it was great for another six months. Then the base exploded into multiple small parts while moving from one side of my kitchen to the other. It is frustrating to see a chair, on wheels, that can't withstand the stress of heavy weight in motion. I resign myself to purchasing these relatively inexpensive saddle chairs yearly, but would gladly pay more for one built to last for someone my size.

It has a light clean fragrance, but does not at all smell like black tea, as I had hoped it would. The consistency is gel like, but a lot stickier than I would prefer. It definitely leaves a tacky feel on my skin. Luckily, it absorbs well overnight and does not leave a mess on my pillow. My skin does look and feel moisturized and soothed in the morning. There are definitely sleeping packs I prefer, such as the Erno Laszlo Hydra-Therapy Memory Sleep Mask. Of course, this product is nearly 9 times less expensive than the Laszlo for 3 times the product. With most skin care, I find you get what you pay for, so this isn't at all surprising. title: ASP Lightless Gel is awesome for repairing a broken natural nail, a must have!
text:
UPDATE 10/13/14 I had originally rated this item a five stars and I've left my original review unedited because it was accurate HOWEVER I've changed the rating to three stars because of the following.

I've found that when I use this product to repair a broken, or pealing or split nail, when its freshly applied, it's awesome BUT when a few days go by and the product starts to get old it starts to lift and the problem is that even being very careful, if the product peals from the nail, IT TAKES A FEW LAYERS OF THE NATURAL NAIL WITH IT and that's what I was one of the things I was trying to prevent when I applied this product...What I ended up doing was soaking off the remainder of this product and patching the now really damaged area of my nail with ASP Fiberglass
http://www.amazon.com/s/ref=nb_sb_ss_i_0_6?url=search-alias%3Daps&field-keywords=asp%20fiberglass&sprefix=ASP+fi%2Caps%2C272 and two layers of brush on nail glue which is the method I plan to continue using from now on since it does not lift and tear my nails...http://www.amazon.com/Spilo-MISC-Bondini-Plus-Brush-On/dp/B0002Z8SE8/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1413205777&sr=8-1&keywords=brush+on+nail+glue.

Although I bought mine at my local Sally's, this product is so awesome, I had to come an give it a thumbs up!

Now let me say that I have natural nails that tend to break at the base (bead) of the nail & so cutting them is not a painfree option nor a pretty one at that ;)

The only reason why I use all three products (listed below) is to repair broken nails, to give them time to grow out while I get to have pretty, all the same length nails ;)

This "light less gel" has a thicker consistency than brush on glue, which by the way, was the method I was using prior to coming across this gem in a YouTube tutorial video.

Now it does not come with a brush applicator so I took an empty nail polish bottle, cleaned it out & I filled it with pure acetone to prevent the brush from getting hard; & that's the brush I use to apply this gel. Just make sure to wipe the brush a few time on a napkin before using to wipe off the acetone.

After I've removed the old nail polish, I wipe my nail clean with either an alcohol pad or some acetone. I then cut an appropriate piece of the fiberglass to cover the break. I apply the fiberglass to the clean nail & I apply a thin line of this gel over the patch, then I take my handy, dandy nail polish brush & I spread out a thin layer of the gel over the entire nail, same as if I was applying nail polish. Then I spray the Gel Cure (which is a god sent because it dries this thick gel almost instantly) & voila! the nail is as good as not, well you know ;) Now depending on the size of the break, use your judgement to determine if you need a 2nd layer. This method last more than the regular nail glue & as such, soaking it off will take a little more time but who cares as long as your nail has time to grown without suffering from either pain or an odd looking manicure ;)

When you add the cost of the fiberglass, the gel & the cure, you are looking at approximately $30 BUT this will last a long, long, long time so for me its cost effective.

If you have natural nails that tend to split, these items are a must. These are staples in my "manicure rescue arsenal".

Highly recommended items for sure!

I bought this "light less gel", the

ASP Gel Cure
http://www.amazon.com/ASP-Gel-Cure/dp/B00IYPRZOW/ref=sr_1_3?s=beauty&ie=UTF8&qid=1402513514&sr=1-3&keywords=lightless+gel

& the ASP All Season Nail Fiberglass Nail Wrap
http://www.amazon.com/All-Season-Nail-Fiberglass-Wrap/dp/B0064TPMIQ/ref=sr_1_1?s=beauty&ie=UTF8&qid=1402513563&sr=1-1&keywords=nail+fiberglass

UPDATE 7/3/14
Just wanted to point out that should you decide to yank off this product with you teeth or if you are a "picker", be prepared to lose a layer or two of your natural nail. WHICH MEANS DAMAGING YOUR NAIL UNTIL IT GROWS OUT WHICH DEFEATS THE PURPOSE OF PURCHASING AND APPLYING THIS PRODUCT. This product should be removed with a cotton ball soaked in acetone, wrapped in aluminum foil for about ten to fifteen minutes so as to remove the product safely WITHOUT damaging your nail. But it truely does last longer than regular nail glue. FYI! ;)

My daughter has TTM and has no natural eyelashes, so magnetics are the ONLY type of lashes that work for here.

She liked the look of the lashes in this set. They weren't all over-the-top, super glam. There were quite a few pairs that she thought she could use for daily wear and even liked the look of "glam" pairs that were included for when she really wants to go all out. So it was HUGELY disappointing that there were NO MAGNETS on ANY of the pairs of lashes. She did try the eyeliner with lashes she already had, but wasn't very impressed with it either. It didn't seem to completely dry down and had a slightly tacky feel even after waiting about 10 minutes. I thought maybe they had mixed up the order and sent her regular lashes & lash glue, but it wasn't tacky ENOUGH to hold a lash in place. Overall, it was a fail for her. title: Better than many other epilators for smooth skin
text:
I've tried a couple of different types of epilators over the past 15-20 years. While I was usually happy enough with the results, I rarely used them since it always seemed like you had to wait until the hair got long enough for the unit to grip the hair in order to yank it out. And rarely did I really want the hair on my legs to reach that amount of stubble. Not to mention the pain that is involved with epilators. Yes, I am a weenie.

This model of the Braun Silk Epil removes much shorter hair. It claims to remove hair that is as short as a grain of sand (0.5mm). I personally find it requires it to be a bit longer than that to grip; but it does do a much better job of reaching short hair than others I've tried. It has a pivoting head which lets it work around all your body contours. A light on the unit allows even the palest, finest hairs to be visible.

In addition to hair removal, this epilator refines your skin. A sonic massage system and high-density brush scrub away old skin cells. This exfoliation helps to stimulate the regeneration of surface skin cells in order to create a smoother skin tone. I do notice a bit of a smoother, more even skin tone on my legs now. This sonic massage is my favorite part of the device...in part because I really don't like the tweezing part.

This model can be used wet or dry and uses rechargeable batteries rather than a power cord.

Unfortunately, I find that it still hurts...although not nearly as much as it used to. With regular use, the hairs on my legs have become fewer. Plus, the already pale fine hair is becoming even thinner and weaker. Braun claims that it will keep your body free of hair for up to 4 weeks. I usually find it to be somewhere in the 2 to 3 week range for me. Still, that's nice for when you're going on vacation or heading off to the beach for a week or two. I allow the growth to get to the slight stubbly stage and then I'm perfectly smooth for a couple of weeks.

title: It works but only on dry hair and with HEAT
text: It's advertised as a no heat hair curler clips but for me it did not work without heat.  Using without heat resulted in kinks.  NEVER use on wet hair or the kinks will be set in your hair until you wash and restyle.  These clips are not a replacement for double prong root clips used in the curly girl method.  I watched every video I could find on how to use these clips and they all used the following steps:  (1) Start with clean dry hair.  Move the top layer of hair out of the way and take a section of hair from underneath.  Put the clips in with some looseness against the scalp.  They should not be tight against your scalp.  Make sure the clip part is turned to the outside and the hair is pulled straight away from scalp.  (2) apply heat gently to hair using medium to high heat and low air flow (3) apply cold air using hair dryer or wait for hair to cool naturally.  Do not leave the clip in too long if you are letting it cool naturally or it may leave kinks.  (3) Take out the clips and comb through with fingers, ruffling slightly to break up any visible kinks.  Blend in top layer so any kinks still visible will be hidden underneath.  Good luck!

text:
In this kit, you get a nice set to complete a French tip design. You get 30 ml of each color, which is a wonderful size. You also get a base and topcoat, an application tool, and a couple of glitters. This would make the perfect kit if it didn't have a few issues.

They also take quite a bit longer to fully cure under an LED UV light than most other poly gels. I did use tips and dual forms. When I remove the dual forms after curing them for 60 seconds on top and bottom, they were still tacky on top. I had to cure them for another 30 seconds. My nails only lasted a little over a week before starting to lift around the edges. This is hardly a long-lasting poly gel, in my opinion.
I'm a still licensed but retired nail technician, so I am very well aware and knowledgeable on how to prep nails properly. User error was not the problem. These gels would be good for practice, but if you are looking for a poly gel that will last for more than a week, you may want to look at another brand. 3.5 Stars ✨

title: Once You Learn How To Use, It's Great
text:
I know it says "Men's" on there, but I am a woman, and I use this razor. I just happen to have very coarse hair on my legs. Lady shavers don't do it for me. In fact, I've always had to use 2 razors, a men's for the legs and a women's for the underarms. I know, more information than you wanted, but it's relevant.

This razor is the only one I have ever had that works for everything. Oh, I had some really nasty razor burn before I got the hang of it, but since then, it's been great! No cleaning and maintaining 2 razors any more.

I have found with this razor, that putting pressure on it is a big no-no. If I do that, it will tear up my skin big time. I have to just sort of guide/glide it over the area, no pressure on it, and it does a beautiful job without the razor burn. Now, I honestly don't know how that would go for a guy and his face, but that's how it works for me on ALL parts I shave.

This razor only needs charged about every two to three weeks. There is no indicator system on this razor, and when it needs charged, it just quits. If you keep playing with the on/off button, it will run for 2 or 3 more minutes, but that's it. It takes one hour (about) to recharge, much better than any razor I ever had before.

This razor is easy to clean, just run the head under the sink, shake the water off, and let it dry out. I do that once a week. Easy peasy.

Like I said, I've no idea how my experience might translate for a guy. I gave it 4 stars because of the lack of a recharge indicator. Other that, it is wonderful for me.

text:
I've never used magnetic lashes before, but was very intrigued! These magnetic lashes + the eyeliner are STRONG! I've attached photos of the lashes after wearing them for 10 hours at my workplace. The magnetic lashes and the liner are so strong in fact, that I actually ripped out a lash because I accidentally had the magnetic liner on my lash!

I'm very impressed by how well it stuck onto my eye throughout the day. I am also VERY surprised of the formula of the eyeliner. I have tried many, many waterproof, smudgeproof eyeliners, but this eyeliner is by far THE MOST waterproof and smudgeproof! I have oily eyelids and my original waterproof eyeliner would still smear on my lower lids (I bought a waterproof Missha eyeliner for $27 and it still smudges!)

Not only that, the liner will also remove very easily with micellar water or makeup removing face wash -- it washes off so clean that I don't have to follow up with another makeup wipe after the shower. This is amazing!

I only really took off 1 star for three reasons:
1) The formula of the eyeliner has a scent that is very perfume-y/chemical-y. This doesn't bother me too much, but I do think that some customers may be bothered by it.
2) The brush of the eyeliner is very flimsy -- it is difficult to get a sharp line, because the brush is so thin.
3) the inner corners of my lashes began to curl up and off my lash line, pulling some eyeliner with it (leaving gaps in my liner).

Overall, I really like this small kit! It is VERY easy to apply and the lashes look so natural! I got very many compliments while wearing these!

I really like the design behind these. You can mount them with screws on a flat surface or corner. And with the included double sided sticky 3M pads, you can do the same without making holes. Plus probably get them on a round pole like a leg of a piece of furniture. The plastic spikes are a good balance of stiff and flexible, though between the two descriptors I'd lean towards stiff. I mounted a couple on my big cat tree (one on a corner and one on the base flat). They obviously blend in fine there. But they're small enough that they would be discrete even if they were put somewhere more out in the open. My cat likes them well enough. She isn't as enamored with them as I had hoped but I've caught her getting the side of her mouth on them more than once already.

Between the cheap price and the non damaging sticky pad option, they're worth trying out if you think your cat would like them. If not, no big loss.

title: Did not work for me
text: Let me begin this review by stating that I have been using Egyptian, Indian and Pakistani 100% henna for over 30 years with beautiful results that lasted a full 3 months.  I decided to try this product because I wanted a change from all the red highlights and thought it would be nice to tone down to a browner hue.  I not only followed the instructions to the letter, but had several exchanges with the seller to make sure what I was doing was correct.  The good news is that this combination beautifully toned down the red from all my prior years of using henna only.  The bad news is that NOT ONE gray hair (I'm dark brown with about 15% gray) gave up being gray! So in addition to the hassle, mess and expense of doing this treatment (and make no mistake - it's messy and time consuming) I will have to double up this month and do my regular henna only routine.  I did a bit of research, by the way, and learned that most henna/indigo distributors, unlike Harvest Moon, suggest mixing up the henna and indigo powders SEPARATELY and then combining.  Based on my experience, I'd have to say this would probably work better (the rationale probably being the same as why combining shampoo and conditioner together don't work as well as shampooing and THEN conditioning).  Likewise, everyone else except Harvest Moon recommends wrapping the hair in plastic wrap and then covering with a shower cap and leaving on for a MINIMUM of 2 hours (Harvest Moon says their product works in less than one hour and is against wrapping.)  Leaves me to wonder if the gray hairs would not be gray had I followed the advice of the other henna/indigo distributors.  Here's a good reference website:  [...]

title: What kind of sorcery is this??!!??! I Cannot stress enough how truly AMAZING this liner is!!!
text:
I originally purchased this eyeliner at a Kohls department store for my daughter for her to practice with makeup. However, I ran out of my regular eyeliner one day and I had to use I had to use hers. It was soooo AMAZING that I immediately went to Amazon to see if they had and to my pleasant surprise, they did.

It glides on with ease, its true to color and doesn't lighten after application. Its EXTREMELY precise and beyond easy to use. It is by far genuinely the EASIEST liquid eyeliner I have used in my 25plus years of using liquid liners. The felt tip is more hardened which makes its SUPER easy to control and place on the eyelid, whereas other liquid liners have softer felt tips which are floppy and they bend easy leaving you with having to press lightly so you don't mess up your straight line. This E.L.F liner is opposite of ALL that, its hard but not TOO hard that it doesn't glide precisely with your stroke. It has a PERFECT sized super thin tip which allows me to give my cat eye a precise small line finish at the corner of eye, it's perfection!

My most FAVORITE part of this liquid eyeliner is that it does NOT get cakey, if I want a thicker more pronounced look, I can go over the same line several times and it doesn't cake up. I mean sure if you're gonna put 10 layers on, I'm sure it'll eventually cake, but building with 3 layers, no cake! First time I tried to do thicker line, I was so nervous not wanting to mess up my entire eye makeup, but I had faith and gave it a try and was SHOCKED that it didn't get thick and cakey, and it still looked like I only had 1 layer of eyeliner on.

Did I mention it stays put! I'll sometimes get watery eyes in the corner of my eyes, and this magic liner doesn't smudge, doesn't rub off, it could be that my make up setting spray helps, or it could be the eyeliner, but whatever it is its definitely some sort of sorcery. Haha.... But regardless with the insanely affordable price, you WON'T be disappointed!!!

It removes SUPER easy with make up remover, or just soap and water, I always wash my face, then use make up remover to get any remaining make up off, and the eyeliner always seems to be gone after just soap and water.

Truly the best bang for your buck!!!!

title: It's a groomer, not a haircutter
text: The item has the attachments to cut hair but it is not designed for full-on haircuts.  It's to keep you groomed between haircuts so you don't have to go as often, hence it being called a groomer. Also, if you're having trouble charging it, that's because you're not likely following what it says right in the instructions...it must be charged for a FULL 24 hours before the first use.  Do this, and it works fine. The neckline trimmer is a godsend.  My neck hair grows faster than that on my head so this does nicely for a neckshave when I don't really need a haircut yet.  Professional haircuts are getting too expensive everywhere to go in every 3-4 weeks when you don't need a full cut but do need a touch-up.  This does the trick in that respect.  The nose hair attachment works fine...again, the idea is not to get to the point where the hair is so long and thick that it doesn't work.  Groom it, keep up with it as it grows.  That's what this thing is for.  I have misplaced one of the attachments, unfortunately, so will be buying a new one but this does a a great job, better than the bigger, bulkier products out there.

Here we have a gorgeous tea canister that is well made and beautiful. It also closes tightly, keeping my tea fresh. A good tea canister is not cheap, so I didn't have sticker shock with this product.

Thankfully, the company thoughtfully puts out refill packs of this delicious and calming tea.
I'll definitely be ordering a refill because not only do I like it myself, but after going through so many different calming and sleep inducing teas, this is my spouse's absolute favorite. Not just because of the taste, but it helps her to totally relax and even sleep throughout the night. Other teas and sleep formulations such as melatonin and valerian supplements just don't do the trick.
For me, it's more about the delightful taste. Slightly floral, slightly sweet. Yes, it does relax me and is helpful as part of a nighttime ritual, but not as much as my spouse. We both love it but for different reasons.

And I just adore the look of the canister. A lovely gloss ceramic, with an Art Deco nod, that fits in any decor. No hiding it, it's proudly on the counter, ready for anytime you need a little tea comfort.

title: Not impressed.
text:
My hair type: naturally curly. Medium thickness/density. Medium/long length. Very fluffy i use no hair products. I usually blow dry it straight after a wash and it lasts for several days before I need to wash it again.

PROS:
- Smells nice. Smells like the essential oils. It's very subtle, not perfumey at all, and really I can't even smell it after my hair is dry.
- Gentle. It does not irritate my scalp
- Cleared up my dandruff/scalp rash from my previous shampoo that irritated my scalp and I was always itchy.
- Cleans well. Some natural shampoos don't seem to remove all natural oils or hair products, but this one does.
- Even without conditioner, I can get a comb through my hair. Not something I can say about most shampoos.

CONS:
- Still need conditioner. I thought with all the oils are nourishing that I wouldn't need a conditioner, but I do.
- My hair gets oily faster. When using this, I need to wash my hair more often. I used to get 4 days out of wash and now I barely get two since switching to this.
- My hair is extremely static-y! It doesn't matter how much conditioner, leave-ins or serums I apply, I cannot get the static to go away. I didn't have this problem before this shampoo.
- Price. It doesn't do anything for me that I can't get from a cheaper shampoo.

OVERALL: The fact that may hair gets greasy fast and and that it's so static-y tells me my hair is too dry. I need a moisturizing shampoo. When my hair/scalp is properly moisturized, it doesn't get greasy and I don't get flyaways. I thought this was a moisturizing shampoo with all the oils in it, but I guess they all just get rinsed away, and then some. I will not buy this again because I cannot stand static-y hair.

title: BEWARE BEWARE BEWARE - LATEX LINER!!
text:
I've read this description page backwards and forwards-- there's not one word here from the seller about LATEX.
And maybe that's my misunderstanding, as I thought it was a metal-based liner product for magnetic lash adhesion. But ONE application later, BLISTERS!! BURNING!! ITCHING!!! SWELLING!! Scratchy throat, tingling lips, and shortness of breath!!!
Didn't realize I'd have to break into emergent allergy protocols just trying on lashes today??!

Several other reviews note sensitivity to the metallic-magnetic liner??
NOPE, this stuff is latex: I immediately washed off adhesive and cleaned the lashes once the reaction was underway, but dried liner product is shiny, sticky, and super-flexible..... and super-consistent with Latex.

This company NEEDS to understand severe customer allergies and label appropriately for liability:
Those of us with severe, respiratory latex allergies can and will have life-threatening reactions to this product. It IS NOT LABELLED. But yep, LATEX LATEX LATEX. BEWARE!!

title: A high-quality soap with great aroma, foaming and cleansing that I plan to use quite often
text:
Review of: TCM Men's Cleansing Activated Charcoal Bar Soap - For all skin types - 5oz (1 Pack)

In the handful of times that I’ve used the TCM Charcoal Bar Soap I’ve noticed a number of items that I’ve been really pleased to experience.

The first is the size of the bar; no wimpy sliver of soap here. The bar right around 3 inches in length, 1 ¾ inches wide and 1 ½ inches tall. A size big enough that, until I used the soap enough times to round off the edges, the size was almost too large to hold easily using just one hand.

A second, immediately noticeable, item was the smell. Not a sweet smell but more of a slight, dusky, flower-like aroma that, for me at least, was super nice. Perhaps, in it’s own way, as nice an aroma as I’ve found with any bar of soap.

The amazing amount of lather this bar gives off was another pleasant surprise, far more than I had expected from something that doesn’t fit into the ‘body-wash’ category. When washing my face, I only need to rub the bar in my hands a couple of times and then when the soap is rubbed onto my face the suds really start forming. The lather is impressive, especially compared to other ‘cleansing’ bars I’ve used before.

The charcoal, or maybe it’s some other ingredient, does seem to do a nice job of cleaning my face, especially after I’ve applied sun screen earlier in the day. Sun screen, in my experience, soaks into my skin really deeply and is almost like a magnet in attracting dirt, and many ‘regular’ soaps simply don’t seem to cut through the grim. The TCM soap, however, removes any embedded dirt and also does away with the slick feeling the sun screen leaves on my face. noticed that many cleaning soaps especially after washing my face.

On the other-side-of-the-coin, however, I’ve noticed that the TCM Charcoal Bar Soap leaves my skin drier than I expected; for me there was no real sense of having any moisturizing left on my face after washing. This dryness was apparent to me as, after washing, my face was almost too dry to be able to comfortably use my electric razor. Still, while that was a surprise to me I don’t consider the dryness to be a major concern compared to the cleaning benefits the soap gives.

All-in-all, the TCM Charcoal Bar is a high-quality soap that I plan to use quite often.

title: Needs Some Work to Make it work!
text: This was my first experience with a wig that wasn’t from Spirit Halloween and I can’t say it was much better. After trying this wig I decided to learn a little more about wigs and I found a ton of info out there about them and how to do a little work on the less expensive ones to make them look better. (ie: thinning them out, plucking the part and hairline, etc.) I also learned about the features of a wig that make it look more realistic, such as synthetic vs human hair/human hair blend, pre-plucked and lace front. Now that I know a bit about wigs I feel more optimistic that I’ll be able to find ones that are affordable yet look more realistic and/or that I’ll be able to work on them a bit to make them look more so. In summary: The part and thickness on this wig are what I think need the most work. There’s virtually no part and the hair on the top is much too dense and puffy. This could be rectified by plucking but the wig is just not worth the work, IMO. The style of it is cute—The length and the waviness of it were exactly what I was looking for. I can’t say the same about the bangs but that’s the part of the wig that would benefit from some plucking and thinning out. The softness is pretty good for a synthetic wig.  I can’t comment on tangling because I didn’t keep the wig long enough to see how it holds up. The color is hard to comment on because it looks so different depending on the light—It can look like an ashy light brown with subtle highlights, a darker, less ashy light brown with no dimension to it, and in others it appears to have a mauve-like tinge to it. (You can see the differences in the pics.) In the end I returned this wig and after doing more research I decided I wouldn’t buy another inexpensive synthetic hair wig and instead look for a human hair blend that may be a little more expensive but looks more realistic. The bottom line: I recommend not buying this wig unless you know how to work on a wig to make it look more realistic.

title: A Necessity for Home Hair Cutting
text:
Back in the golden oldie days B.C. (Before COVID-19), I wouldn’t have known the difference between a barber’s cape and a bullfighter’s cape. But today, home hair cutting is now the norm, and a barber’s cape is practically a necessity.

This SmoTecQ one does the job with little drama. Measuring an adult-sized 57 by 63 inches, it has an elasticized neckband with two thin but sturdy metal clasps that can adjust to fit tightly around any size neck. The fabric in the back tended to gape open a little when I tested it, and it’s much shorter in the back than in the front, but overall it does a good job at what it’s intended to do. Hair doesn’t stick to it too badly, so it’s relatively easy to wipe clean after use. Folding it up to try to put it neatly back into its plastic storage bag was a challenge.

That’s not to say that hair still doesn’t go all over the floor, though, and that’s why my amateur haircuts, whether I’m getting them or giving them, take place on one of my outdoor patios.

Based on my zero knowledge of what makes a good one or a bad one, I have to rate this barber’s cape at a middle-of-the-road three stars. I wish I didn’t need one at all, but in the current reality, it’s a must-have item, and this one seems to do the job.

title: Not the best quality, would be great for a younger child or on the go
text:
A little disappointed in this package. I'll start with the good, the gloves work nicely and fit comfortably. The gloves are soft and easy to adjust on the hand and they're lightweight too so they don't get hot and make your hands sweaty.

The standing lamp is a micro USB cable and receiver for power. There is flex when I gently push the top of the lamp and the base. It feels really fragile. The light is a nice soft blue and doesn't get hot when it's on, the power button is fairly easy to press.

The individual handheld lamp isn't chargeable. It runs off three AAA batteries. The hand lamp is a deep blue light but it seems feint. The pink grips also slide on and off the casing fairly easily. It feels really lightweight and cheaper rather than a quality lightweight material.

I think this would be a great kit for travel, you wouldn't be devastated if you lost or damaged and had to replace these tools or maybe for a younger child who is starting to express interest in gel manicures. You wouldn't mind if there's some wear on these and you would replace them with nice quality items when they get used to handling them. This is the nail kit equivalent of giving your cousin your MadCatz controller instead of the official Nintendo one. It's good to have but I think it's worth it to throw a little more into the savings bank and buying a higher quality set or individual set of lamps.

title: Well Made Unit
text: This is an extremely well-made unit and appears completely waterproof.  It charges in about an hour with a charge that lasts me four showers.  While it removes some skin I would prefer stiffer rubber “bristles.”  The handle is made of a slippery plastic that is impossible to hang into with soapy hands.  Probably OK for the bathtub, but risky in the shower.  Men usually have larger backs and are less flexible.  So I made a longer “handle” with a 12” PVC pipe, attached with a gasket and a hose clamp, easily removed for charging.  The pipe also doesn’t slip in a soapy hand.  With all the running gear in the head the unit is top heavy when in the charger.  Even the suction cups on the charger base can’t hold it upright.  However, the gasket for the handle also pushes the unit enough off center to balance it and prevent fall overs.  The instruction sheet is a riot.  It reads like it was run from Chinese through a translation program into “English.”  The best line is “Especially designed with horny brush and thus removing residual horniness.”  If only it were so simple!  It should be rewritten by a native English speaker.

title: Happily Surprised
text:
I was a bit skeptical before trying because I find most hair masks to be more hype than anything else. This one however was great for my long thick wavy mess of a head of hair. It left my hair soft, manageable, and even a bit shinier than before. My hair felt hydrated without being weighted down, and wasn't left straw like which has happened to me in the past when I try to deep condition. I can usually go about 3-4 days between shampoos and didn't find myself needing to wash my hair any sooner than that. Obviously, if you shampoo more often on the regular you will have a different result than me. But basically it didn't leave my hair feeling dirty the next day.

My process: I shampooed and then like most masks and conditioners I kept it away from my roots and only applied it from the midshaft to my ends (otherwise I end up with oily roots). Then I waited... and waited... and waited. Since I was reviewing the product I wanted to make sure I waited the full 10 mins to give it a chance. I was out of stuff to wash and shave after about 3 min so the last 7 were pretty boring. In the future I will probably only wait 5 min. I didn't apply any other conditioner other than my normal heat protector I spritz onto towel dried hair. Blow-dried as usual and the results let me skip the flat iron.

I was pretty please. I find this an easy mask to recommend. I have spent much more and gotten less of a result. I also like that it didn't leave my hair smelling perfumy afterwards.

title: just like mousse or shaving cream, but is a soap for body
text:
The bottle and texture is very much like a hair mousse or shaving cream, but is a wash for the body. Instead of a pump or squeeze bottle, this comes out though as pressure aerosol - also just like a mousse or shaving cream. The ingredients necessary to make this happen are Butane and Propane. They are aerosol propellents. If you have ever used mousse, hair spray, various perfumes/body sprays, air fresheners, aerosol deodorants, or shaving cream,etc.. then you are already familiar with these ingredients. They are generally recognized as safe, and are used in small, diluted quantities in skin care. Fun fact, "These ingredients are used in cosmetics and personal care products as a replacements for chlorofluorocarbons, or CFC propellants, some of which have been shown to have negative effects on the environment". I'm not a big fan of slathering my body with butane, propane, or isobutane, but I understand their use in this type of medium. So it's up to you to decide.

This company does have non aerosol body wash available too..

The resulting foamy wash comes out thick, it is creamy. Because it reminds me so much of a shaving cream, that it what I have been using it for. Then whatever is left over I use on rest of body. Is pleasant smelling enough to me but it isn't quite a pure aromatherapy experience for me. Clearly it uses a variety of essential oils- rosemary, orange, eucalyptus, peppermint, limonene. However, for whatever reason, it contains "parfum (fragrance)" as an added ingredient. As well as Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, another synthetic fragrance ingredient. Is there not enough naturally occurring scent from the use of essential oils? I think the added synthetic fragrance is redundant and takes away from the olfactory experience.

As an actual wash, it is fine.
3 stars-- this is just a middle of the road rating. I am not in love. The experience is underwhelming. I am much too quickly going through the container. Aromatherapy experience is a little off as I pick up on something other than essential oils. Otherwise the cleansing action is fine. But.. I likely won't repurchase.

I think if I really want a foam wash, I will just use another body wash or make my own wash and pour into a foaming soap dispenser.

title: Best hairdye ever
text:
Hands down best hair dye ever, and I've tried a bunch of brands. It lasts the longest and has the most vibrant colors.
It smells like cherries and has the consistency of something like cold cream.
For best results I bleach my hair to at least a medium blonde, although it is best practice to bleach as light as you can go. Don't even try it with black hair, it won't show at all.
I wash my hair once a week and the vividness last at least a month if using sulfate-free shampoo and cold water. Thereafter the color starts to fade into a lighter and less saturated tone, but still pretty. Since my hair is damaged by the bleach, the dye stains my hair and it settles to it's final color in about 4 months.
The dye helps smooth out my hair considerably after a damaging bleaching session.
I only wish they had more colors and jared versions since getting it out of the bottle is a pain when you reach the bottom. This stuff also stains your furniture and bedding (dark colors moreso than others)

title: I REALLY hope they bring the original formula back because this new version is NOT equal to the original and certainly is not be
text:
I just bought this product at a Dollar Tree store, which USED TO carry the original formula of this lotion. I REALLY hope they bring the original formula back because this new version is NOT equal to the original and certainly is not better.

I am a BIG lotion user. My skin doesn't do well without it. I can't have dry feet and hands, it just doesn't work for me. I bought Suave lotion for years because of the agreeable cost (I'm cheap) and the acceptable quality of the product but when I lucked up on Dermasil at Dollar Tree, I found a gold mine! This stuff was top notch and I haven't looked at Suave since finding it, even though it costs a lot more. It was creamy, rich and thick, didn't evaporate and leave you reapplying continually and it was unscented, which made it great for adding your own fragrance to or using on your face if you're sensitive to fragrance. I routinely would buy 10, 10 oz tubes at a time just to keep a good supply on hand, to satisfy my pack rat compulsion and to take advantage of the price. I keep one at work, one in each of my travel bags, I keep some in a smaller container in my purse, I use it on my face with no negative results, it's great for my feet, you don't need a whopping amount of it, the original is just wonderful stuff!! So this weekend I went hunting for more and happened upon this version. The store only had two tubes of it and they were not 10 oz but I bought them anyway. As soon as I tried it I was extremely glad that I only had two tubes of this stuff to get through. It is not as thick or rich, it is not matte like the original either. It's kinda glossy as it comes out of the tube. And you know how you can feel cold air so much better when you use perfumed lotion? Check! And the crowning offense? It has a smell. A hint of chemical to brighten your day. The original has a faint hint of this same smell, which I only noticed after meeting the new version but this version has it a lot stronger. I wouldn't go near my face with this stuff. It's awful in comparison with the original...AWFUL!! I frankly don't know what I'm going to do with the two tubes I bought. I'll think of something. I'm just glad they were from Dollar Tree because I haven't lost any money to speak of.

If you can find the original, grab all that you can! The original formula is STILL wonderful lotion. This new so-called "Advanced Treatment" molarky, however, is for the birds. I don't know what happened, the good ingredients shot up in price, ceased to be available or what but every formula change is not a GOOD formula change. Uuuuuuugh, that smell...

title: A Thick and Rich Eye Cream.
text:
EDITED REVIEW as of 9/25/21.

I came back to edit this review and to lower my rating from 4 stars to 3 stars. Here's why:

After a few weeks of using this cream, I started to develop some sensitivity to it. When I say sensitivity, here's what I mean: 1) The scent bothered me more than it did when I first used the cream. In fact, I started to sneeze most evening after applying it. 2) I'd used the cream on other areas of my face, and noticed minor breakouts in those areas.

Basically, I think the cream was just too oily for my skin. Even around the eye area, which has virtually no oil glands, the non-absorbency of the cream left me feeling sticky and greasy even though I gave the cream plenty of time to absorb.

End of Edit.

***************************************************************************************************************************

Everything else I said in my original review still stands. But the above edit may help you decide if this is the right eye cream for you.

If you're looking for a natural, plant-based eye cream that is ultra-thick and rich, you'll find it in this 2 oz. jar.

The jar will last a VERY long time, because you only need a tiny amount of this cream to cover the undereye area and the corners where crows feet form.

I'd advise putting the cream on a couple of hours before bed, since it takes quite a while to absorb into the skin. (If you don't wait, you'll end up depositing most of the cream on your pillowcase.)

I've also used a small amount of this cream on other areas of my face (nose to mouth lines) and the results were the same as around my eye area.

So what were the results? The skin around my eye area looked smoother and brighter after one night of use.
The results on other parts of my face were less noticeable, but I believe continued use of the cream will improve the results in both the eye area and on the face.

I'm rating the cream 4 stars instead of 5, because of one major issue I have with it, which is: THE SCENT.
The cream has a rather strong minty (?), menthol (?) medicinal smell that takes some time to fade away.
Since I prefer NO SCENT in eye/facial products, I deducted one star from my rating.

That aside, if scented products don't bother you, and you want a thick, rich eye cream you will probably enjoy using this one.

title: Calming face balm
text:
This is a Korean face balm, that is supposed to sooth sensitive skin and cover up redness on the skin. The instructions and all the ads on Amazon are in Korean, and I HIGHLY recommend that the sellers switch this to include English instructions. I had to go to their website in order to find out the ingredients and what it was supposed to do for the skin, and most people aren't going to do that.
To continue, the balm contains 2 plant ingredientspine sprouts and centella asiatica roots. The cica pine water helps sooth and moisturize sensitive skin. The color in the balm comes from calamine powder, which helps cover red areas of the skin. It is a 100% vegan formula. The balm comes in a compact with a puff applicator. The puff is eco-friendly and anti-bacterial. This is meant to be applied as the last step during the skincare routine and before you apply your makeup.

Overall, I found this product easy to apply. You dip the poof into the cream balm, and then apply it to the skin. It has an almost creamy texture on the skin, and absorbs in quickly. It has a slight white cast when I used it but that went away as it absorbed in. I was hoping to use this as a color corrective on red areas on my skin before I applied concealer (I currently do not use foundation). This product has everything I like. A likeable backstory about the founders, produced in small hand crafted patches, and delivers the quality results that it promises.

I wear my hair short (buzzed on the sides) with about 3-4 inches on top, which I style differently depending on the day. I usually like it combed to the side, and pushed back, but with volume to give it a nice swoop. My hair is fine, but a lot of it.

I’ve never been a fan of pomade in the past because I find it doesn’t hold it’s shape and is too shiny. However, this pomade provides a natural looking shine, while holding my hair in my preferred style. The pomade itself is very light and thin. I didn’t think it would work when applying, but within seconds it began to form my hair into my go-to style. It dries to a “tacky” feel, which allows you to readjust throughout the day, but wouldn’t feel comfortable to run your fingers through it. After applying, the product easily washed off my hands, and out of my hair at the end of the day.

The scent is good but not overwhelming. It has the typical “masculine” scent that you will find in deodorants, body wash, shaving cream, etc. for men. The scent lingers till you wash it out.

Overall, I will definitely be using up this entire jar.

title: I'm not sure this is worth the price asked...
text: I've always wanted to get into the art of doing my own acrylics so when I saw this drill set, I knew I had to review it.  Firstly, it comes with numerous accessories- a fluffy brush for removing dust from the nail and work area, a set of to separaters for painting, a nail board, and the drill bits themselves.  The entire set is nicely packaged and comes nestled in a velvety foam materials.  The bits are held in their own clear container within the box.  The set comes with a detachable adapter that plugs into the end of the drill and then into the wall outlet.  The drill itself is small enough to handle pretty easily, although I can see where it would be difficult for someone with smaller hands than myself (I have large hands.)  Inserting and removing the bits can be a challenge.  The mechanism isn't well made so I have to fight with it.  The power cord is much too short and I had to use an extension cord to give myself some wiggle room away from the wall outlet.  Some of the bits' textures do a better job than the others, while some don't do anything at all.  The over all look and feel of the set isn't worth the price, in my opinion.  It works a bit too awkwardly to be something I'd use that often.

title: Simple to Use & Perfect Results Every Time!!
text:
I LOVE these bun makers!! I have an old bun maker that I've been using for years, but that one just got tossed in the trash because these new ones are SO much easier to use and the finished product looks much better!! These bun makers are unique in that they are foam, which helps to grip your hair to better hold it in place. They also have a very strong inner wire that holds them in place in a perfect circle. I have relatively long (just past my bust line) hair with long layers - the trick to getting all of the end pieces of the layers to stay tucked in place is to pull the bun maker down the length of your ponytail just before you reach the end of the shortest layer. Then, fold all of the rest of the ends upward over the hair piece and tuck them inward towards the center of the ponytail. As you roll the hair piece upwards, continue to tuck any loose ends in so that they are held in place by the rolled hair. The other trick to getting a perfectly round bun is that once you have rolled the hair piece all the way up with your hair, fold the ends inward towards each other to form a circle, but make sure to tighten this circle as much as possible by pushing the ends as close together as you can. Otherwise, these hair pieces are fairly self-explanatory to use, and there are step-by-step instructions included with each of the four bun maker pieces. In addition to these four pieces, this product also includes 2 sets of 8 bobby pins -- 1 set is about 2" long each and the other set is about 3" long.
*I received this product at a discounted price in exchange for an honest, unbiased review.

title: Good coverage for quick and casual makeup days.
text:
I'm 49 with decent skin aside from some minor redness/capillaries near my nose and a couple dark spots here and there.

I bought this for a quick 'more coverage than powder' solution for when I have last minute zoom calls for work.

While definitely good for the purpose I use it for, the coverage is moderate at best. Goes on well and stays on fairly well. Evens out most of my skin tone, aside from a couple dark spots. Definitely works better over a primer than just over moisturizer, which isn't a huge issue for me. And patting it on, as the instructions state versus swirling it on does result in a fuller coverage and nicer finish.

While in person it wasn't as blurred and flawless as a full makeup, it definitely was suitable for video calls or more casual days.

I didn't notice any transfer, but I did have to touchup my chin and nose after a few hours, which was very easy to do (no problem with old over fresh not blending well)

If feels very soft and light on my skin. Very comfortable. I almost forgot to take it off at the end of the day I first wore it, as it felt very natural.

For my purposes, this worked exactly as I hoped. I would definitely consider buying it again, although it is not a holy grail replacement for my liquid foundation.

title: Bargain Water Flosser
text: I guess I was not as impressed with this as others were. It seems very lightweight and fragile. When first taking it out my immediate instinct was to twist or pull off the bottom blue water tank. There is a strange little warning sticker on the back that rules against this. Instructions also say not to do this but then mention cleaning the filter that is in the tank that you cannot remove. I didn't like the little translucent rubber cap covering the charging port. It is not attached to the unit and is sure to get lost. The rubber "O" ring on the tank fill door and the door itself seem poised to fall apart. The unit does, however, function as it is intended. The stream on the high setting is pretty powerful (also good for getting the cat off the table ) the tank lasts about 30 seconds and there is water everywhere. Make sure you use warm water if you have sensitive teeth, shooting cold water at you gum line can be pretty uncomfortable. So I will probably use this till it breaks or looks too dirty to clean, but I think for my next one I will try a Waterpik brand.

title: Softest soft, not for exfoliating
text:
I have been using a loofah but I feel like I wanted something that could easily reach my entire back without having to be a total contortionist in the shower. A brush with handle seemed like the obvious choice.

The first one I bought had bristles on it and it was so hard it hurt to use so I couldn’t even bear the discomfort on my back. That one was better for scrubbing feet or less sensitive areas.

This one is completely different and luxurious. The handle is a thick bamboo that is sealed. It’s a neutral colored wood but very attractive. There is some wrapped smooth rope on the base of the brush for holding. It makes the brush less slick when it’s wet and soapy. There is also a hole with a piece of that same rope for hanging. I use the rope to hang the body brush off of my shower caddy.

The bristles are extremely soft! They are pure white and have been cut so that they have a texture for the skin. The bristles are tightly positioned and there are a ton of tiny ones. They are as soft it not softer than some of my smoothest make up brushes. It’s soft enough that it could be used on my skin without irritating it.

Now the flip side is that because it is so soft there isn’t any exfoliating action. I wouldn’t mind some slightly more rigid like a loofah for really deep cleaning. It’s even softer than a wash cloth but closer to a makeup cloth. This brush is really going to depend on the user and the need. It’s not for exfoliating.

title: Stunning!!
text:
I started my electric shaving experience with a Norelco. It was admittedly awful though somewhat less painful than the blade! I moved to a foil shaver (Braun) for about 10 years (two shavers) and recently had the opportunity for a full-featured upgrade. I was able to try the new Brauns at a local shaver store and was impressed and then tried the Spectra model. I was FLOORED. This is an excellent shaver. Battery life is unreal (I get about four-six weeks -- can't estimate well yet as I have only charged it ONCE after initial charge!), cleans in water, shaves quickly (and well), and very quiet. Yes, there is hype and gimmicry on this model (but the color, display, and battery are great!) and you may do just as well with a [less expensive] Spectra (or Quadra), but this is a great system. It looks and works really really great! :)
UPDATE (11/13/03): I am nearing a year of use on this shaver and nothing has changed. This is a great product. THe battery life I initially reported is amazing still. I can get a decent shave in a minute or two. Am very impressed with this.

title: Great and functional, but similar to very strong liquid latex
text:
Pros:
- fine tipped brush makes it easy to apply
- a fine wing tip is easy to draw, once the product dries and hardens on the brush a bit
- waterproof, smudgeproof, an accidental rub won't ruin it. a hydrogen bomb probably won't remove it.

Cons:
- reminds me of strong liquid latex; sticks to itself and pulls off in pieces. it's difficult to remove without a lot of soap and makeup remover. it gets caught in my eyelashes and hurts like hell trying to pull it out. rubbing it off has been the most effective method of removal after using makeup remover, but then the hardened substance gets in my eyes.
- because it's similar to liquid latex, it makes me (possibly irrationally) believe my skin can't breathe well underneath it.
- dries hard (latexy) in the tube
- if it remotely gets on your eyelashes (which it will), you can forget about using mascara. (see photo)

Other notes:
- it is glossy. I prefer matte, but this is subjective. (see photo. this was taken ~4 hours after application. dried and settled by then.)
- the handle is a little farther from the drawing tip than I'd prefer for finer control
- it took all the king's horses and all the king's men to unscrew the tube for the first time

I'd purchase this product again, if I can't find a comparable non-latex-like product.

title: Dont Judge the Cream by the Packaging
