title: Too dark for blond hair.
text:
I received this product for free through the Vine program.

I requested this for my wife who was looking forward to trying it. She was less impressed after actually using the product and below are her impressions:

Now, to be honest, I have not used eyebrow powder before. I typically use a pencil. I do so because my brows are nonexistent by the time they reach my arch. The included photo shows what I typically get from my pencil on one eye and the new stamp on the other. I found that applying the powder is faster than my usual pencil routine. However, I still had to spend time cleaning up all the excess powder from above and below my brow after application and I had tried to get any excess off the stamp prior to use. This ESpace eyebrow stencil kit is labeled light brown. My hair is medium ash blond, and this eyebrow powder is WAY TOO DARK for my coloring. The stamp has two colors, and I picked the one that looked least dark. I know my head is small and although the kit includes twenty-four eyebrow stencils, they all seem too big for my face. Assuming you have an average head size these stencils might work for you. The kit’s brow razor works fine. If you like dramatic large brows this system might work better for you than it did for me.

title: Nice grooming set
text:
My husband used this kit and took, when asked to do a bit of a review on it for me, took it very seriously. The price isn't cheap so he wanted to make sure to really look at everything as he used it. Here is what he had to say:

"You have a pack of accessories here so I thought I would run through them in turn to tell you what you are getting and my impression of it

Shampoo and body wash.
Okay, I ran through this way too quick and used all of it. It's good. It's really good and I couldn't really get enough of it. So that's a plus and a negative in that there isn't really a lot of it to begin with.

Face wash.
I love to get In there and give my face a right good scrubbing. This helps. The wash is thick and gel like with the exfoliating, and it does feel like you have given your face a good scrub after use. You do feel cleaner after use.

Shave cream
I'm not one for using cream very often. I prefer basic foam from a can. But wow. This stuff leaves your face feeling clean and fresh after shaving. Not only that but incredibly soft.

Moisture cream
This is really not something I use at all. I would think it best to use after shaving because you are stripping moisture from your face, but in that regard the shave cream is sufficient. I just don't personally have a need for a separate moisture cream. So it is sort of hard to form an opinion about it.
What I can tell you is that it doesn't really have a scent, my face does feel super soft. On the downside it is a little messy and I found myself wiping away the excess.

For the most part then I really like this set. It comes in a handy pouch you can use long after the accessories are empty. However, that won't take too long because the bottles are very small. It's something for people who aren't concerned about the cost. It's very expensive. Is it worth the cost for me? Not really. Not in terms of either quality or quantity but if the price was lower I would be recommending to everyone."

There you go guys and gals. That's what he thought about the set. He's still talking about it so he did like it, just thought it was a bit much.

This comes in a one gallon jug. There are two negatives to me. First, the biggest negative is that it takes work to dispense the lotion. Second, this lightweight lotion goes on tacky and takes a few minutes to absorb. Once absorbed, however, it is lightly moisturizing and it leaves my skin soft.

This is vegan per the bottle and the lotion is scentless. My favorite lotion is [[ASIN:B09HYPWMKG Ginger Lily Farms Pure Morocco Argan Oil Butter Lotion]]. That is perfect for a massage as well. It has a fragrance and is cruelty-free but not vegan.

This is decent but the initial tackiness I dislike. The current price of $54.99 for 128 ounces comes to $.43 per ounce, which is almost double the price of the lotion I love.

title: Very nice moisturizer
text:
This intensive moisturizer by Easydew is a very nice cream and runs you $45. I would still consider this a mid-range priced product for the quantity you are getting. It comes in a simplistic looking squeeze tube, that almost looks medicinal in my eyes.

The cream has a very pleasant fragrance that I personally really like. The cream itself is a medium weight in my eyes and does take a little bit to absorb into the skin fully. It does leave a slight greasy residue on the skin that takes some time to fully disappear. Because of this I would recommend this as an evening cream because you wouldn’t want to apply foundation over it, nor would you want to wear a face mask all day while having that on your skin. I found that products like this make me sweat quite heavily under face masks.

I use this in the evenings and do find that in the morning my skin looks nicely moisturized, is soft and smooth. So it does look exactly as I would expect it to with this kind of product. To achieve all this you really don’t need that much of the product either which is great because it is not the cheapest product, however also not the most expensive either. All in all I do really like this but only like using this in the evening.

title: Weird wig, but it worked
text: I used this as part of my Peg Bundy costume for Halloween. I had to make some adjustments, but in the end it worked and looked pretty good. First off, the wig cap itself is oddly large in the top. I think this is how it gets the height for the "bump" of the hair. But when wearing it, it's just empty space between the top of the wig cap and the top of your head. And it's not structured at all to help it hold that shape. So I did what any 80's-90's kid would do, and put bump-its on my head, underneath the wig to help fill out that part and give it structure. Also, a headband was necessary to cover up where the bangs meet the rest of the hair, as it was just really weird looking. Then a little teasing and a little aqua net and boom--good to go. I will say also that the wig cap rubbed on my ears uncomfortably, probably compounded by the fact that I had to wear a headband with it. I mean, it's a costume wig, so you get what you get with those, but this was my experience with this purchase.

Next you get a moisturizing and healing cream. This is great for those who have done some damage to their hands in some physical hand jobs where they hand up with dry and cracked hands. This gives back some moisture and heals those hands.

Last but not least is a nice protect and moisturizer. This adds a nice barrier to your hands but also adds much needed hydration to much abused hands that are dry, cracked and scaly. When you have this on your hands it is much easy to wash and wipe away stubborn dirt.

This is a nice little set that can also be gifted, especially for people who work with their hands like mechanics or wood workers but many others. This works really well and will help restore some of those much abused hands.

title: Careful not to clog tub with crystal rock. Great texture. One bath per 9 ounce bag
text:
I enjoyed using and reviewing this salt/rock mixture. I could never imagine paying $34 for a single bath, so this was likely a once in a lifetime experience for me.

Pros: It smelled great and had a great salt texture. The oils felt silky smooth and I enjoyed the 30 minute bath. However, I did not feel any different after the bath as per usual.

Cons: The bath costs more than a trigger point massage. My back, leg, shoulder muscles felt about the same following a typical epsom salt bath. So the oils and texture appear to be more for the bath experience than the healing.

I regretfully have to deduct 2 full stars for the price and 1 star for the 1 ounce rock that could clog your plumbing if it slides down the drain.

text: I hadn't had much experience with waxing, however I have tried wax pearls before and that definitely wasn't working for me, and though I usually just stick with good old fashioned razors but I thought I would try these easy to use wax strips. They are pretty easy to use too! The instructions are on the back of the box and they even have pictures for you to follow. To heat up the wax strips all you have to do is use your hands and rub them and the heat from your body allows the wax to warm up enough for you to pull the paper apart. You simply stick the wax strips on the area that you want the hair removal. It didn't really say how long you should leave it on before removing it but I feel like it needs to cool a bit to get a bit harder before you pull it off. One of my issues is that I didn't feel like it pulled off all the hair that I wanted to be gone within that area that I put the strip. If I am going to go through some pain for this hair removal I don't want to have to do it multiple times on the same area of skin. To finish up you are supposed to open the post cleaning wipes, however they left my skin oily and feeling kind of greasy and I didn't like those. text:
This is an excellent shampoo and conditioner set. It's nearly perfect. I'm putting this at a 4.5. Now I don't know if this is just my hair being obnoxiously dry or not but that would be the only thing that I could say anything remotely "bad" about. The conditioning was just not quite enough on the ends of my hair. Great on the already healthy stuff, just seemed to ignore the drier ends. Figured I'd get that over with and move on to the good stuff.
This really gave my hair a nice shine to it. My hair is getting old with me and it no longer wants to be as manageable and tame as it once was. With this duo of delight my hair looked healthy after it dried. It looked good when left to air dry, when dried with the hot air brush, and when left to air dry. It looked shiny without the added matching shine spray (which is also a wonderful product) and with. I left out the word smooth in this so far but let me tell you! It was also smooth and sleek without having to use other products to make it stay that way. Granted, under all that grey old hair there has always been fairly thin straight hair so this just really put it back to looking like it used to in that regard. The shampoo cleaned it to the point of being squeaky clean as well.
Give this duet a try if you can. It works really well and smells alright to boot!

title: I really wanted this product to work but...
text:
for me it was an unqualified failure.

I am trying to treat the knuckle of my right ring finger. It is arthritic and I have treated it very successfully in the past at a clinic that, among other things, used a paraffin bath. The bath was by far the most effective part of my therapy. I didn't want to have something so large to store at home so thought these gloves would be perfect.

I am unable to relate to other reviewers who mention the gloves fit almost any hand comfortably. I'm not sure how hands are sized but I can tell you I wear a men's right hand golf glove, size medium and it is a tight fit. The next size up would be the Cadet which, based on the sizes offered at the golf store fits right in the middle of men's sizes. Golf shops allow you to try gloves on without requiring purchase so this may be a good method to see if your hand will fit this product.

The first Paraffin Hands glove I tried would not allow my right ring finger more than half way into the finger of the glove. My little finger would only go in to its space by about 25%. Not wanting to force the issue, I left the glove alone and waited the prescribed 10 minutes. No benefit. The second time I tried the same glove, the plastic at the side of the middle finger ripped through to the inside wax while I was trying to get the glove to fit better. Again no benefit after 10 minutes.

The second Paraffin Hands glove fit much better, with the ring finger going in to its space about 75% and the same for the little finger. The other fingers went in about 90% being about 10% away from the tip of the glove and the space between fingers also being about 10% away from the palm of my hand. Gently pushing the glove toward my palm to get the best fit caused another break in the plastic of the middle finger so it followed its predecessor into the garbage.

This product still sounds like a good idea but the manufacturer really needs to enlarge the size although I am somewhat skeptical there is enough wax in the glove to give one the benefit I am looking for.

It is also supposed to absorb oil, so I suppose it's a deshiner.
On the product page it reads:
"This weightless dry texture spray for hair provides a manageable and light hold without the crunch. It has long staying power and keeps your hairstyle in place without looking or feeling stiff"
Consequently, I thought this would be like a light hairspray, but it's really not.
It smells nice and is easy to apply, but does not hold my hair.

In the end, I feel like this is sort of a body enhancer and mattifier, so maybe more like a waterless shampoo?
Honestly, even after using this I am still not sure.
I feel like this is going to work best for anyone with oily hair who wants to absorb the oiliness to give their hair more lift.

title: Mostly good results, wasteful packaging...
text: I had mixed results with these 3 products.  The eye patches are gel patches and not meant to be wet with serum - the serum is released by the gel when it's in contact with skin.  The patches easily stayed in place, but resulted in no visible improvements, and left my undereye area feeling a little dehydrated.  The lip patch is also a gel patch.  It was odd to wear, but it stayed on while I moved around and almost seemed to form a suction seal around my mouth after 10 minutes.  I liked this patch - it left my lips smooth and soft for a day and a half...nice!  The foot booties are for moisturizing only...these are NOT exfoliating booties that take days to work and lead to skin peeling.  They were easy to use and comfortable to wear.  I wore them for 30 minutes and was quite pleased with how soft my feet still felt after 2 days.  My only issue was that after removing the booties I had to spend a good amount of time massaging in the lotion left on my feet...seriously, even after trying to dry them with a towel my feet felt greasy.  Be sure to allow time for the product to absorb afterwards and don't plan to run out the door like I did.  For all of this, I would give the set 4 stars.  However, there's an EXCESSIVE amount of packaging.  The patches all have plastic protectors on both sides, are enclosed in plastic clam shells, and are sealed in the final package.  I felt guiltier than usual when I saw the pile of trash I generated by using this set...these items are definitely over packaged.

title: Works much better than acetone, but watch your surfaces!
text:
Do you see “100% Natural” and think “Yeah, right!” or do you assume it won’t work as well as products that have chemicals? I do this all the time especially when it comes to cleaning products or makeup. In this case I was offered a bottle of Pure Body Naturals™ 100% Natural Nail Polish Remover and the skeptical part of me was sure this wouldn’t turn out well. But in the spirit of trying new things, I agreed to review it and put it to the test. **See the images for before/after photos**

For my test I painted my nails several different colors. We all know deep reds are harder to get off and glitters can also be a pain to remove. I dedicated my left hand to the Pure Body Naturals™ 100% Natural Nail Polish Remover and my right hand I used a drugstore brand of acetone polish remover (the super cheap stuff I usually use.) Both hands got two good coats of polish.

To remove the polish the Pure Body Naturals™ remover instructions say to drop or dab it on and wait 2-3 minutes before wiping. For the generic acetone remover I just apply and wipe with a cotton ball.

The Pure Body Naturals™ remover wiped right off, taking most of the polish with it. I did have to reapply a small amount, wait a few more minutes and all but one tiny trace of the red polish was gone. The acetone remover left polish near my cuticles even after a hard scrubbing and a second try.

So what did I like?
-I like that it works better than the acetone remover, even on the darkest red and glitter!
-I like that it did not make my nails feel dry.
-I like that the Pure Body Naturals™ remover doesn’t have harsh chemicals.
-I like that it isn’t tested on animals.
-I like that it comes with a handy glass dropper.

The only problem (and it could have been a BIG one) is this polish will eat through any polish, including vanish on my dining room table and styrofoam plates. No kidding. I started out thinking to drip the remover over a plate to keep it off the table but it quickly melted the styrofoam and one small spot of the table varnish.

Only use this stuff in the bathroom over tile or a sink with no finish/paint/lacquer, etc. never over a delicate surface like your dining room table!

I received a free sample of this remover to review. I have given my honest opinion and the real test/comparison results.

title: Decent Brush For Thin Short Hair
text:
As most of us are in quarantine and not currently getting regular hair maintenance, having weird hair right now is just normal. I am growing out a pixie cut, not by choice, but by mandate of the State of Michigan. I have experienced a number of difficult hair transitions during this stay home, stay safe period, all of which I hope to never experience again. Currently, my hair is just too short to tuck behind my ear, so it is constantly falling in my face, but thankfully, I am past the super trendy mullet stage.

When I had my pixie cut for seven years I washed my hair and dried it with a towel and went on with my life. No comb, no brush, no anything. It was really nice. Now that I actually have hair that tangles and needs attention I require tools. I have a brush with tight bristles that I like, but it pulls. I use leave in conditioner gel that seems to help, but I still pull a lot of hair. I have a very inexpensive comb that does absolutely nothing and I should probably just recycle it.

This specific comb and brush set is definitely not the fanciest around. The comb has some heft to it and it does a good job getting my part straight. The brush is very stiff compared to my other brush, but it does not pull all my hair out when it hits a tangle. I also like that this brush doesn't mash my hair down. I have thinner hair and this brush doesn't make me look like I have thin hair.

I don't use any styling products or tools, so I am not hard on my brush. I think this brush will hold up just fine in my hands, but I think if I person were using it with lots of accessories and products it might be a placeholder for a more expensive brush.

title: Questionable ingredients
text:
When I read the product page, it sounded like this foot cream had some of the same ingredients as some of my favorite lotions, so I thought it would help soften my rough, cracked feet. It wasn’t until the package arrived that I saw what was REALLY in this product, and I was NOT pleased. However, I was willing to give it a try.

Aside from the aloe, green tea leaf extract, water and coconut oil, many ingredients in this cream are kind gross or not helpful. The complete list is: urea, salicylic acid, deionized water, green tea leaf extract, coconut oil, dodecane, cetearyl alcohol, polysorbate 60, clyceryl stearate, PEG-100 stearate, cetyl alcohol, aloe barbadensis leaf juice, tea tree oil, glycerin, propylene glycol, carbomer, xanthan gum, ethylhexylglycerin caprylyl glycol, hexylene glycol, phenoxyethanol.

The gross part is the main ingredient: 40% urea—a major component of urine. Salicylic acid is used in wart-removing solutions because it exfoliates your skin. Dodecane is a chemical used in jet fuel which can cause skin, eye, and respiratory tract irritation. Alcohol dries out your skin. Xanthan gum is just a thickening agent made of corn. I am personally allergic to that and stearates. And the other chemicals are kind of sketchy, too.

I tried this stuff on my feet for a couple of weeks, applying before I went to bed and wearing socks to protect my sheets. I really didn’t see any significant change in the condition of my feet than when I apply regular alcohol-free lotion. It makes no sense to me that anyone would use this stuff so full of questionable chemicals, paying $27 for a little pot of this cream, when a regular bottle of lotion works just as good or better and goes for a fraction of the cost.

title: This last year it's gotten pretty bad. I decided to give this stuff a ...
text:
So I have been dealing with adult acne for well.. 10+ years. This last year it's gotten pretty bad. I decided to give this stuff a try, because why not... Well it is actually making a difference, like more than anything else I have tried. I have only been using it a week, but I am seeing a reduction in new acne and I am seeing the skin production rate sort of go up so my skin is healing faster. I think this product causes minor inflammation of the face, which is partially responsible for the smooth looking skin. I am seriously very impressed with this product, and I will follow up in a few more weeks with hopefully some even better results.

I am using Tretinoin .05 also, which dries up my skin a ton. This stuff actually hasn't produced any additional peeling, and I am actually using it in place of lotion. Now my skin has already become accustomed to the super peely tretinoin, so your results may vary. For me though, this is much less irritating and I think it's making a solid companion to my prescription tretinoin.

title: pretty colors, some staying power
text:
Okay, I love eyeshadow palettes and probably have too many, and they range in price and brand. I definitely love the 'sunset/rose gold' palettes, and this reminds me of a Huda palette I have with similar shades. It's in a slim, cardboard palette without a mirror, but this is a lower price point for all the shades you get. The shadow itself is a creamy powder blend, and it suggests that you use your fingers for the metallic shades (I find a small crease blush works fine and tends to have less loose powder that way).

You have a nice mix of matte and metallic shades this way, with a lot of earth tones. Definitely a lot of copper and reds here, some golds and rose golds and pinks. Colors that will stand out but not all of them. These felt nice on the skin and blended well. Why the three stars?

I tried this with and without primer, and this kit definitely needs primer to last more than a couple of hours on my skin. Also? The mattes will last several hours, but not the metallics even with primer (as well as a setting spray on top). I love the metallic colors, but they just fade on me somehow - even if I layer them on top of the matte. I'm used to eyeshadow blending on me after a few hours, but never have I seen metallics melt away on me like this. That's not to mean it won't work better on other people.

Still, for the price it's a nice range of colors and a fun palette to play with, so it's worth a try.

title: Made in USA. Smells fresh and energizing, nice lather, rinses clean
text:
Three pack of individually boxed hard soap bars that smell wonderful and fresh. Quite an uplifting aroma. thyme, rosemary, sage, lemongrass..mmm. Natural chlorophyll and organic cloves create a deep green color. The soap has lather, soft clean feel. I use this as a hand soap, but it can be used all over anytime- very nice soap that inspired me to see what else they have to offer. Not knowing anything about Elsha, I learned that it is a USA company that was established in 1935 offering cologne products, and eventually perfume and soaps. These soaps are handmade in USA. Although the eagle on a flag shield screams, "'merica!", the product listing would do well to say this (their other listings do). The box that the soaps come in are gray with an Elsha sticker on it. No information as to what it is, what is in it, where it is is from, etc. If there was at least an insert of information I would feel better about buying this as a gift. The website had produced just enough information to make me feel better about trying this soap, otherwise I had no idea what was in it or where it originated. That being said, it is a good soap and I would consider it again.

For those who may not know what a power inverter is, it is a basic device that you can plug into a dc vehicle outlet and converts it so you can use an ac device. (DC outlet to AC outlet.) This one does have an extra bonus as it throws in two USB charging ports. The USB ports are rated 1amp and 2.1amp. (Use the higher one for your tablets and heavy power hungry devices.)
This takes in 12volts DC and puts out up to 150 watts which is plenty for normal ac devices such as laptops and portable electronics. It is only 9.6 oz and measures 4.3” x 3” x 1.7”. It is made of metal and is very durable so you can toss in your glove or utility box so it is ready to go. Cable is also nice and long so you can reach from front of the car to the middle area so others can use from all the other seats.

Cons – One thing I did notice is that the DC plug did not have a fuse in line. The description indicates this has over and under voltage protection; however, I am not clear if this is for the usb ports and or if this applies to the ac outlet as well. Other inverters typically offer fuses or a fuse if you remove the end cap on the dc plug. (On the up side, the soldering inside the dc plug was very nice and solid with nothing loose or questionable.)

Tips / Notes – Make sure your vehicle is running when you use this. This has potential to draw a good deal of power if using the upper range of 150watts and can run down your battery if the vehicle is not on allowing your alternator to prevent battery drainage.

Summary – This works as described and is very small. It has a built in fan to keep this cool as it works. It is very quiet and does what is expected. I would recommend this to friends and family.

title: It's coconut oil and really nothing more
text:
Like so many others I want to believe there is something natural that can repair hair bonds down the shaft . . . but we know better don't we? Hair is dead when it grows past your scalp. It's dead. Like the part of your fingernail past your finger.

You can dress it up, but there's no life in it. So repair is a process of closing the cuticle. No oil has been proven to do that.

But hot oils can give temporary relief by essentially overwhelming the hair shaft. But it won't stay that way. And if you have fine hairs, the oil will weigh you down. This did that.

This is no better than ordinary coconut oil. There is no repair, but also there is no temporary closing of the hair shaft cuticle. So . . . minus 2 stars for false advertising (hair repair... no) and minus one star for being just an ordinary oil slick and nothing more.

title: It’s got a thick gooey consistency and spreads pretty easily. Bare in mind that the thinner you ...
text:
This product gets a lot of mixed reviews and that’s probably because people have the wrong idea as to what this mask actually does. At first my expectations were completely off too. It’s a peel off mask so I’m expecting to pull something out expect “What? It didn’t pull anything out at all!” However, the one thing that made me rethink this mask was that even though it didn’t pull anything physical out of my face I did notice these tiny little white spots on the peeled mask and at first I thought they were air bubbles. The next time I used it, I made sure I didn’t have any air bubbles, one slick, black, mask. When I peeled it off again, there they were! Little white spots that are slightly translucent, then it finally clicked. This mask is called Sebum Out! It says nothing about blackheads or whiteheads removal, its meant to tackle sebum (precursor to black/white heads) which is oily/waxy so if the mask is to pull anything out… it’s not going to be anything with a physical shape hence those translucent little spots!

Now with that cleared up, it’s a totally different kind of review! It is very soothing. It’s got a thick gooey consistency and spreads pretty easily. Bare in mind that the thinner you apply this on your face the harder it is to take off. My rule is to apply enough that I no longer see my skin tone coming from underneath the mask. It’s shiny black and smells somewhat minty but very light and the rest of the scent borders medicinal/earthy which isn’t bad or anything. After you apply it, its very cooling and minty. It takes a bit of time to dry completely especially if some areas have a thicker application. The peeling process is pretty painless and easy, slow and steady though. Overall it’s a pleasant experience. I use this mainly for my troubled areas (nose, chin, and T-zone)

title: This Mask Is Awesome
text: So I've tried A LOT of sheet masks and NONE of them worked for me. They either broke me out, or didn't secure on my face right, or they just didn't do anything for my face at all. It wasn't a life-changer or game-changer for my hyperpigmentation, but it's unrealistic and next to impossible for any product to do that after only one use. My skin loved this though, I can tell that this is perfect for my skin type (combination/oily acne prone skin). I thought I'd swore off sheet masks. title: Dinosaur.
text:
You can tell Intuit is feeling the pressure and knows they're losing relevance by the way they've put this together. Quickbooks itself is fine. It works. It does what quickbooks does (which is create headaches and break regularly, along with compromising your security and privacy if you don't lock it down). However, when you pay $250-300 for some software, the software is only a small part of the package.

Customer service and tech help are the two biggest parts of the package, and well.... They're just crap....

Making the payroll side of this a subscription system after charging an extra $100 is just greedy. Forget it. I can find open source payroll systems that're more secure, easier to use and free sans the donation I will make out of appreciation for work well done.

If you're going to charge a subscription, don't make me pay up front. If you want me to pay up front, don't charge a subscription. Under no circumstances will I tolerate double dipping from a software company.

Sadly I'm a bit too lazy to move all of my information over to another system just yet, so it looks like I'm stuck with QB's not-so-funny little quirks for another year.

title: The good, the bad and the ugly...
text:
My review consists of the good, the bad and the ugly. First,
the good - I finally found a curler that 'fits' my eyelid. Huh, you say? Well, it appears that most of the manufacturers believe I have golf balls instead of human eyes. The tool's shape is long and shallow enough of a curve to catch most of the eyelashes. It is comfortable to use, but takes a bit of practice. Once you are comfortable with the scissor motion (sorry, no other way to describe it) used to make the curl, you are rewarded with a nice, non-crimpy curl. The pad in this one is the best I have used. This tool also opens wide enough that even the most nearsighted or lush lashed amoungst us can get it close to the base of the upper lashes. The design over all is very well thought out. I recommend using an magnifying mirror if you have to use bifocals (I do). All that said, now...
the bad - there is no replacement pad and I am questioning how sanitary this is going to be in the long run. I agree completely with folks here who advise to REMOVE ALL EYE MAKEUP before use. Ain't nothing pretty about an eye infection. I am wondering out loud how to properly clean this curler to be certain it remains safe. If you are prone to sties and other types of infection, I would be asking the same questions. Which leads to...
the ugly - until you practice and are used to it (won't take long) the results are a bit odd looking. The black pad is plushier and looks to be made of silicone and not the usual hard rubber. I have found that the hard rubber pads are chiefly responsible for that weird ugly crimp you can get. Not so with this one. I mentioned before the squeezy scissor action your thumb and index finger have to use can be tricky. If you have coordination issues, well - things could get ugly.
SUGGESTIONS for use...wash your hands before use. I keep the little plastic clip to keep the tool closed. You could follow the advise of one person here to heat the tool with a dryer, but I think I may skip that. Use a makeup mirror to assist you. Practice when you have some time. Enjoy, Ladies - get out there and be lovely.

It has a sticky feel coming out of the bottle (mine came with a dropper rather than a pump), and it feels a bit odd going on -- sort of like rubbing mayonnaise into your skin. But then it absorbs well and leaves my skin a bit tighter and smoother. One reviewer has perfectly described the effect as akin to putting on pantyhose -- everything just feels held together nicely.

I can't honestly say I will re-order this, because I use a pore refiner that does a better job of leaving my face makeup-ready, and Vitamin C serum seems to leave my skin clearer and nicer. But this works well enough that I finished the bottle.

For those who want to use bamboo serum, this one is probably worth a try. Take a look at the wide variance in product pricing.

title: Good shampoo, a bit pricey
text:
I recently decided to enter my prophetic career by growing out my beard. I've always keep a few days growth, but I finally cut loose and embrace my inner Moses.

A few months into it, I realized a needed something more than a basic shampoo or soap for my beard. I was pleased to try Mr. Pristine's beard shampoo and so far I've been pleased with the results.

First of all, it smells great. None of the scents are overwhelming or powerful. The faint mint is nice and refreshing. Secondly, the lather is fine. I noticed that if I apply some to my hair and work a lather, it's nice and frothy. I then apply to my beard and give it a good cleaning. If I apply the shampoo directly to my beard, the later is noticeably less frothy. I don't know why this is.

At any rate, it's been working well for me and leaves me feeling nice and crisp after a shower. My only misgiving is the price, which is a bit steep for what you get, in my opinion.

title: Nice masks, nice results!
text: I’ve tried several different Karuna masks...they’re all good, but some are better than others.  This particular set is a great mix of masks designed to help with different needs, including hydrating, soothing and brightening.  The masks are individually wrapped and presented in a box that opens like a book, with suggestions for which masks to use on which days.  The packaging is nice and these would make a great gift.  The masks are very saturated (overly saturated, IMO) with serum, with plenty left over to use on my neck.  They’re large enough to easily cover my entire face, and come with a paper backing that makes them easy to to unfold.  Because they’re so saturated they easily slip while on my face, which makes it impossible to do anything other than sit still for the 20-30 minutes I wear them.  Also, there’s so much serum left on my face after I remove the masks, it’s impossible for my skin to absorb it all.  I’ve discovered that lightly splashing my face with cold water helps remove the excess serum and my skin fully dries more quickly.  Ultimately, all of the face masks left my skin very soft and hydrated, and a few of them plumped my skin and created a lovely even skin tone.  There is one set of eye masks in the kit and that that were surprisingly light and effective, reducing puffiness and brightening my eyes.  These are a tiny bit pricey, but they’re a nice quality and I like having a set of masks that cover a range of needs.

title: Nicer looking in person, drill bits in case attached under drill, files pop off sometimes,
text:
I got this to be able to do my nails from home.
Pros:
* Much nicer in person. The images listed don't do it justice. The box it comes in, the plastic that holds it, and the machine itself is sturdy.
The drill bits can be stored in a little case that pops open when you push the button on the mid-bottom portion of the case. The best part is that it can be stored in the bottom of the machine itself, so you don't lose them.
* The drill is powerful and it has a knob so you can make it faster or slower. (The origional images were lost so I had to retake them after I had tested it. Sorry, I like to take picture of it before use. So excuse the arcylic bits from the nail.)
* It was powerful enough to file acrylic nails but it did get warm around the last nail. Not hot just warm it was pretty good for shaping all 10 acrylic nails.
*Grip it well but just gradually add pressure to the nail if you are a beginner until you get the feel of it.
*You have to hold it down for 3 seconds to turn it on after plugging it in. It will turn blue for forward motion and push it again and the light will switch to red for backward motion.
Cons:
* The reddish-brown filing pieces, that attach to one of the bits, has 4 pieces but they are flimsy. They don't look like they will last very long and they are thin.
*The dial can be adjusted but there are no numbers or levels. You just move it around until you think you have the speed you want. I don't like that because if you know a certain level you are comfortable with you to have to make your own markings with a sharpie or something because it's kinda hard to remember where you had it for a certain nail (real vs acyclic) or for certain drill bits. (minus half a star)
*There is no "click" when putting the drill bits in so you just have to push it in as far as you can. However, I did this and sometimes it would fall off, so I had to push it in as far as I could. (minus half a star)
Conclussion:
All in all I would recommend this for yourself or as a gift. The images from the seller should be updated somehow because their photos make it look kind of cheap or tacky but it really isn't once you see it. It has a good weight to it so it isn't cheap material (but the reddish-brown file did seemer lower quality). The machine itself is really good and we are all in quarintie so they are much cheaper and safer than going to a nail salon. Plus it is powerful enough for acrylic.
**Disclaimer: I got this product free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

This toner contains polyphenols which are actually micro nutrients and good for you, I know it sounds bad so I had to look it up. title: A beauty industry expert's professional opinion
text:
Not all Obagi products are made at the same place -- but i found out that this formula is made by one of the top skincare labs in the US--one that manufactures high-end dermatologist and clinical skincare brands on the market today. So knowing this, i knew there would be *some* efficacy to this product. I actually LIKE that ingredients are straightforward and not full of fluff:

Water (Aqua), Dipropylene Glycol, Ethoxydiglycol, Caffeine, Malonic Acid, Zinc Carbonate, Arginine, Laureth-9, Copper Carbonate Hydroxide, Hydroxyethylcellulose, Sodium Hydroxide, Phenoxyethanol, Ethylhexylglycerin

To be honest--if you're looking to reduce eye puffiness and dark circles, this won't do much. If found no visible evidence of that in my use. BUT--it's really good at minimizing fine lines, plumping up the skin, and returning elasticity to the skin. That's why it's called "Elasti-derm", to help coax the skin into being more hydrated, refined, and pliant, thus reducing the signs of lines. Obagi's main active to do that is malonic acid, and I give a big thumbs up to the addition of arginine-- a powerful delivery vehicle to help drive the malonic acid further into the skin for more efficacy. As many in the skincare industry know, anything with arginine helps make the active ingredient even more "active".

The stainless steel ball is not just a "feel good" gimmick -- it actually helps to massage this serum into the delicate eye skin, further pushing the ingredients into the dermis. After using an entire bottle of this product, i definitely experienced a reduction in the signs of my fine lines. the skin was plumped up and the lines less visible, plus the texture more refined. Used in conjunction with a good eye cream and alternating with Vitamin C serum, this is a great addition to any anti-aging regimen. I would surely purchase again.

I take off one star because I do not like the plastic packaging, as glass is the safest material for stability, and plastic has a tendency to shorten the shelf life of a formula. Plus plastics are not as safe we think.

title: Plenty of foot spas on Amazon...hard to choose, but I chose wisely.
text:
It took me over 2 weeks to finalize my purchase of a foot spa from Amazon. There are so many foot spas and tons of reviews for them all, but we're all looking for the best value here. I finally pulled the trigger and purchased this model. Our previous foot spa was purchased from Walmart and had a heater, massage rollers (manual rollers) and bubbles, roughly costing around $60. So my budget for the next spa would be under $100. Today was my first day using it (1.5 hour usage:)

Pros:

Heater: Works like a champ! I put relatively hot water into the basin to begin with (Onboard thermometer read 101 degrees.) I then increased that heat to 105 and it maintained that temp throughout the duration of my use...only slight temp changes to 106 every once in a while, but that's to be expected.

Shower / Waterfall: I didn't think anything of this when purchasing it, as I felt it was a gimmick. It's actually quite soothing and has a purpose here....I used it for probably 75% of the time.

Automatic massage rollers: Holy cow...they are strong, but feel absolutely amazing. There are 6 separate massage rollers that have several white balls on each that do all the massaging. The rollers are powered by a motor at the bottom of the unit with the drive shaft come directly up, center of the basin, which is a square shaped metal rod that fits into the bottom of the massage roller plate (which can be removed easily.)

Deep basin: I'm 6'3", 200 lbs...water completely submerges my feet and ankles and as plenty of room to move my foot back and forth or side to side.

Cons:

Handle: There is a handle that folds flush with the unit, but beware....each side of the handle is connected to the basin with 2 small metal screws. The entire handle and what it's connected to is plastic and doesnt feel secure when the basin is filled with water. But there is plenty of surface area on the bottom of the unit to easily get ahold of it while moving and the wheels are big enough to set the unit on the floor without squishing your fingers in the process.

Bubbles: Not a con for me, but my wife likes bubbles...So I guess it could be considered a con? Personal pref, but def not a deterant as this foot spa is great without.

Top room / Control panel: I wear size 12 male shoes...I have to point my feet downwards to enter the basin as the control panel is quite large. Just as above, this isn't that much of a con as it is really just an ease of use thing. Once your feet are in the water, you're in Heaven.

Considering how much use we got out of our last foot spa, I can see us using this foot spa multiple times throughout each week. Given that, I'll be sure to update this review as much as possible because I'm quite aware at how difficult it is to purchase a foot spa comfortably without questioning it's worth.

title: Nothing spectacular. I have received more... for this price.
text:
This Hair Removal Device by Ulike just as well as a couple of other IPL devices I have that cost much less. It comes packaged nicely, though I kept trying to open the flat two-sided green piece that covers the accessory side. It doesn't open.
The device does look quite fancy, and I was interested in skin rejuvenation, which is in one of the photos (that is mentioned in the other listing that shows this exact same device). The instruction booklet contains about as much as the empty listing page that I ordered it from. That page has no bullet points, only one photo.
They do have another listing for this same exact device, showing the accessories, extra photos with bits of information, and bullet points telling a little about it. I got my information from there.
The device does have the cooling feature, as many others do, which helps it not to zap too badly. It also comes with a razor and eye protection.
What it lacks, that many others include that are in or around this price range, is more attachments for the device. There needs to be at least one smaller light head for use around the lip area, as it's very hard to use the main one with the device being so large.
This IPL device works pretty much as well as any other, with none having the ability to make you completely hair-free at any point in the future. As far as the studies that I have seen, with diligent use, home IPL devices can only offer a little better than 50-60%-ish less hair.
My preferred device, which costs very little more than this one, has several attachments, including some specifically for skin rejuvenation. You do get a fancy box with this device, and it looks nice, but I don't think it provides any more or less than devices that cost much less.
I haven't found one yet that really only takes 10 minutes to do your legs, but if I ever do, that is the one that would probably take the cake! If you like fancy boxes and a sleek-looking device, I would recommend this one.

title: Very happy with this razor
text:
I am very impressed with this razor. I have used electric razors most of my 35+ years of shaving. I was skeptical using it for the first time, I thought it wasn't working because it is so soft to the face and so quiet. It didn't sound "agressive" like my other razors did. WRONG!!! The shave was close, my skin was not irritated at all, and it cut smooth basically in the first pass. This unit is first class.

My previous razor was a Braun foil. I bought one for myself and another for my son from Frys because of the price. JUNK!!! We both have heavy beards, he more so than I, and both of us had terrible 5 o'clock shadows by 10:00AM! And the skin irritation on my neck, just horrible.

I took a long time comparing all the available models. For me this model provides the best mix of features and price. I definitely recommend the Speed-XL shaving heads. Other nice features are it can be cleaned under the faucet, it charges quickly and maintains that charge for a long time, and it provides what I consider one of the best shaves I've had in a long time. The heft and feel is good. Materials are good. Workmanship is good. The only feature I'd like to have is a battery charge indicator.

The other Speed-XL model is the 8160. It includes the cleaning system with a much higher price. Now there is the SmartTouch-XL which may be overkill. But if price is not an issue...

May, 2012 - I can't believe I wrote the original review almost seven years ago. I'm still using this razor and it still works just as I expressed back then. The battery still keeps a great charge, and the shave is still excellant. I went on a 10 day vacation last year and the charge held for the whole trip. This is truly a great product.

title: Truly devious packaging
text:
I bought this from Target because I'd had a fairly good experience with their deodorant. The shampoo itself is OK, but the bottle it's packaged in is designed to keep you from actually getting what you paid for. I'll explain.

The curved shape of the bottle itself probably makes it very efficient to pack/ship, but it also makes it difficult to squeeze, especially in combination with the thick, rigid plastic they use. And because the "nozzle" (or whatever it's called) is offset rather than centered, you cannot balance it upside-down to make it easier to get the remaining shampoo out as the bottle gets low. The combination of these three factors (rigid plastic, thin curved shape, and offset "nozzle") means that at a certain point, you're going to have shampoo left in the bottle that you can't actually get out, unless you want to rig some kind of device to balance the bottle upside-down.

This may seem like a minor complaint, but with basically ANY other brand of shampoo (or body wash, EMJ does this with those as well), you don't have to deal with this. It's wasteful, and it feels like it was probably designed that way on purpose, to get consumers to buy the next bottle faster. Given that the shampoo and body wash (which I also tried) isn't anything particularly special, I can't recommend anyone bother with this. You can get equal quality and "clean ingredient" shampoos from so many other companies with bottles that aren't designed like this.

I believe this product has really helped clear up some of the discoloration issues that I suffer from and lessened some of the wrinkles that I have started to notice popping up here and there.

The one flaw of that their Retinol Cream has is something that I have run into a few times with different products that I use or have used. The smell. Now, I am not saying that the cream smells bad. title: I want my Remington back
text:
I had a Remington wet/dry that finally got outdated and I thought to replace it. I did a lot of research and decided to try this Panasonic. I was really excited when it got here and the first time I used it I loved it and was all set to write a raving review. But I thought I should wait a couple weeks. I am very unhappy with it, as it turns out. I wish I had my Remington back (or got a new Remington). Yes, the Remington is a little louder. But this one is loud too - you can hear both of them from many rooms away. So really, that's not a big deal. I ended up getting another Remington and it is much better.

What got me is two things with this one:
1) The sides that hold the razor in place are taller than the razor area. So when you go to get a close shave, the sides of the unit scratch/scrape your leg. It is plastic, so no blood drawn or anything, but it doesn't feel good. Has no one else noticed this? I went to do a quick shave on my calves and ended up with stripes from the sides of the unit scraping my legs. And it didn't even get the little stubble. I didn't think the Remington was that fantastic, but it did better than this. Someone suggested to put the side extenders down. I do see the extenders (per the angry reply to this post), but they are down all the way. The won't go any farther down. So your angry post is not applicable. If I did not apply force to my leg with the razor, the length of the stubble it left was ridiculous. Again, maybe very long stubble is just the way it is, but not with my two Remingtons. They got much closer without having to apply force.

2) It vents out the cut hair once in a while all over your leg. You could be shaving along la di da and all of a sudden get a huge area of hair. I thought "I already went over that area?" but it was just the hair that got spit out from the razor. It is a little gross, I'm always wiping the cut hair off my leg. I've had two Remington's that did not do this. The Remington might have left the hair on the ground, or kept it in its head for me to clean later, but I prefer the Remington that didn't spit out puffs of hair on my legs incrementally. Again, the angry reply to this about including a vacuum is a bit silly.

Another disadvantage is that this one's charger plugs straight into the outlet, instead of having a cord. So I have to find an outlet to leave it in to charge that my kids won't get to. I like the cord better, so I can plug the cord in behind my dresser and have it sitting on top of my dresser in the little charger base. This one, you have to put the razor in the charger directly into the outlet. I could deal with this though if it didn't spit hair out all over my leg or leave scrapes down my leg. Yes, you could get an extension cord, so it's not that big of a deal. Just one more thing to add to a poor design IMO.

title: THE Standard in premium shaving
text:
I've tried at least a dozen shave soaps, maybe two dozen. MWF is my go-to, standard. I leave it in a shave bowl in a drawer. I rinse my brush and then swirl the dripping wet brush on top of the soap. In about 20 seconds, you have phenomenal lather. Wet and repeat for more water if needed. Lather around your face further as needed. I often do this, then take a shower and repeat the lathering when I get out of the shower, and then shave.

I have found a few artisan soaps that lather as good, but none better. Those artisan soaps often come in a variety of delightful fragrances, but I don't care that much about fragrance. MWF doesn't have much of any fragrance. In fact after having wet it and let it dry a few dozen times, there is no discernible scent of any kind. If you like the smell of MWF (or any other shave soap), keep it in a covered container between uses. I'd suggest for those who like fragrance in their shave soap to just put MWF in a covered container and sprinkle in a little of their favorite cologne a few times and keep it covered and you'll have a $40 artisanal shave soap!

I like the ingredients. It's tallow based which I prefer. There's lanolin in it which I like. Although it's not a glycerin based soap, there is a little glycerin in the ingredients - it doesn't seem to be a large amount, so if you really like glycerin, get some vegetable glycerin on Amazon and sprinkle it on top of the soap or add it to your pre-shave. It doesn't have shea butter in it, so I sometimes keep an open puck of shea butter shave soap in a shave dish next to MWF and occasionally reach down with my brush and lather from both.

I've seen some reviews that say that it doesn't lather all that well in "hard" water. We have moderately hard water in my city and I've never had trouble at all.

Finally, it's cheap! I lather before showering; after showering, and usually a second time while shaving, and my brush is full of lather when I finish and my single puck will last for maybe 300 shaves?? so maybe 4 cents a shave??

title: Are you a terrorist in search of a new torture technique? LOOK NO FURTHER!
text:
This stuff could be used as a torture device in interrogations...after using it on my chest, stomach, shoulders, and groin, it feels as though I have been laying in the summer sun ALL day. Imagine bright red sunburn with bubbly skin, as though you've gotten sun poisoning. I spot tested it and everything seemed fine. I was so incredibly wrong. Rinsing in the shower really just made it burn even worse, even with seemingly FREEZING cold water. The "Calm Balm" was almost like squirting lemon juice into a fresh, open wound. Even a whole hour after using it, while having a fan blowing cold air on me from outside, it STILL feels like one of the worst sunburns I've ever experienced. Worst part is, I don't even have slightly sensitive skin... Only after using nearly half a tube of Neosporin did the pain begin to subside. However I now look like a giant, shiny, "sexy" red lobster. And I want to scream like a lobster does in a pot of boiling water. I now know their pain. I used the product exactly as directed...using the sticks, waiting ten minutes, and then using the exfoliating glove, which itself caused extreme discomfort while "lightly buffing" the skin (imagine taking 100 grit sandpaper to a sunburn). In fact I think the exfoliating glove is what started all of the pain. I figured "Hell, I'm a manly man, BUFF THROUGH THE PAIN!!!" But holy balls it was like trying to use a hairdryer to put out a forest fire.

In closing, this product is AWFUL, and I want to jump into the nearest frozen lake I can find, in hopes of dying of hypothermia & drowning, because that would be less uncomfortable than these tubes of terrorist cream. To angry wives/girlfriends, this would be PERFECT if your man has been cheating on you and you seek revenge. Otherwise between that, and the previously mentioned terrorist torture techniques, I truly see NO market for this product. Any review that states otherwise is clearly written by a terrorist or angered girlfriend/wife.

I plan to contact the manufacturer for a full refund. This is crap.

title: Its good, but not great!
text:
Its good, but not great!
So I got this Tuesday 2/2/16 and just got around to use it today. I am a 46 yr old Latina woman with very thick, processed hair. My hair is very dry and I am trying to use less damaging tools. My hair is dry in these picture too. I actually wear a bun everyday to work and I had washed my hair last night. So my hair is dried at this point. As you could tell from my before and after pictures its actually works ok. I am giving this product 3 stars cause it actually took 15 mins to get this look afterwards. It actually takes me that much time if I would of used the hair dryer and the hair dryer look is a lot smoother than this look.

The temperature actually gets up to 230c which is equivalent to 446f which really doesn't seem to be that hot. especially because I was holding the bristles with the palm of my other hand when I was brushing it through. (I don't suggest for anyone to do that ok?). And the on/off buttons are literally on the side where I actually have my thumb for more grip to it. Which I hope if this manufacture decides to remodel this, they should really think about moving it cause I kept press the "minus" button and the temperature would go down.

I am going to keep this cause I think my 11 year old would enjoy it more than I did especially because she always seems to be burning herself with my flattener and it just seems safe for her. She also has better hair. A bit wavy, but It actually would be better for her.

Good Luck to everyone and I hope my review was helpful. Cause lord knows there is many reviews here that are not to useful for me. :-)

title: Decently longevity and appearance, but some shades not wearable
text:
This lipstick set comes in 2 sets of 5, Set A and Set B. I wound up only opening the "A" set, as after trying these 5 and finding only 2 to work for me, I decided to give the "B" set away. From the photos, I thought that the colors would be nice and muted, but that's not really the case. The color I am wearing in the photo is "Almost Friday," which is a pretty neutral, nude-ish pink. I also kept "Blush for Me," a light, brownish peach. The red shade, "Red for Me," was very bright and didn't seem to belong to the rest of this collection. But the other shades seemed MUCH less intense than in the product photos. Rather than buying a set of 10 like this, I think most people would be better off choosing individual shades that work best for them.

Two other things to note. When I opened one of the lipsticks, the color cylinder popped out and onto my floor, so I wonder about quality. Also, to open the tubes, you have to unscrew them rather than simply pull the top off. This might be good for some who carry around lipsticks in a bag, but for quick everyday use, it's annoying.

title: Messy Bun Mess
text:
This messy bun is made from synthetic hair and comes with 2 black nylon-like stretchy bands and 10 black bobby pins. Right out of the package, the messy bun was true to its name. It was a mess! It took awhile to find the tousled strands (which I've included a close-up shot of one where it's held into its tousle with a tiny clear rubberband). I sorted through the bun and pulled all of the longer parts through one end so they might hang better for a natural look.

I wear my hair in messy buns a lot, but I just can't get this hairpiece to look good on my head. I believe that the color does play a small role in my dissatisfaction, as the top of my hair is much more blonde BUT the underside of my natural hair that I pull up IS much darker and matches the shade of the brown tones much better.

Unfortunately, the entire design of the bun just doesn't work well on my thin hair. The photos I've shared are of it secured around a bun of my hair with a few bobby pins. I think this piece might work better for people who have thicker hair. I also suggest trying to match the top layer of hair rather than the underside that you pull up if your hair is darker underneath like mine.

text:
I ordered this for a practice run with contouring and highlighting. The price was where I was looking to spend on a first time kit. The product arrived on time and packaged inside bubble wrap. The brush was inside a plastic cover. The makeup was intact.

The makeup is larger than the picture shows. All of the colors seemed to blend to contour well. The darkest color was slightly too dark for my fair skin so a little goes a long way with that one.

The brush is very nice. It’s quite soft and blends the colors smoothly and seamlessly. The handle makes it easy on my wrist.

I did not like the highlighting color. It was not pigmented and did not show up. That is my only complaint about this kit. I ended up using highlight makeup for my eyebrows on the rest of the areas on my face. I had to send it back. I was really hoping to find a one in all kit. Sadly this is not the kit I am looking for.

If you’re looking for a good beginners contour kit this may be a good option if you don’t mind the highlight not showing up well.

title: Wheres the Argan Oil?
text:
I love almost all Amazon products, and am obsessed with Argan Oil. This product really disappointing me, not only does it not smell like Argan oil it doesn't make your hair feel like the oil is in the product at all.I use all Argan products because I have very thick hair and the oil is great for moisture and de-tangling. Most Argan Oil products are very rich with oil, and you can smell it the second you open the bottle.The shampoo was very drying and almost strips your hair of oil, and the conditioner has a weird smell, nothing exotic or musky like Argan oil.

I am literally giving this to my 11 year old son, because I spent $25 dollars on it, the spray for heat is the same issue.... I see alot of great posts, I dont think many of these people have used real Argan Products if this is the case. They are really missing out.

title: Philips Review
text: The Philips Norelco T980 is a very good beard and hair trimmer.  The motor is strong, giving a very even cut.  The vacuum function works very well capturing the clippings easily.  The only negative is that the cutting blade is inset too far into the head making it very difficult to trim close to the nose.  Lip, chin, and jaw are no problem, but the area just under the nose has to have special attention with scissors.

title: Surely is Rapid!
text:
I’ve used many different eye creams in the past. In choosing to take a chance on this one I was literally
shocked at what I witnessed upon applying this under my eyes. I wake with puffy eyes, semi wrinkles coming in at age 50. After cleansing my face I turn to this to work it’s magic. It only takes a very small amount to apply. I’ve never used the word shocked in a review but what I saw within a 2 minute period did just that. The area under my eyes instantly smoothed out & looked as if I had skin of a 20yo again. The longer I let it sit before applying my serum & moisturizer the more smoothing & softened the area became. This isn’t a harsh eye cream. I had no stinging, no bad reaction, it worked perfectly for my skin. There’s no scent to it. It comes nicely out of the dispenser. The smoothed & tightened area that I’ve clearly noticed remains this way even after the rest of my facial regime. I’ve never had anything like this before with truly how rapid it works on my skin upon applying. This morning I used it & moisturized my face only. What an amazing difference that again has lasted. Rapid Reduction it definitely is. A 1 ounce tube will last me awhile since a little goes a long way. Genuine quality with this cream & I highly recommend it. You’ll see the results!

title: Best for the very young and perfect complexions
text:
I do not know a lot about makeup. I am not sure if it is common knowledge that foundation powder like this is only good for nearly perfect and youthful skin. I did not know that until now! I'm in my late 30's and using this powder really highlighted every pore and I never thought my skin looked crepe-y until I put this powder on it.

My photo comparison top to bottom is: no makeup, then using this powder foundation (in light), then using just my normal concealer that I just smear all over my face and call it a day.

It did help even my skin tone though and covered up broken capillaries. But overall it made me look much older than I ever thought I looked. If you are very young and have microscopic pores and just want to even out your skin tone I would recommend this.

title: Clean Teeth, short battery life
text:
I am enjoying this toothbrush. After a good brushing job, my teeth feel almost like i left the dentists. The 'sonic waves' really do dislodge plaque and leave a very clean mouth.

Great for me because i travel frequently and do not feel like carrying a toothbrush charger.

One odd thing, though, is that my first set of batteries only lasted a week. I just put in a second pair of batteries and am waiting to see how long they last. I brush twice a day, so ordinary amount of usage. I tried a pair of fully - charged NiMH batteries today (I think all NiMH rechargeables are 1.2 V) and the tooth brush would not start. Seems that it needs 1.5V batteries. It worked fine with ordinary alkaline batteries.
